ADAR.basis: The primary role of ADAR is to edit and 'mask' cellular dsRNAs, which are frequently produced, and prevent recognition by innate immune receptors

ADCY5.job: makes a messenger molecule that passes signals inside cells
ADCY5.basis: Catalyzes the formation of the signaling molecule cAMP in response to G protein signaling

ADGRG1.job: helps brain cells settle into the right layers as the brain develops
ADGRG1.basis: Involved in cortical development, specifically in maintenance of the pial basement membrane integrity and in cortical lamination: association with COL3A1 in the developing brain inhibits neuronal migration

ADGRL1.job: helps nerve cells form connections and release their chemical messages
ADGRL1.basis: Receptor for TENM2 that mediates heterophilic synaptic cell-cell contact and postsynaptic specialization. Receptor probably implicated in the regulation of exocytosis

ADK.job: helps cells recycle adenosine, a building block of DNA's chemical cousin RNA
ADK.basis: Adenosine kinase that mediates the phosphorylation of the purine nucleoside adenosine ... Plays a key role in the detoxification of modified adenosines ... Modified nucleosides are derived from the degradation of RNAs

ADNP.job: helps control genes needed for brain cells to develop
ADNP.basis: May be involved in transcriptional regulation ... May be required for neural induction and neuronal differentiation
ADNP.alt: helps control which genes are switched on, including in developing brain cells

ADSL.job: helps cells build AMP, one of the building blocks of DNA and RNA
ADSL.basis: Catalyzes two non-sequential steps in de novo AMP synthesis ... and thereby also contributes to de novo IMP synthesis

AFF2.job: is thought to help decide how genetic messages are cut and pieced together
AFF2.basis: RNA-binding protein. Might be involved in alternative splicing regulation
AFF2.alt: may help decide how genetic messages are cut and pieced together

AFG2A.job: helps cells copy their DNA smoothly by clearing worn-out parts of the copying machinery
AFG2A.basis: promotes replisome proteostasis to maintain replication fork progression and genome stability ... facilitating their proteolytic turnover from chromatin to ensure DNA replication

AFG3L2.job: clears out faulty proteins inside the cell's power plants, the mitochondria
AFG3L2.basis: The m-AAA protease carries out quality control in the inner membrane of the mitochondria by mediating degradation of mistranslated or misfolded polypeptides

AGA.job: cuts sugar chains off proteins so cells can break them down
AGA.basis: Cleaves the GlcNAc-Asn bond which joins oligosaccharides to the peptide of asparagine-linked glycoproteins

AGBL5.job: trims chemical tags off the cell's internal scaffolding fibers
AGBL5.basis: mediates deglutamylation of tubulin and non-tubulin target proteins ... Catalyzes the removal of polyglutamate side chains present on the gamma-carboxyl group of glutamate residues within the C-terminal tail of alpha- and beta-tubulin

AGK.job: helps bring certain proteins into the cell's energy factories, the mitochondria
AGK.basis: acts as a component of the TIM22 complex ... The TIM22 complex mediates the import and insertion of multi-pass transmembrane proteins into the mitochondrial inner membrane

AGL.job: helps break down glycogen, the body's stored sugar, for energy
AGL.basis: Multifunctional enzyme acting as 1,4-alpha-D-glucan:1,4-alpha-D-glucan 4-alpha-D-glycosyltransferase and amylo-1,6-glucosidase in glycogen degradation

AGO1.job: uses tiny RNA guides to block the reading of matching gene messages
AGO1.basis: Required for RNA-mediated gene silencing (RNAi). Binds to short RNAs such as microRNAs (miRNAs) or short interfering RNAs (siRNAs), and represses the translation of mRNAs which are complementary to them

AGO2.job: uses tiny RNA guides to find and silence gene messages
AGO2.basis: Required for RNA-mediated gene silencing (RNAi) by the RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC) ... AGO2 bound to a short guide RNA such as a microRNA (miRNA) or short interfering RNA (siRNA). These guide RNAs direct RISC to complementary mRNAs that are targets for RISC-mediated gene silencing

AGPAT2.job: adds a fatty acid to a building block cells use to make fats
AGPAT2.basis: Converts 1-acyl-sn-glycerol-3-phosphate (lysophosphatidic acid or LPA) into 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol-3-phosphate (phosphatidic acid or PA) by incorporating an acyl moiety at the sn-2 position of the glycerol backbone

AGPS.job: helps make special fats called ether lipids that build cell membranes
AGPS.basis: yielding the first ether linked intermediate ... in the pathway of ether lipid biosynthesis

AGTPBP1.job: trims chemical tails off the cell's internal scaffolding fibers
AGTPBP1.basis: Metallocarboxypeptidase that mediates protein deglutamylation of tubulin ... Catalyzes the removal of polyglutamate side chains present on the gamma-carboxyl group of glutamate residues within the C-terminal tail of alpha- and beta-tubulin

AGXT.job: turns a harmful waste chemical in the liver into a harmless amino acid
AGXT.basis: catalyzes the transamination of glyoxylate to glycine and contributes to the glyoxylate detoxification

AHCY.job: splits a chemical in cells into adenosine and homocysteine
AHCY.basis: Catalyzes the hydrolysis of S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine to form adenosine and homocysteine

AHDC1.job: switches on genes that help the skin's outer layer form in early development
AHDC1.basis: Transcription factor required for the proper patterning of the epidermis, which plays a key role in early epithelial morphogenesis

AHI1.job: helps cells build their antenna-like sensing hairs
AHI1.basis: required for ciliogenesis, formation of primary non-motile cilium

AICDA.job: edits antibody genes in immune cells so they make better, more varied antibodies
AICDA.basis: Involved in somatic hypermutation (SHM), gene conversion, and class-switch recombination (CSR) in B-lymphocytes by deaminating C to U during transcription of Ig-variable (V) and Ig-switch (S) region DNA ... necessary for efficient antibody responses

AIFM1.job: helps build the cell's energy-making machinery and can trigger cell self-destruct
AIFM1.basis: Functions both as NADH oxidoreductase and as regulator of apoptosis ... functions as a pro-apoptotic factor ... Plays an important role in the regulation of respiratory chain biogenesis

AIMP1.job: helps the cell's protein-building machinery work
AIMP1.basis: Non-catalytic component of the multisynthase complex. Stimulates the catalytic activity of cytoplasmic arginyl-tRNA synthase ... Possesses inflammatory cytokine activity
AIMP1.alt: helps the cell's protein-building machinery load amino acids, and signals immune responses

AIMP2.job: helps hold the cell's protein-building machinery together
AIMP2.basis: Required for assembly and stability of the aminoacyl-tRNA synthase complex
AIMP2.alt: holds together the cell's team of enzymes that load amino acids for protein-building

AIPL1.job: is thought to help other proteins fold properly and stay stable
AIPL1.basis: May be important in protein trafficking and/or protein folding and stabilization
AIPL1.alt: may help other proteins fold properly and stay stable

AIRE.job: teaches developing immune cells in the thymus not to attack the body's own tissues
AIRE.basis: Transcription factor playing an essential role to promote self-tolerance in the thymus by regulating the expression of a wide array of self-antigens ... induces the expression of thousands of tissue-restricted proteins, which are presented on major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) and MHC-II molecules to developing T-cells

AK2.job: helps balance the cell's energy supply and supports blood cell formation
AK2.basis: Plays an important role in cellular energy homeostasis ... Plays a key role in hematopoiesis

AKR1D1.job: helps the liver make bile acids and break down steroid hormones
AKR1D1.basis: reduction of the C4-C5 double bond of bile acid intermediates and steroid hormones ... This cis-configuration is crucial for bile acid biosynthesis and plays important roles in steroid metabolism

AKT2.job: helps cells take in sugar from the blood when insulin signals
AKT2.basis: AKT regulates glucose uptake by mediating insulin-induced translocation of the SLC2A4/GLUT4 glucose transporter to the cell surface

AKT3.job: helps cells grow and survive, and plays an important role in brain development
AKT3.basis: regulate many processes including metabolism, proliferation, cell survival, growth and angiogenesis ... It plays an important role in brain development

ALAS2.job: starts making heme, the part of red blood cells that carries oxygen
ALAS2.basis: condensation of succinyl-CoA and glycine to form aminolevulinic acid (ALA) ... Contributes significantly to heme formation during erythropoiesis

ALB.job: keeps fluid in the blood and carries fats, hormones, minerals and drugs
ALB.basis: Binds water, Ca(2+), Na(+), K(+), fatty acids, hormones, bilirubin and drugs ... Its main function is the regulation of the colloidal osmotic pressure of blood ... Major zinc transporter in plasma ... Major calcium and magnesium transporter in plasma

ALDH18A1.job: helps cells make the building blocks proline and arginine from glutamate
ALDH18A1.basis: converts glutamate to glutamate 5-semialdehyde, an intermediate in the biosynthesis of proline, ornithine and arginine

ALDH5A1.job: helps break down GABA, a chemical messenger that calms brain activity
ALDH5A1.basis: Catalyzes one step in the degradation of the inhibitory neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)

ALDH7A1.job: protects cells by breaking down harmful aldehydes left over from damaged fats
ALDH7A1.basis: Protects cells from oxidative stress by metabolizing a number of lipid peroxidation-derived aldehydes

ALDOB.job: helps the body break down fructose, the sugar in fruit
ALDOB.basis: In fructolysis, metabolizes fructose 1-phosphate derived from the phosphorylation of dietary fructose by fructokinase into dihydroxyacetone phosphate and D-glyceraldehyde

ALG1.job: adds a sugar to the sugar chains that cells attach to new proteins
ALG1.basis: Mannosyltransferase that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation ... Once assembled, the oligosaccharide is transferred from the lipid to nascent proteins ... Catalyzes ... the addition of the first mannose residues to the dolichol-linked oligosaccharide chain

ALG12.job: adds a sugar to the sugar chains that get attached to new proteins
ALG12.basis: Mannosyltransferase that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation ... Once assembled, the oligosaccharide is transferred from the lipid to nascent proteins ... adds the eighth mannose residue

ALG13.job: helps build the sugar chains that cells attach to newly made proteins
ALG13.basis: Catalytic subunit of the UDP-N-acetylglucosamine transferase complex that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation ... Once assembled, the oligosaccharide is transferred from the lipid to nascent proteins

ALG2.job: helps build the sugar chains that get attached to newly made proteins
ALG2.basis: Mannosyltransferase that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation ... Once assembled, the oligosaccharide is transferred from the lipid to nascent proteins

ALG3.job: adds a sugar to the sugar chain that gets attached to newly made proteins
ALG3.basis: alpha-1,3-mannosyltransferase that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation ... Once assembled, the oligosaccharide is transferred from the lipid to nascent proteins

ALG6.job: adds a sugar to the sugar chains that get attached to newly made proteins
ALG6.basis: operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation ... adds the first glucose residue ... Once assembled, the oligosaccharide is transferred from the lipid to nascent proteins

ALG8.job: adds a sugar to the sugar chains that get attached to new proteins
ALG8.basis: operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation ... Once assembled, the oligosaccharide is transferred from the lipid to nascent proteins ... adds the second glucose residue

ALG9.job: adds sugar building blocks to the sugar chains that get attached to new proteins
ALG9.basis: Mannosyltransferase that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation ... Once assembled, the oligosaccharide is transferred from the lipid to nascent proteins

ALPK1.job: detects a sugar molecule made by bacteria and sounds the immune alarm
ALPK1.basis: detects bacterial pathogen-associated molecular pattern metabolites (PAMPs) and initiates an innate immune response ... Specifically recognizes and binds ADP-D-glycero-beta-D-manno-heptose (ADP-Heptose), a potent PAMP present in all Gram-negative and some Gram-positive bacteria

ALPK3.job: helps young heart muscle cells mature

ALS2.job: helps the spinal nerve cells that control muscles survive and grow
ALS2.basis: Controls survival and growth of spinal motoneurons
ALS2.alt: helps keep the nerve cells that control movement alive and growing

ALX1.job: switches on genes that shape the face and skull as they develop
ALX1.basis: Sequence-specific DNA-binding transcription factor that binds palindromic sequences within promoters and may activate or repress the transcription of a subset of genes ... Most probably regulates the expression of genes involved in the development of mesenchyme-derived craniofacial structures

ALX3.job: helps guide how body tissues are laid out as an embryo develops
ALX3.basis: Transcriptional regulator with a possible role in patterning of mesoderm during development
ALX3.alt: helps switch on genes that shape body tissues as an embryo develops

ALX4.job: switches on genes that shape the skull, face, limbs, skin and hair
ALX4.basis: Transcription factor involved in skull and limb development. Plays an essential role in craniofacial development, skin and hair follicle development

AMACR.job: flips certain branched fats into their mirror-image form, including some used to make bile
AMACR.basis: Catalyzes the interconversion of (R)- and (S)-stereoisomers of alpha-methyl-branched-chain fatty acyl-CoA esters ... trihydroxycoprostanoyl-CoA (an intermediate in bile acid synthesis)

AMER1.job: helps tune a key growth signal that guides how cells develop
AMER1.basis: Regulator of the canonical Wnt signaling pathway ... Acts both as a positive and negative regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway, depending on the context

AMT.job: helps break down glycine, a building block of protein
AMT.basis: The glycine cleavage system catalyzes the degradation of glycine

ANGPTL3.job: is a liver hormone that helps control fat and sugar levels in the blood
ANGPTL3.basis: Acts in part as a hepatokine that is involved in regulation of lipid and glucose metabolism ... Has a stimulatory effect on plasma triglycerides (TG)

ANK1.job: helps red blood cells keep their shape by anchoring their outer membrane
ANK1.basis: involved in the stability and shape of the erythrocyte membrane ... Attaches integral membrane proteins to cytoskeletal elements

ANK2.job: holds salt and calcium channels in place in heart and muscle cell membranes
ANK2.basis: Plays an essential role in the localization and membrane stabilization of ion transporters and ion channels in several cell types, including cardiomyocytes, as well as in striated muscle cells

ANKRD11.job: adjusts how DNA is packed to control genes in developing brain cells
ANKRD11.basis: Chromatin regulator which modulates histone acetylation and gene expression in neural precursor cells ... Has a role in proliferation and development of cortical neural precursors

ANKRD17.job: helps the body's first-line defenses sense invading viruses and bacteria
ANKRD17.basis: Involved in innate immune defense against viruse by positively regulating the viral dsRNA receptors DDX58 and IFIH1 signaling pathways ... suggesting a role in innate antibacterial immune pathways too

ANKRD26.job: helps control how fat cells form and how much we eat
ANKRD26.basis: Acts as a regulator of adipogenesis. Involved in the regulation of the feeding behavior

ANO10.job: can hold back the activity of a related protein called ANO1
ANO10.basis: Does not exhibit calcium-activated chloride channel (CaCC) activity. Can inhibit the activity of ANO1
ANO10.alt: helps control a channel that lets salt move in and out of cells

ANO5.job: helps repair tears in the cell's outer membrane
ANO5.basis: Plays a role in plasma membrane repair in a process involving annexins

ANOS1.job: guides growing nerve cells and fibers that carry the sense of smell
ANOS1.basis: Has a dual branch-promoting and guidance activity, which may play an important role in the patterning of mitral and tufted cell collaterals to the olfactory cortex ... Chemoattractant for fetal olfactory epithelial cells

ANTXR1.job: helps cells grip the collagen around them and move
ANTXR1.basis: Plays a role in cell attachment and migration ... Mediates adhesion of cells to type 1 collagen and gelatin

ANTXR2.job: helps cells attach to the supportive material around them
ANTXR2.basis: Necessary for cellular interactions with laminin and the extracellular matrix

ANXA11.job: helps a dividing cell finish splitting into two
ANXA11.basis: Required for midbody formation and completion of the terminal phase of cytokinesis

AP1B1.job: helps sort proteins inside cells and send them to the right places
AP1B1.basis: plays a role in protein sorting in the late-Golgi/trans-Golgi network (TGN) and/or endosomes ... recognition of sorting signals within the cytosolic tails of transmembrane cargo molecules

AP1G1.job: helps sort proteins into the right delivery packages inside the cell
AP1G1.basis: Subunit of clathrin-associated adaptor protein complex 1 that plays a role in protein sorting in the late-Golgi/trans-Golgi network (TGN) and/or endosomes ... recognition of sorting signals within the cytosolic tails of transmembrane cargo molecules

AP1S1.job: is part of a machine that sorts proteins for shipping at the cell's packaging hub
AP1S1.basis: Subunit of clathrin-associated adaptor protein complex 1 that plays a role in protein sorting in the late-Golgi/trans-Golgi network (TGN) and/or endosomes ... recognition of sorting signals within the cytosolic tails of transmembrane cargo molecules
AP1S1.alt: helps sort proteins and send them to the right places inside the cell

AP1S2.job: is a small part of a sorting machine that packages proteins for delivery inside cells
AP1S2.basis: Subunit of clathrin-associated adaptor protein complex 1 that plays a role in protein sorting in the late-Golgi/trans-Golgi network (TGN) and/or endosomes ... recognition of sorting signals within the cytosolic tails of transmembrane cargo molecules
AP1S2.alt: helps sort proteins and send them to the right places inside the cell

AP2M1.job: helps cells pull in materials from their surface by pinching off tiny bubbles
AP2M1.basis: Component of the adaptor protein complex 2 (AP-2) ... AP-2 is involved in clathrin-dependent endocytosis in which cargo proteins are incorporated into vesicles ... The AP-2 mu subunit binds to transmembrane cargo proteins

AP3B1.job: helps sort proteins into packages headed for the cell's recycling centers and related compartments
AP3B1.basis: plays a role in protein sorting in the late-Golgi/trans-Golgi network (TGN) and/or endosomes ... involved in the sorting of a subset of transmembrane proteins targeted to lysosomes and lysosome-related organelles
AP3B1.alt: helps sort and ship proteins to the cell's recycling centers and related compartments

AP3B2.job: sorts proteins into tiny bubbles shipped out to the tips of nerve cells
AP3B2.basis: plays a role in protein sorting ... AP-3 is required to target cargos into vesicles assembled at cell bodies for delivery into neurites and nerve terminals
AP3B2.alt: helps nerve cells sort and ship proteins to their nerve endings

AP4B1.job: is the beta part of a coat that sorts proteins leaving the cell's packaging center
AP4B1.basis: Component of the adaptor protein complex 4 (AP-4) ... vesicle coat components involved both in vesicle formation and cargo selection ... AP-4 forms a non clathrin-associated coat on vesicles departing the trans-Golgi network (TGN)
AP4B1.alt: helps package proteins into tiny bubbles and send them to the right place in cells

AP4E1.job: is part of a coat on tiny bubbles that ship proteins out of the cell's packing center
AP4E1.basis: Component of the adaptor protein complex 4 (AP-4). Adaptor protein complexes are vesicle coat components involved both in vesicle formation and cargo selection ... AP-4 forms a non clathrin-associated coat on vesicles departing the trans-Golgi network (TGN)
AP4E1.alt: helps package proteins into tiny bubbles and send them to the right places in cells

AP4M1.job: helps cells pack proteins into tiny bubbles and ship them to the right place
AP4M1.basis: Adaptor protein complexes are vesicle coat components involved both in vesicle formation and cargo selection. They control the vesicular transport of proteins ... AP4M1 is directly involved in the recognition and binding of tyrosine-based sorting signals found in the cytoplasmic part of cargos

AP4S1.job: is the sigma piece of a coat that sorts proteins leaving the cell's shipping hub
AP4S1.basis: Component of the adaptor protein complex 4 (AP-4). Adaptor protein complexes are vesicle coat components involved both in vesicle formation and cargo selection ... AP-4 forms a non clathrin-associated coat on vesicles departing the trans-Golgi network (TGN)
AP4S1.alt: helps package proteins into tiny bubbles and ship them to the right place in cells

AP5Z1.job: helps sort materials inside cells as part of a cargo-handling complex
AP5Z1.basis: As part of AP-5, a probable fifth adaptor protein complex it may be involved in endosomal transport
AP5Z1.alt: helps move materials between compartments inside the cell

APC.job: breaks down a growth signal so cells don't divide out of control
APC.basis: Tumor suppressor. Promotes rapid degradation of CTNNB1 and participates in Wnt signaling as a negative regulator

APC2.job: steadies the cell's internal scaffolding of tiny tubes

APOB.job: forms the particles that carry fat and cholesterol through the blood
APOB.basis: Apolipoprotein B is a major protein constituent of chylomicrons (apo B-48), LDL (apo B-100) and VLDL (apo B-100) ... functions as a recognition signal for the cellular binding and internalization of LDL particles

APOL1.job: helps blood kill certain parasites by punching holes in them
APOL1.basis: A component of trypanosome lytic factor of human serum; plays a crucial role in killing Trypanosoma brucei by forming pores in parasite lysosomal membranes

APP.job: helps nerve cells grow branches and form connections with each other
APP.basis: performs physiological functions on the surface of neurons relevant to neurite growth, neuronal adhesion and axonogenesis. Interaction between APP molecules on neighboring cells promotes synaptogenesis

AR.job: responds to male hormones like testosterone by switching certain genes on
AR.basis: Steroid hormone receptors are ligand-activated transcription factors that regulate eukaryotic gene expression ... androgen receptor signaling

ARF1.job: helps package and ship proteins between compartments inside the cell
ARF1.basis: Small GTPase involved in protein trafficking between different compartments ... Modulates vesicle budding and uncoating within the Golgi complex

ARFGEF1.job: helps cells package and ship materials and keep their Golgi sorting center intact
ARFGEF1.basis: Involved in vesicular trafficking. Required for the maintenance of Golgi structure

ARFGEF2.job: helps cells package and ship materials in small bubbles between compartments
ARFGEF2.basis: Involved in the regulation of Golgi vesicular transport ... Involved in trafficking from the trans-Golgi network (TGN) to endosomes

ARG1.job: finishes turning waste nitrogen into urea so the body can get rid of it
ARG1.basis: Catalyzes the final step of the urea cycle by hydrolyzing L-arginine into urea, a nitrogenous waste product

ARHGAP29.job: switches off a cell signal so new blood vessels can form hollow tubes
ARHGAP29.basis: GTPase activator for the Rho-type GTPases by converting them to an inactive GDP-bound state ... suppresses RhoA signaling ... plays an essential role in blood vessel tubulogenesis

ARHGEF9.job: helps organize the connections between nerve cells
ARHGEF9.basis: Acts as a guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) for CDC42. Promotes formation of GPHN clusters
ARHGEF9.alt: helps gather the anchor protein gephyrin into clusters at nerve cell connections

ARID1B.job: helps unpack DNA to switch certain genes on or off
ARID1B.basis: Involved in transcriptional activation and repression of select genes by chromatin remodeling (alteration of DNA-nucleosome topology)

ARID2.job: helps unpack DNA to switch certain genes on or off
ARID2.basis: Involved in transcriptional activation and repression of select genes by chromatin remodeling (alteration of DNA-nucleosome topology)

ARL13B.job: helps shape the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
ARL13B.basis: Cilium-specific protein required to control the microtubule-based, ciliary axoneme structure

ARL2BP.job: helps a gene-switching protein get into the cell's nucleus
ARL2BP.basis: plays a role in the nuclear translocation, retention and transcriptional activity of STAT3
ARL2BP.alt: helps a signaling protein called STAT3 move into the cell's nucleus to switch genes on

ARL6.job: helps deliver proteins into the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
ARL6.basis: Involved in membrane protein trafficking at the base of the ciliary organelle ... required for sorting of specific membrane proteins to the primary cilia

ARL6IP1.job: helps cells take up glutamate, a nerve-signaling chemical, and shape inner membrane tubes
ARL6IP1.basis: Positively regulates SLC1A1/EAAC1-mediated glutamate transport ... Plays a role in the formation and stabilization of endoplasmic reticulum tubules

ARMC2.job: helps build the sperm's swimming tail
ARMC2.basis: Required for sperm flagellum axoneme organization and function

ARMC9.job: helps cells build their hair-like antennae and set their length
ARMC9.basis: Involved in ciliogenesis ... regulation of cilium length

ARPC1B.job: helps build branching protein scaffolds that let cells move and change shape
ARPC1B.basis: Component of the Arp2/3 complex ... The Arp2/3 complex mediates the formation of branched actin networks in the cytoplasm, providing the force for cell motility

ARSA.job: helps the cell's recycling centers break down sulfur-tagged fats
ARSA.basis: Lysosomal enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of cerebroside-3-sulfate ... into cerebroside and sulfate

ARSB.job: helps break down long sugar chains by snipping off their sulfate tags
ARSB.basis: Removes sulfate groups from chondroitin-4-sulfate (C4S) and regulates its degradation

ARSL.job: is thought to help build the right mix of materials in growing cartilage and bone
ARSL.basis: May be essential for the correct composition of cartilage and bone matrix during development
ARSL.alt: may help build the right mix of materials in growing cartilage and bone

ARX.job: switches on genes that guide brain cells and hormone-making pancreas cells as they develop
ARX.basis: DNA-binding transcription factor that plays a central role in the differentiation and development of type A pancreatic cells ... Required for normal brain development: plays a role in neuronal proliferation, interneuronal migration and differentiation in the embryonic forebrain

ASAH1.job: helps the cell's recycling centers break down fats called ceramides
ASAH1.basis: Lysosomal ceramidase that hydrolyzes sphingolipid ceramides into sphingosine and free fatty acids at acidic pH

ASH1L.job: adds chemical tags to the proteins DNA wraps around, helping control genes
ASH1L.basis: Histone methyltransferase specifically trimethylating 'Lys-36' of histone H3 forming H3K36me3

ASL.job: helps the liver turn waste nitrogen into urea and makes the amino acid arginine
ASL.basis: an intermediate step reaction in the urea cycle mostly providing for hepatic nitrogen detoxification into excretable urea as well as de novo L-arginine synthesis

ASNS.job: makes asparagine, one of the building blocks of proteins
ASNS.basis: Catalyzes the ATP-dependent synthesis of L-asparagine from L-aspartate

ASPA.job: breaks down a brain chemical called NAA to help keep the brain's wiring healthy
ASPA.basis: Catalyzes the deacetylation of N-acetylaspartic acid (NAA) to produce acetate and L-aspartate. NAA occurs in high concentration in brain and its hydrolysis NAA plays a significant part in the maintenance of intact white matter

ASPM.job: helps organize the machinery that pulls dividing cells apart, especially in the growing brain
ASPM.basis: Involved in mitotic spindle regulation and coordination of mitotic processes ... May have a preferential role in regulating neurogenesis

ASS1.job: helps the liver turn toxic ammonia from protein breakdown into harmless urea
ASS1.basis: One of the enzymes of the urea cycle, the metabolic pathway transforming neurotoxic amonia produced by protein catabolism into inocuous urea in the liver

ASXL1.job: helps control which genes are switched on or off by adjusting how DNA is packed
ASXL1.basis: Probable Polycomb group (PcG) protein involved in transcriptional regulation ... The PR-DUB complex is an epigenetic regulator of gene expression and acts as a transcriptional coactivator ... The ASXL proteins are essential for chromatin recruitment and transcriptional activation of associated genes

ASXL2.job: helps adjust how DNA is packed to switch genes on or keep them off
ASXL2.basis: required to maintain the transcriptionally repressive state of homeotic genes throughout development ... The PR-DUB complex is an epigenetic regulator of gene expression and acts as a transcriptional coactivator

ASXL3.job: helps control which genes stay on or off as the body develops
ASXL3.basis: PcG proteins act by forming multiprotein complexes, which are required to maintain the transcriptionally repressive state of homeotic genes throughout development ... The PR-DUB complex is an epigenetic regulator of gene expression and acts as a transcriptional coactivator, affecting genes involved in development

ATF6.job: switches on genes that help cells cope with badly folded proteins
ATF6.basis: Endoplasmic reticulum stress promotes processing of this form, releasing the transcription factor form that translocates into the nucleus, where it activates transcription of genes involved in the unfolded protein response (UPR)

ATG7.job: helps cells break down and recycle their own worn-out parts
ATG7.basis: E1-like activating enzyme involved in the 2 ubiquitin-like systems required for cytoplasm to vacuole transport (Cvt) and autophagy ... Required for mitophagy which contributes to regulate mitochondrial quantity and quality by eliminating the mitochondria

ATL1.job: joins tubes of the cell's internal membrane network so it stays connected
ATL1.basis: mediates the GTP-dependent fusion of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membranes, maintaining the continuous ER network ... facilitates the formation of three-way junctions where ER tubules intersect

ATN1.basis: Transcriptional corepressor. Recruits NR2E1 to repress transcription.

ATP13A3.job: pumps polyamines, small molecules cells need to grow, into the cell's interior
ATP13A3.basis: ATP-driven pump involved in endocytosis-dependent polyamine transport ... transfer polyamine precursor putrescine from the endosomal compartment to the cytosol

ATP1A1.job: pumps sodium out of cells and potassium in, using the cell's energy
ATP1A1.basis: Na(+)/K(+)-ATPase pump that hydrolyzes ATP to exchange ions across the plasma membrane, exporting 3 Na(+) and importing 2 K(+) per cycle

ATP1A2.job: pumps sodium out of cells and potassium in, using the cell's energy
ATP1A2.basis: Catalytic subunit of the Na(+)/K(+)-ATPase that hydrolyzes ATP to exchange ions across the plasma membrane, exporting 3 Na(+) and importing 2 K(+) per cycle

ATP1A3.job: pumps sodium out of and potassium into nerve cells so they can fire signals
ATP1A3.basis: Neuron-specific alpha catalytic component of the Na(+)/K(+)-transporting ATPase ... Transports 3 Na(+) ions out of the cell and 2 K(+) ions into the cell ... In the brain, ATP1A3 is critical for neuronal cell signaling

ATP2B2.job: pumps calcium out of cells in the inner ear and brain
ATP2B2.basis: ATP-driven Ca(2+) ion pump involved in the maintenance of basal intracellular Ca(2+) levels in specialized cells of cerebellar circuit and vestibular and cochlear systems ... transport cytosolic Ca(2+) ions across the plasma membrane to the extracellular compartment

ATP5PO.job: is part of the machine that makes energy in the cell's power plants
ATP5PO.basis: Subunit OSCP, of the mitochondrial membrane ATP synthase complex (F(1)F(0) ATP synthase or Complex V) that produces ATP from ADP

ATP6AP1.job: is part of a pump that keeps compartments inside cells acidic
ATP6AP1.basis: Accessory subunit of the V0 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase) ... V-ATPase is responsible for acidifying and maintaining the pH of intracellular compartments

ATP6AP2.job: helps build the pump that keeps the cell's recycling centers acidic
ATP6AP2.basis: involved in the assembly of the lysosomal proton-transporting V-type ATPase (V-ATPase) and the acidification of the endo-lysosomal system ... Through its function in V-type ATPase (v-ATPase) assembly and acidification of the lysosome it regulates protein degradation

ATP6V0A2.job: is part of a pump that keeps compartments inside cells acidic
ATP6V0A2.basis: Subunit of the V0 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase) ... V-ATPase is responsible for acidifying and maintaining the pH of intracellular compartments

ATP6V1B1.job: is part of a pump that moves acid out of kidney cells into urine
ATP6V1B1.basis: Non-catalytic subunit of the V1 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase) ... In renal intercalated cells, mediates secretion of protons (H+) into the urine thereby ensuring correct urinary acidification

ATP7A.job: pumps copper inside cells to enzymes that need it and out when there's too much
ATP7A.basis: ATP-driven copper (Cu(+)) ion pump that plays an important role in intracellular copper ion homeostasis ... transfers Cu(+) ions to cuproenzymes of the secretory pathway ... responsible for the export of excess Cu(+) ions

ATP7B.job: moves extra copper out of liver cells into bile
ATP7B.basis: involved in the export of copper out of the cells ... ensures the efflux of copper from hepatocytes into the bile in response to copper overload

ATRX.job: reshapes how DNA is packed, especially at the protective tips of chromosomes
ATRX.basis: Involved in transcriptional regulation and chromatin remodeling ... Involved in maintaining telomere structural integrity

ATXN2.job: helps control how cells respond to growth signals
ATXN2.basis: Involved in EGFR trafficking, acting as negative regulator of endocytic EGFR internalization at the plasma membrane
ATXN2.alt: helps control when growth-signal receptors are pulled from the cell surface into the cell

AUH.job: helps the body break down leucine, an amino acid from food
AUH.basis: Catalyzes the fifth step in the leucine degradation pathway

AURKC.job: helps sort chromosomes evenly when cells divide, including when making sperm
AURKC.basis: a complex that acts as a key regulator of mitosis ... ensuring correct chromosome alignment and segregation ... Also plays a role in meiosis and more particularly in spermatogenesis

AUTS2.job: helps switch on genes and guides brain cells as the brain develops
AUTS2.basis: the complex mediates transcriptional activation ... plays a role in axon and dendrite elongation and in neuronal migration during embryonic brain development

AXIN2.job: helps keep a key growth-signaling pathway switched off when it isn't needed
AXIN2.basis: Inhibitor of the Wnt signaling pathway. Down-regulates beta-catenin.

B3GALNT2.job: adds sugars to a protein that anchors muscle cells to their surroundings
B3GALNT2.basis: Involved in alpha-dystroglycan (DAG1) glycosylation ... a carbohydrate structure present in alpha-dystroglycan, which is required for binding laminin G-like domain-containing extracellular proteins with high affinity

B3GLCT.job: adds a sugar to certain proteins to help them fold and work properly
B3GLCT.basis: Beta-1,3-glucosyltransferase involved in one of the two pathways responsible for protein O-linked fucosylation ... B3GLCT extends this modification by transferring a glucose molecule from UDP-glucose to the fucose

B4GALNT1.job: helps make gangliosides, sugar-coated fats found mostly in nerve cells
B4GALNT1.basis: Involved in the biosynthesis of gangliosides GM2, GD2, GT2 and GA2

B4GALT1.job: adds galactose sugar to proteins and fats, and helps make milk sugar
B4GALT1.basis: Catalyzes the transfer of galactose (Gal) from UDP-alpha-D-galactose in beta(1->4) linkage to the non-reducing terminal N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) moieties of glycolipids and complex-type N-linked glycans ... With LALBA/alpha-lactalbumin forms the lactose synthase complex responsible for production of large amounts of lactose in the lactating mammary gland

B4GALT7.job: helps attach the sugar chains that coat proteins in skin and connective tissue
B4GALT7.basis: Required for the biosynthesis of the tetrasaccharide linkage region of proteoglycans, especially for small proteoglycans in skin fibroblasts

B9D1.job: forms part of the gate at the base of the cell's sensing antenna
B9D1.basis: Component of the tectonic-like complex, a complex localized at the transition zone of primary cilia and acting as a barrier that prevents diffusion of transmembrane proteins between the cilia and plasma membranes
B9D1.alt: guards the base of the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs, controlling what enters

BAG3.job: helps the cell's protein-folding helpers handle and release the proteins they care for
BAG3.basis: Co-chaperone and adapter protein that connects different classes of molecular chaperones ... promoting the release of ADP from HSP70s, thereby triggering client protein release

BAP1.job: removes chemical tags from DNA's packaging proteins to help switch genes on
BAP1.basis: Deubiquitinating enzyme that plays a key role in chromatin by mediating deubiquitination of histone H2A ... The PR-DUB complex is an epigenetic regulator of gene expression and acts as a transcriptional coactivator

BARD1.job: teams up with BRCA1 to repair damaged DNA
BARD1.basis: The BRCA1-BARD1 heterodimer ... coordinates a diverse range of cellular pathways such as DNA damage repair ... to maintain genomic stability

BBIP1.job: is part of a team that sorts proteins into the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
BBIP1.basis: The BBSome complex is thought to function as a coat complex required for sorting of specific membrane proteins to the primary cilia ... Required for primary cilia assembly and BBSome stability

BBS1.job: helps deliver proteins into the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
BBS1.basis: The BBSome complex is thought to function as a coat complex required for sorting of specific membrane proteins to the primary cilia ... Required for proper BBSome complex assembly and its ciliary localization

BBS10.job: helps assemble the machinery that builds the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
BBS10.basis: Probable molecular chaperone that assists the folding of proteins ... Plays a role in the assembly of BBSome, a complex involved in ciliogenesis

BBS12.job: helps assemble the machinery that builds the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
BBS12.basis: molecular chaperone complex that assists the folding of proteins ... may play a role in the assembly of BBSome, a complex involved in ciliogenesis regulating transports vesicles to the cilia

BBS2.job: is part of a crew that ships certain proteins into the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
BBS2.basis: The BBSome complex is thought to function as a coat complex required for sorting of specific membrane proteins to the primary cilia ... Required for proper BBSome complex assembly and its ciliary localization
BBS2.alt: helps deliver proteins into the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs

BBS4.job: helps deliver proteins into the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
BBS4.basis: The BBSome complex is thought to function as a coat complex required for sorting of specific membrane proteins to the primary cilia ... Required for proper BBSome complex assembly and its ciliary localization

BBS5.job: helps carry certain proteins into the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
BBS5.basis: The BBSome complex is thought to function as a coat complex required for sorting of specific membrane proteins to the primary cilia ... Required for BBSome complex ciliary localization

BBS7.job: helps assemble a protein crew that delivers cargo into the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
BBS7.basis: The BBSome complex is thought to function as a coat complex required for sorting of specific membrane proteins to the primary cilia ... Required for proper BBSome complex assembly and its ciliary localization
BBS7.alt: helps deliver proteins into the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs

BBS9.job: helps deliver proteins to the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
BBS9.basis: The BBSome complex is thought to function as a coat complex required for sorting of specific membrane proteins to the primary cilia ... Required for proper BBSome complex assembly and its ciliary localization

BCAP31.job: helps cells ship newly made proteins out and flag misfolded ones for disposal
BCAP31.basis: Functions as a chaperone protein ... Plays a role in the export of secreted proteins in the ER, the recognition of abnormally folded protein and their targeting to the ER associated-degradation (ERAD)

BCAT2.job: starts breaking down three essential amino acids from food
BCAT2.basis: Catalyzes the first reaction in the catabolism of the essential branched chain amino acids leucine, isoleucine, and valine

BCKDHA.job: helps break down three amino acids from protein-rich food to make energy
BCKDHA.basis: The BCKD complex catalyzes the multi-step oxidative decarboxylation of alpha-ketoacids derived from the branched-chain amino-acids valine, leucine and isoleucine producing CO2 and acyl-CoA which is subsequently utilized to produce energy

BCKDHB.job: helps break down three amino acids from food so they can be used for energy
BCKDHB.basis: The BCKD complex catalyzes the multi-step oxidative decarboxylation of alpha-ketoacids derived from the branched-chain amino-acids valine, leucine and isoleucine producing CO2 and acyl-CoA which is subsequently utilized to produce energy

BCKDK.job: switches off the breakdown of certain amino acids from protein in food
BCKDK.basis: Phosphorylates and inactivates mitochondrial BCKDH complex ... each involved in different steps of BCAA catabolism

BCL10.job: relays alarm signals inside immune cells to switch on the body's defenses
BCL10.basis: Plays a key role in both adaptive and innate immune signaling by bridging CARD domain-containing proteins to immune activation ... stimulate expression of genes encoding pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines

BCL11A.job: switches off fetal hemoglobin so blood makes the adult kind after birth
BCL11A.basis: Transcription factor ... Involved in regulation of the developmental switch from gamma- to beta-globin, probably via direct repression of HBG1; hence indirectly repressing fetal hemoglobin (HbF) level

BCL11B.job: helps a type of immune cell called T cells develop and survive
BCL11B.basis: Key regulator of both differentiation and survival of T-lymphocytes during thymocyte development

BCOR.basis: Transcriptional corepressor. May specifically inhibit gene expression when recruited to promoter regions by sequence-specific DNA-binding proteins such as BCL6 and MLLT3
BCOR.alt: helps switch off certain genes by teaming up with DNA-reading proteins

BCS1L.job: helps assemble the energy-making machinery inside mitochondria, the cell's power plants
BCS1L.basis: Chaperone necessary for the incorporation of Rieske iron-sulfur protein UQCRFS1 into the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex III ... respiratory chain assembly

BEST1.job: opens when calcium arrives to let chloride and other charged particles cross cell membranes
BEST1.basis: Ligand-gated anion channel that allows the movement of anions across cell membranes when activated by calcium (Ca2+) ... Allows the movement of chloride and hydrogencarbonate

BGN.job: is thought to help assemble the collagen fibers that give tissues their strength
BGN.basis: May be involved in collagen fiber assembly
BGN.alt: may help assemble the collagen fibers that give tissues their strength

BICRA.job: is part of a team that unpacks DNA to control which genes are used
BICRA.basis: Component of SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling subcomplex GBAF ... changing chromatin structure by altering DNA-histone contacts within a nucleosome ... May play a role in BRD4-mediated gene transcription

BIN1.job: bends cell membranes, building the tiny tunnels that help muscles contract
BIN1.basis: Is a key player in the control of plasma membrane curvature, membrane shaping and membrane remodeling. Required in muscle cells for the formation of T-tubules, tubular invaginations of the plasma membrane that function in depolarization-contraction coupling

BLM.job: unwinds DNA to help copy and repair it
BLM.basis: ATP-dependent DNA helicase that unwinds double-stranded (ds)DNA ... Participates in DNA replication and repair

BLNK.job: relays signals inside antibody-making immune cells to help them develop and respond
BLNK.basis: Functions as a central linker protein, downstream of the B-cell receptor (BCR), bridging the SYK kinase to a multitude of signaling pathways and regulating biological outcomes of B-cell function and development

BLOC1S5.job: helps build the cell compartments that make skin pigment and help blood clot
BLOC1S5.basis: Component of the BLOC-1 complex, a complex that is required for normal biogenesis of lysosome-related organelles (LRO), such as platelet dense granules and melanosomes

BLOC1S6.job: helps cells build special storage sacs, like pigment and platelet granules
BLOC1S6.basis: Component of the BLOC-1 complex, a complex that is required for normal biogenesis of lysosome-related organelles (LRO), such as platelet dense granules and melanosomes

BLTP1.job: forms a bridge that moves fats between compartments inside cells
BLTP1.basis: Bridge-like lipid transfer protein that functions as molecular bridges between endoplasmic reticulum and the membranes targeted for lipid delivery ... allows the transport of phospholipids

BMP4.job: sends growth signals that shape the developing body, including bones, blood vessels and teeth
BMP4.basis: Growth factor of the TGF-beta superfamily that plays essential roles in many developmental processes, including neurogenesis, vascular development, angiogenesis and osteogenesis ... Required for MSX1-mediated mesenchymal molar tooth bud development

BMPR1A.job: picks up bone-building growth signals that guide how cells develop
BMPR1A.basis: Receptor for BMP2, BMP4, GDF5 and GDF6 ... Positively regulates chondrocyte differentiation through GDF5 interaction. Mediates induction of adipogenesis by GDF6

BMPR2.job: picks up bone morphogenetic protein signals and passes them into the cell
BMPR2.basis: On ligand binding, forms a receptor complex ... Type II receptors phosphorylate and activate type I receptors which autophosphorylate, then bind and activate SMAD transcriptional regulators ... Binds to BMP7, BMP2 and, less efficiently, BMP4

BOLA3.job: helps load iron-sulfur parts into proteins inside the cell's power plants
BOLA3.basis: Acts as a mitochondrial iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster assembly factor that facilitates (Fe-S) cluster insertion into a subset of mitochondrial proteins

BPTF.job: helps arrange how DNA is packed so genes can be read
BPTF.basis: chromatin remodeling complexes, which form ordered nucleosome arrays on chromatin and facilitate access to DNA during DNA-templated processes such as DNA replication, transcription, and repair

BRAF.job: passes growth signals from the cell's surface to its center
BRAF.basis: Protein kinase involved in the transduction of mitogenic signals from the cell membrane to the nucleus

BRAT1.job: helps assemble a cell machine that trims gene messages, and helps respond to DNA damage
BRAT1.basis: required for the assembly of the RNA endonuclease module of the integrator complex ... also involved in DNA damage response

BRD4.job: reads chemical tags on DNA packaging to help switch genes on
BRD4.basis: Chromatin reader protein that recognizes and binds acetylated histones and plays a key role in transmission of epigenetic memory across cell divisions and transcription regulation

BRIP1.job: unwinds DNA to help repair breaks and keep chromosomes stable
BRIP1.basis: DNA-dependent ATPase and 5'-3' DNA helicase required for the maintenance of chromosomal stability ... Involved in the repair of DNA double-strand breaks by homologous recombination

BRPF1.job: holds together teams of proteins that tag DNA's packaging to switch genes on
BRPF1.basis: Scaffold subunit of various histone acetyltransferase (HAT) complexes ... which have a histone H3 acetyltransferase activity ... Positively regulates the transcription of RUNX1 and RUNX2

BRSK2.job: helps young nerve cells grow their long signal-sending fibers
BRSK2.basis: plays a key role in polarization of neurons and axonogenesis ... acts as a key regulator of polarization of cortical neurons

BRWD3.job: helps cells keep their shape by organizing their inner scaffolding
BRWD3.basis: Required for regulation of cell morphology and cytoskeletal organization
BRWD3.alt: helps cells keep their shape and inner scaffolding

BSCL2.job: helps fat cells form the tiny droplets that store fat
BSCL2.basis: Mediates the formation of lipid droplets during the differentiation and maturation of adipocytes

BSND.job: helps salt channels work in the kidneys and inner ear
BSND.basis: Regulatory subunit of anion-selective CLCNKA:BSND and CLCNKB:BSND heteromeric channels involved in basolateral chloride conductance along the nephron to achieve urine concentration ... and in the stria vascularis of the inner ear to establish the endocochlear potential necessary for normal hearing

BTD.job: frees the vitamin biotin from used proteins so the body can reuse it
BTD.basis: Catalytic release of biotin from biocytin, the product of biotin-dependent carboxylases degradation

BTK.job: helps antibody-making immune cells grow up and switch on
BTK.basis: Non-receptor tyrosine kinase indispensable for B lymphocyte development, differentiation and signaling ... Binding of antigen to the B-cell antigen receptor (BCR) triggers signaling that ultimately leads to B-cell activation

BUB1B.job: makes dividing cells wait until every chromosome is properly attached before splitting
BUB1B.basis: component of the mitotic checkpoint complex (MCC), which inhibits APC/C and delays chromosome segregation until all chromosomes are properly attached to the mitotic spindle

C19orf12.job: helps fat cells control how much fat they store
C19orf12.basis: Adipocyte protein localized at lipid droplet-mitochondria contact sites that governs lipid storage through regulation of mitochondrial fatty acid metabolism

C1QA.job: helps the immune system spot germs and destroy them
C1QA.basis: Core component of the complement C1 complex, a multiprotein complex that initiates the classical pathway of the complement system, a cascade of proteins that leads to phagocytosis and breakdown of pathogens ... C1QA, together with C1QB and C1QC, specifically recognizes and binds the Fc regions of IgG or IgM
C1QA.alt: forms the A chain of C1q, which spots antibody-coated germs and starts their destruction

C1QB.job: is one of three building blocks of an immune sensor that spots antibody-coated germs
C1QB.basis: Core component of the complement C1 complex ... that initiates the classical pathway of the complement system, a cascade of proteins that leads to phagocytosis and breakdown of pathogens ... C1QA, together with C1QB and C1QC, specifically recognizes and binds the Fc regions of IgG or IgM
C1QB.alt: starts an immune chain reaction that marks antibody-coated germs for destruction

C1QBP.job: helps the cell's power plants build their own proteins
C1QBP.basis: Multifunctional and multicompartmental protein involved in ... protein synthesis in mitochondria ... Required for protein synthesis in mitochondria

C1QTNF5.job: helps muscle cells burn fat and take up sugar for energy
C1QTNF5.basis: Involved in cellular energy homeostasis ... In myocytes, it induces adiponectin receptors-independent AMPK phosphorylation and activation, thereby increasing the phosphorylation of acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) and stimulating fatty acid oxidation and glucose uptake

C2CD3.job: helps cells build their antenna-like sensing hairs
C2CD3.basis: Promotes assembly of centriolar distal appendage, a structure at the distal end of the mother centriole that acts as an anchor of the cilium ... Required for primary cilium formation

C3.job: helps the immune system tag germs so they can be destroyed
C3.basis: Precursor of non-enzymatic components of the classical, alternative, lectin and GZMK complement pathways ... leads to phagocytosis and breakdown of pathogens

C9orf72.job: helps cells break down and recycle their worn-out parts
C9orf72.basis: Component of the C9orf72-SMCR8 complex where both subunits display GEF activity and that regulates autophagy ... Promotes initiation of autophagy

CA2.job: converts carbon dioxide and water into bicarbonate, helping cells control acidity
CA2.basis: Catalyzes the reversible hydration of carbon dioxide ... Contributes to intracellular pH regulation

CA5A.job: turns carbon dioxide into bicarbonate inside the cell's power plants
CA5A.basis: Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase that catalyzes the reversible conversion of carbon dioxide to bicarbonate/HCO3

CABP4.job: helps light-sensing eye cells and hearing cells pass signals to nerves
CABP4.basis: Involved in normal synaptic function through regulation of Ca(2+) influx and neurotransmitter release in photoreceptor synaptic terminals and in auditory transmission

CACNA1C.job: lets calcium into heart and blood vessel muscle cells so they contract
CACNA1C.basis: Mediates influx of calcium ions into the cytoplasm ... Plays an important role in excitation-contraction coupling in the heart ... Required for normal contraction of smooth muscle cells in blood vessels and in the intestine

CACNA1E.job: lets calcium into nerve cells to help shape how they fire
CACNA1E.basis: Voltage-sensitive calcium channels (VSCC) mediate the entry of calcium ions into excitable cells ... could be involved in the modulation of firing patterns of neurons

CACNA1F.job: lets calcium into cells that send electrical signals
CACNA1F.basis: Voltage-sensitive calcium channels (VSCC) mediate the entry of calcium ions into excitable cells ... The isoform alpha-1F gives rise to L-type calcium currents

CACNA1G.job: lets calcium into nerve and heart cells to help set their rhythm
CACNA1G.basis: mediate the entry of calcium ions into excitable cells ... T-type channels serve pacemaking functions in both central neurons and cardiac nodal cells

CACNA1S.job: helps nerve signals trigger skeletal muscles to contract
CACNA1S.basis: voltage-gated calcium channel that gives rise to L-type calcium currents in skeletal muscle ... play an important role in excitation-contraction coupling in skeletal muscle ... ultimately results in muscle contraction

CACNA2D4.job: helps control how calcium flows into cells through calcium channels
CACNA2D4.basis: The alpha-2/delta subunit of voltage-dependent calcium channels regulates calcium current density and activation/inactivation kinetics of the calcium channel

CAD.job: carries out the first three steps of making building blocks for DNA and RNA
CAD.basis: Multifunctional protein that encodes the first 3 enzymatic activities of the de novo pyrimidine pathway

CALM1.job: senses calcium and switches on many other proteins inside cells
CALM1.basis: Calmodulin acts as part of a calcium signal transduction pathway by mediating the control of a large number of enzymes, ion channels, aquaporins and other proteins through calcium-binding

CALM2.job: senses calcium and uses it to switch many other proteins on or off
CALM2.basis: Calmodulin acts as part of a calcium signal transduction pathway by mediating the control of a large number of enzymes, ion channels, aquaporins and other proteins through calcium-binding

CALM3.job: senses calcium and uses it to switch many other proteins on or off
CALM3.basis: Calmodulin acts as part of a calcium signal transduction pathway by mediating the control of a large number of enzymes, ion channels, aquaporins and other proteins through calcium-binding

CAMK2A.job: helps brain cells strengthen their connections for learning and memory
CAMK2A.basis: involved in various processes, such as synaptic plasticity, neurotransmitter release and long-term potentiation ... regulates NMDAR-dependent potentiation of the AMPAR and therefore excitatory synaptic transmission

CAMK2D.job: helps control the calcium flow that makes heart muscle squeeze and relax
CAMK2D.basis: Calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase involved in the regulation of Ca(2+) homeostatis and excitation-contraction coupling (ECC) in heart

CAMTA1.job: switches on other genes based on calcium signals inside the cell

CANT1.job: breaks down certain energy-carrying molecules and helps build sugar-coated proteins
CANT1.basis: Calcium-dependent nucleotidase with a preference for ribonucleosides diphosphate UDP, GDP and IDP ... Involved in proteoglycan synthesis

CAPN3.job: cuts other proteins in response to calcium signals
CAPN3.basis: Calcium-regulated non-lysosomal thiol-protease. Proteolytically cleaves CTBP1 ... Mediates, with UTP25, the proteasome-independent degradation of p53/TP53
CAPN3.alt: cuts up other proteins when switched on by calcium

CAPN5.job: cuts other proteins when switched on by calcium

CARD11.job: passes on alarm signals that switch on immune cells after they spot germs
CARD11.basis: Adapter protein that plays a key role in adaptive immune response by transducing the activation of NF-kappa-B downstream of T-cell receptor (TCR) and B-cell receptor (BCR) engagement

CARMIL2.job: helps cells extend their inner scaffolding to crawl, and helps activate immune T cells
CARMIL2.basis: plays a role in the regulation of actin polymerization ... enhances actin polymerization ... Involved as well in cell migration ... involved in naive T cells activation

CASK.job: anchors key proteins at the junctions where brain cells connect
CASK.basis: Multidomain scaffolding ... protein kinase ... plays a role in synaptic transmembrane protein anchoring and ion channel trafficking ... Contributes to neural development

CASP8.job: acts as a switch that tells damaged or unneeded cells to self-destruct
CASP8.basis: plays a key role in programmed cell death by acting as a molecular switch for apoptosis, necroptosis and pyroptosis

CASR.job: senses calcium levels in the blood and helps keep them steady
CASR.basis: senses changes in the extracellular concentration of calcium ions and plays a key role in maintaining calcium homeostasis ... Senses fluctuations in the circulating calcium concentration

CAV1.job: helps form tiny pockets in the cell's outer membrane
CAV1.basis: May act as a scaffolding protein within caveolar membranes ... drives caveolae formation

CAV3.job: helps muscle cells, including heart muscle, quickly reseal tears in their outer membrane
CAV3.basis: Plays a role in the sarcolemma repair mechanism of both skeletal muscle and cardiomyocytes that permits rapid resealing of membranes disrupted by mechanical stress

CAVIN1.job: helps build caveolae, tiny pouch-like dents in the cell's outer membrane
CAVIN1.basis: Plays an important role in caveolae formation and organization. Essential for the formation of caveolae in all tissues

CBFB.job: partners with RUNX proteins to help them grip DNA and switch genes on or off
CBFB.basis: Forms the heterodimeric complex core-binding factor (CBF) with RUNX family proteins ... RUNX members modulate the transcription of their target genes ... CBFB is a non-DNA-binding regulatory subunit that allosterically enhances the sequence-specific DNA-binding capacity of RUNX

CBL.job: tags activated growth-signal receptors for disposal to switch their signals off
CBL.basis: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that acts as a negative regulator of many signaling pathways by mediating ubiquitination of cell surface receptors ... Recognizes activated receptor tyrosine kinases ... and mediates their ubiquitination to terminate signaling

CBS.job: helps the body clear homocysteine, a harmful byproduct of protein breakdown
CBS.basis: This catabolic route allows the elimination of L-methionine and the toxic metabolite L-homocysteine

CC2D1A.job: helps brain cells mature their connections and controls a serotonin receptor gene
CC2D1A.basis: represses HTR1A gene transcription in neuronal cells ... Performs essential function in controlling functional maturation of synapses

CC2D2A.job: guards the base of the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs, controlling what enters them
CC2D2A.basis: Component of the tectonic-like complex, a complex localized at the transition zone of primary cilia and acting as a barrier that prevents diffusion of transmembrane proteins between the cilia and plasma membranes ... Required for ciliogenesis
CC2D2A.alt: forms a gate at the base of the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs

CCDC39.job: helps build the machinery that makes the cell's tiny hairs beat
CCDC39.basis: Required for assembly of dynein regulatory complex (DRC) and inner dynein arm (IDA) complexes, which are responsible for ciliary beat regulation, thereby playing a central role in motility in cilia and flagella

CCDC40.job: helps build the machinery that lets cells' tiny hairs beat and move
CCDC40.basis: Required for assembly of dynein regulatory complex (DRC) and inner dynein arm (IDA) complexes, which are responsible for ciliary beat regulation, thereby playing a central role in motility in cilia and flagella

CCM2.job: helps blood vessels form and keeps their walls sealed tight
CCM2.basis: crucial regulator of heart and vessel formation and integrity ... May act through the stabilization of endothelial cell junctions

CCN6.job: helps cells make energy and supports normal bone and cartilage growth
CCN6.basis: Plays a role in mitochondrial electron transport and mitochondrial respiration ... may play a role in normal postnatal skeletal growth and cartilage homeostasis

CCND2.job: helps cells get ready to copy their DNA and divide
CCND2.basis: Regulatory component of the cyclin D2-CDK4 (DC) complex ... regulates the cell-cycle during G(1)/S transition ... responsible for the progression through the G(1) phase

CCNO.job: helps cells build the many tiny hairs that line airways and other passages
CCNO.basis: Specifically required for generation of multiciliated cells ... promote mother centriole amplification and maturation

CD19.job: helps antibody-making immune cells respond to germs
CD19.basis: Functions as a coreceptor for the B-cell antigen receptor complex (BCR) on B-lymphocytes ... Decreases the threshold for activation of downstream signaling pathways and for triggering B-cell responses to antigens ... Required for normal levels of serum immunoglobulins, and for production of high-affinity antibodies in response to antigen challenge

CD247.job: helps immune T cells pass on the alarm when they spot a germ
CD247.basis: Part of the TCR-CD3 complex present on T-lymphocyte cell surface that plays an essential role in adaptive immune response ... TCR-mediated signals are transmitted across the cell membrane by the CD3 chains CD3D, CD3E, CD3G and CD247/CD3Z

CD27.job: helps switch on immune cells and keep them multiplying to fight infection
CD27.basis: Costimulatory immune-checkpoint receptor expressed at the surface of T-cells, NK-cells and B-cells ... mediates antigen-specific T-cell activation and expansion

CD2AP.job: links proteins at the cell's surface to its inner support scaffolding
CD2AP.basis: Seems to act as an adapter protein between membrane proteins and the actin cytoskeleton

CD320.job: helps cells take in vitamin B12 from the blood
CD320.basis: Receptor for transcobalamin saturated with cobalamin (TCbl) ... Plays an important role in cobalamin uptake

CD3D.job: helps immune T cells pass on signals when they spot germs
CD3D.basis: Part of the TCR-CD3 complex present on T-lymphocyte cell surface that plays an essential role in adaptive immune response. When antigen presenting cells (APCs) activate T-cell receptor (TCR), TCR-mediated signals are transmitted across the cell membrane by the CD3 chains

CD3E.job: helps immune T cells pass on the alarm when they spot an invader
CD3E.basis: Part of the TCR-CD3 complex present on T-lymphocyte cell surface that plays an essential role in adaptive immune response ... TCR-mediated signals are transmitted across the cell membrane by the CD3 chains CD3D, CD3E, CD3G and CD247/CD3Z

CD3G.job: helps immune T cells pass on the alarm when they spot a germ
CD3G.basis: Part of the TCR-CD3 complex present on T-lymphocyte cell surface that plays an essential role in adaptive immune response ... TCR-mediated signals are transmitted across the cell membrane by the CD3 chains CD3D, CD3E, CD3G and CD247/CD3Z

CD40.job: picks up signals that push immune cells to make antibodies
CD40.basis: Receptor for TNFSF5/CD40LG ... Transduces TRAF6- and MAP3K8-mediated signals that activate ERK in macrophages and B cells, leading to induction of immunoglobulin secretion

CD40LG.job: helps immune cells signal each other so B cells multiply and make antibodies
CD40LG.basis: Cytokine that acts as a ligand to CD40/TNFRSF5 ... Costimulates T-cell proliferation and cytokine production ... Mediates B-cell proliferation ... Involved in immunoglobulin class switching

CD46.job: shields the body's own cells from attack by the immune system
CD46.basis: Acts as a cofactor for complement factor I ... which protects autologous cells against complement-mediated injury

CD70.job: signals T cells to activate and multiply so they can guard against infection
CD70.basis: it is the ligand of the CD27 receptor which is specifically expressed at the surface of T cells ... The CD70-CD27 signaling pathway mediates antigen-specific T cell activation and expansion

CD79A.job: helps immune B cells pass on the alarm when they spot a germ
CD79A.basis: Required in cooperation with CD79B for initiation of the signal transduction cascade activated by binding of antigen to the B-cell antigen receptor complex (BCR)

CD79B.job: helps immune B cells pass on the alarm when they spot germs
CD79B.basis: Required in cooperation with CD79A for initiation of the signal transduction cascade activated by the B-cell antigen receptor complex (BCR)

CDAN1.job: helps control how DNA is packed up inside the cell
CDAN1.basis: May act as a negative regulator of ASF1 in chromatin assembly
CDAN1.alt: helps control how DNA is packed up inside cells

CDC14A.job: helps cells split cleanly in two when they divide
CDC14A.basis: Required for centrosome separation and productive cytokinesis during cell division

CDC42.job: acts as a switch that helps cells set their shape, direction and movement
CDC42.basis: small GTPase which cycles between an active GTP-bound and an inactive GDP-bound state ... Involved in epithelial cell polarization processes ... Regulates cell migration ... organization of the F-actin cytoskeleton

CDC45.job: helps unzip DNA so cells can copy it before dividing
CDC45.basis: Required for initiation of chromosomal DNA replication ... the molecular machine that unwinds template DNA during replication

CDC73.job: helps cells read genes and copy them into messages
CDC73.basis: Component of the PAF1 complex (PAF1C) which has multiple functions during transcription by RNA polymerase II ... is involved in transcriptional elongation

CDH1.job: glues neighboring cells together in skin and the linings of organs
CDH1.basis: Cadherins are calcium-dependent cell adhesion proteins ... CDH1 is involved in mechanisms regulating cell-cell adhesions, mobility and proliferation of epithelial cells

CDH11.job: helps cells stick to similar neighboring cells
CDH11.basis: Cadherins are calcium-dependent cell adhesion proteins. They preferentially interact with themselves in a homophilic manner in connecting cells

CDH2.job: helps cells stick to matching neighbors, including in the brain and nerves
CDH2.basis: Calcium-dependent cell adhesion protein; preferentially mediates homotypic cell-cell adhesion by dimerization with a CDH2 chain from another cell ... Required for proper neurite branching. Required for pre- and postsynaptic organization

CDH23.job: keeps the inner ear's sound-sensing hairs organized so we can hear
CDH23.basis: CDH23 is required for establishing and/or maintaining the proper organization of the stereocilia bundle of hair cells in the cochlea ... Required for normal hearing

CDH3.job: helps cells of the same kind stick together
CDH3.basis: Cadherins are calcium-dependent cell adhesion proteins. They preferentially interact with themselves in a homophilic manner in connecting cells

CDHR1.job: helps hold together the light-sensing tips of the eye's photoreceptor cells
CDHR1.basis: Potential calcium-dependent cell-adhesion protein. May be required for the structural integrity of the outer segment (OS) of photoreceptor cells

CDK13.job: helps cells read genes and edit their messages into working instructions
CDK13.basis: acting as a key regulator of transcription elongation ... Required for RNA splicing

CDK4.job: helps push cells forward through the steps that lead to dividing
CDK4.basis: regulate the cell-cycle during G(1)/S transition ... responsible for the progression through the G(1) phase

CDK5RAP2.job: helps organize the cell's scaffolding that pulls chromosomes apart when cells divide
CDK5RAP2.basis: Regulates centrosomal maturation by recruitment of the gamma-tubulin ring complex (gTuRC) onto centrosomes ... contributes to microtubules nucleation and extension from the centrosome to the cell periphery ... Involved in regulation of mitotic spindle orientation

CDKL5.job: helps brain cells grow and form connections with each other
CDKL5.basis: Serine/threonine-protein kinase involved in neuronal development and function ... Required for normal dendritic arborization, spine morphogenesis, synaptic transmission

CDKN1B.job: puts the brakes on cell division
CDKN1B.basis: Important regulator of cell cycle progression ... Involved in G1 arrest. Potent inhibitor of cyclin E- and cyclin A-CDK2 complexes

CDKN1C.job: puts the brakes on cell division
CDKN1C.basis: Potent tight-binding inhibitor of several G1 cyclin/CDK complexes ... Negative regulator of cell proliferation

CDKN2A.job: puts the brakes on cell division
CDKN2A.basis: Acts as a negative regulator of the proliferation of normal cells by interacting strongly with CDK4 and CDK6

CDT1.job: gets DNA ready to be copied before a cell divides
CDT1.basis: Required for both DNA replication and mitosis ... DNA replication licensing factor, required for pre-replication complex assembly

CEACAM16.job: helps keep a gel-like layer in the inner ear intact for hearing
CEACAM16.basis: Required for proper hearing, plays a role in maintaining the integrity of the tectorial membrane

CEBPA.job: switches on genes that make immature cells stop dividing and mature into specialized cells
CEBPA.basis: Transcription factor that coordinates proliferation arrest and the differentiation of myeloid progenitors, adipocytes, hepatocytes, and cells of the lung and the placenta ... acting as an activator on distinct target genes

CEP120.job: helps build the cell's centrioles and hair-like antennae, and position brain cells
CEP120.basis: Required for centriole duplication and maturation during mitosis and subsequent ciliogenesis ... for proper positioning of neurons during brain development

CEP152.job: helps cells copy the structure that organizes their division
CEP152.basis: Necessary for centrosome duplication ... Acts as a molecular scaffold facilitating the interaction of PLK4 and CPAP, 2 molecules involved in centriole formation

CEP164.job: helps cells build their antenna-like sensing hairs
CEP164.basis: Plays a role in microtubule organization and/or maintenance for the formation of primary cilia (PC), a microtubule-based structure that protrudes from the surface of epithelial cells

CEP250.job: keeps the cell's two centrosomes, its division organizers, linked together
CEP250.basis: Plays an important role in centrosome cohesion during interphase ... Maintains centrosome cohesion by forming intercentriolar linkages

CEP290.job: helps cells build their antenna-like sensing hairs and control what enters them
CEP290.basis: Involved in early and late steps in cilia formation ... may play a role in ciliary transport processes ... may regulate ciliary membrane composition ... May play a role in controlling entry of the BBSome complex to cilia

CEP41.job: helps add chemical tags that keep the cell's antenna-like hairs working
CEP41.basis: Required during ciliogenesis for tubulin glutamylation in cilium ... participating in the transport of TTLL6, a tubulin polyglutamylase, between the basal body and the cilium

CEP57.job: helps anchor the cell's internal scaffolding to its central organizing hub
CEP57.basis: Centrosomal protein which may be required for microtubule attachment to centrosomes

CEP78.job: helps cells build their antenna-like sensing hairs and control their length
CEP78.basis: regulates centriole and cilia biogenesis ... Involved in cilium biogenesis and controls cilium length

CEP83.job: helps cells start building their antenna-like sensing hairs
CEP83.basis: Component of the distal appendage region of the centriole involved in the initiation of primary cilium assembly

CEP85L.job: helps young nerve cells move to their proper places in the brain
CEP85L.basis: Plays an essential role in neuronal cell migration

CERKL.job: helps protect cells from dying under oxidative stress
CERKL.basis: Overexpression of CERKL protects cells from apoptosis in oxidative stress conditions

CFAP221.job: helps build the cell's microscopic hairs and keep them moving
CFAP221.basis: May play a role in cilium morphogenesis and ciliary function
CFAP221.alt: may help build and run the cell's hair-like antennae

CFAP300.job: helps build the motors that make cells' hair-like cilia and sperm tails beat
CFAP300.basis: Cilium- and flagellum-specific protein that plays a role in axonemal structure organization and motility. May play a role in outer and inner dynein arm assembly

CFAP410.job: helps cells build and maintain their hair-like antennae
CFAP410.basis: Plays a role in cilia formation and/or maintenance

CFAP418.job: is thought to help build the stacked disks in the eye's light-sensing cells
CFAP418.basis: May be involved in photoreceptor outer segment disk morphogenesis
CFAP418.alt: may help build the stacked disks in the eye's light-sensing cells

CFAP43.job: helps build and power the sperm's swimming tail
CFAP43.basis: Flagellar protein involved in sperm flagellum axoneme organization and function

CFAP54.job: helps build and run the cell's hair-like antennae and sperm tails
CFAP54.basis: Required for assembly and function of cilia and flagella

CFH.job: keeps part of the immune system from attacking the body's own cells
CFH.basis: maintaining a well-balanced immune response by modulating complement activation ... Acts as a soluble inhibitor of complement, where its binding to self markers such as glycan structures prevents complement activation and amplification on cell surfaces

CFI.job: keeps part of the immune system from attacking the body's own healthy cells
CFI.basis: plays an essential role in regulating the immune response by controlling all complement pathways ... The presence of these cofactors on healthy cells allows degradation of deposited C3b by CFI in order to prevent undesired complement activation

CFL2.job: helps build and break down actin fibers to keep muscles in shape
CFL2.basis: Controls reversibly actin polymerization and depolymerization ... Required for muscle maintenance

CHAMP1.job: helps line up and divide chromosomes evenly when a cell splits
CHAMP1.basis: Required for proper alignment of chromosomes at metaphase and their accurate segregation during mitosis

CHAT.job: makes acetylcholine, a chemical messenger nerves use to signal muscles and other cells
CHAT.basis: Catalyzes the reversible synthesis of acetylcholine (ACh) from acetyl CoA and choline at cholinergic synapses

CHCHD10.job: helps keep the folded inner walls of the cell's power plants in shape
CHCHD10.basis: May be involved in the maintenance of mitochondrial organization and mitochondrial cristae structure

CHD2.job: reshapes how DNA is packed to switch on certain genes, including muscle-building ones
CHD2.basis: ATP-dependent chromatin-remodeling factor that specifically binds to the promoter of target genes, leading to chromatin remodeling ... Involved in myogenesis ... promoting their expression

CHD3.job: reshapes how DNA is packed to help turn genes off
CHD3.basis: ATP-dependent chromatin-remodeling factor that binds and distorts nucleosomal DNA ... Involved in transcriptional repression as part of the NuRD complex

CHD4.job: reshapes how DNA is packed to help switch genes off
CHD4.basis: ATP-dependent chromatin-remodeling factor that binds and distorts nucleosomal DNA ... Acts as a component of the histone deacetylase NuRD complex which participates in the remodeling of chromatin ... to promote transcriptional repression

CHD7.job: reshapes how DNA is packed to help control which genes are used
CHD7.basis: ATP-dependent chromatin-remodeling factor, slides nucleosomes along DNA ... Probable transcription regulator

CHEK2.job: pauses cell division when DNA breaks so the damage can be repaired
CHEK2.basis: required for checkpoint-mediated cell cycle arrest, activation of DNA repair and apoptosis in response to the presence of DNA double-strand breaks

CHM.job: helps attach fatty anchors to Rab proteins, which guide cargo inside cells
CHM.basis: Substrate-binding subunit of the Rab geranylgeranyltransferase (GGTase) complex. Binds unprenylated Rab proteins and presents the substrate peptide to the catalytic component ... The component A is thought to be regenerated by transferring its prenylated Rab back to the donor membrane
