CHMP2B.job: helps cells pinch off small bubbles of membrane to send used proteins for recycling
CHMP2B.basis: Probable core component of the endosomal sorting required for transport complex III (ESCRT-III) which is involved in multivesicular bodies (MVBs) formation and sorting of endosomal cargo proteins into MVBs ... mostly are delivered to lysosomes enabling degradation of membrane proteins ... ESCRT-III proteins are believed to mediate the necessary vesicle extrusion and/or membrane fission activities

CHN1.job: helps growing nerve fibers find their way to build movement circuits
CHN1.basis: Involved in the assembly of neuronal locomotor circuits as a direct effector of EPHA4 in axon guidance

CHRNA1.job: is part of the muscle's switch that opens when nerves send a chemical signal
CHRNA1.basis: Upon acetylcholine binding, the AChR responds by an extensive change in conformation that affects all subunits and leads to opening of an ion-conducting channel across the plasma membrane

CHRNA4.job: is part of a brain receptor that helps nerve cells pass signals to each other
CHRNA4.basis: Component of neuronal acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) ... nAChRs are excitatory neurotrasnmitter receptors ... known to mediate synaptic transmission in the nervous system ... Is the most abundant nAChR subtype expressed in the central nervous system

CHRNB1.job: is part of the gate on muscle cells that opens when nerves release acetylcholine
CHRNB1.basis: After binding acetylcholine, the AChR responds by an extensive change in conformation that affects all subunits and leads to opening of an ion-conducting channel across the plasma membrane
CHRNB1.alt: is part of a channel that lets nerves signal muscles

CHRNB2.job: is part of a brain receptor that lets nerve cells pass on signals
CHRNB2.basis: Component of neuronal acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) ... nAChRs are excitatory neurotrasnmitter receptors formed by a collection of nAChR subunits known to mediate synaptic transmission in the nervous system

CHRNG.job: is the gamma piece of a gate that opens when nerves release acetylcholine
CHRNG.basis: After binding acetylcholine, the AChR responds by an extensive change in conformation that affects all subunits and leads to opening of an ion-conducting channel across the plasma membrane
CHRNG.alt: opens a channel in muscle cells when it receives a nerve's chemical signal

CHST14.job: adds sulfur-containing tags to long sugar chains that coat cells and tissues
CHST14.basis: Catalyzes the transfer of sulfate to position 4 of the N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) residue of dermatan sulfate ... Plays a pivotal role in the formation of 4-0-sulfated IdoA blocks in dermatan sulfate

CHST3.job: adds sulfur tags to the sugar chains that make up cartilage
CHST3.basis: Sulfotransferase that ... catalyze the transfer of sulfate to position 6 of the N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) residue of chondroitin ... Chondroitin sulfate constitutes the predominant proteoglycan present in cartilage

CHST6.job: adds sulfur tags to sugar chains that keep the cornea clear
CHST6.basis: catalyze the transfer of sulfate to position 6 of non-reducing N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) residues of keratan ... Involved in biosynthesis of keratan sulfate in cornea, with an impact on proteoglycan fibril organization and corneal transparency

CHSY1.job: helps build chondroitin, a long sugar chain found in cartilage and tissues
CHSY1.basis: Catalytic component of CHSY1-CHPF2 and CHSY1-CHPF chondroitin sulfate synthase complexes ... to the non-reducing end of the elongating chondroitin polymer

CIB2.job: helps inner ear hair cells turn sound vibrations into nerve signals
CIB2.basis: Acts as an auxiliary subunit of the sensory mechanoelectrical transduction (MET) channel in hair cells ... Essential for mechanoelectrical transduction (MET) currents in auditory hair cells and thereby required for hearing

CIC.job: switches off certain genes to help the brain develop
CIC.basis: Transcriptional repressor which plays a role in development of the central nervous system (CNS) ... involved in brain development

CIITA.job: switches on genes for the molecules immune cells use to show germ fragments
CIITA.basis: Essential for transcriptional activity of the HLA class II promoter ... Also mediates enhanced MHC class I transcription

CILK1.job: helps control the length of the cell's hair-like antennae
CILK1.basis: Required for ciliogenesis ... Involved in the control of ciliary length

CISD2.job: helps control how cells break down and recycle their own parts
CISD2.basis: Regulator of autophagy that contributes to antagonize BECN1-mediated cellular autophagy at the endoplasmic reticulum ... Involved in life span control, probably via its function as regulator of autophagy

CLCN4.job: swaps chloride for hydrogen ions across cell membranes
CLCN4.basis: H(+)/Cl(-)exchanger which mediates the exchange of chloride ions against protons

CLCN5.job: swaps chloride for acid inside cell compartments, helping the kidneys work
CLCN5.basis: Proton-coupled chloride transporter. Functions as antiport system and exchanges chloride ions against protons ... Important for normal acidification of the endosome lumen. May play an important role in renal tubular function

CLCN7.job: swaps chloride for acid to keep the cell's recycling centers acidic
CLCN7.basis: mediating the exchange of chloride ions against protons ... contributes to the acidification of the lysosome lumen and may be involved in maintaining lysosomal pH

CLDN14.job: seals the tiny gaps between neighboring cells
CLDN14.basis: Plays a major role in tight junction-specific obliteration of the intercellular space, through calcium-independent cell-adhesion activity

CLDN16.job: helps the kidneys reclaim magnesium and calcium from urine
CLDN16.basis: Forms paracellular channels ... Involved in the maintenance of ion gradients along the nephron ... contributing to the lumen-positive transepithelial potential that drives paracellular magnesium and calcium reabsorption

CLN3.job: helps move materials to the cell's recycling centers and keep them working
CLN3.basis: Mediates microtubule-dependent, anterograde transport connecting the Golgi network, endosomes, autophagosomes, lysosomes and plasma membrane ... regulation of lysosomal pH, lysosome protein degradation

CLN5.job: makes a special fat that helps the cell's recycling centers handle cholesterol
CLN5.basis: Catalyzes the synthesis of bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate (BMP) ... BMP also known as lysobisphosphatidic acid plays a key role in the formation of intraluminal vesicles and in maintaining intracellular cholesterol homeostasis

CLN8.job: is thought to help young nerve cells grow and survive
CLN8.basis: Could play a role in cell proliferation during neuronal differentiation and in protection against cell death
CLN8.alt: may help young nerve cells grow and protect cells from dying

CLPP.job: breaks down proteins as part of general cleanup inside mitochondria, the cell's power plants
CLPP.basis: Protease component of the ClpXP complex that cleaves peptides and various proteins in an ATP-dependent process ... may be responsible for a fairly general and central housekeeping function ... Cleaves PINK1 in the mitochondrion

CLRN1.job: is thought to help ear and eye sensory cells pass signals to nerve cells
CLRN1.basis: May have a role in the excitatory ribbon synapse junctions between hair cells and cochlear ganglion cells and presumably also in analogous synapses within the retina
CLRN1.alt: may help ear and eye sensory cells pass signals to nerve cells

CLXN.job: helps attach the motors that make cells' hair-like cilia and sperm tails beat
CLXN.basis: Component of the outer dynein arm-docking complex (ODA-DC) that mediates outer dynein arms (ODA) binding onto the doublet microtubule ... Regulates ciliary and flagellar motility

CNGA1.job: forms a channel in the eye's rod cells that turns dim light into nerve signals
CNGA1.basis: Pore-forming subunit of the rod cyclic nucleotide-gated channel. Mediates rod photoresponses at dim light converting transient changes in intracellular cGMP levels into electrical signals

CNGA3.job: forms a channel that helps the eye's color-sensing cells respond to bright light
CNGA3.basis: Pore-forming subunit of the cone cyclic nucleotide-gated channel. Mediates cone photoresponses at bright light converting transient changes in intracellular cGMP levels into electrical signals

CNGB1.job: forms a channel that helps the eye's rod cells sense dim light and the nose sense smells
CNGB1.basis: Pore-forming subunit of the rod cyclic nucleotide-gated channel. Mediates rod photoresponses at dim light ... Pore-forming subunit of the olfactory cyclic nucleotide-gated channel. Operates in the cilia of olfactory sensory neurons where chemical stimulation of the odorant is converted to an electrical signal

CNGB3.job: helps the eye's color-sensing cells turn bright light into nerve signals
CNGB3.basis: Pore-forming subunit of the cone cyclic nucleotide-gated channel. Mediates cone photoresponses at bright light converting transient changes in intracellular cGMP levels into electrical signals

CNKSR2.job: is thought to help relay growth signals inside cells
CNKSR2.basis: May function as an adapter protein or regulator of Ras signaling pathways
CNKSR2.alt: may help relay growth signals inside cells by linking signaling proteins together

CNNM2.job: moves magnesium and similar metals across cell membranes
CNNM2.basis: Divalent metal cation transporter. Mediates transport of divalent metal cations in an order of Mg(2+) > Co(2+) > Mn(2+)

CNNM4.job: is thought to move metals in and out of cells
CNNM4.basis: Probable metal transporter. ... May play a role in biomineralization and retinal function
CNNM4.alt: probably moves metal ions in and out of cells, with possible roles in vision and mineralization

CNOT1.job: holds together a group of proteins that clears away used gene messages
CNOT1.basis: Scaffolding component of the CCR4-NOT complex which is one of the major cellular mRNA deadenylases ... bulk mRNA degradation

CNOT3.job: is part of a team that breaks down gene messages to tune protein production
CNOT3.basis: Component of the CCR4-NOT complex which is one of the major cellular mRNA deadenylases ... including bulk mRNA degradation

CNTN2.job: helps organize the insulated nerve fibers that carry fast signals
CNTN2.basis: contributes to the organization of axonal domains at nodes of Ranvier by maintaining voltage-gated potassium channels at the juxtaparanodal region

CNTNAP2.job: helps organize insulated nerve fibers so signals travel quickly
CNTNAP2.basis: Required, with CNTNAP1, for radial and longitudinal organization of myelinated axons ... critical for saltatory conduction of nerve impulses in myelinated nerve fibers

COA6.job: helps build the machinery cells use to make energy from oxygen
COA6.basis: Involved in the maturation of the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex IV subunit MT-CO2/COX2 ... may regulate early steps of complex IV assembly ... catalyzes the transfer of electrons from intermembrane space cytochrome c to molecular oxygen ... contributes to the proton gradient involved in mitochondrial ATP synthesis

COA7.job: helps build the energy-making machinery inside mitochondria, the cell's power plants
COA7.basis: Required for assembly of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I and complex IV

COA8.job: helps build and protect a key part of the cell's energy-making machinery
COA8.basis: Required for cytochrome c complex (COX) IV assembly and function Protects COX assembly from oxidation-induced degradation, COX being the terminal component of the mitochondrial respiratory chain

COCH.job: helps shape and move cells in the eye's fluid drainage tissue
COCH.basis: Plays a role in the control of cell shape and motility in the trabecular meshwork
COCH.alt: helps shape and move cells in the eye's fluid-draining tissue

COG4.job: helps the cell's packaging center sort and ship proteins
COG4.basis: Required for normal Golgi function ... Golgi-to-ER retrograde transport

COG5.job: helps the Golgi, the cell's packaging center, work properly
COG5.alt: is part of a team that keeps the Golgi, the cell's packaging center, working

COG6.job: helps the Golgi, the cell's packaging center, work properly
COG6.alt: helps the cell's packaging center, the Golgi, work normally

COG7.job: helps the Golgi, the cell's packaging center, work properly
COG7.alt: helps the Golgi, the cell's packing and shipping center, work properly

COG8.job: helps the Golgi, the cell's packaging center, work properly
COG8.alt: helps the Golgi, the cell's packaging center, work normally

COL10A1.job: forms a collagen in growing cartilage where bone starts to form
COL10A1.basis: Type X collagen is a product of hypertrophic chondrocytes and has been localized to presumptive mineralization zones of hyaline cartilage

COL11A2.job: helps control the thickness of collagen fibers that strengthen cartilage
COL11A2.basis: May play an important role in fibrillogenesis by controlling lateral growth of collagen II fibrils

COL18A1.job: helps shape the retina and close the early spinal cord and brain
COL18A1.basis: Probably plays a major role in determining the retinal structure as well as in the closure of the neural tube

COL1A1.job: helps build collagen, the strong fibers that give bones and skin their strength
COL1A1.basis: Type I collagen is a member of group I collagen (fibrillar forming collagen)
COL1A1.alt: forms the alpha-1 strand of type I collagen, a protein that builds fibers

COL1A2.job: is one strand of type I collagen, the fibers that give bones and skin their strength
COL1A2.basis: Type I collagen is a member of group I collagen (fibrillar forming collagen)
COL1A2.alt: is part of collagen, the tough fibers that give tissues their strength

COL2A1.job: forms the main framework of cartilage and helps the skeleton grow
COL2A1.basis: Type II collagen is specific for cartilaginous tissues. It is essential for the normal embryonic development of the skeleton, for linear growth and for the ability of cartilage to resist compressive forces

COL3A1.job: is part of the collagen that gives soft tissues like skin and blood vessels strength
COL3A1.basis: Collagen type III occurs in most soft connective tissues along with type I collagen

COL4A1.job: forms the mesh of the thin support sheets under tissues, including kidney filters
COL4A1.basis: Type IV collagen is the major structural component of glomerular basement membranes (GBM), forming a 'chicken-wire' meshwork together with laminins, proteoglycans and entactin/nidogen
COL4A1.alt: forms the mesh-like sheets that support and filter tissues, including in the kidneys

COL4A3.job: forms the alpha-3 strand of the collagen mesh lining the kidney's blood filters
COL4A3.basis: Type IV collagen is the major structural component of glomerular basement membranes (GBM), forming a 'chicken-wire' meshwork
COL4A3.alt: builds the mesh-like filter sheet inside the kidney's tiny blood-filtering units

COL4A4.job: is one strand of the chicken-wire collagen mesh in the kidney's blood filters
COL4A4.basis: Type IV collagen is the major structural component of glomerular basement membranes (GBM), forming a 'chicken-wire' meshwork
COL4A4.alt: builds the mesh-like sheet that filters blood in the kidneys

COL4A5.job: is one strand of the collagen mesh that lines the kidney's blood filters
COL4A5.basis: Type IV collagen is the major structural component of glomerular basement membranes (GBM), forming a 'chicken-wire' meshwork
COL4A5.alt: builds the mesh-like support layer in the kidney's blood filters

COL5A1.job: helps form the collagen fibers that give connective tissue its strength
COL5A1.basis: Type V collagen is a member of group I collagen (fibrillar forming collagen). It is a minor connective tissue component of nearly ubiquitous distribution

COL5A2.job: helps build collagen fibers that give skin and other tissues their strength
COL5A2.basis: Type V collagen is a member of group I collagen (fibrillar forming collagen). It is a minor connective tissue component of nearly ubiquitous distribution ... Type V collagen is a key determinant in the assembly of tissue-specific matrices

COL6A1.job: helps build a fiber that anchors cells to the tissue around them
COL6A1.basis: Collagen VI acts as a cell-binding protein
COL6A1.alt: is one strand of collagen VI, a fiber that helps cells grip the tissue around them

COL6A2.job: helps build a fiber that anchors cells to the tissue around them
COL6A2.basis: Collagen VI acts as a cell-binding protein
COL6A2.alt: is the alpha-2 strand, one of three woven into collagen VI, a fiber that binds cells

COL6A3.job: helps build a fiber that anchors cells to the tissue around them
COL6A3.basis: Collagen VI acts as a cell-binding protein
COL6A3.alt: is part of collagen VI, a fiber that helps cells attach to the supportive mesh around them

COL9A1.job: is one of the building blocks of cartilage and of the clear gel that fills the eye
COL9A1.basis: Structural component of hyaline cartilage and vitreous of the eye
COL9A1.alt: helps build cartilage and the clear gel that fills the eye

COL9A3.job: forms the third strand of a collagen that strengthens cartilage and the eye's inner gel
COL9A3.basis: Structural component of hyaline cartilage and vitreous of the eye
COL9A3.alt: helps build the tough cartilage in joints and the clear gel inside the eye

COMP.job: helps hold cartilage together by linking its structural proteins
COMP.basis: Plays a role in the structural integrity of cartilage via its interaction with other extracellular matrix proteins such as the collagens and fibronectin

COQ2.job: helps make coenzyme Q10, which cells need to turn food into energy
COQ2.basis: Plays a central role in the biosynthesis of CoQ10 ... CoQ10 is a vital molecule that transports electrons from mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes

COQ4.job: helps make coenzyme Q10, which cells need to produce energy

COQ6.job: helps make coenzyme Q10, which cells need to produce energy
COQ6.basis: FAD-dependent monooxygenase required for two non-consecutive steps during ubiquinone biosynthesis

COQ7.job: helps make coenzyme Q10, which cells need to produce energy
COQ7.basis: participates in the biosynthesis of ubiquinone

COQ8B.job: helps cells make coenzyme Q, a molecule they need to make energy
COQ8B.basis: involved in the biosynthesis of coenzyme Q, also named ubiquinone, an essential lipid-soluble electron transporter for aerobic cellular respiration

COQ9.job: helps cells make coenzyme Q, which they need to turn oxygen into energy
COQ9.basis: Participates in the biosynthesis of coenzyme Q, also named ubiquinone, an essential lipid-soluble electron transporter for aerobic cellular respiration

CORO1A.job: helps fast-moving cells like immune cells reshape their outer edges to crawl
CORO1A.basis: May be a crucial component of the cytoskeleton of highly motile cells ... forming protrusions of the plasma membrane involved in cell locomotion

COX10.job: turns heme, an iron-holding molecule, into a modified form called heme O
COX10.basis: Converts protoheme IX and farnesyl diphosphate to heme O

COX15.job: helps make a heme part that cells' power plants need to burn oxygen for energy
COX15.basis: Catalyzes the second reaction in the biosynthesis of heme A, a prosthetic group of mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase (CcO)

COX20.job: helps build the machine mitochondria use to make energy from oxygen
COX20.basis: Essential for the assembly of the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex IV (CIV), also known as cytochrome c oxidase

COX6A1.job: is part of the enzyme that uses oxygen to make energy in the cell's power plants
COX6A1.basis: Component of the cytochrome c oxidase, the last enzyme in the mitochondrial electron transport chain which drives oxidative phosphorylation ... Cytochrome c oxidase is the component of the respiratory chain that catalyzes the reduction of oxygen to water

COX6B1.job: is part of the cell's power plant machinery that uses oxygen to make energy
COX6B1.basis: Component of the cytochrome c oxidase, the last enzyme in the mitochondrial electron transport chain which drives oxidative phosphorylation ... catalyzes the reduction of oxygen to water ... drives transmembrane transport and the ATP synthase

COXFA4.job: is part of the cell's power plant machinery that uses oxygen to make energy
COXFA4.basis: Component of the cytochrome c oxidase, the last enzyme in the mitochondrial electron transport chain which drives oxidative phosphorylation ... Cytochrome c oxidase is the component of the respiratory chain that catalyzes the reduction of oxygen to water ... COXFA4 is required for complex IV maintenance

CP.job: carries copper and readies iron so the blood can move it around the body
CP.basis: copper-binding (6-7 atoms per molecule) glycoprotein ... It has ferroxidase activity oxidizing Fe(2+) to Fe(3+) ... It is involved in iron transport across the cell membrane ... Oxidizes highly toxic ferrous ions to the ferric state for further incorporation onto apo-transferrins

CPLANE1.job: helps cells build their hair-like antennae and point in the right direction
CPLANE1.basis: Involved in ciliogenesis ... Involved in the establishment of cell polarity required for directional cell migration

CPOX.job: helps make heme, the iron-holding part of blood that carries oxygen
CPOX.basis: participates to the sixth step in the heme biosynthetic pathway

CPS1.job: helps the liver clear excess ammonia by starting the urea cycle
CPS1.basis: Involved in the urea cycle of ureotelic animals where the enzyme plays an important role in removing excess ammonia from the cell

CPT1A.job: helps carry fats into the cell's power plants to be burned for energy
CPT1A.basis: an essential step for the mitochondrial uptake of long-chain fatty acids and their subsequent beta-oxidation in the mitochondrion

CRADD.job: helps trigger the planned self-destruction of damaged or unneeded cells
CRADD.basis: Adapter protein that associates with PIDD1 and the caspase CASP2 to form the PIDDosome, a complex that activates CASP2 and triggers apoptosis

CRB1.job: helps shape the eye's light-sensing cells as they form
CRB1.basis: Plays a role in photoreceptor morphogenesis in the retina ... May maintain cell polarization and adhesion

CRB2.job: helps cells know top from bottom as the early embryo and retina form
CRB2.basis: Apical polarity protein that plays a central role during the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) at gastrulation ... Plays a role in the maintenance of retinal neuroepithelium organization, structural integrity, adhesion, photoreceptor polarity

CREBBP.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging proteins that help switch genes on
CREBBP.basis: Acetylates histones, giving a specific tag for transcriptional activation

CRPPA.job: makes a sugar building block that helps muscle cells anchor to their surroundings
CRPPA.basis: Catalyzes the formation of CDP-ribitol nucleotide sugar from D-ribitol 5-phosphate ... a carbohydrate structure present in alpha-dystroglycan (DAG1), which is required for binding laminin G-like domain-containing extracellular proteins with high affinity

CRX.job: switches on the genes that the eye's light-sensing cells need
CRX.basis: Transcription factor that binds and transactivates the sequence 5'-TAATC[CA]-3' which is found upstream of several photoreceptor-specific genes ... Essential for the maintenance of mammalian photoreceptors

CSDE1.job: helps control how long certain gene messages last before being broken down
CSDE1.basis: RNA-binding protein involved in translationally coupled mRNA turnover ... decay interplay of the FOS mRNA

CSF1R.job: picks up signals that keep germ-eating immune cells called macrophages alive and growing
CSF1R.basis: acts as a cell-surface receptor for CSF1 and IL34 and plays an essential role in the regulation of survival, proliferation and differentiation of hematopoietic precursor cells, especially mononuclear phagocytes, such as macrophages and monocytes

CSF2RA.job: picks up a growth signal that helps blood and immune cells multiply and mature
CSF2RA.basis: Low affinity receptor for granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor. Transduces a signal that results in the proliferation, differentiation, and functional activation of hematopoietic cells

CSF2RB.job: picks up signals that tell the body to make immune and blood cells
CSF2RB.basis: Cell surface receptor that plays a role in immune response and controls the production and differentiation of hematopoietic progenitor cells into lineage-restricted cells

CSNK2A1.job: adds chemical tags to many other proteins to steer cell growth, division and survival
CSNK2A1.basis: phosphorylates a large number of substrates ... Regulates numerous cellular processes, such as cell cycle progression, apoptosis and transcription

CSNK2B.job: helps steer an enzyme that adds chemical tags to many other proteins
CSNK2B.basis: Regulatory subunit of casein kinase II/CK2 ... regulates the basal catalytic activity of the alpha subunit a constitutively active serine/threonine-protein kinase that phosphorylates a large number of substrates

CSPP1.job: is thought to help organize the cell's inner scaffolding as cells divide
CSPP1.basis: May play a role in cell-cycle-dependent microtubule organization
CSPP1.alt: may help organize the cell's internal scaffolding as cells grow and divide

CSRP3.job: helps organize the inner framework of heart muscle cells and build muscle
CSRP3.basis: Positive regulator of myogenesis ... Plays a crucial and specific role in the organization of cytosolic structures in cardiomyocytes ... Proposed to contribute to the maintenance of muscle cell integrity through an actin-based mechanism

CSTB.job: blocks protein-cutting enzymes inside cells to keep them in check
CSTB.basis: This is an intracellular thiol proteinase inhibitor. Tightly binding reversible inhibitor of cathepsins L, H and B

CTC1.job: helps copy and maintain the protective caps on the ends of chromosomes
CTC1.basis: involved in several aspects of telomere replication ... Involved in telomere maintenance

CTCF.job: folds DNA into loops that keep genes apart from the wrong switches
CTCF.basis: regulates the 3D structure of chromatin ... Binds together strands of DNA, thus forming chromatin loops ... Defines the boundaries between active and heterochromatic DNA via binding to chromatin insulators, thereby preventing interaction between promoter and nearby enhancers and silencers

CTH.job: makes the amino acid cysteine, a building block for the body's antioxidant glutathione
CTH.basis: Catalyzes the last step in the trans-sulfuration pathway from L-methionine to L-cysteine ... Part of the L-cysteine derived from the trans-sulfuration pathway is utilized for biosynthesis of the ubiquitous antioxidant glutathione

CTLA4.job: puts the brakes on immune T cells so they don't overreact
CTLA4.basis: Inhibitory receptor acting as a major negative regulator of T-cell responses

CTNNA1.job: helps link cell-to-cell glue to the cell's inner scaffolding
CTNNA1.basis: Associates with the cytoplasmic domain of a variety of cadherins. The association of catenins to cadherins produces a complex which is linked to the actin filament network, and which seems to be of primary importance for cadherins cell-adhesion properties

CTNNB1.job: carries outside signals into the nucleus to switch genes on, and helps cells stick together
CTNNB1.basis: Key downstream component of the canonical Wnt signaling pathway ... accumulates in the nucleus, where it acts as a coactivator for transcription factors of the TCF/LEF family, leading to activate Wnt responsive genes ... Involved in the regulation of cell adhesion, as component of an E-cadherin:catenin adhesion complex

CTNND1.job: helps cells stick together by keeping their adhesion molecules in place
CTNND1.basis: Key regulator of cell-cell adhesion that associates with and regulates the cell adhesion properties of both C-, E- and N-cadherins, being critical for their surface stability

CTNS.job: carries cystine, a building block of protein, out of the cell's recycling centers
CTNS.basis: mediates export of cystine, the oxidized dimer of cysteine, from lysosomes

CTPS1.job: makes a building block for DNA and RNA, helping immune cells multiply
CTPS1.basis: Cytidine triphosphate synthase involved in the de novo synthesis of CTP, a precursor of DNA, RNA and phospholipids ... plays a crucial role in the proliferation of activated lymphocytes and immunity

CTSA.job: protects two sugar-trimming enzymes in the cell's recycling centers so they keep working
CTSA.basis: Protective protein appears to be essential for both the activity of beta-galactosidase and neuraminidase, it associates with these enzymes and exerts a protective function necessary for their stability and activity

CTSD.job: breaks down unwanted proteins inside cells
CTSD.basis: Acid protease active in intracellular protein breakdown

CTSF.job: helps cells break down and recycle old proteins
CTSF.basis: Thiol protease which is believed to participate in intracellular degradation and turnover of proteins

CTSK.job: breaks down old bone so it can be rebuilt
CTSK.basis: Thiol protease involved in osteoclastic bone resorption

CUL3.job: tags worn-out or unneeded proteins so the cell can break them down
CUL3.basis: Core component of multiple cullin-RING-based BCR (BTB-CUL3-RBX1) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes which mediate the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins

CUL4B.job: tags unwanted proteins so the cell can break them down
CUL4B.basis: Core component of multiple cullin-RING-based E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes which mediate the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins

CWC27.job: helps cut and paste the gene's working copy so it can build proteins
CWC27.basis: As part of the spliceosome, plays a role in pre-mRNA splicing

CWF19L1.job: helps cells cut and paste gene messages to make different protein versions
CWF19L1.basis: Acts as a splicing regulator which modulates global alternative splicing

CXCR4.job: picks up chemical signals that guide where cells move, including blood-forming cells
CXCR4.basis: Receptor for the C-X-C chemokine CXCL12/SDF-1 ... Plays a role in regulation of cell migration, e.g. during wound healing ... Involved in hematopoiesis

CYB5A.job: passes electrons to enzymes that use oxygen to process chemicals in cells
CYB5A.basis: membrane-bound hemoprotein functioning as an electron carrier for several membrane-bound oxygenases

CYB5R3.job: recharges a partner protein, cytochrome b5, by handing it electrons
CYB5R3.basis: Catalyzes the reduction of two molecules of cytochrome b5 using NADH as the electron donor

CYFIP2.job: helps immune cells stick to other cells and helps damaged cells self-destruct
CYFIP2.basis: Involved in T-cell adhesion and p53/TP53-dependent induction of apoptosis

CYLD.job: removes chemical tags from other proteins to calm signals that drive inflammation and cell survival
CYLD.basis: Deubiquitinase that specifically cleaves 'Lys-63'- and linear 'Met-1'-linked polyubiquitin chains and is involved in NF-kappa-B inhibition ... Plays a role in the regulation of cell survival, inflammation and innate immune response, via its effects on NF-kappa-B

CYP11B2.job: makes aldosterone, a hormone that balances salt and water to control blood pressure
CYP11B2.basis: catalyzes the biosynthesis of aldosterone, the main mineralocorticoid in the human body responsible for salt and water homeostasis, thus involved in blood pressure regulation

CYP1B1.job: helps process hormones, fats and vitamins, and helps the eye develop
CYP1B1.basis: involved in the metabolism of various endogenous substrates, including fatty acids, steroid hormones and vitamins ... Plays an important role in retinal vascular development

CYP27A1.job: helps turn extra cholesterol into bile acids
CYP27A1.basis: Regulates cholesterol homeostasis by catalyzing the conversion of excess cholesterol to bile acids

CYP27B1.job: turns vitamin D into its active form in the kidney
CYP27B1.basis: Catalyzes the rate-limiting step in the activation of vitamin D in the kidney ... to form the hormonally active form of vitamin D3

CYP2U1.job: helps process a fat called arachidonic acid that cells use as a signal
CYP2U1.basis: involved in the metabolism of arachidonic acid and its conjugates ... May modulate the arachidonic acid signaling pathway and play a role in other fatty acid signaling processes

CYP4V2.job: helps process fats in the eye, including omega-3 fats
CYP4V2.basis: involved in fatty acid metabolism in the eye ... Catalyzes the omega-hydroxylation of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) docosahexaenoate (DHA) and its precursor eicosapentaenoate (EPA)

CYP7B1.job: helps break down cholesterol-based molecules and some hormones
CYP7B1.basis: involved in the metabolism of endogenous oxysterols and steroid hormones, including neurosteroids ... Hydroxylates oxysterols, including 25-hydroxycholesterol ... which may be transported to the liver and converted to bile acids
CYP7B1.alt: helps break down cholesterol-derived molecules and steroid hormones, including ones made in the brain

D2HGDH.job: clears away a natural cell byproduct by turning it into a useful molecule
D2HGDH.basis: Catalyzes the oxidation of D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D-2-HG) to alpha-ketoglutarate

DAG1.job: helps build the mesh around cells and keeps muscle cell membranes sturdy
DAG1.basis: laminin deposition and extracellular matrix assembly ... sarcolemmal stability

DARS2.job: attaches the building block aspartate to its carrier molecule for making proteins
DARS2.basis: Catalyzes the attachment of aspartate to tRNA(Asp)

DBT.job: helps the body break down certain amino acids from protein in food
DBT.basis: The branched-chain alpha-keto dehydrogenase complex catalyzes the overall conversion of alpha-keto acids to acyl-CoA and CO(2) ... the catalytic function of this enzyme is to accept, and to transfer to coenzyme A, acyl groups that are generated by the branched-chain alpha-keto acid decarboxylase component

DCAF17.job: helps choose which proteins the cell tags for disposal
DCAF17.basis: May function as a substrate receptor for CUL4-DDB1 E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex
DCAF17.alt: helps pick out which proteins the cell tags for disposal

DCC.job: helps growing nerve fibers find their way in the developing nervous system
DCC.basis: Receptor for netrin required for axon guidance. Mediates axon attraction of neuronal growth cones in the developing nervous system

DCDC2.job: helps cells build their hair-like antennae and set their length
DCDC2.basis: Involved in the control of ciliogenesis and ciliary length

DCLRE1C.job: helps immune cells build the genes they use to recognize germs
DCLRE1C.basis: Nuclease involved in DNA non-homologous end joining (NHEJ); required for double-strand break repair and V(D)J recombination ... the process by which exons encoding the antigen-binding domains of immunoglobulins and T-cell receptor proteins are assembled from individual V, (D), and J gene segments
DCLRE1C.alt: cuts and trims broken DNA ends so immune cells can build their germ-recognizing genes

DCX.job: helps young nerve cells travel to their places in the developing brain
DCX.basis: required for initial steps of neuronal dispersion and cortex lamination during cerebral cortex development ... signaling pathways that promote neuronal migration

DDB2.job: spots DNA damaged by sunlight and calls in the repair crew
DDB2.basis: a complex that recognizes UV-induced DNA damage and recruit proteins of the nucleotide excision repair pathway (the NER pathway) to initiate DNA repair

DDC.job: makes the brain chemicals dopamine and serotonin
DDC.basis: Catalyzes the decarboxylation of L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (DOPA) to dopamine and L-5-hydroxytryptophan to serotonin

DDHD1.job: breaks down certain fats in cell membranes, helping shape mitochondria and nerve cells
DDHD1.basis: Phospholipase A1 (PLA1) that hydrolyzes ester bonds at the sn-1 position of glycerophospholipids producing a free fatty acid and a lysophospholipid ... Involved in the regulation of the endogenous content of polyunsaturated PI and PS lipids in the nervous system ... Regulates mitochondrial morphology

DDR2.job: senses collagen around cells and helps bones develop normally
DDR2.basis: It functions as a cell surface receptor for fibrillar collagen ... Required for normal bone development

DDX11.job: unwinds DNA so it can be copied and repaired accurately
DDX11.basis: ATP-dependent DNA helicase that participates in various functions in genomic stability, including DNA replication, DNA repair ... to preserve replication fork progression, and hence ensure DNA replication fidelity

DDX3X.job: unwinds tangled RNA messages so cells can read certain genes into proteins
DDX3X.basis: Multifunctional ATP-dependent RNA helicase ... promotes efficient translation of selected complex mRNAs, containing highly structured 5'-untranslated regions (UTR) ... Might facilitate translation by resolving secondary structures of 5'-UTRs during ribosome scanning

DDX41.job: senses foreign DNA from germs and helps raise the body's immune alarm
DDX41.basis: Plays pivotal roles in innate immune sensing ... Recognizes foreign or self-nucleic acids generated during microbial infection, thereby initiating anti-pathogen responses

DEGS1.job: helps make sphingosine, a building block of the fats in cell membranes
DEGS1.basis: Has sphingolipid-delta-4-desaturase activity. Converts D-erythro-sphinganine to D-erythro-sphingosine (E-sphing-4-enine)

DEPDC5.job: tells cells to stop growing when nutrients called amino acids run low
DEPDC5.basis: functions as an inhibitor of the amino acid-sensing branch of the mTORC1 pathway ... In response to amino acid depletion ... inhibiting mTORC1 signaling

DES.job: forms a fiber network that holds muscle cells together and keeps them strong
DES.basis: Muscle-specific type III intermediate filament essential for proper muscular structure and function ... forming a fibrous network connecting myofibrils to each other and to the plasma membrane ... thus providing strength for the muscle fiber during activity

DGKE.job: converts one fatty signaling molecule into another to switch cell messages
DGKE.basis: converts diacylglycerol/DAG into phosphatidic acid/phosphatidate/PA and regulates the respective levels of these two bioactive lipids ... acts as a central switch between the signaling pathways activated by these second messengers

DGUOK.job: helps make DNA building blocks for the cell's energy-producing powerhouses
DGUOK.basis: Phosphorylates deoxyguanosine and deoxyadenosine in the mitochondrial matrix ... mtDNA synthesis depends solely on DGUOK and TK2

DHCR24.job: carries out a final step in making cholesterol
DHCR24.basis: Catalyzes the reduction of the delta-24 double bond of sterol intermediates during cholesterol biosynthesis

DHCR7.job: carries out the final step in making cholesterol
DHCR7.basis: Oxidoreductase that catalyzes the last step of the cholesterol synthesis pathway, which transforms cholesta-5,7-dien-3beta-ol (7-dehydrocholesterol,7-DHC) into cholesterol

DHDDS.job: helps make a fatty carrier that attaches sugars to newly made proteins
DHDDS.basis: an essential component of the dolichol monophosphate (Dol-P) biosynthetic machinery ... a precursor of dolichol phosphate which is utilized as a sugar carrier in protein glycosylation

DHODH.job: helps cells make the building blocks for DNA and RNA
DHODH.basis: Catalyzes the conversion of dihydroorotate to orotate ... Required for UMP biosynthesis via de novo pathway

DHTKD1.job: helps the body break down the amino acids lysine and tryptophan from food
DHTKD1.basis: Responsible for the last step of L-lysine, L-hydroxylysine and L-tryptophan catabolism

DHX30.job: helps build the protein-making machines inside the cell's power plants
DHX30.basis: RNA-dependent helicase ... Plays an important role in the assembly of the mitochondrial large ribosomal subunit

DIAPH1.job: helps build the protein fibers that give cells their shape
DIAPH1.basis: Actin nucleation and elongation factor required for the assembly of F-actin structures ... Plays a role in the regulation of cell morphology and cytoskeletal organization. Required in the control of cell shape

DICER1.job: cuts RNA into tiny pieces that help turn down specific genes
DICER1.basis: Cleaves naturally occurring long dsRNAs and short hairpin pre-microRNAs (miRNA) into fragments of twenty-one to twenty-three nucleotides ... The miRNA pathway on the other side is a mean to specifically regulate the expression of target genes

DIS3L2.job: breaks down tagged genetic messages the cell no longer needs
DIS3L2.basis: 3'-5'-exoribonuclease that specifically recognizes RNAs polyuridylated at their 3' end and mediates their degradation ... mediates degradation of both mRNAs and miRNAs that have been polyuridylated

DKC1.job: helps build the cell's protein factories and protect chromosome tips
DKC1.basis: Required for ribosome biogenesis and telomere maintenance

DLD.job: is part of several enzyme teams that help cells turn food into energy
DLD.basis: E3 component of three alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complexes (pyruvate-, alpha-ketoglutarate-, and branched-chain amino acid-dehydrogenase complex) ... The pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex catalyzes the overall conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA and CO(2), and thereby links cytoplasmic glycolysis and the mitochondrial tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle

DLG3.job: holds signal receivers in place where brain cells connect
DLG3.basis: Post-synaptic scaffolding protein involved in the clustering of NMDA receptors ... at excitatory synapses

DLG4.job: holds key proteins in place where brain cells connect, helping them form and strengthen
DLG4.basis: Postsynaptic scaffolding protein that plays a critical role in synaptogenesis and synaptic plasticity by providing a platform for the postsynaptic clustering of crucial synaptic proteins

DLL1.job: signals to neighboring cells to guide which cell types they become
DLL1.basis: Transmembrane ligand protein of NOTCH1, NOTCH2 and NOTCH3 receptors ... triggers Notch signaling ... the DLL1-induced Notch signaling is mediated through an intercellular communication that regulates cell lineage, cell specification

DMD.job: anchors muscle cells' inner scaffolding to their outer membrane, keeping them stable
DMD.basis: Anchors the extracellular matrix to the cytoskeleton via F-actin ... has a structural function in stabilizing the sarcolemma

DMRT1.job: switches on genes that build the testes and keep sperm production going
DMRT1.basis: Transcription factor that plays a key role in male sex determination and differentiation by controlling testis development and male germ cell proliferation ... allowing abundant and continuous production of sperm

DNAAF1.job: helps put together the motors that make the cell's tiny hairs move
DNAAF1.basis: Cilium-specific protein required for the stability of the ciliary architecture. Plays a role in cytoplasmic preassembly of dynein arms

DNAAF11.job: helps build the motors that make cell hairs and sperm tails beat
DNAAF11.basis: Involved in dynein arm assembly ... transporting outer dynein arm (ODA) proteins from the cytoplasm to the cilia ... crucial component in the formation and motility of spermatozoal flagella

DNAAF19.job: helps attach the motors that make the cell's hair-like cilia beat
DNAAF19.basis: Dynein-attachment factor required for cilia motility

DNAAF2.job: helps assemble the motors that make the cell's tiny hairs and sperm tails beat
DNAAF2.basis: Required for cytoplasmic pre-assembly of axonemal dyneins, thereby playing a central role in motility in cilia and flagella

DNAAF3.job: helps put together the motors that make the cell's tiny hairs beat
DNAAF3.basis: Required for the assembly of axonemal inner and outer dynein arms. Involved in preassembly of dyneins into complexes before their transport into cilia

DNAAF4.job: helps assemble the motors that make cells' tiny hairs beat
DNAAF4.basis: Axonemal dynein assembly factor required for ciliary motility

DNAAF5.job: helps assemble the motors that make the cell's tiny hairs beat
DNAAF5.basis: involved in the delivery of the dynein machinery to the motile cilium ... required for the assembly of the axonemal dynein inner and outer arms ... that play a crucial role in cilium motility

DNAAF6.job: helps put together the motors that make the cell's tiny hairs beat
DNAAF6.basis: Plays a role in cytoplasmic pre-assembly of axonemal dynein

DNAH1.basis: Force generating protein of cilia required for sperm flagellum motility

DNAH11.job: powers the beating of tiny hairs that line the airways
DNAH11.basis: Force generating protein required for cilia beating in respiratory epithelia

DNAH5.job: powers the beating of tiny hairs that line the airways
DNAH5.basis: Force generating protein of respiratory cilia ... Key component of dynein, a family of motor proteins

DNAH6.job: powers the beating of tiny hairs that line the airways
DNAH6.basis: Force generating protein of respiratory cilia

DNAH8.basis: Force generating protein component of the outer dynein arms (ODAs) in the sperm flagellum ... Involved in sperm motility

DNAH9.job: powers the beating of tiny hairs that line the airways
DNAH9.basis: Force generating protein required for cilia beating in respiratory epithelia

DNAI1.job: is part of the motor that makes the hair-like cilia lining the airways beat
DNAI1.basis: Component of dynein, a family of motor proteins essential for movement along microtubules ... Required for structural and functional integrity of cilia ... Part of the dynein complex of respiratory cilia
DNAI1.alt: is part of the motor that makes cell hairs beat, including in the airways

DNAI2.job: is one of two linking parts of the motor that beats the airway's tiny hairs
DNAI2.basis: Component of dynein, a family of motor proteins essential for movement along microtubules ... Required for structural and functional integrity of cilia ... Part of the dynein complex of respiratory cilia
DNAI2.alt: is part of the motor that makes the hair-like cilia in the airways beat

DNAJB11.job: helps other proteins fold into the right shape as they are made
DNAJB11.basis: As a co-chaperone for HSPA5 it is required for proper folding, trafficking or degradation of proteins ... Binds directly to both unfolded proteins that are substrates for ERAD and nascent unfolded peptide chains

DNAJB2.job: helps cells refold or dispose of misshapen proteins
DNAJB2.basis: Functions as a co-chaperone, regulating the substrate binding and activating the ATPase activity of chaperones of the HSP70/heat shock protein 70 family ... contributes to the ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation of misfolded proteins ... promote the functional recovery of misfolded proteins

DNAJB6.job: helps other proteins fold properly and keeps them from clumping together
DNAJB6.basis: acts as a co-chaperone of HSP70 ... Acts as an endogenous molecular chaperone for neuronal proteins ... Suppresses aggregation and toxicity of polyglutamine-containing, aggregation-prone proteins

DNAJC12.job: helps fold the enzymes that process certain amino acids from food
DNAJC12.basis: Probable co-chaperone that participates in the proper folding of biopterin-dependent aromatic amino acid hydroxylases

DNAJC19.job: helps import proteins into mitochondria, the cell's power plants, and shape their fats
DNAJC19.basis: Mitochondrial co-chaperone which forms a complex with prohibitins to regulate cardiolipin remodeling ... May be a component of the PAM complex, a complex required for the translocation of transit peptide-containing proteins from the inner membrane into the mitochondrial matrix

DNAJC21.job: helps cells build ribosomes, the machines that make proteins
DNAJC21.basis: May play a role in ribosomal RNA (rRNA) biogenesis, possibly in the maturation of the 60S subunit

DNAJC30.job: helps the cell's power plants make energy, especially in nerve cells
DNAJC30.basis: Mitochondrial protein enriched in neurons that acts as a regulator of mitochondrial respiration ... facilitates ATP synthesis

DNAL1.job: helps power the beating of the cell's tiny hair-like cilia
DNAL1.basis: Part of the multisubunit axonemal ATPase complexes that generate the force for cilia motility ... Important for ciliary function in the airways

DNASE1L3.job: chops up DNA left behind by dying cells so the immune system ignores it
DNASE1L3.basis: Has DNA hydrolytic activity ... Acts in internucleosomal DNA fragmentation (INDF) during apoptosis and necrosis ... Is active on chromatin in apoptotic cell-derived membrane-coated microparticles and thus suppresses anti-DNA autoimmunity

DNM1.job: pinches off tiny bubbles of membrane so nerve cells can recycle their message packets
DNM1.basis: utilizes this energy to mediate vesicle scission and participates in many forms of endocytosis, such as clathrin-mediated endocytosis or synaptic vesicle endocytosis ... Controls plastic adaptation of the synaptic vesicle recycling machinery

DNM1L.job: pinches mitochondria, the cell's power plants, in two so they can divide
DNM1L.basis: Functions in mitochondrial and peroxisomal division ... wrap around the scission site to constrict and sever the mitochondrial membrane

DNM2.job: pinches off tiny bubbles of membrane so cells can take in materials
DNM2.basis: utilizes this energy to mediate vesicle scission at plasma membrane during endocytosis ... self-assembles into ring-like structure through oligomerization to form a helical polymer around the vesicle membrane and leading to vesicle scission

DNMT1.job: copies DNA's chemical tags onto new DNA so genes stay switched off
DNMT1.basis: DNA methyltransferase that methylates CpG residues ... Associates with DNA replication sites in S phase maintaining the methylation pattern in the newly synthesized strand ... Mediates transcriptional repression

DNMT3B.job: adds chemical tags to DNA that help set which genes stay off
DNMT3B.basis: DNA (cytosine-5)-methyltransferase that mediates genome-wide de novo methylation and which is essential for the establishment of DNA methylation patterns during development ... Acts as a transcriptional corepressor

DOCK11.job: switches on a cell-shaping protein and helps certain immune B cells develop
DOCK11.basis: Guanine nucleotide-exchange factor (GEF) that activates CDC42 ... Required for marginal zone (MZ) B-cell development ... Facilitates filopodia formation through the activation of CDC42

DOCK2.job: helps immune cells reshape themselves to move toward signals
DOCK2.basis: Activates RAC1 and RAC2 ... Involved in cytoskeletal rearrangements required for lymphocyte migration in response of chemokines

DOCK6.basis: Acts as a guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) for CDC42 and RAC1 small GTPases ... may regulate neurite outgrowth
DOCK6.alt: switches on helpers that reshape cells, which may help nerve fibers grow

DOCK7.job: helps young nerve cells grow their main signal-sending fiber and develop in the brain
DOCK7.basis: Required for STMN1 'Ser-15' phosphorylation during axon formation and consequently for neuronal polarization ... Involved in the regulation of cortical neurogenesis

DOCK8.job: helps immune cells move through tissues and kill infected cells
DOCK8.basis: required for interstitial dendritic cell (DC) migration ... Required for CD4(+) T-cell migration in response to chemokine stimulation ... Is involved in NK cell cytotoxicity

DOK7.job: helps muscles build the junctions where nerves connect to them
DOK7.basis: Probable muscle-intrinsic activator of MUSK that plays an essential role in neuromuscular synaptogenesis

DOLK.job: makes a fatty carrier the cell needs to attach sugar chains to proteins
DOLK.basis: Catalyzes CTP-mediated phosphorylation of dolichol, the terminal step in de novo dolichyl monophosphate (Dol-P) biosynthesis ... Dol-P is a lipid carrier essential for the synthesis of N-linked and O-linked oligosaccharides

DPAGT1.job: starts building the sugar chains that cells attach to many proteins
DPAGT1.basis: operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation ... Catalyzes the initial step of dolichol-linked oligosaccharide biosynthesis

DPF2.job: reads chemical tags on DNA's packaging to help switch genes on or off
DPF2.basis: Plays an active role in transcriptional regulation by binding modified histones H3 and H4

DPH1.job: helps finish a key part of the cell's protein-building machinery
DPH1.basis: Catalyzes the first step of diphthamide biosynthesis, a post-translational modification of histidine which occurs in elongation factor 2
DPH1.alt: adds a special chemical tweak to a key protein-building helper

DPM1.job: makes a sugar building block the cell uses to coat proteins with sugars
DPM1.basis: Transfers mannose from GDP-mannose to dolichol monophosphate to form dolichol phosphate mannose (Dol-P-Man) which is the mannosyl donor in pathways leading to N-glycosylation ... and O-mannosylation of proteins

DPY19L2.job: adds a type of sugar to certain other proteins
DPY19L2.basis: Probable C-mannosyltransferase that mediates C-mannosylation of tryptophan residues on target proteins
DPY19L2.alt: adds a sugar called mannose to certain other proteins

DRC1.job: helps hold together and control the beating of the cell's moving hairs
DRC1.basis: Component of the nexin-dynein regulatory complex (N-DRC) a key regulator of ciliary/flagellar motility which maintains the alignment and integrity of the distal axoneme and regulates microtubule sliding in motile axonemes

DRC2.job: helps cells' whip-like hairs beat properly
DRC2.basis: Component of the nexin-dynein regulatory complex (N-DRC), a key regulator of ciliary/flagellar motility

DRC4.job: helps cells' tiny moving hairs beat in step
DRC4.basis: a key regulator of ciliary/flagellar motility ... in motile cilia to coordinate cilia movement

DSC2.job: glues neighboring cells together so tissues stay strong
DSC2.basis: A component of desmosome cell-cell junctions which are required for positive regulation of cellular adhesion ... maintenance of intestinal epithelial cell intercellular adhesion strength

DSE.job: reshapes sugar units to help build a long sugar chain found in skin and tissues
DSE.basis: Converts D-glucuronic acid to L-iduronic acid (IdoUA) residues. Plays an important role in the biosynthesis of the glycosaminoglycan/mucopolysaccharide dermatan sulfate

DSP.job: anchors the cell's inner scaffolding to the junctions that glue cells together
DSP.basis: A component of desmosome cell-cell junctions which are required for positive regulation of cellular adhesion ... Required for keratin filament anchoring at the desmosome junction

DSPP.job: helps build and harden dentin, the hard layer beneath tooth enamel
DSPP.basis: DSP may be an important factor in dentinogenesis ... DPP may bind high amount of calcium and facilitate initial mineralization of dentin matrix collagen

DST.job: links the internal support fibers of nerve, muscle and skin cells together
DST.basis: Cytoskeletal linker protein. Acts as an integrator of intermediate filaments, actin and microtubule cytoskeleton networks. Required for anchoring either intermediate filaments to the actin cytoskeleton in neural and muscle cells or keratin-containing intermediate filaments to hemidesmosomes in epithelial cells.

DTNBP1.job: helps build the cell compartments that hold pigment and clotting chemicals
DTNBP1.basis: Component of the BLOC-1 complex, a complex that is required for normal biogenesis of lysosome-related organelles (LRO), such as platelet dense granules and melanosomes

DYNC1H1.job: powers the transport of cargo along tracks inside cells
DYNC1H1.basis: Cytoplasmic dynein 1 acts as a motor for the intracellular retrograde motility of vesicles and organelles along microtubules

DYNC2H1.job: powers transport back down the cell's hair-like antennae to help build them
DYNC2H1.basis: May function as a motor for intraflagellar retrograde transport. Functions in cilia biogenesis.

DYNC2I1.job: is part of a motor that carries cargo back down the cell's antenna-like hairs
DYNC2I1.basis: one of several non-catalytic accessory components of the cytoplasmic dynein 2 complex (dynein-2 complex), a motor protein complex that drives the movement of cargos along microtubules within cilia and flagella ... plays a major role in retrograde ciliary protein trafficking in cilia and flagella

DYNC2I2.job: is part of a motor that ferries cargo back down the cell's antenna-like hairs
DYNC2I2.basis: non-catalytic accessory components of the cytoplasmic dynein 2 complex (dynein-2 complex), a motor protein complex that drives the movement of cargos along microtubules within cilia and flagella ... plays a major role in retrograde ciliary protein trafficking and in ciliogenesis

DYRK1A.job: helps repair broken DNA and switch genes on inside the cell
DYRK1A.basis: Plays an important role in double-strand breaks (DSBs) repair following DNA damage ... Also acts as a positive regulator of transcription

DYSF.job: helps muscle cells quickly patch tears in their outer membrane
DYSF.basis: Plays a role in the sarcolemma repair mechanism of both skeletal muscle and cardiomyocytes that permits rapid resealing of membranes disrupted by mechanical stress

DZIP1L.job: helps cells build their antenna-like sensing hairs
DZIP1L.basis: Involved in primary cilium formation ... required for localization of PKD1/PC1 and PKD2/PC2 to the ciliary membrane

EARS2.job: loads the amino acid glutamate onto carriers that build proteins inside mitochondria
EARS2.basis: catalyzes aminoacylation of both mitochondrial tRNA(Glu) and tRNA(Gln) and participates in RNA aminoacylation for mitochondrial protein translation ... Attachs glutamate to tRNA(Glu) or tRNA(Gln)

EBF3.job: switches on other genes by binding to specific stretches of DNA
EBF3.basis: Transcriptional activator ... Recognizes variations of the palindromic sequence 5'-ATTCCCNNGGGAATT-3'

EBP.job: carries out one step in how the body makes cholesterol
EBP.basis: Isomerase that catalyzes the conversion of Delta(8)-sterols to their corresponding Delta(7)-isomers a catalytic step in the postlanosterol biosynthesis of cholesterol

ECHS1.job: helps cells burn fats for energy
ECHS1.basis: Plays a key role in the beta-oxidation spiral of short- and medium-chain fatty acid oxidation

EDAR.job: receives a signal from a partner protein and passes it into the cell
EDAR.basis: Receptor for EDA isoform A1 ... Mediates the activation of NF-kappa-B and JNK
EDAR.alt: receives a signal from a partner protein called EDA and passes it into the cell

EEF1A2.job: delivers building blocks to the cell's protein-making machines as they build proteins
EEF1A2.basis: Translation elongation factor that catalyzes the GTP-dependent binding of aminoacyl-tRNA (aa-tRNA) to the A-site of ribosomes during the elongation phase of protein synthesis

EFEMP1.job: latches onto a cell's growth-signal receiver and switches it on
EFEMP1.basis: Binds EGFR, the EGF receptor, inducing EGFR autophosphorylation and the activation of downstream signaling pathways

EFEMP2.job: helps build the stretchy fibers that keep the aorta and other tissues elastic
EFEMP2.basis: Plays a crucial role in elastic fiber formation in tissue ... and in the mechanical properties and wall integrity maintenance of the aorta

EFL1.job: helps finish building the cell's protein-making machines so they can start work
EFL1.basis: GTPase involved in the biogenesis of the 60S ribosomal subunit and translational activation of ribosomes ... thereby activating ribosomes for translation competence

EFNB1.job: signals to touching cells to guide how nerves, blood vessels and tissues develop
EFNB1.basis: Cell surface transmembrane ligand for Eph receptors ... crucial for migration, repulsion and adhesion during neuronal, vascular and epithelial development ... Binding to Eph receptors residing on adjacent cells leads to contact-dependent bidirectional signaling into neighboring cells

EFTUD2.job: helps cut and paste genetic messages before they're used to make proteins
EFTUD2.basis: Required for pre-mRNA splicing as component of the spliceosome

EGLN1.job: senses oxygen levels and tells cells when they're getting enough
EGLN1.basis: Cellular oxygen sensor that catalyzes, under normoxic conditions, the post-translational formation of 4-hydroxyproline in hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) alpha proteins ... Hydroxylated HIFs are then targeted for proteasomal degradation ... Under hypoxic conditions, the hydroxylation reaction is attenuated allowing HIFs to escape degradation

EGR2.job: switches on genes that build the insulating coating around nerves
EGR2.basis: Sequence-specific DNA-binding transcription factor ... in Schwann cell myelination by regulating the expression of genes involved in the formation and maintenance of myelin

EHMT1.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging proteins that switch genes off
EHMT1.basis: Histone methyltransferase that specifically mono-, di- and trimethylates 'Lys-9' of histone H3 ... H3K9me represents a specific tag for epigenetic transcriptional repression

EIF2AK4.job: senses when cells run low on amino acids and slows protein-making to cope
EIF2AK4.basis: Metabolic-stress sensing protein kinase that phosphorylates the alpha subunit of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 (EIF2S1/eIF-2-alpha) in response to low amino acid availability ... converts EIF2S1/eIF-2-alpha into a global protein synthesis inhibitor ... required for adaptation to amino acid starvation

EIF2B1.job: is the alpha part of a switch that starts the cell's protein-making and can pause it
EIF2B1.basis: component of the translation initiation factor 2B (eIF2B) complex, which catalyzes the exchange of GDP for GTP on eukaryotic initiation factor 2 ... Its guanine nucleotide exchange factor activity is repressed when bound to eIF2 complex phosphorylated on the alpha subunit ... consequently global translation is repressed
EIF2B1.alt: is part of a switch that lets cells start making new proteins

EIF2B2.job: is the beta piece of a switch that lets cells start making proteins
EIF2B2.basis: Acts as a component of the translation initiation factor 2B (eIF2B) complex, which catalyzes the exchange of GDP for GTP on eukaryotic initiation factor 2 (eIF2) ... global translation is repressed
EIF2B2.alt: helps cells start making proteins, and slows this down under stress

EIF2B3.job: helps cells start making new proteins
EIF2B3.basis: component of the translation initiation factor 2B (eIF2B) complex, which catalyzes the exchange of GDP for GTP on the eukaryotic initiation factor 2 (eIF2) complex ... global translation

EIF2B4.job: is the delta part of the switch that lets cells start making new proteins
EIF2B4.basis: Acts as a component of the translation initiation factor 2B (eIF2B) complex, which catalyzes the exchange of GDP for GTP on eukaryotic initiation factor 2 (eIF2) ... global translation
EIF2B4.alt: is part of a switch that lets cells start making new proteins

EIF2B5.job: is the epsilon piece of a switch that lets cells start making new proteins
EIF2B5.basis: Acts as a component of the translation initiation factor 2B (eIF2B) complex, which catalyzes the exchange of GDP for GTP on eukaryotic initiation factor 2 (eIF2) gamma subunit ... consequently global translation is repressed
EIF2B5.alt: helps cells start making new proteins

EIF2S3.job: helps cells start building new proteins
EIF2S3.basis: Member of the eIF2 complex that functions in the early steps of protein synthesis

EIF3F.job: is part of a team that helps cells start making new proteins
EIF3F.basis: Component of the eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 (eIF-3) complex, which is required for several steps in the initiation of protein synthesis

ELAC2.job: trims the ends of molecules that help mitochondria, the cell's power plants, make proteins
ELAC2.basis: mitochondrial tRNA 3'-processing endonuclease activity ... Involved in tRNA maturation, by removing a 3'-trailer from precursor tRNA

ELANE.job: helps white blood cells kill bacteria by chopping up their proteins
ELANE.basis: Shows microbicidal activity in neutrophils by mediating cleavage and degradation of bacterial proteins

ELF4.job: switches on genes that guide immune cells and keep inflammation in check
ELF4.basis: Transcriptional activator that binds to DNA sequences ... Plays a role in the development and function of NK and NK T-cells and in innate immunity ... Is a transcriptional regulator of inflammation ... Required for sustained transcription of anti-inflammatory genes

ELN.job: makes blood vessels and other tissues stretchy so they spring back
ELN.basis: Major structural protein of tissues such as aorta and nuchal ligament, which must expand rapidly and recover completely

ELOVL4.job: lengthens fats into the extra-long building blocks used in cell membranes
ELOVL4.basis: allows the addition of 2 carbons to the chain of long- and very long-chain fatty acids (VLCFAs) per cycle ... precursors of membrane lipids

ELP2.job: helps fine-tune the molecules cells use to build proteins
ELP2.basis: Component of the elongator complex which is required for multiple tRNA modifications
ELP2.alt: is part of a team that chemically fine-tunes the cell's protein-building adapter molecules

EMG1.job: helps build ribosomes, the cell's protein-making machines
EMG1.basis: Also has an essential role in 40S ribosomal subunit biogenesis ... Part of the small subunit (SSU) processome, first precursor of the small eukaryotic ribosomal subunit

EMILIN1.job: helps build the stretchy and strong fibers that support tissues
EMILIN1.basis: Involved in elastic and collagen fibers formation

EML1.job: helps organize the cell's inner scaffolding so brain cells divide properly during development
EML1.basis: Modulates the assembly and organization of the microtubule cytoskeleton ... Required for normal proliferation of neuronal progenitor cells in the developing brain and for normal brain development

ENG.job: helps build new blood vessels and keep their walls sound
ENG.basis: plays an important role in the regulation of angiogenesis ... Required for normal structure and integrity of adult vasculature

ENPP1.job: makes a natural substance that stops calcium deposits from forming in soft tissues
ENPP1.basis: Nucleotide pyrophosphatase that generates diphosphate (PPi) and functions in bone mineralization and soft tissue calcification by regulating pyrophosphate levels ... PPi inhibits bone mineralization and soft tissue calcification by binding to nascent hydroxyapatite crystals, thereby preventing further growth of these crystals

ENTPD1.job: breaks down energy molecules outside cells, which helps keep blood flowing smoothly
ENTPD1.basis: Catalyzes the hydrolysis of nucleoside triphosphates (NTPs) and diphosphates (NDPs) ... This activity contributes to the regulation of extracellular levels of nucleotides ... By hydrolyzing pro-inflammatory ATP and platelet-activating ADP to AMP, it blocks platelet aggregation and supports blood flow

EOGT.job: attaches a small sugar tag to proteins found outside cells
EOGT.basis: Catalyzes the transfer of a single N-acetylglucosamine from UDP-GlcNAc to a serine or threonine residue in extracellular proteins

EP300.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging proteins that help switch genes on
EP300.basis: Functions as a histone acetyltransferase and regulates transcription via chromatin remodeling ... Histone acetylation gives an epigenetic tag for transcriptional activation

EPCAM.job: helps gut lining cells and immune cells stick together to block infection
EPCAM.basis: May act as a physical homophilic interaction molecule between intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) and intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs) at the mucosal epithelium for providing immunological barrier as a first line of defense against mucosal infection

EPG5.job: helps cells finish breaking down and recycling their own worn-out parts
EPG5.basis: Involved in autophagy. May play a role in a late step of autophagy, such as clearance of autophagosomal cargo

EPHB4.job: helps shape the heart and blood vessels as they form
EPHB4.basis: plays a central role in heart morphogenesis, angiogenesis and blood vessel remodeling

EPM2A.job: keeps the body's stored sugar, glycogen, from clumping into insoluble lumps
EPM2A.basis: Plays an important role in preventing glycogen hyperphosphorylation and the formation of insoluble aggregates, via its activity as glycogen phosphatase

ERCC2.job: unzips DNA so damaged pieces, such as from sunlight, can be cut out and replaced
ERCC2.basis: ATP-dependent 5'-3' DNA helicase ... Required for transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair (NER) of damaged DNA ... Sequestered in chromatin on UV-damaged DNA ... In NER, TFIIH acts by opening DNA around the lesion to allow the excision of the damaged oligonucleotide and its replacement by a new DNA fragment. The ATP-dependent helicase activity of XPD/ERCC2 is required for DNA opening

ERCC3.job: unzips DNA so genes can be read and damaged spots repaired
ERCC3.basis: Binds dsDNA rather than ssDNA, unzipping it ... TFIIH is required for promoter opening ... In NER, TFIIH acts by opening DNA around the lesion to allow the excision of the damaged oligonucleotide and its replacement by a new DNA fragment

ERCC4.job: cuts out damaged stretches of DNA so they can be repaired
ERCC4.basis: structure-specific DNA repair endonuclease responsible for the 5-prime incision during DNA repair, and which is essential for nucleotide excision repair (NER)

ERCC5.job: cuts out damaged pieces of DNA so they can be repaired
ERCC5.basis: Single-stranded structure-specific DNA endonuclease involved in DNA excision repair ... Makes the 3'incision in DNA nucleotide excision repair (NER)

ERCC6.job: helps repair damaged DNA in genes that are being actively read
ERCC6.basis: Essential factor involved in transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair (TC-NER), a process during which RNA polymerase II-blocking lesions are rapidly removed from the transcribed strand of active genes

ERCC6L2.job: helps join broken DNA strands back together during repair
ERCC6L2.basis: Promotes double-strand break (DSB) end-joining ... plays a role in DNA repair

ERCC8.job: helps repair damaged DNA in genes the cell is actively reading
ERCC8.basis: involved in transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair (TC-NER), a process during which RNA polymerase II-blocking lesions are rapidly removed from the transcribed strand of active genes

ERF.job: switches off certain genes, including some that make cells grow and divide
ERF.basis: Potent transcriptional repressor that binds to the H1 element of the Ets2 promoter. May regulate other genes involved in cellular proliferation

ERLIN1.job: helps cells clear away certain calcium-release channels and keep cholesterol in balance
ERLIN1.basis: mediates the endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD) of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptors (IP3Rs) ... Involved in regulation of cellular cholesterol homeostasis

ERLIN2.job: helps cells break down certain proteins and keep cholesterol levels in balance
ERLIN2.basis: mediates the endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD) of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptors (IP3Rs) ... Involved in regulation of cellular cholesterol homeostasis

ESCO2.job: helps hold copied chromosomes together until the cell divides
ESCO2.basis: Acetyltransferase required for the establishment of sister chromatid cohesion ... Couples the processes of cohesion and DNA replication to ensure that only sister chromatids become paired together

ESRRB.job: switches on genes that keep early embryo stem cells flexible and help build the inner ear
ESRRB.basis: Transcription factor that binds ... promoter and enhancer of targets genes regulating their expression ... Plays a role ... in maintainance of self-renewal and pluripotency of embryonic and trophoblast stem cells ... Also plays a role inner ear development by controlling expression of ion channels and transporters

ETFA.job: helps cells burn fats and amino acids for energy
ETFA.basis: accepts electrons from several mitochondrial dehydrogenases ... transfers the electrons to the main mitochondrial respiratory chain ... Required for normal mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation and normal amino acid metabolism

ETFB.job: passes energy from burning fats and amino acids to the cell's power plants
ETFB.basis: accepts electrons from several mitochondrial dehydrogenases ... It transfers the electrons to the main mitochondrial respiratory chain ... Required for normal mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation and normal amino acid metabolism

ETFDH.job: helps cells get energy from fats and protein building blocks
ETFDH.basis: Links fatty acid beta-oxidation and amino acid catabolism to the respiratory chain by transferring electrons from the electron transfer flavoprotein (ETF) to ubiquinone

ETHE1.job: helps clear hydrogen sulfide, a toxic gas, inside the cell's energy factories
ETHE1.basis: plays an essential role in hydrogen sulfide catabolism in the mitochondrial matrix ... preventing the accumulation of supraphysiological H(2)S levels that have toxic effects

ETV6.job: switches off certain genes and helps the body make blood cells
ETV6.basis: Transcriptional repressor; binds to the DNA sequence 5'-CCGGAAGT-3'. Plays a role in hematopoiesis

EVC.job: helps cells' antenna-like hairs pass on growth signals that shape the skeleton
EVC.basis: Component of the EvC complex that positively regulates ciliary Hedgehog (Hh) signaling ... Involved in endochondral growth and skeletal development

EVC2.job: helps cells' antenna-like hairs pass on growth signals that shape bones
EVC2.basis: Component of the EvC complex that positively regulates ciliary Hedgehog (Hh) signaling. Plays a critical role in bone formation and skeletal development

EXOC6B.job: helps cells dock the small packages they send out at the cell's surface
EXOC6B.basis: Component of the exocyst complex involved in the docking of exocytic vesicles with fusion sites on the plasma membrane

EXT1.job: helps build long sugar chains that help cells signal
EXT1.basis: heparan sulfate polymerase which catalyzes the elongation of the heparan sulfate glycan backbone ... Heparan sulfate proteoglycans are ubiquitous components of the extracellular matrix and play an important role in tissue homeostasis and signaling

EYA1.job: helps the ears, kidneys and skeleton form before birth
EYA1.basis: Required for normal embryonic development of the craniofacial and trunk skeleton, kidneys and ears

EYA4.job: helps repair damaged DNA and guide how organs form
EYA4.basis: Promotes efficient DNA repair by dephosphorylating H2AX ... its role in transcription regulation during organogenesis

EYS.job: helps keep the eye's light-sensing cells healthy and intact
EYS.basis: Required to maintain the integrity of photoreceptor cells

EZH2.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging proteins that switch genes off
EZH2.basis: Catalytic subunit of the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex ... that methylates 'Lys-9' (H3K9me) and 'Lys-27' (H3K27me) of histone H3, leading to transcriptional repression of the affected target gene

F10.job: turns on the main clotting protein that makes blood clot
F10.basis: converts prothrombin to thrombin in the presence of factor Va, calcium and phospholipid during blood clotting

F12.job: helps start the chain reaction that clots blood
F12.basis: participates in the initiation of blood coagulation

F13A1.job: links strands of a blood clot together to make it stronger
F13A1.basis: catalyzes the formation of gamma-glutamyl-epsilon-lysine cross-links between fibrin chains, thus stabilizing the fibrin clot

F13B.basis: The B chain of factor XIII is not catalytically active, but is thought to stabilize the A subunits and regulate the rate of transglutaminase formation by thrombin
F13B.alt: steadies the clot-strengthening factor XIII so it works when blood clots

F2.job: turns a blood protein into the mesh that forms a clot
F2.basis: Thrombin ... converts fibrinogen to fibrin and activates factors V, VII, VIII, XIII ... Functions in blood homeostasis, inflammation and wound healing

F5.job: helps blood clot by speeding the making of thrombin
F5.basis: Central regulator of hemostasis. It serves as a critical cofactor for the prothrombinase activity of factor Xa that results in the activation of prothrombin to thrombin

F8.basis: acts as a cofactor for F9/factor IXa when it converts F10/factor X to the activated form, factor Xa

F9.basis: participates in the intrinsic pathway of blood coagulation by converting factor X to its active form

FA2H.job: modifies fats used to build the protective coating around nerves and the skin's barrier
FA2H.basis: Catalyzes the hydroxylation of free fatty acids at the C-2 position to produce 2-hydroxy fatty acids, which are building blocks of sphingolipids and glycosphingolipids common in neural tissue and epidermis ... Plays an essential role in the synthesis of galactosphingolipids of the myelin sheath ... critical for skin permeability barrier

FAH.job: helps the body break down tyrosine, an amino acid from food
FAH.basis: Catalyzes the final step in the breakdown of the amino acid tyrosine

FAM111A.job: cuts away proteins stuck to DNA so cells can copy their DNA
FAM111A.basis: mediates the proteolytic cleavage of covalent DNA-protein cross-links (DPCs) during DNA synthesis, thereby playing a key role in maintaining genomic integrity ... Protects replication fork from stalling by removing DPCs

FAM20C.job: adds phosphate tags to proteins that cells send out, helping harden bones and teeth
FAM20C.basis: phosphorylates secretory pathway proteins within Ser-x-Glu/pSer motifs and plays a key role in biomineralization of bones and teeth ... Constitutes the main protein kinase for extracellular proteins

FAN1.job: cuts out faulty links that tie the two strands of DNA together
FAN1.basis: Nuclease required for the repair of DNA interstrand cross-links (ICL) ... allowing to excise an ICL from one strand through flanking incisions

FANCA.job: helps repair DNA and keep chromosomes stable
FANCA.basis: DNA repair protein ... maintenance of normal chromosome stability

FANCB.basis: DNA repair protein required for FANCD2 ubiquitination

FANCC.job: helps repair damaged DNA and keep chromosomes stable
FANCC.basis: DNA repair protein ... May be implicated in interstrand DNA cross-link repair and in the maintenance of normal chromosome stability

FANCD2.job: helps repair broken DNA and keep chromosomes intact
FANCD2.basis: Required for maintenance of chromosomal stability ... Involved in the repair of DNA double-strand breaks

FANCE.job: helps repair DNA strands that have become stuck together

FANCF.job: helps repair damaged DNA and keep chromosomes stable
FANCF.basis: DNA repair protein ... May be implicated in interstrand DNA cross-link repair and in the maintenance of normal chromosome stability

FANCG.job: helps repair DNA and keep chromosomes stable
FANCG.basis: DNA repair protein ... May be implicated in interstrand DNA cross-link repair and in the maintenance of normal chromosome stability

FANCI.job: helps repair broken or tangled DNA
