FANCI.basis: Plays an essential role in the repair of DNA double-strand breaks by homologous recombination and in the repair of interstrand DNA cross-links (ICLs)

FANCL.job: tags another protein to switch on the cell's DNA repair system
FANCL.basis: Ubiquitin ligase protein that mediates monoubiquitination of FANCD2 in the presence of UBE2T, a key step in the DNA damage pathway

FANCM.job: helps repair DNA damage and keep chromosomes from breaking
FANCM.basis: Required for the normal activation of the FA pathway, leading to monoubiquitination of the FANCI-FANCD2 complex in response to DNA damage ... and prevention of chromosomal breakage

FARS2.job: loads the amino acid phenylalanine for building proteins inside mitochondria, the cell's power plants
FARS2.basis: Is responsible for the charging of tRNA(Phe) with phenylalanine in mitochondrial translation

FAS.job: picks up signals that tell a cell to self-destruct
FAS.basis: Receptor for TNFSF6/FASLG ... initiates the subsequent cascade of caspases (aspartate-specific cysteine proteases) mediating apoptosis

FASLG.job: tells unwanted or worn-out cells, including used-up immune cells, to self-destruct
FASLG.basis: Cytokine that binds to TNFRSF6/FAS, a receptor that transduces the apoptotic signal into cells ... Initiates fratricidal/suicidal activation-induced cell death (AICD) in antigen-activated T-cells contributing to the termination of immune responses

FASTKD2.job: helps build the protein-making machines inside the cell's power plants
FASTKD2.basis: Plays an important role in assembly of the mitochondrial large ribosomal subunit ... is required for intra-mitochondrial translation

FAT1.job: helps cells line up, move in the right direction and touch their neighbors
FAT1.basis: Plays an essential role for cellular polarization, directed cell migration and modulating cell-cell contact

FAT4.job: helps cells line up in the right direction and keeps cell growth in check
FAT4.basis: Cadherins are calcium-dependent cell adhesion proteins. FAT4 plays a role in the maintenance of planar cell polarity as well as in inhibition of YAP1-mediated neuroprogenitor cell proliferation

FBN1.job: helps build the stretchy fibers that support blood vessels, skin and lungs
FBN1.basis: Structural component of the 10-12 nm diameter microfibrils of the extracellular matrix, which conveys both structural and regulatory properties to load-bearing connective tissues ... In tissues such as the lung, blood vessels and skin, microfibrils form the periphery of the elastic fiber, acting as a scaffold for the deposition of elastin

FBN2.job: helps build the stretchy fibers that give tissues their elasticity
FBN2.basis: Fibrillins are structural components of 10-12 nm extracellular calcium-binding microfibrils ... Fibrillin-2-containing microfibrils regulate the early process of elastic fiber assembly

FBP1.job: helps the body make its own sugar when food runs low
FBP1.basis: acting as a rate-limiting enzyme in gluconeogenesis

FBXL4.job: keeps cells from destroying too many of their own energy-making mitochondria
FBXL4.basis: plays a role in the restriction of mitophagy by controlling the degradation of BNIP3 and NIX mitophagy receptors

FCHO1.job: helps cells bend their outer membrane inward to bring in material from outside
FCHO1.basis: Functions in an early step of clathrin-mediated endocytosis ... Has both a membrane binding/bending activity and the ability to recruit proteins essential to the formation of functional clathrin-coated pits

FDXR.job: passes electrons to enzymes in the cell's powerhouses that make steroid hormones
FDXR.basis: Serves as the first electron transfer protein in all the mitochondrial P450 systems including cholesterol side chain cleavage in all steroidogenic tissues

FECH.job: adds iron in the last step of making heme, the iron-holding part of blood
FECH.basis: Catalyzes the ferrous insertion into protoporphyrin IX and participates in the terminal step in the heme biosynthetic pathway

FERMT1.job: helps skin cells grip the layer beneath them and move to heal wounds
FERMT1.basis: Involved in cell adhesion ... Required for normal adhesion of keratinocytes to fibronectin and laminin, and for normal keratinocyte migration to wound sites

FERMT3.job: helps blood cells grip blood vessel walls and each other, including clot-forming platelets
FERMT3.basis: Plays a central role in cell adhesion in hematopoietic cells ... Required for integrin-mediated platelet adhesion and leukocyte adhesion to endothelial cells

FGA.job: forms the mesh of fibers that holds a blood clot together
FGA.basis: polymerize to form an insoluble fibrin matrix. Fibrin has a major function in hemostasis as one of the primary components of blood clots

FGB.job: forms the fibers that hold blood clots together
FGB.basis: polymerize to form an insoluble fibrin matrix. Fibrin has a major function in hemostasis as one of the primary components of blood clots

FGD1.job: switches on a signaling protein that shapes the cell's internal skeleton
FGD1.basis: Activates CDC42 ... by exchanging bound GDP for free GTP. Plays a role in regulating the actin cytoskeleton and cell shape

FGD4.job: switches on a partner protein that shapes the cell's inner scaffolding
FGD4.basis: Activates CDC42 ... Plays a role in regulating the actin cytoskeleton and cell shape

FGF12.job: helps nerve cells fire signals by tuning their sodium channels
FGF12.basis: Involved in the positive regulation of voltage-gated sodium channel activity. Promotes neuronal excitability

FGF3.job: helps the inner ear form as an embryo develops
FGF3.basis: Plays an important role in the regulation of embryonic development ... Required for normal ear development

FGF9.job: guides how cells grow and specialize as the embryo develops
FGF9.basis: Plays an important role in the regulation of embryonic development, cell proliferation, cell differentiation and cell migration

FGFR1.job: picks up growth signals that guide how the body develops before birth
FGFR1.basis: acts as a cell-surface receptor for fibroblast growth factors and plays an essential role in the regulation of embryonic development, cell proliferation, differentiation and migration

FGFR2.job: picks up growth signals that guide how bones, skin and other tissues form
FGFR2.basis: acts as a cell-surface receptor for fibroblast growth factors and plays an essential role in the regulation of cell proliferation, differentiation ... Required for normal embryonic patterning ... osteogenesis and skin development ... required for normal skeleton development

FGFR3.job: picks up growth signals that guide how cartilage and bone grow
FGFR3.basis: acts as a cell-surface receptor for fibroblast growth factors ... Plays an essential role in the regulation of chondrocyte differentiation, proliferation and apoptosis, and is required for normal skeleton development

FGG.job: forms the mesh of fibers that holds a blood clot together
FGG.basis: polymerizes to form an insoluble fibrin matrix. Has a major function in hemostasis as one of the primary components of blood clots

FH.job: helps cells turn food into energy by converting fumarate to malate
FH.basis: Catalyzes the reversible stereospecific interconversion of fumarate to L-malate

FHOD3.job: helps organize the protein fibers that shape cells, including heart muscle cells
FHOD3.basis: Actin-organizing protein ... may play a role in actin filament polymerization in cardiomyocytes

FIG4.job: helps control a signaling fat that cells use to manage their recycling compartments
FIG4.basis: component of the PI(3,5)P2 regulatory complex which regulates both the synthesis and turnover of phosphatidylinositol 3,5-bisphosphate (PtdIns(3,5)P2)

FITM2.job: helps cells form tiny fat-storage droplets
FITM2.basis: required for maintaining ER structure and for lipid droplets (LDs) biogenesis, which are lipid storage organelles

FKRP.job: helps attach a sugar chain to a protein that anchors muscle cells
FKRP.basis: Catalyzes the transfer of a ribitol 5-phosphate ... to the phosphorylated O-mannosyl trisaccharide ... a carbohydrate structure present in alpha-dystroglycan (DAG1)

FKTN.job: adds sugar links to a protein that anchors muscle cells to their surroundings
FKTN.basis: Catalyzes the transfer of a ribitol-phosphate from CDP-ribitol to the distal N-acetylgalactosamine of the phosphorylated O-mannosyl trisaccharide ... a carbohydrate structure present in alpha-dystroglycan (DAG1) ... May interact with and reinforce a large complex encompassing the outside and inside of muscle membranes

FLAD1.job: turns vitamin B2 into a form that many enzymes need to work
FLAD1.basis: FAD synthase catalyzes the adenylation of flavin mononucleotide (FMN) to form flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) coenzyme ... the protein also facilitates the delivery of FAD to client apo-flavoproteins
FLAD1.alt: turns vitamin B2 into a helper molecule that many enzymes need to work

FLCN.job: helps cells sense available nutrients and adjust their growth accordingly
FLCN.basis: involved in both the cellular response to amino acid availability ... The GTPase-activating activity is inhibited during starvation and activated in presence of nutrients ... thereby activating the kinase activity of mTORC1

FLNA.job: links the cell's inner support fibers to its outer membrane
FLNA.basis: Promotes orthogonal branching of actin filaments and links actin filaments to membrane glycoproteins. Anchors various transmembrane proteins to the actin cytoskeleton

FLNB.job: links the cell's outer skin to its inner support scaffolding
FLNB.basis: Connects cell membrane constituents to the actin cytoskeleton ... Anchors various transmembrane proteins to the actin cytoskeleton

FLNC.job: helps build and organize the contracting units inside muscle cells
FLNC.basis: Muscle-specific filamin, which plays a central role in sarcomere assembly and organization ... functions as a large actin-cross-linking protein with structural functions at the Z lines in muscle cells

FLT4.job: picks up signals that help grow lymph vessels and blood vessels
FLT4.basis: acts as a cell-surface receptor for VEGFC and VEGFD, and plays an essential role in adult lymphangiogenesis and in the development of the vascular network

FLVCR1.job: brings choline into cells to build their outer membranes
FLVCR1.basis: mediates the transport of extracellular choline and ethanolamine into cells, thereby playing a key role in phospholipid biosynthesis ... Also acts as a heme b transporter

FLVCR2.job: carries choline, a key nutrient, from the blood into the brain
FLVCR2.basis: Choline uniporter that specifically mediates choline uptake at the blood-brain-barrier ... Responsible for the majority of choline uptake across the blood-brain-barrier from the circulation into the brain ... Choline, a nutrient critical for brain development

FMO3.job: helps the liver break down certain drugs and food compounds, including fishy-smelling trimethylamine
FMO3.basis: Essential hepatic enzyme that catalyzes the oxygenation of a wide variety of nitrogen- and sulfur-containing compounds including drugs as well as dietary compounds ... Plays an important role in the metabolism of trimethylamine (TMA)

FMR1.job: controls which proteins brain cells make at their connections, shaping brain development
FMR1.basis: RNA-binding protein that plays a central role in neuronal development and synaptic plasticity through the regulation of ... postsynaptic local protein synthesis of target mRNAs ... Acts as a repressor of mRNA translation in synaptic regions

FN1.job: helps cells stick to the material around them and heal wounds
FN1.basis: Fibronectins bind cell surfaces and various compounds including collagen, fibrin ... Fibronectins are involved in cell adhesion, cell motility, opsonization, wound healing

FNIP1.job: helps cells sense available nutrients and adjust growth and recycling to match
FNIP1.basis: involved in the cellular response to amino acid availability by regulating the non-canonical mTORC1 signaling cascade ... Together with FLCN, regulates autophagy

FOLR1.job: brings the vitamin folate into cells
FOLR1.basis: Binds to folate and reduced folic acid derivatives and mediates delivery of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate and folate analogs into the interior of cells

FOXC1.job: switches on genes that help the eye, bones, heart and kidneys develop
FOXC1.basis: DNA-binding transcriptional factor that plays a role in a broad range of cellular and developmental processes such as eye, bones, cardiovascular, kidney and skin development

FOXC2.job: acts as a switch that turns on other genes

FOXE1.job: switches on genes that help shape the roof of the mouth and thyroid
FOXE1.basis: Transcription factor that binds consensus sites on a variety of gene promoters and activate their transcription. Involved in proper palate formation ... Also implicated in thyroid gland morphogenesis

FOXE3.job: switches on genes that help the eye's lens grow and form
FOXE3.basis: Transcription factor that controls lens epithelial cell growth ... During lens development, controls the ratio of the lens fiber cells to the cells of the anterior lens epithelium

FOXG1.job: switches off genes to help shape the front of the developing brain
FOXG1.basis: Transcription repression factor which plays an important role in the establishment of the regional subdivision of the developing brain and in the development of the telencephalon

FOXJ1.job: switches on the genes that build the cell's moving, hair-like brushes
FOXJ1.basis: Transcription factor specifically required for the formation of motile cilia ... Acts by activating transcription of genes that mediate assembly of motile cilia

FOXN1.job: switches on genes that build the thymus, where immune T cells mature
FOXN1.basis: Transcriptional regulator which regulates the development, differentiation, and function of thymic epithelial cells (TECs) ... Plays a crucial role in the early prenatal stages of T-cell ontogeny

FOXP1.job: switches off certain genes to guide how lungs, nerves, heart and immune cells develop
FOXP1.basis: Transcriptional repressor ... Plays an important role in the specification and differentiation of lung epithelium ... Essential transcriptional regulator of B-cell development. Involved in regulation of cardiac muscle cell proliferation. Involved in the columnar organization of spinal motor neurons

FOXP2.job: switches off other genes to help the brain, lungs and gut develop
FOXP2.basis: Transcriptional repressor that may play a role in the specification and differentiation of lung epithelium. May also play a role in developing neural, gastrointestinal and cardiovascular tissues

FOXP3.job: switches on the genes that let special immune cells calm the immune system
FOXP3.basis: Transcriptional regulator which is crucial for the development and inhibitory function of regulatory T-cells (Treg) ... Plays an essential role in maintaining homeostasis of the immune system by allowing the acquisition of full suppressive function

FOXRED1.job: helps build the first machine in the cell's power plants that makes energy
FOXRED1.basis: Required for the assembly of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I)

FRAS1.job: helps attach the skin's outer layer to the thin sheet beneath it during development
FRAS1.basis: Required for the regulation of epidermal-basement membrane adhesion responsible for proper organogenesis during embryonic development

FRMPD4.job: helps shape the tiny branches where brain cells receive signals
FRMPD4.basis: Positive regulator of dendritic spine morphogenesis and density. Required for the maintenance of excitatory synaptic transmission

FRRS1L.job: helps tune the signals brain cells use to talk to each other
FRRS1L.basis: Important modulator of glutamate signaling pathway
FRRS1L.alt: helps tune glutamate signals that brain cells use to talk to each other

FTL.job: stores iron safely inside cells until the body needs it
FTL.basis: Stores iron in a soluble, non-toxic, readily available form

FTSJ1.job: tags the cell's protein-building helpers so proteins get made accurately
FTSJ1.basis: Methylates the 2'-O-ribose of nucleotides at positions 32 and 34 of the tRNA anticodon loop of substrate tRNAs ... Requisite for faithful cytoplasmic translation

FUCA1.job: helps break down sugar chains by trimming off a sugar called fucose
FUCA1.basis: Alpha-L-fucosidase is responsible for hydrolyzing the alpha-1,6-linked fucose joined to the reducing-end N-acetylglucosamine of the carbohydrate moieties of glycoproteins

FUS.job: helps cells process and move the RNA copies of their genes
FUS.basis: DNA/RNA-binding protein that plays a role in various cellular processes such as transcription regulation, RNA splicing, RNA transport

FUT8.job: adds a sugar called fucose to sugar chains on proteins, including antibodies
FUT8.basis: Catalyzes the addition of fucose in alpha 1-6 linkage to the first GlcNAc residue, next to the peptide chains in N-glycans ... attached on the fragment crystallizable (Fc) of IgGs

FXN.job: helps the cell's power plants build tiny iron-sulfur parts that many proteins need
FXN.basis: component of the core iron-sulfur cluster (ISC) assembly complex and participates to the [2Fe-2S] cluster assembly ... the first step of the mitochondrial iron-sulfur protein biogenesis

FZD4.job: picks up signals that help blood vessels grow in the eye's retina
FZD4.basis: Receptor for Wnt proteins ... Plays a critical role in retinal vascularization by acting as a receptor for Wnt proteins and norrin (NDP)

G6PC1.job: releases stored sugar into the blood to keep blood sugar steady
G6PC1.basis: Hydrolyzes glucose-6-phosphate to glucose ... the complex responsible for glucose production in the terminal step of glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis ... the key enzyme in homeostatic regulation of blood glucose levels

G6PC3.job: turns a stored form of sugar back into plain glucose inside cells
G6PC3.basis: Hydrolyzes glucose-6-phosphate to glucose in the endoplasmic reticulum ... responsible for glucose production

G6PD.job: helps cells turn sugar into the building blocks for fats and DNA
G6PD.basis: The main function of this enzyme is to provide reducing power (NADPH) and pentose phosphates for fatty acid and nucleic acid synthesis ... dissimilation of carbohydrates

GAA.job: breaks down stored sugar inside the cell's recycling centers
GAA.basis: Essential for the degradation of glycogen in lysosomes

GABRA1.job: is part of a channel that calms brain cells, slowing their signals
GABRA1.basis: Alpha subunit of the heteropentameric ligand-gated chloride channel gated by Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), a major inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain ... Chloride influx into the postsynaptic neuron following GABAAR opening decreases the neuron ability to generate a new action potential, thereby reducing nerve transmission

GABRB2.job: is part of a channel that calms brain cells by slowing their signals
GABRB2.basis: Beta subunit of the heteropentameric ligand-gated chloride channel gated by gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), a major inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain ... Chloride influx into the postsynaptic neuron following GABAAR opening decreases the neuron ability to generate a new action potential, thereby reducing nerve transmission

GABRB3.job: is part of a channel that calms brain cells by letting chloride in
GABRB3.basis: Beta subunit of the heteropentameric ligand-gated chloride channel gated by gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), a major inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain ... Chloride influx into the postsynaptic neuron following GABAAR opening decreases the neuron ability to generate a new action potential, thereby reducing nerve transmission

GABRG2.job: is part of a channel that calms nerve cells in the brain
GABRG2.basis: Gamma subunit of the heteropentameric ligand-gated chloride channel gated by gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), a major inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain ... Chloride influx into the postsynaptic neuron following GABAAR opening decreases the neuron ability to generate a new action potential, thereby reducing nerve transmission

GAD1.job: makes GABA, a chemical messenger that calms brain activity
GAD1.basis: Catalyzes the synthesis of the inhibitory neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)

GALC.job: helps the cell's recycling centers break down a fat found in nerve insulation
GALC.basis: Lysosomal hydrolase that removes the terminal galactose from galactosylceramide, a major lipid of the myelin sheath

GALE.job: helps the body turn galactose, a milk sugar, into usable glucose
GALE.basis: the reversible epimerization of UDP-glucose to UDP-galactose ... plays a critical role in the Leloir pathway of galactose catabolism in which galactose is converted to the glycolytic intermediate glucose 6-phosphate. It contributes to the catabolism of dietary galactose

GALK1.job: helps the body break down galactose, a sugar found in milk
GALK1.basis: Catalyzes the transfer of a phosphate from ATP to alpha-D-galactose and participates in the first committed step in the catabolism of galactose

GALM.job: helps the body use galactose, a sugar from milk, by reshaping it
GALM.basis: Mutarotase that catalyzes the interconversion of beta-D-galactose and alpha-D-galactose during galactose metabolism ... Beta-D-galactose is metabolized in the liver into glucose 1-phosphate, the primary metabolic fuel

GALNS.job: helps the cell's recycling centers break down long sugar chains
GALNS.basis: Lysosomal enzyme that hydrolyzes sulfate groups from glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), keratan sulfate (KS) and chondroitin-6-sulfate (C6S)

GALNT2.job: starts attaching sugar chains to proteins, including ones that handle blood fats
GALNT2.basis: Catalyzes the initial reaction in O-linked oligosaccharide biosynthesis, the transfer of an N-acetyl-D-galactosamine residue to a serine or threonine residue on the protein receptor ... Involved in O-linked glycosylation of APOC-III, ANGPTL3 and PLTP

GALNT3.job: attaches the first sugar that starts sugar chains on other proteins
GALNT3.basis: Catalyzes the initial reaction in O-linked oligosaccharide biosynthesis, the transfer of an N-acetyl-D-galactosamine residue to a serine or threonine residue on the protein receptor

GAMT.job: makes creatine, a molecule that helps store energy in muscles and the brain

GAN.job: helps keep the internal scaffolding of nerve cells in good shape
GAN.basis: plays an important role in neurofilament architecture ... is critical for neuronal maintenance and survival

GANAB.job: trims sugars off newly made proteins so they can mature properly
GANAB.basis: cleaves sequentially the 2 innermost alpha-1,3-linked glucose residues from the Glc(2)Man(9)GlcNAc(2) oligosaccharide precursor of immature glycoproteins ... Required for PKD1/Polycystin-1 and PKD2/Polycystin-2 maturation

GARS1.job: loads the amino acid glycine onto its carrier so cells can build proteins
GARS1.basis: Catalyzes the ATP-dependent ligation of glycine to the 3'-end of its cognate tRNA

GATA1.job: switches on the genes that turn young cells into red blood cells
GATA1.basis: Transcriptional activator or repressor which serves as a general switch factor for erythroid development ... binds to DNA sites ... within regulatory regions of globin genes and of other genes expressed in erythroid cells

GATA2.job: switches on genes in the cells lining blood vessels
GATA2.basis: Transcriptional activator which regulates endothelin-1 gene expression in endothelial cells
GATA2.alt: switches on genes in the cells that line blood vessels

GATA3.job: switches on genes that help certain immune cells develop
GATA3.basis: Transcriptional activator which binds to the enhancer of the T-cell receptor alpha and delta genes ... Required for the T-helper 2 (Th2) differentiation process following immune and inflammatory responses

GATA4.job: switches on genes that build and run the heart
GATA4.basis: Transcriptional activator that binds to the consensus sequence 5'-AGATAG-3' and plays a key role in cardiac development and function ... promotes cardiomyocyte gene expression

GATA6.job: switches on genes that shape the heart, stomach lining and skin's oil glands
GATA6.basis: Transcriptional activator ... Involved in gene regulation specifically in the gastric epithelium ... Involved in bone morphogenetic protein (BMP)-mediated cardiac-specific gene expression ... Triggers ductal and sebaceous differentiation

GATAD2B.job: helps repack DNA to switch certain genes off
GATAD2B.basis: Transcriptional repressor ... Acts as a component of the histone deacetylase NuRD complex which participates in the remodeling of chromatin

GATM.job: starts making creatine, a fuel store for muscles, heart and brain
GATM.basis: Catalyzes the rate-limiting step of creatine biosynthesis ... Provides creatine as a source for ATP generation in tissues with high energy demands, in particular skeletal muscle, heart and brain

GBA1.job: helps the cell's recycling centers break down a sugar-coated fat
GBA1.basis: catalyzes, within the lysosomal compartment, the hydrolysis of glucosylceramides/GlcCers ... into free ceramides ... and glucose ... Plays a central role in the degradation of complex lipids and the turnover of cellular membranes

GBA2.job: breaks down sugar-coated fats in cell membranes, outside the cell's recycling centers
GBA2.basis: Non-lysosomal glucosylceramidase that catalyzes the hydrolysis of glucosylceramides/GlcCers ... to free glucose and ceramides ... GlcCers are membrane glycosphingolipids

GBE1.job: adds branches to glycogen, the body's stored form of sugar
GBE1.basis: Glycogen-branching enzyme participates in the glycogen biosynthetic process ... Generates alpha-1,6-glucosidic branches from alpha-1,4-linked glucose chains

GCDH.job: helps the body break down three amino acids from food
GCDH.basis: degradative pathway of L-lysine, L-hydroxylysine, and L-tryptophan metabolism

GCH1.job: helps blood vessel cells make nitric oxide
GCH1.basis: Positively regulates nitric oxide synthesis in umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). May be involved in dopamine synthesis.
GCH1.alt: helps blood vessel cells make nitric oxide and may help make dopamine

GCK.job: senses blood sugar levels so the pancreas releases the right amount of insulin
GCK.basis: GCK acts as a glucose sensor in the pancreatic beta cell ... In pancreas, plays an important role in modulating insulin secretion

GCSH.job: helps break down the amino acid glycine
GCSH.basis: The glycine cleavage system catalyzes the degradation of glycine. The H protein (GCSH) shuttles the methylamine group of glycine

GDAP1.job: helps split the cell's energy-making mitochondria into smaller pieces
GDAP1.basis: Regulates the mitochondrial network by promoting mitochondrial fission

GDF2.job: travels in the blood and keeps new blood vessels from growing too much
GDF2.basis: Potent circulating inhibitor of angiogenesis ... Signaling through SMAD1 in endothelial cells

GEMIN5.job: helps build the cell's machinery that edits gene messages before they're used
GEMIN5.basis: The SMN complex catalyzes the assembly of small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs), the building blocks of the spliceosome, and thereby plays an important role in the splicing of cellular pre-mRNAs ... Within the SMN complex, GEMIN5 recognizes and delivers the small nuclear RNAs (snRNAs) to the SMN complex

GFAP.job: forms internal support fibers in star-shaped support cells of the brain
GFAP.basis: GFAP, a class-III intermediate filament, is a cell-specific marker that ... distinguishes astrocytes from other glial cells

GFER.job: helps proteins fold into shape inside the cell's power plants
GFER.basis: regenerates the redox-active disulfide bonds in CHCHD4/MIA40, a chaperone essential for disulfide bond formation and protein folding in the mitochondrial intermembrane space

GFI1B.job: switches genes on or off to help red blood cells and platelet-making cells develop
GFI1B.basis: Essential proto-oncogenic transcriptional regulator necessary for development and differentiation of erythroid and megakaryocytic lineages ... Transcriptional repressor or activator

GFPT1.job: starts the process that turns glucose into building blocks for sugar tags on proteins
GFPT1.basis: Rate-limiting enzyme of the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway (HBP) that catalyzes the formation of glucosamine-6-phosphate from fructose-6-phosphate and glutamine, thereby controlling the flux of glucose into this pathway ... regulates the availability of precursors for N- and O-linked protein glycosylation

GGCX.job: uses vitamin K to switch on blood-clotting and bone proteins
GGCX.basis: Mediates the vitamin K-dependent carboxylation of glutamate residues to calcium-binding gamma-carboxyglutamate (Gla) residues ... Catalyzes gamma-carboxylation of blood coagulation factors (F2, F7, F9 and F10) ... Catalyzes gamma-carboxylation of osteocalcin/BGLAP, which is essential for bone metabolism

GIGYF1.job: helps cells respond to growth signals
GIGYF1.basis: May act cooperatively with GRB10 to regulate tyrosine kinase receptor signaling. May increase IGF1 receptor phosphorylation under IGF1 stimulation
GIGYF1.alt: helps cells respond to insulin-like growth signals

GIPC3.job: helps the inner ear's sound-sensing hair cells mature and survive
GIPC3.basis: Required for postnatal maturation of the hair bundle and long-term survival of hair cells and spiral ganglion

GJB1.job: forms tiny tunnels that let small molecules pass between neighboring cells
GJB1.basis: pairs of transmembrane channels, the connexons, through which materials of low MW diffuse from one cell to a neighboring cell
GJB1.alt: forms channels that let small molecules pass directly between neighboring cells

GJB2.job: forms tiny channels that let small molecules pass between neighboring cells
GJB2.basis: Structural component of gap junctions ... Gap junctions are dodecameric channels that connect the cytoplasm of adjoining cells ... Small molecules and ions diffuse from one cell to a neighboring cell via the central pore

GJB3.job: forms channels that let small molecules pass between skin and inner ear cells
GJB3.basis: transmembrane channels, the connexons, through which materials of low MW diffuse from one cell to a neighboring cell
GJB3.alt: forms tiny channels that let small molecules pass between neighboring cells

GJB6.job: forms tiny tunnels that let small molecules pass between neighboring cells
GJB6.basis: transmembrane channels, the connexons, through which materials of low MW diffuse from one cell to a neighboring cell
GJB6.alt: forms tiny channels that let small molecules pass between neighboring cells

GJC2.job: is thought to help insulate nerve fibers in the brain
GJC2.basis: One gap junction consists of a cluster of closely packed pairs of transmembrane channels ... through which materials of low MW diffuse from one cell to a neighboring cell. May play a role in myelination in central and peripheral nervous systems
GJC2.alt: forms channels between neighboring cells and may help insulate nerve fibers

GK.job: helps the body use glycerol, a building block of fats, for energy and fat-making
GK.basis: plays a key role in glycerol metabolism ... the synthesis of glycerolipids and triglycerides, glycogenesis, glycolysis and gluconeogenesis

GLA.job: helps the cell's recycling centers break down certain fatty molecules
GLA.basis: Catalyzes the hydrolysis of glycosphingolipids and participates in their degradation in the lysosome

GLB1.job: trims sugar pieces off fatty and sugar-coated molecules so they can be broken down
GLB1.basis: Cleaves beta-linked terminal galactosyl residues from gangliosides, glycoproteins, and glycosaminoglycans

GLDC.job: helps break down glycine, an amino acid, inside cells
GLDC.basis: The glycine cleavage system catalyzes the degradation of glycine. The P protein (GLDC) binds the alpha-amino group of glycine

GLDN.job: helps build the gaps along insulated nerve fibers that speed up nerve signals
GLDN.basis: plays a role in the formation and maintenance of the nodes of Ranvier on myelinated axons ... Nodes of Ranvier contain clustered sodium channels that are crucial for the saltatory propagation of action potentials along myelinated axons

GLI3.job: switches genes on or off to shape the brain and limbs as they form
GLI3.basis: Transcription factor that acts as a key effector of the smoothened signaling pathway, and which plays a role in the development and patterning of various body structures, including the brain and limbs ... to activate or repress the expression of target genes

GLS.job: breaks down the amino acid glutamine, helping balance body acid and brain signals
GLS.basis: Catalyzes the first reaction in the primary pathway for the renal catabolism of glutamine. Plays a role in maintaining acid-base homeostasis. Regulates the levels of the neurotransmitter glutamate

GLUD1.job: turns the amino acid glutamate into fuel for the cell's energy factories
GLUD1.basis: Mitochondrial glutamate dehydrogenase that catalyzes the conversion of L-glutamate into alpha-ketoglutarate ... an important intermediate in the tricarboxylic acid cycle

GM2A.job: helps the cell's recycling centers break down a fatty molecule found in nerve cells
GM2A.basis: Lipid-binding and transfer protein essential for lysosomal degradation of ganglioside GM2 ... Extracts single GM2 molecules from intralysosomal luminal vesicle (ILV) membranes and presents them in soluble form to beta-hexosaminidase A (HEXA) for cleavage

GMPPA.job: keeps the supply of a sugar building block, used to coat proteins, in check
GMPPA.basis: Regulatory subunit of the GMPPA-GMPPB mannose-1-phosphate guanylyltransferase complex; reduces the catalytic activity of GMPPB ... Together with GMPPB regulates GDP-alpha-D-mannose levels

GMPPB.job: makes a building block the body uses to attach sugar chains to proteins and fats
GMPPB.basis: Catalyzes the formation of GDP-mannose, an essential precursor of glycan moieties of glycoproteins and glycolipids

GNAI1.job: relays messages from the cell's surface inward, acting as an on-off switch
GNAI1.basis: function as transducers downstream of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) in numerous signaling cascades ... alternates between an active, GTP-bound state and an inactive, GDP-bound state

GNAO1.job: relays signals inside brain cells to quiet the release of chemical messengers
GNAO1.basis: function as transducers downstream of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) in numerous signaling cascades, such as regulation of postsynaptic neurotransmitter release ... Plays a key role in postsynaptic inhibition of neurotransmitter release

GNAT1.job: passes light signals along inside the eye's dim-light sensing cells
GNAT1.basis: transduces signals from the G protein-coupled photoreceptor rhodopsin (RHO). Essential for normal RHO-mediated light perception in retinal rod photoreceptors ... Under dim light conditions

GNAT2.job: passes on light signals inside the eye's color-sensing cone cells
GNAT2.basis: transduces signals from the G protein-coupled cone photoreceptors (blue, green and red cones) ... to mediate the phototransduction cascade

GNE.job: starts making sialic acid, a sugar that coats the outside of cells
GNE.basis: serves as the initiator of the biosynthetic pathway leading to the production of N-acetylneuraminic acid (NeuAc), a critical precursor in the synthesis of sialic acids ... Sialic acids represent a category of negatively charged sugars that reside on the surface of cells

GNPAT.job: starts making plasmalogens, a special kind of fat found in cell membranes
GNPAT.basis: catalyzing the first step in the biosynthesis of plasmalogens, a subset of phospholipids ... membrane biology

GNPTAB.job: adds address tags that send digestive enzymes to the cell's recycling centers
GNPTAB.basis: Catalyzes the formation of mannose 6-phosphate (M6P) markers ... which mediate the vesicular transport of lysosomal enzymes to the endosomal/prelysosomal compartment

GNPTG.job: helps tag enzymes with an address label that sends them to the cell's recycling centers
GNPTG.basis: Non-catalytic subunit of the N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphotransferase complex, an enzyme that catalyzes the formation of mannose 6-phosphate (M6P) markers on high mannose type oligosaccharides ... Enhances the rate of N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate transfer to the oligosaccharides of acid hydrolase acceptors

GNS.job: helps break down long sugar chains by snipping off sulfate groups
GNS.basis: Hydrolyzes 6-sulfate groups in N-acetyl-d-glucosaminide units of heparin sulfate and keratan sulfate

GORAB.job: helps the cell's packaging center add sugars to proteins that support tissues
GORAB.basis: Plays a role in the organization and function of the Golgi apparatus. Involved in protein post-translational modification, particularly glycosylation of extracellular matrix proteins

GOSR2.job: helps move proteins through the cell's packaging and shipping center
GOSR2.basis: Involved in transport of proteins from the cis/medial-Golgi to the trans-Golgi network

GP1BA.job: helps platelets stick to injured blood vessel walls to plug leaks
GP1BA.basis: a surface membrane protein of platelets, participates in the formation of platelet plugs by binding to the A1 domain of vWF, which is already bound to the subendothelium

GP1BB.job: helps platelets stick to injured blood vessel walls to plug wounds
GP1BB.basis: Gp-Ib, a surface membrane protein of platelets, participates in the formation of platelet plugs by binding to von Willebrand factor, which is already bound to the subendothelium

GP6.job: lets platelets grab onto collagen at injuries to start blood clotting
GP6.basis: Collagen receptor involved in collagen-induced platelet adhesion and activation. Plays a key role in platelet procoagulant activity and subsequent thrombin and fibrin formation

GP9.job: is part of a receptor that lets platelets stick to injured blood vessels
GP9.basis: The GPIb-V-IX complex functions as the vWF receptor and mediates vWF-dependent platelet adhesion to blood vessels ... The adhesion of platelets to injured vascular surfaces

GPAA1.job: helps attach proteins to fatty anchors that hold them on the cell surface
GPAA1.basis: Component of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchor (GPI-anchor) transamidase (GPI-T) complex that catalyzes the formation of the linkage between a proprotein and a GPI-anchor and participates in GPI anchored protein biosynthesis

GPC3.job: sits on the cell surface and tunes growth signals that shape the developing body
GPC3.basis: Cell surface proteoglycan ... Negatively regulates the hedgehog signaling pathway ... Positively regulates the canonical Wnt signaling pathway ... Plays a role in limb patterning and skeletal development ... Modulates the effects of growth factors

GPR143.job: helps pigment cells build and move the packets that hold their pigment
GPR143.basis: Receptor for tyrosine, L-DOPA and dopamine ... involved in melanosome biogenesis, organization and transport

GPR161.job: keeps a key growth signal switched off in the cell's antenna until needed
GPR161.basis: acts as a key inhibitor of the smoothened signaling pathway in primary cilia ... Inhibits the smoothened signaling pathway in absence of hedgehog ... Involved in regulation of the smoothened signaling pathway during early neural tube development, forelimb formation, skeletal development

GPSM2.job: helps dividing cells line up and split in the right direction
GPSM2.basis: Plays an important role in mitotic spindle pole organization ... Plays a role in metaphase spindle orientation ... Also plays an important role in asymmetric cell divisions

GPT2.job: swaps parts between amino acids, helping the body make and use them for energy
GPT2.basis: Catalyzes the reversible transamination between alanine and 2-oxoglutarate to form pyruvate and glutamate

GREM1.job: blocks growth signals that shape developing limbs and kidneys
GREM1.basis: metanephric kidney organogenesis, as a BMP antagonist required for early limb outgrowth and patterning ... Down-regulates the BMP4 signaling

GRHL2.job: switches on genes that help form the neural tube and build linings and skin
GRHL2.basis: Transcription factor playing an important role in primary neurulation and in epithelial development ... acting as an activator and repressor on distinct target genes

GRHL3.job: switches on genes that build the skin's protective barrier and close the developing spine
GRHL3.basis: Transcription factor playing important roles in primary neurulation and in the differentiation of stratified epithelia ... essential to form the epidermal barrier ... Essential for spinal closure

GRIA2.job: helps brain cells pass fast signals to each other
GRIA2.basis: L-glutamate acts as an excitatory neurotransmitter at many synapses in the central nervous system and plays an important role in fast excitatory synaptic transmission ... converts the chemical signal to an electrical impulse

GRIA3.job: helps brain cells pass fast signals to each other
GRIA3.basis: Ionotropic glutamate receptor that functions as a ligand-gated cation channel ... plays an important role in fast excitatory synaptic transmission ... converts the chemical signal to an electrical impulse

GRIK2.job: helps brain cells pass on signals by turning a chemical messenger into an electrical one
GRIK2.basis: Ionotropic glutamate receptor that functions as a cation-permeable ligand-gated ion channel ... L-glutamate acts as an excitatory neurotransmitter at many synapses in the central nervous system ... converting the chemical signal to an electrical impulse

GRIN1.job: helps brain cells signal each other for learning and memory
GRIN1.basis: Component of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors (NMDARs) that function as heterotetrameric, ligand-gated cation channels ... NMDARs participate in synaptic plasticity for learning and memory formation

GRIN2B.job: helps brain cells signal each other for learning and memory
GRIN2B.basis: Component of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors (NMDARs) that function as heterotetrameric, ligand-gated cation channels ... Participates in synaptic plasticity for learning and memory formation

GRIN2D.job: helps brain cells signal each other for learning and memory
GRIN2D.basis: Component of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors (NMDARs) that function as heterotetrameric, ligand-gated cation channels ... Participates in synaptic plasticity for learning and memory formation

GRIP1.job: helps nerve cells move signal receivers to the right spots
GRIP1.basis: localized scaffold for the assembly of a multiprotein signaling complex and as mediator of the trafficking of its binding partners at specific subcellular location in neurons ... controls the intracellular fate of AMPAR and the endosomal sorting of the GRIA2 subunit toward recycling and membrane targeting

GRK1.job: switches off the eye's light sensor after it catches light, so vision resets
GRK1.basis: Retina-specific kinase involved in the regulation of phototransduction, playing a key role in terminating the light-activated rhodopsin (RHO) signal in rod photoreceptors ... permits rapid adaptation to changes in illumination

GRM6.job: picks up the messenger glutamate to help the eye pass on light signals
GRM6.basis: G protein-coupled receptor for glutamate ... Required for normal vision

GRN.job: helps run the cell's recycling centers and helps wounds heal
GRN.basis: acts as a key regulator of lysosomal function and as a growth factor involved in inflammation, wound healing and cell proliferation

GRXCR1.job: helps shape the tiny sensing hairs of the inner ear as they develop
GRXCR1.basis: May play a role in actin filament architecture in developing stereocilia of sensory cells
GRXCR1.alt: may help shape the inner ear's sound-sensing hairs as they develop

GSDME.job: punches holes in a cell's outer membrane when the cell is told to die
GSDME.basis: Precursor of a pore-forming protein that converts non-inflammatory apoptosis to pyroptosis ... upon cleavage, the released N-terminal moiety (Gasdermin-E, N-terminal) binds to membranes and forms pores, triggering pyroptosis

GSS.job: makes glutathione, a molecule that protects cells from damage
GSS.basis: Catalyzes the production of glutathione ... required for numerous processes including the protection of cells against oxidative damage

GTPBP2.job: helps restart the cell's protein-making machinery when it gets stuck
GTPBP2.basis: Involved in the rescue of ribosome stalling due to the presence of non-functional tRNA

GTPBP3.job: helps the cell's power plants build their own proteins
GTPBP3.basis: catalyzes the 5-taurinomethyluridine (taum(5)U) modification at the 34th wobble position (U34) of mitochondrial tRNAs (mt-tRNAs), which plays a role in mt-tRNA decoding and mitochondrial translation
GTPBP3.alt: chemically tunes molecules that help the cell's power plants build their own proteins

GUCA1A.job: helps the eye's light-sensing cells reset after seeing light
GUCA1A.basis: This regulation is a key event in recovery of the dark state of both cone and rod photoreceptors following light exposure

GUCY2D.job: helps the eye's light-sensing cells reset after catching light
GUCY2D.basis: Catalyzes the synthesis of cyclic GMP (cGMP) in cone and rod photoreceptors, playing an essential role in phototransduction. Restores cytoplasmic cGMP levels, thereby returning photoreceptor cells to their dark-adapted state

GUSB.job: helps break down long sugar chains so cells can recycle them
GUSB.basis: Plays an important role in the degradation of dermatan and keratan sulfates

GYG1.job: starts the sugar chains the body builds into glycogen, its stored fuel
GYG1.basis: Glycogenin participates in the glycogen biosynthetic process ... these chains act as primers for the elongation reaction catalyzed by glycogen synthase

GYS1.job: builds glycogen, the sugar store that fuels muscles
GYS1.basis: Glycogen synthase participates in the glycogen biosynthetic process ... Extends the primer composed of a few glucose units formed by glycogenin by adding new glucose units to it
GYS1.alt: links sugar units into glycogen, the body's stored form of sugar

GYS2.job: builds glycogen, the liver's stored sugar, by linking glucose units into long chains
GYS2.basis: Glycogen synthase participates in the glycogen biosynthetic process ... Extends the primer composed of a few glucose units formed by glycogenin by adding new glucose units to it
GYS2.alt: links sugar units into glycogen, the body's stored sugar

H1-4.job: helps pack DNA tightly into compact coils inside the cell's nucleus
H1-4.basis: binds to linker DNA between nucleosomes forming the macromolecular structure known as the chromatin fiber ... necessary for the condensation of nucleosome chains into higher-order structured fibers

H3-3A.job: helps package DNA, especially around genes that are switched on
H3-3A.basis: Variant histone H3 which replaces conventional H3 in a wide range of nucleosomes in active genes ... Nucleosomes wrap and compact DNA into chromatin

H4C5.job: helps wrap and pack DNA into tight bundles inside the cell
H4C5.basis: Core component of nucleosome. Nucleosomes wrap and compact DNA into chromatin

HAAO.job: helps the body break down tryptophan, an amino acid from food
HAAO.basis: Catalyzes the oxidative ring opening of 3-hydroxyanthranilate to 2-amino-3-carboxymuconate semialdehyde, which spontaneously cyclizes to quinolinate

HACD1.job: helps cells make extra-long fats used to build cell membranes
HACD1.basis: long-chain fatty acids elongation cycle ... allows the addition of two carbons to the chain of long- and very long-chain fatty acids/VLCFAs per cycle ... participates in the production of VLCFAs ... as precursors of membrane lipids

HADH.job: helps cells burn short and medium-length fats for energy
HADH.basis: Mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation enzyme that catalyzes the third step of the beta-oxidation cycle for medium and short-chain 3-hydroxy fatty acyl-CoAs

HADHA.job: helps cells break down long fat molecules for energy
HADHA.basis: Mitochondrial trifunctional enzyme catalyzes the last three of the four reactions of the mitochondrial beta-oxidation pathway ... The mitochondrial beta-oxidation pathway is the major energy-producing process in tissues ... shows specificity for long-chain fatty acids, such as those from dietary and stored fats

HADHB.job: helps cells break down long-chain fats for energy
HADHB.basis: Mitochondrial trifunctional enzyme catalyzes the last three of the four reactions of the mitochondrial beta-oxidation pathway ... The mitochondrial beta-oxidation pathway is the major energy-producing process in tissues ... shows specificity for long-chain fatty acids, such as those from dietary and stored fats

HAMP.job: is a liver hormone that controls how much iron the body absorbs and releases
HAMP.basis: Liver-produced hormone that constitutes the main circulating regulator of iron absorption and distribution across tissues ... Controls the major flows of iron into plasma: absorption of dietary iron in the intestine ... and mobilization of stored iron from hepatocytes

HBA1.job: forms the alpha chains of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen from the lungs to the body
HBA1.basis: Involved in oxygen transport from the lung to the various peripheral tissues
HBA1.alt: carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body

HBA2.job: forms the alpha chain of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen from the lungs to the body
HBA2.basis: Involved in oxygen transport from the lung to the various peripheral tissues
HBA2.alt: carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body

HBB.job: forms the beta half of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen from the lungs to the body
HBB.basis: Involved in oxygen transport from the lung to the various peripheral tissues
HBB.alt: carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body

HCFC1.job: helps bring together proteins that switch genes on or off, including cell-division genes
HCFC1.basis: Transcriptional coregulator ... Serves as a scaffold protein, bridging interactions between transcription factors ... and transcriptional coregulators ... Involved in control of the cell cycle

HCN1.job: lets sodium and potassium into cells to set the rhythm of heart and nerve signals
HCN1.basis: Hyperpolarization-activated ion channel that are permeable to sodium and potassium ions ... Contributes to the native pacemaker currents in heart (If) and in the generation of the I(h) current which controls neuron excitability

HCN2.job: lets sodium and potassium into cells to help set the heartbeat and nerve rhythms
HCN2.basis: Hyperpolarization-activated ion channel that is permeable to sodium and potassium ions ... Contributes to the native pacemaker currents in heart (If) and in neurons (Ih)

HCN4.job: lets charged particles into heart cells to help set the heartbeat's rhythm
HCN4.basis: ion channel that are permeable to Na(+) and K(+) ions ... Contributes to the native pacemaker currents in heart (If) that regulate the rhythm of heart beat

HDAC8.job: removes chemical tags from DNA's packaging proteins to help switch genes off
HDAC8.basis: Histone deacetylase that catalyzes the deacetylation of lysine residues on the N-terminal part of the core histones ... Histone deacetylation gives a tag for epigenetic repression and plays an important role in transcriptional regulation

HECW2.job: tags another protein to keep it stable and help it switch genes on
HECW2.basis: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that mediates ubiquitination of TP73. Acts to stabilize TP73 and enhance activation of transcription by TP73

HEPACAM.job: helps brain support cells place a salt channel that keeps nerves balanced
HEPACAM.basis: In glia, associates and targets CLCN2 at astrocytic processes and myelinated fiber tracts where it may regulate transcellular chloride flux involved in neuron excitability

HEXA.job: helps break down certain fatty sugar molecules, especially in nerve cells
HEXA.basis: Hydrolyzes the non-reducing end N-acetyl-D-hexosamine ... of glycoconjugates, such as the oligosaccharide moieties from proteins and neutral glycolipids ... Only the isozyme A is responsible for the degradation of GM2 gangliosides

HEXB.job: helps break down sugar-coated fats and proteins so cells can recycle them
HEXB.basis: Hydrolyzes the non-reducing end N-acetyl-D-hexosamine and/or sulfated N-acetyl-D-hexosamine of glycoconjugates, such as the oligosaccharide moieties from proteins and neutral glycolipids

HFE.job: helps control how much iron cells take in from the blood
HFE.basis: Binds to transferrin receptor (TFR) and reduces its affinity for iron-loaded transferrin

HGSNAT.job: helps the cell's recycling centers break down long sugar chains
HGSNAT.basis: Lysosomal acetyltransferase that acetylates the non-reducing terminal alpha-glucosamine residue of intralysosomal heparin or heparan sulfate, converting it into a substrate for luminal alpha-N-acetyl glucosaminidase

HIBCH.job: helps the body break down valine, an amino acid from food
HIBCH.basis: Hydrolyzes 3-hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA (HIBYL-CoA), a saline catabolite ... functions in valine catabolism

HIKESHI.job: carries heat-protective proteins into the cell's control center during heat stress
HIKESHI.basis: Acts as a specific nuclear import carrier for HSP70 proteins following heat-shock stress ... HSP70 proteins import is required to protect cells from heat shock damages

HINT1.job: breaks down small energy-molecule leftovers and helps control which genes switch on
HINT1.basis: Exhibits adenosine 5'-monophosphoramidase activity, hydrolyzing purine nucleotide phosphoramidates ... to yield AMP and NH2 ... functions as scaffolding protein that modulates transcriptional activation by the LEF1/TCF1-CTNNB1 complex

HJV.job: helps control how much iron the body takes in and stores
HJV.basis: Through enhancement of BMP signaling regulates hepcidin (HAMP) expression and regulates iron homeostasis

HLCS.job: attaches the vitamin biotin to enzymes that process fats, sugars and amino acids
HLCS.basis: Biotin--protein ligase catalyzing the biotinylation of the 4 biotin-dependent carboxylases acetyl-CoA-carboxylase, pyruvate carboxylase, propionyl-CoA carboxylase, and methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase

HMBS.job: helps make heme, the iron-holding part of blood that carries oxygen
HMBS.basis: As part of the heme biosynthetic pathway, catalyzes the sequential polymerization of four molecules of porphobilinogen to form hydroxymethylbilane

HMGA2.job: helps switch on genes that drive growth
HMGA2.basis: Functions as a transcriptional regulator ... Positively regulates IGF2 expression

HMGCL.job: helps make ketones, a backup fuel the body uses when sugar runs low
HMGCL.basis: a key step in ketogenesis ... Ketone bodies (beta-hydroxybutyrate, acetoacetate and acetone) are essential as an alternative source of energy to glucose

HMGCS2.job: helps the body make ketones, a backup fuel made from fat
HMGCS2.basis: Catalyzes the first irreversible step in ketogenesis

HMOX1.job: breaks down heme, the iron-holding part of blood, freeing its iron
HMOX1.basis: Catalyzes the oxidative cleavage of heme ... while releasing the central heme iron chelate as ferrous iron ... catabolize free heme

HMX1.job: helps shape the developing face, including the eyes and ears
HMX1.basis: May function as a transcriptional repressor ... May play an important role in the development of craniofacial structures such as the eye and ear

HNF1A.job: switches on genes in the liver and the pancreas's insulin-making cells
HNF1A.basis: Transcriptional activator that regulates the tissue specific expression of multiple genes, especially in pancreatic islet cells and in liver

HNF1B.job: switches on other genes by binding to specific stretches of DNA
HNF1B.basis: Transcription factor that binds to the inverted palindrome 5'-GTTAATNATTAAC-3'

HNF4A.job: switches on genes that help the liver develop
HNF4A.basis: Transcriptional regulator which controls the expression of hepatic genes during the transition of endodermal cells to hepatic progenitor cells

HNRNPD.job: latches onto gene messages to control how long they last before breakdown
HNRNPD.basis: Binds with high affinity to RNA molecules that contain AU-rich elements (AREs) found within the 3'-UTR of many proto-oncogenes and cytokine mRNAs ... May be involved in translationally coupled mRNA turnover

HNRNPDL.job: helps switch genes on or off and binds the messages genes send out
HNRNPDL.basis: Acts as a transcriptional regulator. Promotes transcription repression. Promotes transcription activation ... Binds with high affinity to RNA molecules that contain AU-rich elements (AREs) found within the 3'-UTR of many proto-oncogenes and cytokine mRNAs

HNRNPH1.job: helps edit gene messages so one gene can make different protein versions
HNRNPH1.basis: component of the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein (hnRNP) complexes which provide the substrate for the processing events that pre-mRNAs undergo before becoming functional, translatable mRNAs ... Mediates pre-mRNA alternative splicing regulation

HNRNPH2.job: helps prepare the genetic messages that cells use as recipes for proteins
HNRNPH2.basis: component of the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein (hnRNP) complexes which provide the substrate for the processing events that pre-mRNAs undergo before becoming functional, translatable mRNAs

HNRNPK.job: grabs freshly copied genetic messages and helps process them inside the cell's nucleus
HNRNPK.basis: One of the major pre-mRNA-binding proteins ... Likely to play a role in the nuclear metabolism of hnRNAs

HNRNPR.job: helps process the gene messages that cells use to make proteins
HNRNPR.basis: Component of ribonucleosomes ... hnRNP play an important role in processing of precursor mRNA in the nucleus

HNRNPU.job: grips DNA and RNA to help organize genes and control which are used
HNRNPU.basis: DNA- and RNA-binding protein involved in several cellular processes such as nuclear chromatin organization ... transcription, mRNA alternative splicing and stability

HOGA1.job: helps the body break down hydroxyproline, a building block of collagen
HOGA1.basis: Catalyzes the final step in the metabolic pathway of hydroxyproline

HOXA1.job: switches on genes that shape the brainstem, ears and heart in the embryo
HOXA1.basis: Sequence-specific transcription factor ... Regulates multiple developmental processes including brainstem, inner and outer ear, abducens nerve and cardiovascular development and morphogenesis

HOXA13.job: tells cells where they sit in the growing body so they develop correctly
HOXA13.basis: transcription factor which is part of a developmental regulatory system that provides cells with specific positional identities on the anterior-posterior axis

HPCA.job: senses calcium in brain cells and helps adjust their activity
HPCA.basis: Calcium-binding protein that may play a role in the regulation of voltage-dependent calcium channels
HPCA.alt: senses calcium in brain cells and helps tune their calcium channels

HPD.job: helps the body break down tyrosine, an amino acid from food
HPD.basis: Catalyzes the conversion of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvic acid to homogentisic acid, one of the steps in tyrosine catabolism

HPRT1.job: recycles leftover DNA building blocks so cells can reuse them
HPRT1.basis: Converts guanine to guanosine monophosphate, and hypoxanthine to inosine monophosphate ... Plays a central role in the generation of purine nucleotides through the purine salvage pathway

HPS1.job: is part of a team that helps pigment cells build their melanin-making compartments
HPS1.basis: Component of the BLOC-3 complex ... The BLOC-3 complex plays an important role in the control of melanin production and melanosome biogenesis
HPS1.alt: helps cells build the compartments that make skin and hair pigment

HPS3.job: helps build the cell compartments that make skin, hair and eye pigment
HPS3.basis: Involved in early stages of melanosome biogenesis and maturation

HPS4.job: helps pigment cells make melanin, the pigment in skin, hair and eyes
HPS4.basis: Component of the BLOC-3 complex ... The BLOC-3 complex plays an important role in the control of melanin production and melanosome biogenesis
HPS4.alt: partners with HPS1 to help pigment cells build the compartments that make melanin

HPS5.job: helps cells build storage compartments, like the ones that make skin and eye pigment
HPS5.basis: May regulate the synthesis and function of lysosomes and of highly specialized organelles, such as melanosomes and platelet dense granules

HPS6.job: helps build the cell's recycling centers and pigment-making compartments
HPS6.basis: May regulate the synthesis and function of lysosomes and of highly specialized organelles, such as melanosomes

HRAS.job: relays signals that tell cells to grow, divide and survive
HRAS.basis: Signal transducer in the Ras-MAPK signaling pathway that regulates cell proliferation and survival

HSD11B2.job: switches off the stress hormone cortisol so it can't act like a salt-regulating hormone
HSD11B2.basis: Catalyzes the conversion of biologically active 11beta-hydroxyglucocorticoids (11beta-hydroxysteroid) such as cortisol, to inactive 11-ketoglucocorticoids (11-oxosteroid) such as cortisone ... thus protecting the nonselective mineralocorticoid receptor from occupation by glucocorticoids

HSD17B10.job: helps the cell's power plants break down fats, an amino acid, and some hormones
HSD17B10.basis: Mitochondrial dehydrogenase involved in pathways of fatty acid, branched-chain amino acid and steroid metabolism ... a step in isoleucine degradation pathway ... Has hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activity toward steroid hormones and bile acids

HSD17B4.job: helps break down fats inside the cell's small fat-processing compartments
HSD17B4.basis: Bifunctional enzyme acting on the peroxisomal fatty acid beta-oxidation pathway. Catalyzes two of the four reactions in fatty acid degradation

HSD3B7.job: helps the liver make bile acids from cholesterol to digest fats
HSD3B7.basis: HSD VII is active against four 7-alpha-hydroxylated sterols ... Involved in bile acid synthesis

HSPB1.job: keeps other proteins from clumping when cells are under stress
HSPB1.basis: Small heat shock protein which functions as a molecular chaperone probably maintaining denatured proteins in a folding-competent state ... Plays a role in stress resistance

HSPB8.job: helps cells clear out worn or damaged proteins, especially in muscle
HSPB8.basis: Involved in the chaperone-assisted selective autophagy (CASA), a crucial process for protein quality control, particularly in mechanical strained cells and tissues such as muscle

HTRA2.job: helps trigger the planned self-destruction of damaged or unneeded cells
HTRA2.basis: Serine protease ... Promotes apoptosis by either relieving the inhibition of BIRC proteins on caspases, leading to an increase in caspase activity

HUWE1.job: tags many other proteins for disposal so the cell can break them down
HUWE1.basis: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase which mediates ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins

HYCC1.job: helps form the cells that wrap nerves in their insulating coating
HYCC1.basis: HYCC1 plays a key role in oligodendrocytes formation ... its importance in myelination of the central and peripheral nervous system

HYDIN.job: helps the cell's hair-like cilia beat and move

IARS2.job: loads the amino acid isoleucine onto its carrier so cells can build proteins
IARS2.basis: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase that catalyzes the specific attachment of isoleucine to its cognate tRNA (tRNA(Ile))

IBA57.job: helps build tiny iron-sulfur parts that power-plant proteins in the cell need to work
IBA57.basis: Mitochondrial protein involved in the maturation of mitochondrial [4Fe-4S]-proteins in the late stage of the iron-sulfur cluster assembly pathway

ICOS.job: boosts immune T cells so they can help make antibodies against germs
ICOS.basis: Stimulatory receptor expressed in activated or antigen-experienced T-cells that plays an important role in the immune response ... delivers costimulatory signals that enhances all basic T-cell responses to a foreign antigen ... Essential both for efficient interaction between T and B-cells and for normal antibody responses

IDH2.job: helps cells turn food into energy inside their power plants
IDH2.basis: Catalyzes the NADP(+)-dependent oxidative decarboxylation of isocitrate (D-threo-isocitrate) to 2-ketoglutarate (2-oxoglutarate), playing a role in intermediary metabolism and energy production

IDS.job: helps the cell's recycling centers break down long sugar chains
IDS.basis: Lysosomal enzyme involved in the degradation pathway of dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate

IFIH1.job: senses virus genetic material inside cells and sounds the immune alarm
IFIH1.basis: Innate immune receptor which acts as a cytoplasmic sensor of viral nucleic acids and plays a major role in sensing viral infection and in the activation of a cascade of antiviral responses

IFNAR1.job: picks up interferon, the body's alarm signal against viruses, to switch on defenses
IFNAR1.basis: Together with IFNAR2, forms the heterodimeric receptor for type I interferons ... resulting in transcriptional activation or repression of interferon-regulated genes that encode the effectors of the interferon response

IFNAR2.job: picks up interferon alarm signals that help cells fight viruses
IFNAR2.basis: Together with IFNAR1, forms the heterodimeric receptor for type I interferons ... Type I interferon binding activates the JAK-STAT signaling cascade, resulting in transcriptional activation or repression of interferon-regulated genes that encode the effectors of the interferon response

IFT122.job: helps move cargo along the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
IFT122.basis: required for retrograde ciliary transport ... it is required in ciliogenesis and ciliary protein trafficking

IFT140.job: moves cargo along the cell's hair-like antennae to build and maintain them
IFT140.basis: Component of the IFT complex A (IFT-A), a complex required for retrograde ciliary transport ... its role in ciliogenesis and/or cilium maintenance

IFT172.job: helps cells build and keep their antenna-like sensing hairs
IFT172.basis: Required for the maintenance and formation of cilia

IFT27.job: helps carry cargo out of the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
IFT27.basis: component of the intraflagellar transport (IFT) complex B that promotes the exit of the BBSome complex from cilia

IFT74.job: carries building blocks into the cell's hair-like antennae to build them
IFT74.basis: forms a tubulin-binding module that specifically mediates transport of tubulin within the cilium ... Required for ciliogenesis

IFT80.job: helps build and maintain the cell's hair-like antennae
IFT80.basis: Component of the intraflagellar transport (IFT) complex B, which is essential for the development and maintenance of motile and sensory cilia

IGF2.job: acts as a growth hormone that helps the baby and placenta grow before birth
IGF2.basis: Major fetal growth hormone in mammals. Plays a key role in regulating fetoplacental development

IGHMBP2.job: unwinds paired strands of RNA and DNA so cells can read them
IGHMBP2.basis: 5' to 3' helicase that unwinds both RNA and DNA duplexes in an ATP-dependent reaction ... May play a role in RNA metabolism, ribosome biogenesis or initiation of translation

IKBKB.job: switches on immune and stress-response genes when cells sense infection or damage
IKBKB.basis: plays an essential role in the NF-kappa-B signaling pathway which is activated by multiple stimuli such as inflammatory cytokines, bacterial or viral products, DNA damages or other cellular stresses ... free NF-kappa-B is translocated into the nucleus and activates the transcription of hundreds of genes involved in immune response

IKBKG.job: helps switch on a master control that turns on the body's defense and survival genes
IKBKG.basis: Regulatory subunit of the IKK core complex which phosphorylates inhibitors of NF-kappa-B thus leading to the dissociation of the inhibitor/NF-kappa-B complex and ultimately the degradation of the inhibitor ... Involved in TLR3- and IFIH1-mediated antiviral innate response

IKZF1.job: switches on genes that guide blood cells, especially immune cells, as they mature
IKZF1.basis: Transcription regulator of hematopoietic cell differentiation ... Plays a role in the development of lymphocytes, B- and T-cells

IL10RA.job: picks up a signal that tells the immune system to calm inflammation
IL10RA.basis: Cell surface receptor for the cytokine IL10 that participates in IL10-mediated anti-inflammatory functions, limiting excessive tissue disruption caused by inflammation

IL10RB.job: picks up immune messengers that calm inflammation and fight viruses
IL10RB.basis: Shared cell surface receptor required for the activation of five class 2 cytokines: IL10, IL22, IL26, IL28, and IFNL1 ... mediates their antiviral activity

IL11RA.job: picks up a signal that guides how skull bones and teeth form
IL11RA.basis: Receptor for interleukin-11 (IL11) ... Essential for the normal development of craniofacial bones and teeth

IL1RAPL1.job: helps nerve cells form connections with each other
IL1RAPL1.basis: May regulate secretion and presynaptic differentiation ... During dendritic spine formation can bidirectionally induce pre- and post-synaptic differentiation of neurons by trans-synaptically binding to PTPRD

IL21R.job: picks up interleukin-21, a chemical message passed between immune cells
IL21R.basis: This is a receptor for interleukin-21

IL2RA.job: picks up a signal that lets peacekeeping immune cells keep immune attacks in check
IL2RA.basis: Receptor for interleukin-2. The receptor is involved in the regulation of immune tolerance by controlling regulatory T cells (TREGs) activity. TREGs suppress the activation and expansion of autoreactive T-cells

IL2RG.job: is a shared part of the receptors that pick up immune system signals
IL2RG.basis: Common subunit for the receptors for a variety of interleukins

IL7R.job: picks up a chemical signal that helps immune cells grow
IL7R.basis: Receptor for interleukin-7. Also acts as a receptor for thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP)

ILDR1.job: helps seal the gaps where cells meet, keeping the inner ear's hearing cells alive
ILDR1.basis: Maintains epithelial barrier function by recruiting MARVELD2/tricellulin to tricellular tight junctions (tTJs) ... Crucial for normal hearing by maintaining the structural and functional integrity of tTJs, which are critical for the survival of auditory neurosensory HCs

IMPDH1.job: helps cells make guanine, one of the building blocks of DNA and RNA
IMPDH1.basis: the first committed and rate-limiting step in the de novo synthesis of guanine nucleotides

IMPG1.job: helps build the scaffold of gel that surrounds the eye's light-sensing cells
IMPG1.basis: May serve to form a basic macromolecular scaffold comprising the insoluble interphotoreceptor matrix

IMPG2.job: helps build the cushioning gel around the eye's light-sensing cells
IMPG2.basis: proteoglycan involved in the organization of interphotoreceptor matrix; may participate in the maturation and maintenance of the light-sensitive photoreceptor outer segment

INF2.job: cuts and reshapes the actin fibers that form a cell's inner scaffold
INF2.basis: Severs actin filaments and accelerates their polymerization and depolymerization

INPP5E.job: trims phosphate tags from membrane fats to help cells build their antenna-like sensing hairs
INPP5E.basis: Phosphatidylinositol (PtdIns) phosphatase that specifically hydrolyzes the 5-phosphate ... Plays an essential role in the primary cilium by controlling ciliary growth

INPPL1.job: turns down insulin and growth signals inside cells by removing a phosphate tag
INPPL1.basis: specifically hydrolyzes the 5-phosphate of phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-trisphosphate ... thereby negatively regulating the PI3K (phosphoinositide 3-kinase) pathways ... Plays a central role in regulation of PI3K-dependent insulin signaling ... Involved in EGF signaling pathway

INS.job: is the hormone that controls blood sugar by moving sugar into cells
INS.basis: Hormone secreted by pancreatic islet beta cells ... the central controller of blood glucose homeostasis ... stimulates glucose uptake into skeletal muscle and adipose tissue

INSR.job: picks up insulin's signal so cells take in sugar from the blood
INSR.basis: Receptor tyrosine kinase which mediates the pleiotropic actions of insulin ... The net effect of this pathway is to produce a translocation of the glucose transporter SLC2A4/GLUT4 from cytoplasmic vesicles to the cell membrane to facilitate glucose transport

INTU.job: helps cells build their antenna-like sensing hairs
INTU.basis: Plays a key role in ciliogenesis and embryonic development. Regulator of cilia formation

INVS.job: helps the kidneys develop and the body set its left and right sides
INVS.basis: Required for normal renal development and establishment of left-right axis

IQCB1.job: helps cells build their antenna-like sensing hairs
IQCB1.basis: Involved in ciliogenesis. The function in an early step in cilia formation

IQSEC2.job: helps brain cells adjust their connections by moving signal receivers at synapses
IQSEC2.basis: Is involved in the regulation of synaptic transmission and plasticity, controlling trafficking and removal of AMPA receptors GRIA2/GLUA2 and GRIA3/GLUA3 at synapses

IRF2BPL.job: tags certain proteins for disposal and helps the brain and nerves develop
IRF2BPL.basis: Probable E3 ubiquitin protein ligase involved in the proteasome-mediated ubiquitin-dependent degradation of target proteins ... Probably plays a role in the development of the central nervous system and in neuronal maintenance

IRF4.job: switches on genes that help immune cells develop and work
IRF4.basis: Transcriptional activator ... specific to lymphoid cells. Involved in CD8(+) dendritic cell differentiation ... in immune cells, leading to ... activation of genes

IRF6.job: switches on genes that tell skin cells to stop dividing and mature
IRF6.basis: Probable DNA-binding transcriptional activator. Key determinant of the keratinocyte proliferation-differentiation switch involved in appropriate epidermal development

ISCA2.job: helps build tiny iron-sulfur parts that power proteins in the cell's energy factories
ISCA2.basis: Involved in the maturation of mitochondrial 4Fe-4S proteins functioning late in the iron-sulfur cluster assembly pathway

ISCU.job: serves as a workbench for building tiny iron-sulfur parts in the cell's power plants
ISCU.basis: Mitochondrial scaffold protein, of the core iron-sulfur cluster (ISC) assembly complex, that provides the structural architecture on which the [2Fe-2S] clusters are assembled

ISL1.job: switches on genes that help the heart, eye nerves and motor nerves develop
ISL1.basis: DNA-binding transcriptional activator ... essential for retinal ganglion cell (RGC) differentiation ... Involved in the specification of motor neurons ... Essential for heart development

ITCH.job: tags other proteins for disposal, helping keep immune and inflammation signals in check
ITCH.basis: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase which accepts ubiquitin from an E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme ... directly transfers the ubiquitin to targeted substrates ... Involved in the control of inflammatory signaling pathways ... ensures the transient nature of inflammatory signaling pathways ... probably plays an important role in the regulation of immune response

ITGA2B.job: helps platelets stick together to plug wounds in blood vessels
ITGA2B.basis: brings about platelet/platelet interaction through binding of soluble fibrinogen ... This step leads to rapid platelet aggregation which physically plugs ruptured endothelial cell surface

ITGA3.job: helps cells grip the supporting framework of proteins around them
ITGA3.basis: Integrin alpha-3/beta-1 is a receptor for fibronectin, laminin, collagen ... may participate in the adhesion

ITGB3.job: helps platelets stick together to plug wounds and stop bleeding
ITGB3.basis: Following activation integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 brings about platelet/platelet interaction through binding of soluble fibrinogen ... This step leads to rapid platelet aggregation which physically plugs ruptured endothelial surface

ITK.job: helps immune T cells switch on when they spot an invader
ITK.basis: Tyrosine kinase that plays an essential role in regulation of the adaptive immune response. Regulates the development, function and differentiation of conventional T-cells ... When antigen presenting cells (APC) activate T-cell receptor (TCR), a series of phosphorylation lead to the recruitment of ITK ... ultimately lead to lymphokine production, T-cell proliferation and differentiation

ITPA.job: clears faulty building blocks so they don't get built into DNA and RNA
ITPA.basis: hydrolyzes the non-canonical purine nucleotides ... Probably excludes non-canonical purines from RNA and DNA precursor pools, thus preventing their incorporation into RNA and DNA

ITPR1.job: releases stored calcium inside cells when a chemical signal arrives
ITPR1.basis: Inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate-gated calcium channel that, upon inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate binding, mediates calcium release from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)

ITPR3.job: releases stored calcium inside cells when a chemical messenger signals
ITPR3.basis: Inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate-gated calcium channel that, upon 1D-myo-inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate binding, transports calcium from the endoplasmic reticulum lumen to cytoplasm, thus releasing the intracellular calcium

IVD.job: helps break down leucine, an amino acid from food
IVD.basis: A mitochondrial matrix enzyme that catalyzes the third step in leucine catabolism

JAG1.job: signals neighboring cells to help decide what kind of cell they become
JAG1.basis: Ligand for multiple Notch receptors and involved in the mediation of Notch signaling ... May be involved in cell-fate decisions

JAK1.job: passes on signals from immune messenger molecules like interferons to the cell's inside
JAK1.basis: protein tyrosine kinase that phosphorylates signal-transducing subunits of cytokine receptor complexes ... is involved in the IFN-alpha/beta/gamma signal pathway ... activates STAT signaling

JAK3.job: passes on signals that immune cells need to develop and respond
JAK3.basis: Mediates essential signaling events in both innate and adaptive immunity and plays a crucial role in hematopoiesis during T-cells development

JARID2.job: helps switch off genes in the right places as an embryo develops
JARID2.basis: acts as a regulator of histone methyltransferase complexes, thereby playing an essential role in embryonic development ... Mediates the recruitment of the PRC2 complex to target genes in embryonic stem cells, thereby playing a key role in stem cell differentiation and normal embryonic development

JPH2.job: links the heart muscle cell's surface to its inner calcium stores so it can contract
JPH2.basis: provides a structural bridge between the plasma membrane and the sarcoplasmic reticulum and is required for normal excitation-contraction coupling in cardiomyocytes ... functional cross-talk between the cell surface and intracellular Ca(2+) release channels

KANSL1.job: is part of a team that tags DNA's packaging to help switch genes on
KANSL1.basis: Non-catalytic component of the NSL histone acetyltransferase complex ... mediates histone H4 acetylation ... at transcription start sites and promotes transcription initiation
