KAT6A.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging proteins to help switch genes on
KAT6A.basis: Histone acetyltransferase that acetylates lysine residues in histone H3 and histone H4 ... May act as a transcriptional coactivator

KAT6B.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging to help switch genes on or off
KAT6B.basis: Histone acetyltransferase which may be involved in both positive and negative regulation of transcription

KATNIP.job: is thought to help keep the cell's inner scaffolding stable
KATNIP.basis: May influence the stability of microtubules (MT)
KATNIP.alt: may help keep the cell's internal scaffolding stable

KBTBD13.job: helps pick out specific proteins and tag them for the cell to break down
KBTBD13.basis: Substrate-specific adapter of a BCR (BTB-CUL3-RBX1) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex
KBTBD13.alt: helps the cell tag certain proteins for disposal

KCNA1.job: lets potassium out of nerve cells to keep their signals calm and steady
KCNA1.basis: Voltage-gated potassium channel that mediates transmembrane potassium transport in excitable membranes, primarily in the brain and the central nervous system ... Contributes to the regulation of the membrane potential and nerve signaling, and prevents neuronal hyperexcitability

KCNA2.job: lets potassium out of brain cells to keep their electrical signals steady
KCNA2.basis: Voltage-gated potassium channel that mediates transmembrane potassium transport in excitable membranes, primarily in the brain and the central nervous system ... Prevents aberrant action potential firing and regulates neuronal output

KCNB1.job: lets potassium out of brain cells to calm their electrical firing
KCNB1.basis: Voltage-gated potassium channel that mediates transmembrane potassium transport in excitable membranes, primarily in the brain ... outward potassium current ... plays a role in homeostatic attenuation of electrical excitability throughout the brain

KCNC1.job: lets potassium out of brain cells so they can fire rapidly
KCNC1.basis: Voltage-gated potassium channel ... through which potassium ions pass ... Plays an important role in the rapid repolarization of fast-firing brain neurons

KCNC2.job: lets potassium out of brain cells so they can fire rapidly
KCNC2.basis: Voltage-gated potassium channel that mediates transmembrane potassium transport in excitable membranes, primarily in the brain ... sustained high-frequency firing in neurons of the central nervous system

KCNC3.job: lets potassium out of brain cells so they can reset quickly between signals
KCNC3.basis: Voltage-gated potassium channel that plays an important role in the rapid repolarization of fast-firing brain neurons ... forming a potassium-selective channel through which potassium ions pass

KCNH1.job: forms a channel that lets potassium flow out of cells when they fire
KCNH1.basis: Pore-forming (alpha) subunit of a voltage-gated delayed rectifier potassium channel that mediates outward-rectifying potassium currents which, on depolarization, reaches a steady-state level

KCNH2.job: forms a channel that lets potassium cross cell membranes to reset electrical charge
KCNH2.basis: Pore-forming (alpha) subunit of voltage-gated inwardly rectifying potassium channel ... during subsequent repolarization

KCNH5.job: forms a channel that lets potassium flow out of cells when they are electrically excited
KCNH5.basis: Pore-forming (alpha) subunit of a voltage-gated delayed rectifier potassium channel that mediates outward-rectifying potassium currents which, on depolarization, reaches a steady-state level

KCNJ1.job: lets potassium pass through cells in the kidney to keep body levels balanced
KCNJ1.basis: Inward rectifier potassium channels ... In the kidney, probably plays a major role in potassium homeostasis

KCNJ10.job: lets potassium into brain support cells and kidney cells to keep salt levels balanced
KCNJ10.basis: May be responsible for potassium buffering action of glial cells in the brain ... allow potassium to flow into the cell rather than out of it ... In the kidney, together with KCNJ16, mediates basolateral K(+) recycling in distal tubules; this process is critical for Na(+) reabsorption

KCNJ11.job: forms a potassium channel that senses the cell's energy level, including in the pancreas
KCNJ11.basis: forms the pore of ATP-sensitive potassium channels (KATP), regulating potassium permeability as a function of cytoplasmic ATP and ADP concentrations in many different cells ... In pancreatic cells, it forms KATP channels with ABCC8/SUR1

KCNJ13.basis: Inward rectifier potassium channels are characterized by a greater tendency to allow potassium to flow into the cell rather than out of it

KCNJ16.job: lets potassium through kidney cells, helping the kidneys hold on to salt
KCNJ16.basis: Inward rectifier potassium channels ... In the kidney, together with KCNJ10, mediates basolateral K(+) recycling in distal tubules; this process is critical for Na(+) reabsorption at the tubules

KCNJ5.job: lets potassium flow into cells when signaled from outside
KCNJ5.basis: Inward rectifier potassium channels are characterized by a greater tendency to allow potassium to flow into the cell rather than out of it ... This potassium channel is controlled by G proteins

KCNK3.job: lets potassium flow out of cells to keep nerve and other cells calm
KCNK3.basis: K(+) channel that conducts voltage-dependent outward rectifying currents upon membrane depolarization ... may hyperpolarize the resting membrane potential to limit intrinsic neuronal excitability ... contributes to the maintenance of a hyperpolarized resting membrane potential

KCNMA1.job: lets potassium out of cells to calm nerve and muscle activity
KCNMA1.basis: Potassium channel ... that mediates export of K(+) ... Its activation dampens the excitatory events ... Plays a key role in controlling excitability in a number of systems, such as regulation of the contraction of smooth muscle

KCNQ1.job: forms a channel that lets potassium out of cells to reset each heartbeat
KCNQ1.basis: Pore-forming subunit of the voltage-gated potassium (Kv) channel involved in the regulation of cardiomyocyte excitability ... participates in cardiac repolarization by associating with KCNE1 to form the I(Ks) cardiac potassium current

KCNQ2.job: forms a potassium channel that keeps brain cells from firing too easily
KCNQ2.basis: Pore-forming subunit of the voltage-gated potassium (Kv) M-channel which is responsible for the M-current, a key controller of neuronal excitability

KCNQ3.job: forms a potassium channel that keeps brain cells from firing too easily
KCNQ3.basis: Pore-forming subunit of the voltage-gated potassium (Kv) M-channel which is responsible for the M-current, a key controller of neuronal excitability

KCNQ4.job: lets potassium flow out of the inner ear's sound-sensing cells
KCNQ4.basis: Pore-forming subunit of the voltage-gated potassium (Kv) channel involved in the regulation of sensory cells excitability in the cochlea ... Promotes the outflow of potassium ions ... Important for normal physiological function of inner ear such as sensory perception of sound

KCNT1.job: lets potassium out of nerve cells to calm their electrical activity
KCNT1.basis: Sodium-activated K(+) channel ... Acts as an important mediator of neuronal membrane excitability ... Contributes to the delayed outward currents

KCNT2.job: lets potassium out of nerve cells to help control how easily they fire
KCNT2.basis: Sodium-activated and chloride-activated potassium channel ... Produces rapidly activating outward rectifier K(+) currents ... Contributes to regulate neuronal excitability

KCNV2.job: helps control the flow of potassium in and out of cells
KCNV2.basis: Potassium channel subunit. Modulates channel activity

KCTD1.job: helps tune several signals that tell cells which genes to switch on
KCTD1.basis: Is a regulator of different signaling pathways ... Is a repressor of transcriptional activation mediated by AP-2 family members

KCTD7.job: helps tag other proteins for disposal or change, including ones that calm nerve cells
KCTD7.basis: Substrate-specific adapter of a BCR (BTB-CUL3-RBX1) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that mediates the ubiquitination of multiple substrates, leading to either their proteasomal or lysosomal degradation, or modulating their activity ... Regulates voltage-gated potassium channels, thereby modulating hyperpolarizing potassium currents in neurons and inducing potassium-dependent membrane hyperpolarization

KDF1.job: helps form the outer layer of skin early in development
KDF1.basis: Plays a role in the regulation of the epidermis formation during early development

KDM1A.job: removes chemical tags from DNA's packaging proteins to switch genes on or off
KDM1A.basis: Histone demethylase that can demethylate both 'Lys-4' (H3K4me) and 'Lys-9' (H3K9me) of histone H3, thereby acting as a coactivator or a corepressor, depending on the context

KDM3B.job: removes chemical tags from DNA's packaging proteins to help switch genes on
KDM3B.basis: Histone demethylase that specifically demethylates 'Lys-9' of histone H3, thereby playing a central role in histone code

KDM4B.job: removes chemical tags from DNA's packaging proteins to help switch genes on
KDM4B.basis: Histone demethylase that specifically demethylates 'Lys-9' of histone H3, thereby acting as a key regulator of nascent transcription

KDM5C.job: removes chemical tags from DNA's packaging to help switch certain genes off
KDM5C.basis: Histone demethylase that specifically demethylates 'Lys-4' of histone H3, thereby playing a central role in histone code ... Participates in transcriptional repression of neuronal genes

KDM6A.job: removes chemical tags from DNA's packaging proteins to help switch genes on
KDM6A.basis: Histone demethylase that specifically demethylates 'Lys-27' of histone H3, thereby playing a central role in histone code ... regulating HOX gene expression

KDM6B.job: removes chemical tags from DNA's packaging proteins to switch genes back on
KDM6B.basis: Histone demethylase that specifically demethylates 'Lys-27' of histone H3, thereby playing a central role in histone code ... by regulating HOX gene expression

KDR.job: picks up growth signals that tell new blood vessels to form
KDR.basis: acts as a cell-surface receptor for VEGFA, VEGFC and VEGFD. Plays an essential role in the regulation of angiogenesis, vascular development ... Promotes proliferation, survival, migration and differentiation of endothelial cells

KDSR.job: helps make sphingolipids, a family of fats that build cell membranes
KDSR.basis: Catalyzes the reduction of 3'-oxosphinganine (3-ketodihydrosphingosine/KDS) to sphinganine (dihydrosphingosine/DHS), the second step of de novo sphingolipid biosynthesis

KIAA1549.job: is thought to help the eye's light-sensing cells work
KIAA1549.basis: May play a role in photoreceptor function
KIAA1549.alt: may help the eye's light-sensing cells do their work

KIDINS220.job: helps nerve cells respond to growth signals so their fibers can grow
KIDINS220.basis: Promotes a prolonged MAP-kinase signaling by neurotrophins ... Plays a role in nerve growth factor (NGF)-induced recruitment of RAPGEF2 to late endosomes and neurite outgrowth

KIF11.job: helps build the machinery that pulls chromosomes apart when cells divide
KIF11.basis: Motor protein required for establishing a bipolar spindle and thus contributing to chromosome congression during mitosis

KIF1A.job: carries signal-sending supplies along nerve fibers to where nerve cells connect
KIF1A.basis: Kinesin motor with a plus-end-directed microtubule motor activity ... It is required for anterograde axonal transport of synaptic vesicle precursors

KIF26A.job: helps nerve cells of the gut and brain develop
KIF26A.basis: plays a key role in enteric neuron development ... Plays a critical role in cerebral cortical development

KIF5A.job: carries building materials along nerve fibers
KIF5A.basis: Microtubule-dependent motor required for slow axonal transport of neurofilament proteins ... vesicular transport of VAPA, VAPB, SURF4, RAB11A, RAB11B and RTN3 proteins in neurons

KIFBP.job: helps nerve cells grow and maintain their long fibers
KIFBP.basis: Required for organization of axonal microtubules, and axonal outgrowth and maintenance during peripheral and central nervous system development

KIZ.job: keeps the cell's spindle anchor points sturdy while the cell divides
KIZ.basis: Centrosomal protein required for establishing a robust mitotic centrosome architecture that can endure the forces that converge on the centrosomes during spindle formation

KLHL3.job: helps the kidneys control how much salt the body keeps
KLHL3.basis: acts as a regulator of ion transport in the distal nephron ... in distal convoluted tubule cells of kidney, thereby regulating NaCl reabsorption

KLHL40.basis: acts as a key regulator of skeletal muscle development

KLKB1.job: helps start blood clotting and widen blood vessels
KLKB1.basis: Participates in the surface-dependent activation of blood coagulation ... Releases bradykinin from HMW kininogen
KLKB1.alt: helps start blood clotting and releases bradykinin, a blood-vessel-widening signal

KMT2A.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging that help switch genes on
KMT2A.basis: Histone methyltransferase that plays an essential role in early development and hematopoiesis ... predominantly forms H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 methylation marks at active chromatin sites where transcription and DNA repair take place ... Required for transcriptional activation of HOXA9

KMT2B.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging that help switch genes on
KMT2B.basis: Histone methyltransferase that catalyzes methyl group transfer ... to ... histone H3 (H3K4) ... predominantly forms H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 methylation marks at active chromatin sites where transcription and DNA repair take place

KMT2C.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging that help switch genes on
KMT2C.basis: Histone methyltransferase that catalyzes methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to the epsilon-amino group of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4) ... forms H3K4me1 methylation marks at active chromatin sites where transcription and DNA repair take place ... enriching H3K4me1 mark on primed and active enhancer elements

KMT2E.job: binds to the packaging around active genes to help control when they switch on
KMT2E.basis: Associates with chromatin regions downstream of transcriptional start sites of active genes and thus regulates gene transcription

KMT5B.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging proteins that keep genes switched off
KMT5B.basis: Histone methyltransferase that specifically methylates ... 'Lys-20' ... of histone H4 ... and thus regulates transcription and maintenance of genome integrity ... H4 'Lys-20' trimethylation represents a specific tag for epigenetic transcriptional repression

KNG1.basis: HMW-kininogen plays an important role in blood coagulation by helping to position optimally prekallikrein and factor XI next to factor XII
KNG1.alt: helps start blood clotting by lining up clotting factors

KPTN.job: helps cells sense nutrients and hold back growth when amino acids run low
KPTN.basis: functions in the amino acid-sensing branch of the TORC1 signaling pathway ... required to negatively regulate mTORC1 signaling in absence of amino acids

KRAS.job: passes on signals that tell cells to grow and divide
KRAS.basis: Signal transducer in the Ras-MAPK signaling pathway that regulates cell proliferation and survival

KYNU.job: helps break down kynurenine, a chemical the body makes from food protein
KYNU.basis: Catalyzes the cleavage of L-kynurenine (L-Kyn) and L-3-hydroxykynurenine (L-3OHKyn) into anthranilic acid (AA) and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (3-OHAA)

L1CAM.job: helps nerve cells stick together and wire up the developing brain
L1CAM.basis: Neural cell adhesion molecule involved in the dynamics of cell adhesion ... During brain development, critical in multiple processes, including neuronal migration, axonal growth and fasciculation, and synaptogenesis

L2HGDH.job: clears away a leftover byproduct inside the cell's power plants
L2HGDH.basis: Catalyzes the oxidation of L-2-hydroxyglutarate to 2-oxoglutarate in the mitochondrial matrix ... mediating degradation of L-2-hydroxyglutarate

LAMA2.job: helps cells attach to each other and organize into tissues
LAMA2.basis: laminin is thought to mediate the attachment, migration and organization of cells into tissues during embryonic development

LAMA5.job: helps cells attach and arrange themselves into tissues as the body develops
LAMA5.basis: laminin is thought to mediate the attachment, migration and organization of cells into tissues during embryonic development

LAMP2.job: helps the cell's recycling centers take in and break down worn-out proteins
LAMP2.basis: Lysosomal membrane glycoprotein which plays an important role in lysosome biogenesis, lysosomal pH regulation and autophagy ... Functions by binding target proteins ... and targeting them for lysosomal degradation

LAMP3.job: helps the cell's recycling centers join up with waste bubbles to break them down
LAMP3.basis: Lysosomal membrane glycoprotein ... Plays a role in the process of fusion of the lysosome with the autophagosome, thereby modulating the autophagic process

LARGE1.job: builds a sugar chain that lets muscle cells grip the tissue around them
LARGE1.basis: involved in the maturation of alpha-dystroglycan (DAG1) by glycosylation leading to DAG1 binding to laminin G-like domain-containing extracellular proteins with high affinity ... adding repeating units [-3-Xylose-alpha-1,3-GlcA-beta-1-] to produce a heteropolysaccharide ... Plays a key role in skeletal muscle function

LARS2.job: loads the building block leucine onto its carrier molecule for making proteins
LARS2.basis: Catalyzes the attachment of leucine to its cognate tRNA

LAT.job: helps immune T cells pass on signals when they detect germs
LAT.basis: Required for TCR (T-cell antigen receptor)- and pre-TCR-mediated signaling, both in mature T-cells and during their development ... Couples activation of these receptors and their associated kinases with distal intracellular events

LCA5.job: helps carry proteins to the light-sensing part of the eye's photoreceptor cells
LCA5.basis: Involved in intraflagellar protein (IFT) transport in photoreceptor cilia. Plays a role in the ciliary transport of photoreceptors outer segment proteins

LCK.job: switches on immune T cells when they spot a germ
LCK.basis: plays an essential role in the selection and maturation of developing T-cells in the thymus and in the function of mature T-cells ... Plays a key role in T-cell antigen receptor (TCR)-linked signal transduction pathways ... Association of the TCR with a peptide antigen-bound MHC complex ... initiating the TCR-CD3 signaling pathway

LCP2.job: helps immune cells pass on the alarm when they spot a germ
LCP2.basis: Adapter protein primarily involved in signaling pathways within T-cells, as well as other immune cells ... Plays a crucial role for transducing signal from the T-cell receptor (TCR) after antigen recognition leading to T-cell activation

LDB3.job: helps connect signals to the inner scaffolding of muscle cells
LDB3.basis: May function as an adapter in striated muscle to couple protein kinase C-mediated signaling via its LIM domains to the cytoskeleton
LDB3.alt: helps link chemical signals to the internal scaffolding of muscle cells

LDLR.job: pulls cholesterol-carrying LDL particles out of the blood into cells
LDLR.basis: Binds low density lipoprotein /LDL, the major cholesterol-carrying lipoprotein of plasma, and transports it into cells by endocytosis

LDLRAP1.job: helps liver cells pull LDL cholesterol in from the blood
LDLRAP1.basis: required for efficient endocytosis of the LDL receptor (LDLR) in polarized cells such as hepatocytes ... May be required for LDL binding and internalization

LGI1.job: helps brain cells pass signals by tuning potassium channels and signal receivers
LGI1.basis: Regulates voltage-gated potassium channels ... Ligand for ADAM22 that positively regulates synaptic transmission mediated by AMPA-type glutamate receptors

LHFPL5.job: helps the inner ear's hair cells turn sound into nerve signals
LHFPL5.basis: Auxiliary subunit of the mechanotransducer (MET) non-specific cation channel complex located at the tips of the shorter stereocilia of cochlear hair cells and that mediates sensory transduction in the auditory system

LHX2.job: switches on genes that guide developing nerve and immune cells
LHX2.basis: Acts as a transcriptional activator ... Transcriptional regulatory protein involved in the control of cell differentiation in developing lymphoid and neural cell types

LIFR.job: picks up chemical messages at the cell surface and passes them inside
LIFR.basis: Functions as a membrane-bound signal-transducing subunit ... Signal transmission is initiated either by binding directly to cytokines, such as OSM or LIF or CTF1

LIG1.job: seals breaks in DNA during repair and copying
LIG1.basis: DNA ligase that seals nicks in double-stranded during DNA repair ... Also involved in DNA replication

LIG3.job: seals breaks in DNA, both in the cell's core and its power plants
LIG3.basis: in the nucleus and can correct defective DNA strand-break repair ... Isoform 1 is targeted to mitochondria, where it functions as a DNA ligase in mitochondrial base-excision DNA repair

LIG4.job: reseals broken DNA by joining the cut ends back together
LIG4.basis: DNA ligase involved in DNA non-homologous end joining (NHEJ); required for double-strand break (DSB) repair ... resealing the DNA breaks

LIPA.job: breaks down cholesterol and fats inside the cell's recycling centers
LIPA.basis: Catalyzes the deacylation of cholesteryl ester core lipids of endocytosed low density lipoproteins to generate free fatty acids and cholesterol ... Hydrolyzes triglycerides

LITAF.job: helps send unneeded proteins to the cell's recycling centers to be broken down
LITAF.basis: Plays a role in endosomal protein trafficking and in targeting proteins for lysosomal degradation

LMAN1.job: carries certain newly made proteins to the cell's shipping center
LMAN1.basis: The LMAN1-MCFD2 complex forms a specific cargo receptor for the ER-to-Golgi transport of selected proteins

LMBRD1.job: helps move vitamin B12 out of the cell's recycling centers so it can be used
LMBRD1.basis: Lysosomal membrane chaperone required to export cobalamin (vitamin B12) from the lysosome to the cytosol, allowing its conversion to cofactors

LMNA.job: forms a sturdy mesh that lines and supports the cell's nucleus
LMNA.basis: Lamins are intermediate filament proteins that assemble into a filamentous meshwork, and which constitute the major components of the nuclear lamina, a fibrous layer on the nucleoplasmic side of the inner nuclear membrane ... Lamins provide a framework for the nuclear envelope

LMNB1.job: forms a mesh lining the nucleus that gives it shape and organizes DNA
LMNB1.basis: Lamins are intermediate filament proteins that assemble into a filamentous meshwork, and which constitute the major components of the nuclear lamina ... Lamins provide a framework for the nuclear envelope, bridging the nuclear envelope and chromatin, thereby playing an important role in nuclear assembly, chromatin organization

LMOD2.job: helps build and size the protein threads that make heart muscle contract
LMOD2.basis: Mediates nucleation of actin filaments and thereby promotes actin polymerization ... Plays a role in the regulation of actin filament length ... Required for normal sarcomere organization in the heart, and for normal heart function

LMOD3.job: helps build the thin protein threads that let skeletal muscles contract
LMOD3.basis: Essential for the organization of sarcomeric actin thin filaments in skeletal muscle ... Increases the rate of actin polymerization

LMX1A.job: switches on genes that guide how the brain, spinal cord and spine develop
LMX1A.basis: Acts as a transcriptional activator ... Required for development of the roof plate and, in turn, for specification of dorsal cell fates in the CNS and developing vertebrae

LMX1B.job: switches on genes that shape the back of limbs and kidney filter cells
LMX1B.basis: Transcription factor involved in the regulation of podocyte-expressed genes ... Essential for the specification of dorsal limb fate

LOX.job: strengthens collagen and elastin fibers that give tissues like the aorta their structure
LOX.basis: Responsible for the post-translational oxidative deamination of peptidyl lysine residues in precursors to fibrous collagen and elastin ... Plays a role in the aortic wall architecture

LOXHD1.job: helps the inner ear's hair cells work so we can hear
LOXHD1.basis: Involved in hearing. Required for normal function of hair cells in the inner ear

LPIN1.job: helps cells make and store fats
LPIN1.basis: catalyzes the conversion of phosphatidic acid to diacylglycerol during triglyceride, phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine biosynthesis and therefore controls the metabolism of fatty acids

LPIN2.job: helps cells make fats and the building blocks of cell membranes
LPIN2.basis: catalyzes the conversion of phosphatidic acid to diacylglycerol during triglyceride, phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine biosynthesis ... Plays important roles in controlling the metabolism of fatty acids

LRAT.job: turns vitamin A into its stored form, which the eye needs for vision
LRAT.basis: producing all-trans retinyl esters ... Retinyl esters are storage forms of vitamin A ... LRAT plays a critical role in vision

LRBA.job: helps immune cells send their defense molecules to the right place
LRBA.basis: Involved in coupling signal transduction and vesicle trafficking to enable polarized secretion and/or membrane deposition of immune effector molecules

LRP4.job: helps nerves connect to muscles and helps keep bone growth in check
LRP4.basis: Plays a key role in the formation and the maintenance of the neuromuscular junction (NMJ), the synapse between motor neuron and skeletal muscle ... Mediates SOST-dependent inhibition of bone formation

LRP5.job: picks up Wnt growth signals that help build strong bones and eye blood vessels
LRP5.basis: coreceptor with members of the frizzled family of seven-transmembrane spanning receptors to transduce signal by Wnt proteins ... During bone development, regulates osteoblast proliferation and differentiation thus determining bone mass ... required for retinal vascular development

LRPPRC.job: helps cells handle the RNA messages used to build parts of their energy factories
LRPPRC.basis: May play a role in RNA metabolism in both nuclei and mitochondria ... In mitochondria binds to poly(A) mRNA. Plays a role in translation or stability of mitochondrially encoded cytochrome c oxidase (COX) subunits

LRRK2.job: helps control how cells ship and recycle materials in small bubbles
LRRK2.basis: Serine/threonine-protein kinase which phosphorylates a broad range of proteins involved in multiple processes such as neuronal plasticity, innate immunity, autophagy, and vesicle trafficking ... Is a key regulator of RAB GTPases

LTBP2.job: helps build the stretchy elastic fibers that let tissues spring back
LTBP2.basis: May play an integral structural role in elastic-fiber architectural organization and/or assembly
LTBP2.alt: helps build the stretchy fibers that let tissues bend and spring back

LYRM7.job: helps build part of the cell's energy-making machinery in mitochondria
LYRM7.basis: Assembly factor required for Rieske Fe-S protein UQCRFS1 incorporation into the cytochrome b-c1 (CIII) complex ... within the mitochondrial inner membrane

LYST.job: controls the size and number of the cell's recycling and storage sacs
LYST.basis: Adapter protein that regulates and/or fission of intracellular vesicles such as lysosomes ... has role in the regulation of size, number and exocytosis of lytic granules

LZTFL1.job: controls which proteins enter the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
LZTFL1.basis: Regulates ciliary localization of the BBSome complex. Together with the BBSome complex, controls SMO ciliary trafficking

LZTR1.job: tags certain growth-signal switches for removal, keeping cell growth signals in check
LZTR1.basis: mediates ubiquitination of Ras GTPases ... Acts as a negative regulator of RAS-MAPK signaling by controlling Ras levels

MAB21L1.job: helps the embryo develop, especially the eyes
MAB21L1.basis: required for several aspects of embryonic development including normal development of the eye

MAB21L2.job: helps the eye and other body parts form in the growing embryo
MAB21L2.basis: Required for several aspects of embryonic development including normal development of the eye

MAG.job: attaches nerve fibers to their insulating coating and helps keep that coating intact
MAG.basis: Adhesion molecule that mediates interactions between myelinating cells and neurons ... seems to play a role in the maintenance of normal axon myelination

MAGED2.job: helps the kidneys take back salt from urine
MAGED2.basis: Regulates the expression, localization to the plasma membrane and function of the sodium chloride cotransporters SLC12A1 and SLC12A3, two key components of salt reabsorption in the distal renal tubule

MAGEL2.job: helps cells sort and recycle materials taken in at their surface
MAGEL2.basis: Acts as a regulator of retrograde transport via its interaction with VPS35. Recruited to retromer-containing endosomes ... leading to promote endosomal F-actin assembly

MAGT1.job: helps attach sugar chains to newly made proteins
MAGT1.basis: Accessory component of the STT3B-containing form of the N-oligosaccharyl transferase (OST) complex which catalyzes the transfer of a high mannose oligosaccharide ... to an asparagine residue ... in nascent polypeptide chains ... Involved in N-glycosylation of STT3B-dependent substrates

MAK.job: controls the length of cells' antenna-like hairs, helping keep light-sensing eye cells alive
MAK.basis: Essential for the regulation of ciliary length and required for the long-term survival of photoreceptors

MALT1.job: relays alarm signals inside immune cells that switch on the body's defenses
MALT1.basis: channel adaptive and innate immune signaling ... to activate NF-kappa-B and MAP kinase p38 pathways which stimulate expression of genes encoding pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines

MAN1B1.job: trims sugar tags so the cell can flag misfolded molecules for disposal
MAN1B1.basis: Involved in glycoprotein quality control targeting of misfolded glycoproteins for degradation. It primarily trims a single alpha-1,2-linked mannose residue

MAN2B1.job: helps cells break down sugar chains left over from used proteins
MAN2B1.basis: Can hydrolyze a variety of glycan substrates containing terminal alpha-mannosidic linkages ... Cleaves ... mannose residues on oligosaccharides generated by N-glycoprotein degradation pathways

MANBA.job: trims a sugar from proteins so cells can break them down
MANBA.basis: Exoglycosidase that cleaves the single beta-linked mannose residue from the non-reducing end of all N-linked glycoprotein oligosaccharides

MAOA.job: breaks down brain chemical messengers such as serotonin
MAOA.basis: Catalyzes the oxidative deamination of primary and some secondary amine such as neurotransmitters ... has important functions in the metabolism of neuroactive and vasoactive amines in the central nervous system ... Preferentially oxidizes serotonin

MAP1B.job: helps shape the inner scaffolding of nerve cells as they grow their branches
MAP1B.basis: required for proper microtubule dynamics and plays a role in the cytoskeletal changes that accompany neuronal differentiation and neurite extension

MAP2K2.job: switches on other relay proteins by adding chemical tags to them
MAP2K2.basis: Catalyzes the concomitant phosphorylation of a threonine and a tyrosine residue in a Thr-Glu-Tyr sequence located in MAP kinases. Activates the ERK1 and ERK2 MAP kinases

MAP3K20.job: senses stress inside cells and relays signals that can tell damaged cells to die
MAP3K20.basis: Stress-activated component of a protein kinase signal transduction cascade that promotes programmed cell death in response to various stress

MAPK8IP3.job: helps nerve fibers grow by moving cargo along them
MAPK8IP3.basis: Promotes neuronal axon elongation in a kinesin- and JNK-dependent manner ... promotes kinesin-1 motility along microtubules and is essential for axon elongation and regeneration ... drives NTRK2/TRKB axonal but not dendritic anterograde transport

MAPKBP1.job: tones down an immune sensor that helps cells react to bacteria
MAPKBP1.basis: Negative regulator of NOD2 function. It down-regulates NOD2-induced processes such as activation of NF-kappa-B signaling, IL8 secretion and antibacterial response

MARVELD2.job: seals the gaps where three cells meet, keeping the inner ear's fluids separate
MARVELD2.basis: Plays a role in the formation of tricellular tight junctions and of epithelial barriers ... Required for normal hearing via its role in the separation of the endolymphatic and perilymphatic spaces of the organ of Corti in the inner ear

MASP1.job: helps start an immune chain reaction that destroys germs in the blood
MASP1.basis: serum protease that activates the complement pathway of the complement system, a cascade of proteins that leads to phagocytosis and breakdown of pathogens

MAT1A.job: turns the amino acid methionine into a molecule that cells use to tag DNA and proteins
MAT1A.basis: Catalyzes the formation of S-adenosylmethionine from methionine and ATP

MATR3.job: helps build the inner scaffolding of the cell's nucleus and holds on to faulty RNA messages
MATR3.basis: may interact with other nuclear matrix proteins to form the internal fibrogranular network ... may play a role in nuclear retention of defective RNAs
MATR3.alt: helps form the scaffolding inside the cell's nucleus and handles genetic messages

MAX.job: pairs with partner proteins to grab DNA and switch genes on or off
MAX.basis: Transcription regulator. Forms a sequence-specific DNA-binding protein complex with MYC or MAD ... The MYC:MAX complex is a transcriptional activator, whereas the MAD:MAX complex is a repressor

MBD5.job: helps a team of proteins remove chemical tags on DNA packaging to control genes
MBD5.basis: Non-catalytic component of the polycomb repressive deubiquitinase (PR-DUB) complex, a complex that specifically mediates deubiquitination of histone H2A ... The PR-DUB complex is an epigenetic regulator of gene expression

MBOAT7.job: attaches fatty acids to fats that build cell membranes, helping balance fat in the liver
MBOAT7.basis: catalyzes the transfer of an acyl group from an acyl-CoA to a lysophosphatidylinositol ... leading to the production of a phosphatidylinositol ... participates in the reacylation step of the phospholipid remodeling pathway ... In liver, participates in the regulation of triglyceride metabolism

MBTPS1.job: cuts and switches on other proteins, including ones that control cholesterol making
MBTPS1.basis: Serine protease that cleaves ... Catalyzes the first step in the proteolytic activation of the sterol regulatory element-binding proteins (SREBPs) SREBF1/SREBP1 and SREBF2/SREBP2

MBTPS2.job: cuts certain proteins free from membranes so they can switch genes on
MBTPS2.basis: Zinc metalloprotease that mediates intramembrane proteolysis of proteins such as ATF6, ATF6B, SREBF1/SREBP1 and SREBF2/SREBP2 ... cleaves SREBPs within the first transmembrane segment, thereby releasing the N-terminal segment ... Mature N-terminal SREBP fragments shuttle to the nucleus and activate gene transcription

MCCC1.job: helps the body break down leucine, an amino acid from food
MCCC1.basis: Biotin-attachment subunit of the 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase ... a critical step for leucine and isovaleric acid catabolism

MCCC2.job: helps the body break down leucine, an amino acid from food
MCCC2.basis: Carboxyltransferase subunit of the 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase ... a critical step for leucine and isovaleric acid catabolism

MCEE.job: helps the body break down certain amino acids and fats
MCEE.basis: Methylmalonyl-CoA epimerase involved in propionyl-CoA metabolism

MCM3AP.job: helps carry genetic messages out of the cell's nucleus
MCM3AP.basis: As a component of the TREX-2 complex, involved in the export of mRNAs to the cytoplasm through the nuclear pores

MCM9.job: helps repair broken and damaged DNA
MCM9.basis: Component of the MCM8-MCM9 complex, which is involved in the repair of double-stranded DNA breaks (DBSs) and DNA interstrand cross-links (ICLs) by homologous recombination (HR) ... Acts as a helicase in DNA mismatch repair (MMR)

MCOLN1.job: releases calcium from the cell's recycling centers to help them move and work
MCOLN1.basis: Proposed to play a major role in Ca(2+) release from late endosome and lysosome vesicles to the cytoplasm, which is important for many lysosome-dependent cellular events, including the fusion and trafficking of these organelles

MCPH1.job: helps cells pack chromosomes and respond to DNA damage
MCPH1.basis: Implicated in chromosome condensation and DNA damage induced cellular responses

MECOM.job: switches other genes on or off, helping blood cells form
MECOM.basis: Functions as a transcriptional regulator binding to DNA sequences in the promoter region of target genes and regulating positively or negatively their expression ... Involved in hematopoiesis

MECP2.job: reads chemical tags on DNA and helps keep tagged genes switched off
MECP2.basis: Chromosomal protein that binds to methylated DNA ... Mediates transcriptional repression through interaction with histone deacetylase and the corepressor SIN3A

MED12.job: is part of a bridge passing gene on-off signals to the gene-reading machinery
MED12.basis: Component of the Mediator complex ... Mediator functions as a bridge to convey information from gene-specific regulatory proteins to the basal RNA polymerase II transcription machinery
MED12.alt: helps pass on-switch signals to the machinery that reads genes

MED12L.job: is thought to help pass on signals that switch genes on
MED12L.basis: May be a component of the Mediator complex, a coactivator involved in the regulated transcription of nearly all RNA polymerase II-dependent genes ... Mediator functions as a bridge to convey information from gene-specific regulatory proteins to the basal RNA polymerase II transcription machinery
MED12L.alt: may help pass on signals that switch genes on in the cell

MED13.job: is part of a hub that passes gene on-off signals to the machinery reading genes
MED13.basis: Component of the Mediator complex, a coactivator involved in the regulated transcription of nearly all RNA polymerase II-dependent genes ... Mediator functions as a bridge to convey information from gene-specific regulatory proteins to the basal RNA polymerase II transcription machinery
MED13.alt: is part of a hub that passes on-off signals to the machinery that reads genes

MED13L.job: is part of a bridge that passes gene on-switch signals to the gene-reading machinery
MED13L.basis: Component of the Mediator complex, a coactivator involved in the regulated transcription of nearly all RNA polymerase II-dependent genes. Mediator functions as a bridge to convey information from gene-specific regulatory proteins to the basal RNA polymerase II transcription machinery
MED13L.alt: is part of a hub that passes on-switch signals to the machinery that reads genes

MED27.job: is one piece of Mediator, a bridge that relays on-switch signals to the gene-reading machinery
MED27.basis: Component of the Mediator complex, a coactivator involved in the regulated transcription of nearly all RNA polymerase II-dependent genes ... Mediator functions as a bridge to convey information from gene-specific regulatory proteins to the basal RNA polymerase II transcription machinery
MED27.alt: is part of a hub that helps switch on nearly all of the cell's genes

MEF2C.job: switches on genes that help build muscle, the heart and the brain
MEF2C.basis: Transcription activator which binds specifically to the MEF2 element present in the regulatory regions of many muscle-specific genes. Controls cardiac morphogenesis and myogenesis ... Crucial for normal neuronal development

MEFV.job: helps the immune system control inflammation
MEFV.basis: Involved in the regulation of innate immunity and the inflammatory response ... hence preventing excessive IL1B- and IL18-mediated inflammation ... acting as an innate immune sensor

MEGF10.job: helps cleanup cells recognize and swallow dying cells
MEGF10.basis: Membrane receptor involved in phagocytosis by macrophages and astrocytes of apoptotic cells ... Plays role in muscle cell proliferation, adhesion and motility

MEIS2.job: teams up with other proteins to switch genes on, including during development
MEIS2.basis: Involved in transcriptional regulation. Binds to HOX or PBX proteins to form dimers ... involved in the transcriptional activation of EPHA8 in the developing midbrain

MEN1.job: helps control which genes are switched on, keeping cell growth in check
MEN1.basis: Essential component of a MLL/SET1 histone methyltransferase (HMT) complex ... Functions as a transcriptional regulator ... Plays a role in TGFB1-mediated inhibition of cell-proliferation

MERTK.job: helps cells swallow and clear away dead cells, including worn-out bits of the eye's light sensors
MERTK.basis: phagocytosis of apoptotic cells (efferocytosis) ... Functions in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) as a regulator of rod outer segments fragments phagocytosis

MET.job: picks up a growth signal that tells cells to grow, move and survive
MET.basis: Receptor tyrosine kinase that transduces signals from the extracellular matrix into the cytoplasm by binding to hepatocyte growth factor/HGF ligand. Regulates many physiological processes including proliferation, scattering, morphogenesis and survival

METTL23.job: tags DNA's packaging to help switch genes on
METTL23.basis: Histone methyltransferase that dimethylates histone H3 ... leading to activate transcription via chromatin remodeling
METTL23.alt: adds chemical tags to DNA-packing proteins that help switch genes on

MFN2.job: helps the cell's power plants fuse together
MFN2.basis: Mitochondrial outer membrane GTPase that mediates mitochondrial clustering and fusion

MFSD8.job: lets chloride flow through the walls of the cell's recycling centers
MFSD8.basis: Outward-rectifying chloride channel involved in endolysosomal chloride homeostasis

MGME1.job: trims DNA to help maintain the genetic material inside the cell's power plants
MGME1.basis: single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) exonuclease involved in mitochondrial genome maintenance

MGP.job: sits in bone and cartilage and helps hold back bone formation
MGP.basis: Associates with the organic matrix of bone and cartilage. Thought to act as an inhibitor of bone formation

MICOS13.job: helps shape the inner folds of mitochondria, the cell's power plants
MICOS13.basis: Component of the MICOS complex, a large protein complex of the mitochondrial inner membrane that plays crucial roles in the maintenance of crista junctions, inner membrane architecture ... required for the formation of cristae junction (CJ) and maintenance of cristae morphology

MICU1.job: senses calcium and controls when the cell's power plants let calcium in
MICU1.basis: Calcium sensor of the mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) channel ... At low calcium levels, MICU1 occludes the pore of the MCU channel, preventing mitochondrial calcium uptake ... At higher calcium levels ... allowing calcium permeation through the MCU channel

MID1.job: tags another protein so the cell can break down a key enzyme
MID1.basis: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that promotes the monoubiquitination of IGBP1, which results in deprotection of the catalytic subunit of protein phosphatase PP2A, and its subsequent degradation

MINAR2.job: is thought to help manage cholesterol in the inner ear's hair cells
MINAR2.basis: Binds cholesterol and may regulate the distribution and homeostasis of cholesterol in hair cells
MINAR2.alt: may help manage cholesterol in the inner ear's hair cells

MINPP1.job: trims phosphate tags off small messenger molecules that steer many cell activities
MINPP1.basis: Multiple inositol polyphosphate phosphatase that hydrolyzes ... to a range of less phosphorylated inositol phosphates. This regulates the availability of these various small molecule second messengers and metal chelators which control many aspects of cell physiology

MITF.job: switches on the genes that let pigment cells develop and make color
MITF.basis: Transcription factor that acts as a master regulator of melanocyte survival and differentiation as well as melanosome biogenesis ... found in the promoter of pigmentation genes, such as tyrosinase (TYR)

MKKS.job: helps assemble a protein kit that builds the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
MKKS.basis: Probable molecular chaperone that assists the folding of proteins ... Plays a role in the assembly of BBSome, a complex involved in ciliogenesis

MKS1.job: forms a gate at the base of the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
MKS1.basis: Component of the tectonic-like complex, a complex localized at the transition zone of primary cilia and acting as a barrier that prevents diffusion of transmembrane proteins between the cilia and plasma membranes ... Required for ciliary structure and function

MLC1.job: helps brain support cells control their water and salt balance
MLC1.basis: Transmembrane protein mainly expressed in brain astrocytes ... Regulates the response of astrocytes to hypo-osmosis by promoting calcium influx ... May function as regulatory protein of membrane protein complexes such as ion channels

MLH1.job: helps fix spelling mistakes made when DNA is copied
MLH1.basis: a component of the post-replicative DNA mismatch repair system (MMR) ... assure that only the newly mutated DNA strand is going to be corrected

MLYCD.job: helps muscles balance burning sugar and burning fat
MLYCD.basis: Catalyzes the conversion of malonyl-CoA to acetyl-CoA ... Plays a role in the metabolic balance between glucose and lipid oxidation in muscle

MMAA.job: helps deliver vitamin B12 where the cell's power plants need it
MMAA.basis: Involved in intracellular vitamin B12 metabolism, mediates the transport of cobalamin (Cbl) into mitochondria ... assists AdoCbl cofactor delivery from MMAB to the methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (MMUT)
MMAA.alt: helps deliver vitamin B12 to an enzyme in the cell's power plants

MMAB.job: turns vitamin B12 into the active form one enzyme needs to work
MMAB.basis: Converts cob(I)alamin to adenosylcobalamin (adenosylcob(III)alamin), a coenzyme for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, therefore participates in the final step of the vitamin B12 conversion ... directly delivers the cofactor to MUT

MMACHC.job: helps turn vitamin B12 from food into forms the body can use
MMACHC.basis: Cobalamin (vitamin B12) cytosolic chaperone ... Cyanocobalamin constitutes the inactive form of vitamin B12 introduced from the diet, and is converted into the active cofactors methylcobalamin (MeCbl) ... and 5'-deoxyadenosylcobalamin (AdoCbl)

MMADHC.job: helps cells process vitamin B12 into its two working forms
MMADHC.basis: Involved in cobalamin metabolism and trafficking ... Plays a role in regulating the biosynthesis and the proportion of two coenzymes, methylcob(III)alamin (MeCbl) and 5'-deoxyadenosylcobalamin (AdoCbl)

MME.job: breaks down small signaling proteins, including the body's natural painkillers
MME.basis: almost confined on acting on polypeptides of up to 30 amino acids ... Biologically important in the destruction of opioid peptides such as Met- and Leu-enkephalins ... Catalyzes cleavage of bradykinin, substance P and neurotensin peptides

MMUT.job: helps break down certain amino acids and fats so cells can use them for energy
MMUT.basis: Catalyzes the reversible isomerization of methylmalonyl-CoA (MMCoA) (generated from branched-chain amino acid metabolism and degradation of dietary odd chain fatty acids and cholesterol) to succinyl-CoA ... a key intermediate of the tricarboxylic acid cycle

MN1.job: switches on genes that help the roof of the mouth and skull bones form
MN1.basis: Transcriptional activator which specifically regulates expression of TBX22 in the posterior region of the developing palate ... Necessary for normal development of the membranous bones of the skull

MOCOS.job: helps activate a metal-containing helper that certain enzymes need
MOCOS.basis: Sulfurates the molybdenum cofactor ... Sulfation of molybdenum is essential for xanthine dehydrogenase (XDH) and aldehyde oxidase (ADO) enzymes
MOCOS.alt: adds sulfur to a metal-containing helper that certain enzymes need to work

MOCS1.job: helps make a metal-containing helper that certain enzymes need
MOCS1.basis: Isoform MOCS1A and isoform MOCS1B probably form a complex that catalyzes the conversion of 5'-GTP to cyclic pyranopterin monophosphate (cPMP) ... MOCS1A catalyzes the cyclization of GTP ... MOCS1B catalyzes the subsequent conversion ... to cPMP
MOCS1.alt: converts GTP, a common cell molecule, into a ring-shaped compound called cPMP

MOCS2.job: helps make molybdopterin, a helper molecule, by adding sulfur to its precursor
MOCS2.basis: Catalytic subunit of the molybdopterin synthase complex, a complex that catalyzes the conversion of precursor Z into molybdopterin ... mediating the incorporation of 2 sulfur atoms from thiocarboxylated MOCS2A into precursor Z

MOGS.job: trims a sugar from sugar chains being added to newly made proteins
MOGS.basis: cleaves the distal alpha 1,2-linked glucose residue from the Glc(3)Man(9)GlcNAc(2) oligosaccharide precursor

MORC2.job: packs DNA tightly to keep certain genes and jumping DNA switched off
MORC2.basis: ATP-dependent chromatin remodeler essential for epigenetic silencing by the HUSH (human silencing hub) complex ... Represses germ cell-related genes and L1 retrotransposons

MPC1.job: carries a sugar breakdown product into the cell's power plants to make energy
MPC1.basis: Mediates the uptake of pyruvate into mitochondria to maintain the balance between glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation

MPDU1.job: helps cells use a sugar donor to build sugar chains on proteins
MPDU1.basis: Required for normal utilization of mannose-dolichol phosphate (Dol-P-Man) in the synthesis of N-linked and O-linked oligosaccharides and GPI anchors

MPI.job: turns one sugar into another, mannose, used to coat proteins with sugar chains
MPI.basis: catalyzes the interconversion of fructose-6-P and mannose-6-P and has a critical role in the supply of D-mannose derivatives required for many eukaryotic glycosylation reactions

MPIG6B.job: keeps platelet-making cells and platelets from becoming overactive
MPIG6B.basis: Inhibitory receptor that acts as a critical regulator of hematopoietic lineage differentiation, megakaryocyte function and platelet production ... Inhibits platelet aggregation and activation

MPL.job: picks up the hormone signal that tells the body to make platelets
MPL.basis: Receptor for thrombopoietin that regulates hematopoietic stem cell renewal, megakaryocyte differentiation, and platelet formation ... ultimately leading to increased platelet production

MPV17.job: helps keep the DNA inside mitochondria, the cell's power plants, healthy
MPV17.basis: Non-selective channel that modulates the membrane potential ... and is involved in mitochondrial homeostasis ... Involved in mitochondrial deoxynucleoside triphosphates (dNTP) pool homeostasis and mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) maintenance

MPZ.job: holds together the insulating layers wrapped around nerves in the body
MPZ.basis: adhesion molecule necessary for normal myelination in the peripheral nervous system ... mediates adhesion between adjacent myelin wraps and ultimately drives myelin compaction

MPZL2.job: helps cells of the same kind stick to each other

MRPL44.job: is part of the machine that builds proteins inside the cell's power plants
MRPL44.basis: Component of the 39S subunit of mitochondrial ribosome

MSH2.job: spots and helps fix spelling mistakes made when DNA is copied
MSH2.basis: Component of the post-replicative DNA mismatch repair system (MMR) ... which binds to DNA mismatches thereby initiating DNA repair

MSH6.job: spots and helps fix spelling mistakes made when DNA is copied
MSH6.basis: Component of the post-replicative DNA mismatch repair system (MMR) ... binds to DNA mismatches thereby initiating DNA repair

MSL3.job: is part of a team that tags DNA's packaging to keep it loose
MSL3.basis: Non-catalytic component of the MSL histone acetyltransferase complex ... mediates the majority of histone H4 acetylation at 'Lys-16' (H4K16ac), an epigenetic mark that prevents chromatin compaction

MSN.job: links the cell's inner scaffolding to its outer membrane, shaping cells
MSN.basis: connects the actin cytoskeleton to the plasma membrane ... These rearrangements regulate many cellular processes, including cell shape determination

MSRB3.job: repairs proteins damaged by oxidation, and is needed for hearing
MSRB3.basis: Catalyzes the reduction of free and protein-bound methionine sulfoxide to methionine. Isoform 2 is essential for hearing

MSTO1.job: helps the cell's energy factories merge and spread out properly
MSTO1.basis: Involved in the regulation of mitochondrial distribution and morphology ... Required for mitochondrial fusion and mitochondrial network formation

MSX1.job: switches genes off to guide how teeth, the palate and facial bones form
MSX1.basis: Acts as a transcriptional repressor ... Regulates, in a stage-specific manner, a developmental program of gene expression in the fetal tooth bud ... required for correct development and fusion of the palatal shelves and embryonic mandibular formation ... Plays a role in embryonic bone formation of the middle ear, skull and nasal bones

MSX2.job: switches genes on and off to guide bone development
MSX2.basis: Acts as a transcriptional regulator in bone development

MTFMT.job: helps the cell's power plants start making their own proteins
MTFMT.basis: formylates methionyl-tRNA in mitochondria and is crucial for translation initiation

MTHFD1.job: converts the vitamin folate into forms cells use to build DNA and amino acids
MTHFD1.basis: Trifunctional enzyme that catalyzes the interconversion of three forms of one-carbon-substituted tetrahydrofolate ... These derivatives of tetrahydrofolate are differentially required in nucleotide and amino acid biosynthesis

MTM1.job: helps keep skeletal muscle cells in good working shape
MTM1.basis: Lipid phosphatase which dephosphorylates phosphatidylinositol 3-monophosphate (PI3P) ... Required for skeletal muscle maintenance but not for myogenesis

MTMR2.job: removes phosphate tags from fats that help cells recycle their own parts
MTMR2.basis: Lipid phosphatase that specifically dephosphorylates the D-3 position of phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate and phosphatidylinositol 3,5-bisphosphate ... Regulates the level of these phosphoinositides critical for various biological processes including autophagy initiation and autophagosome maturation

MTO1.job: tunes the reading molecules that help mitochondria build their own proteins
MTO1.basis: catalyzes the 5-taurinomethyluridine (taum(5)U) modification at the 34th wobble position (U34) of mitochondrial tRNAs (mt-tRNAs), which plays a role in mt-tRNA decoding and mitochondrial translation

MTOR.job: tells cells when to grow and build, based on available nutrients and energy
MTOR.basis: central regulator of cellular metabolism, growth and survival in response to hormones, growth factors, nutrients, energy and stress signals

MTPAP.job: adds protective tails to genetic messages made inside the cell's power plants
MTPAP.basis: Polymerase that creates the 3' poly(A) tail of mitochondrial transcripts

MTR.job: uses vitamin B12 to turn homocysteine into the amino acid methionine
MTR.basis: Catalyzes the transfer of a methyl group from methylcob(III)alamin (MeCbl) to homocysteine, yielding enzyme-bound cob(I)alamin and methionine ... MeCbl is an active form of cobalamin (vitamin B12) used as a cofactor for methionine biosynthesis

MTRFR.job: frees stuck protein-making machines in the cell's power plants
MTRFR.basis: Part of a mitoribosome-associated quality control pathway that prevents aberrant translation by responding to interruptions during elongation ... ejects the unfinished nascent chain and peptidyl transfer RNA (tRNA), respectively, from stalled ribosomes

MTRR.job: recharges the vitamin B12 that another enzyme needs to make the amino acid methionine
MTRR.basis: Key enzyme in methionine and folate homeostasis responsible for the reactivation of methionine synthase (MTR/MS) activity ... Cobalamin (vitamin B12) forms a complex with MTR ... in order to produce methionine

MTX2.job: helps bring proteins into the cell's power plants
MTX2.basis: Involved in transport of proteins into the mitochondrion

MUSK.job: helps build and maintain the junctions where nerves connect to muscles
MUSK.basis: plays a central role in the formation and the maintenance of the neuromuscular junction (NMJ), the synapse between the motor neuron and the skeletal muscle

MUTYH.job: fixes DNA mistakes caused by oxygen damage by removing wrongly paired letters
MUTYH.basis: Involved in oxidative DNA damage repair ... removing the inappropriately paired adenine base from the DNA backbone

MVK.job: helps cells make cholesterol and related fatty building blocks
MVK.basis: Catalyzes the phosphorylation of mevalonate to mevalonate 5-phosphate, a key step in isoprenoid and cholesterol biosynthesis

MYBPC3.job: helps control how muscle fibers contract, especially in the heart
MYBPC3.basis: Thick filament-associated protein located in the crossbridge region of vertebrate striated muscle a bands ... It may modulate muscle contraction or may play a more structural role

MYCN.basis: Positively regulates the transcription of MYCNOS
MYCN.alt: helps switch on another gene, called MYCNOS

MYH10.job: is a motor protein that helps cells divide and hold their shape
MYH10.basis: Cellular myosin that appears to play a role in cytokinesis, cell shape

MYH11.job: helps smooth muscle contract, like the muscle in blood vessel and gut walls

MYH2.job: powers muscle contraction by pulling on muscle fibers
MYH2.basis: Myosins are actin-based motor molecules with ATPase activity essential for muscle contraction

MYH6.job: is the motor that makes heart muscle contract

MYH7.job: is the motor that makes heart and skeletal muscle contract
MYH7.basis: actin-based motor molecules with ATPase activity essential for muscle contraction ... constitute the fundamental contractile unit of skeletal and cardiac muscle

MYH9.job: acts as a tiny motor that helps cells divide, change shape and move
MYH9.basis: Cellular myosin that appears to play a role in cytokinesis, cell shape ... Promotes cell motility

MYL2.job: helps heart muscle contract with each heartbeat
MYL2.basis: Contractile protein that plays a role in heart development and function ... plays a role in cross-bridge cycling kinetics and cardiac muscle contraction

MYL3.job: is a small part of the motor that makes muscles contract
MYL3.alt: is a small helper piece of myosin, the motor that makes muscles contract

MYLK.job: switches on smooth muscle contraction, like in blood vessels, airways and gut
MYLK.basis: myosin light chain kinase implicated in smooth muscle contraction via phosphorylation of myosin light chains ... Required for tonic airway smooth muscle contraction ... Necessary for gastrointestinal motility ... Implicated in the regulation of endothelial as well as vascular permeability

MYMK.job: helps young muscle cells fuse together to build muscle fibers
MYMK.basis: mediates myoblast fusion, an essential step for the formation of multi-nucleated muscle fibers

MYO15A.job: helps arrange the sound-sensing hairs in the inner ear
MYO15A.basis: Myosins are actin-based motor molecules ... Required for the arrangement of stereocilia in mature hair bundles

MYO18B.job: helps move materials around inside muscle cells
MYO18B.basis: May be involved in intracellular trafficking of the muscle cell when in the cytoplasm, whereas entering the nucleus, may be involved in the regulation of muscle specific genes

MYO3A.job: shapes the inner ear's sound-sensing hairs so we can hear
MYO3A.basis: playing an essential role in hearing ... Required for normal cochlear hair bundle development and hearing ... thereby contributing to the architecture of the hair bundle

MYO5A.job: carries pigment packets and other cargo along the cell's inner tracks
MYO5A.basis: Processive actin-based motor ... Involved in melanosome transport. Also mediates the transport of vesicles to the plasma membrane

MYO6.job: is a tiny motor that carries cargo inside cells, including inner ear hair cells
MYO6.basis: Myosins are actin-based motor molecules ... Unconventional myosins serve in intracellular movements ... Functions in a variety of intracellular processes such as vesicular membrane trafficking ... Required for structural integrity of inner ear hair cells

MYO7A.job: is a tiny motor that moves cargo inside cells of the inner ear and eye
MYO7A.basis: Myosins are actin-based motor molecules ... Unconventional myosins serve in intracellular movements ... In the retina, plays an important role in the renewal of the outer photoreceptor disks ... In the inner ear, plays an important role in differentiation, morphogenesis and organization of cochlear hair cell bundles

MYOC.job: is released by cells to signal neighbors about sticking, shaping and moving
MYOC.basis: Secreted glycoprotein regulating the activation of different signaling pathways in adjacent cells to control different processes including cell adhesion, cell-matrix adhesion, cytoskeleton organization and cell migration

MYPN.job: helps hold together the building blocks of heart and skeletal muscle
MYPN.basis: Component of the sarcomere that tethers together nebulin (skeletal muscle) and nebulette (cardiac muscle) to alpha-actinin, at the Z lines

MYRF.job: switches on genes that build the protective coating around nerves in the brain
MYRF.basis: Myelin regulatory factor, N-terminal component that specifically activates transcription of central nervous system (CNS) myelin genes

MYSM1.job: helps blood stem cells make new blood and immune cells
MYSM1.basis: plays important regulator roles in hematopoietic stem cell function, blood cell production and immune response

MYT1L.job: switches off non-nerve genes so developing cells become nerve cells
MYT1L.basis: Transcription factor that plays a key role in neuronal differentiation by specifically repressing expression of non-neuronal genes during neuron differentiation

NAA10.job: adds a small chemical tag to the starting end of many newly made proteins
NAA10.basis: Catalytic subunit of N-terminal acetyltransferase complexes which display alpha (N-terminal) acetyltransferase activity ... Acetylates amino termini that are devoid of initiator methionine

NAA15.job: helps add a small chemical tag to the starting end of new proteins
NAA15.basis: Auxillary subunit of N-terminal acetyltransferase complexes which display alpha (N-terminal) acetyltransferase (NAT) activity

NACC1.job: switches off certain genes, especially in nerve cells
NACC1.basis: Functions as a transcriptional repressor. Seems to function as a transcriptional corepressor in neuronal cells

NADSYN1.job: makes NAD, a helper molecule cells need to turn food into energy
NADSYN1.basis: Catalyzes the final step of the nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) de novo synthesis pathway

NAF1.job: helps the cell build its protein factories
NAF1.basis: RNA-binding protein required for the maturation of box H/ACA snoRNPs complex and ribosome biogenesis
NAF1.alt: helps assemble small RNA-protein kits the cell needs to build its protein factories

NAGA.job: helps the cell's recycling centers break down sugar-coated fats and proteins
NAGA.basis: Removes terminal alpha-N-acetylgalactosamine residues from glycolipids ... as well as glycopeptides, helping degrade glycoconjugates in the lysosome

NAGLU.job: helps the cell's recycling centers break down long sugar chains
NAGLU.basis: Involved in the degradation of heparan sulfate

NAGS.job: makes a helper molecule that lets the liver clear waste nitrogen as urea
NAGS.basis: Plays a role in the regulation of ureagenesis by producing the essential cofactor N-acetylglutamate (NAG)

NANS.job: helps make sialic acid, a sugar that coats cells
NANS.basis: Catalyzes the condensation of phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) and N-acetylmannosamine 6-phosphate (ManNAc-6-P) to synthesize N-acetylneuraminate-9-phosphate (Neu5Ac-9-P) ... Neu5Ac-9-P and KDN-9-P are the phosphorylated forms of sialic acids

NARS2.job: loads the amino acid asparagine onto its carrier so mitochondria can build proteins
NARS2.basis: Mitochondrial aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase that catalyzes the specific attachment of the asparagine amino acid (aa) to the homologous transfer RNA (tRNA), further participating in protein synthesis

NAXD.job: repairs damaged copies of a key molecule cells use to handle energy
NAXD.basis: the enzyme allows the repair of both epimers of NAD(P)HX, a damaged form of NAD(P)H

NAXE.job: helps repair a damaged form of a key energy-carrying molecule in cells
NAXE.basis: Catalyzes the epimerization of the S- and R-forms of NAD(P)HX, a damaged form of NAD(P)H ... This is a prerequisite for the S-specific NAD(P)H-hydrate dehydratase to allow the repair of both epimers of NAD(P)HX

NBEA.job: holds a signaling enzyme in place at the cell's membranes
NBEA.basis: Binds to type II regulatory subunits of protein kinase A and anchors/targets them to the membrane

NBEAL2.job: helps platelets build the storage packets they release to aid healing
NBEAL2.basis: Probably involved in thrombopoiesis. Plays a role in the development or secretion of alpha-granules, that contain several growth factors important for platelet biogenesis

NBN.job: helps gather the repair crew that fixes broken DNA
NBN.basis: Component of the MRN complex, which plays a central role in double-strand break (DSB) repair ... NBN acts as a protein-protein adapter, which specifically recognizes and binds phosphorylated proteins, promoting their recruitment to DNA damage sites

NCKAP1.job: helps cells reshape their inner scaffolding so they can crawl and extend
NCKAP1.basis: Part of the WAVE complex that regulates lamellipodia formation ... regulates actin filament reorganization

NDE1.job: helps dividing cells sort their chromosomes, building the brain's outer layer
NDE1.basis: Required for centrosome duplication and formation and function of the mitotic spindle. Essential for the development of the cerebral cortex.

NDP.job: signals blood vessels to grow in the retina at the back of the eye
NDP.basis: Plays a central role in retinal vascularization by acting as a ligand for FZD4

NDUFA12.job: helps the cell's power plants turn food into energy
NDUFA12.basis: Accessory subunit of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I), that is believed not to be involved in catalysis ... Complex I functions in the transfer of electrons from NADH to the respiratory chain
NDUFA12.alt: is a helper piece in the alpha section of the cell power plant's first energy machine

NDUFA2.job: helps the cell's power plants turn food into energy
NDUFA2.basis: Accessory subunit of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I), that is believed not to be involved in catalysis. Complex I functions in the transfer of electrons from NADH to the respiratory chain
NDUFA2.alt: is a helper piece of the first machine in the cell's power plants that turns food into energy

NDUFAF2.job: helps assemble the machinery that makes energy inside cells' power plants
NDUFAF2.basis: Acts as a molecular chaperone for mitochondrial complex I assembly ... Complex I functions in the transfer of electrons from NADH to the respiratory chain

NDUFAF3.job: helps build the first machine in the cell's energy-making chain
NDUFAF3.basis: Essential factor for the assembly of mitochondrial NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase complex (complex I)

NDUFAF4.job: helps build a key part of the cell's energy-making machinery
NDUFAF4.basis: Involved in the assembly of mitochondrial NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase complex (complex I)

NDUFAF5.job: helps build the first part of the cell's energy-making machinery
NDUFAF5.basis: involved in the assembly of mitochondrial NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase complex (complex I, MT-ND1) at early stages

NDUFAF6.job: helps build the first part of the cell's energy-making machinery
NDUFAF6.basis: Involved in the assembly of mitochondrial NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase complex (complex I) at early stages

NDUFB11.job: helps the cell's power plants turn food into energy
NDUFB11.basis: Accessory subunit of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I), that is believed not to be involved in catalysis. Complex I functions in the transfer of electrons from NADH to the respiratory chain
NDUFB11.alt: is a support piece in the beta section of the first energy-making machine in mitochondria

NDUFB3.job: helps the cell's power plants turn food into energy
NDUFB3.basis: Accessory subunit of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I), that is believed not to be involved in catalysis. Complex I functions in the transfer of electrons from NADH to the respiratory chain
NDUFB3.alt: is a support piece in the beta section of mitochondria's first energy-making machine

NDUFS1.job: is part of the cell's power plant machinery that turns food into energy
NDUFS1.basis: Core subunit of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I) which catalyzes electron transfer from NADH through the respiratory chain

NDUFS2.job: is part of the machinery that helps cells' power plants make energy
NDUFS2.basis: Core subunit of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I) which catalyzes electron transfer from NADH through the respiratory chain

NDUFS4.job: helps the cell's power plants turn food into energy
NDUFS4.basis: Accessory subunit of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I), that is believed not to be involved in catalysis ... Complex I functions in the transfer of electrons from NADH to the respiratory chain
NDUFS4.alt: is a support piece of complex I, which starts energy-making in the cell's power plants

NDUFS6.job: helps the cell's power plants turn food into energy
NDUFS6.basis: Accessory subunit of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I), that is believed not to be involved in catalysis ... Complex I functions in the transfer of electrons from NADH to the respiratory chain
NDUFS6.alt: is a support piece in the iron-sulfur arm of the cell's first energy-making machine

NDUFS7.job: is part of the machinery that makes energy inside the cell's power plants
NDUFS7.basis: Core subunit of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I) which catalyzes electron transfer from NADH through the respiratory chain

NDUFS8.job: is part of the machine in mitochondria that turns food into energy
NDUFS8.basis: Core subunit of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I) which catalyzes electron transfer from NADH through the respiratory chain ... Essential for the catalytic activity and assembly of complex I

NDUFV1.job: helps the cell's power plants turn food into energy
NDUFV1.basis: Core subunit of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I) which catalyzes electron transfer from NADH through the respiratory chain

NDUFV2.job: is part of the machinery that makes energy inside the cell's power plants
NDUFV2.basis: Core subunit of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I) which catalyzes electron transfer from NADH through the respiratory chain

NECTIN1.job: helps cells stick together, guiding how the nervous system develops
NECTIN1.basis: Cell adhesion molecule that promotes cell-cell contacts and plays important roles in the development of the nervous system

NEDD4L.job: tags salt and other channels on the cell surface for removal
NEDD4L.basis: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that mediates the polyubiquitination of lysine and cysteine residues on target proteins ... Promotes ubiquitination and internalization of various plasma membrane channels such as ENaC, SCN2A/Nav1.2

NEFH.job: helps build the internal scaffolding that keeps nerve fibers wide and sturdy
NEFH.basis: Neurofilaments usually contain three intermediate filament proteins: NEFL, NEFM, and NEFH which are involved in the maintenance of neuronal caliber. NEFH has an important function in mature axons

NEFL.job: helps build the inner scaffolding that keeps nerve fibers thick and sturdy
NEFL.basis: Neurofilaments usually contain three intermediate filament proteins: NEFL, NEFM, and NEFH which are involved in the maintenance of neuronal caliber ... to form neuronal filamentous networks

NEK1.job: helps cells repair damaged DNA and build their antenna-like sensing hairs
NEK1.basis: Involved in DNA damage checkpoint control and for proper DNA damage repair ... Involved in cilium assembly

NEK10.job: helps airway cells sweep away mucus
NEK10.basis: Plays a role in the cellular response to UV irradiation. Mediates G2/M cell cycle arrest ... In ciliated cells of airways, it is involved in the regulation of mucociliary transport
NEK10.alt: helps airway cells sweep mucus and makes cells pause dividing after UV damage

NEK8.job: helps keep the kidney's tiny tubes intact and builds cells' hair-like antennae
NEK8.basis: Required for renal tubular integrity ... May regulate ciliary biogenesis through targeting of proteins to the cilia

NEMF.job: helps clear half-made proteins from stalled protein-making machinery in cells
NEMF.basis: mediates the extraction of incompletely synthesized nascent chains from stalled ribosomes as well as their ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation

NEU1.job: helps the cell's recycling centers trim sugar tips off proteins and fats
NEU1.basis: Lysosomal exo-alpha-sialidase that catalyzes the removal of sialic acid (N-acetylneuraminic acid) moieties from glycoproteins and glycolipids

NEXMIF.job: helps young nerve cells grow their branches and stick to each other
NEXMIF.basis: Involved in neurite outgrowth by regulating cell-cell adhesion via the N-cadherin signaling pathway

NF1.job: switches off Ras, a protein that tells cells to grow
NF1.basis: Stimulates the GTPase activity of Ras ... May be a regulator of Ras activity

NF2.job: helps keep cells from dividing too much
NF2.basis: Probable regulator of the Hippo/SWH (Sav/Wts/Hpo) signaling pathway, a signaling pathway that plays a pivotal role in tumor suppression by restricting proliferation ... Suppresses cell proliferation

NFIA.job: is the A-type of nuclear factor 1, which binds DNA to switch genes on
NFIA.basis: Recognizes and binds the palindromic sequence 5'-TTGGCNNNNNGCCAA-3' present in viral and cellular promoters ... These proteins are individually capable of activating transcription
NFIA.alt: attaches to specific DNA spots to switch genes on

NFIB.job: switches on genes needed for the brain to develop properly
NFIB.basis: Transcriptional activator of GFAP, essential for proper brain development

NFIX.job: attaches to DNA to switch genes on
NFIX.basis: Recognizes and binds the palindromic sequence 5'-TTGGCNNNNNGCCAA-3' present in viral and cellular promoters ... These proteins are individually capable of activating transcription
NFIX.alt: latches onto a specific DNA signal in the cell's nucleus to switch genes on

NFKB1.job: switches genes on or off to steer the body's immune defenses
NFKB1.basis: pleiotropic transcription factor ... initiated by a vast array of stimuli related to many biological processes such as inflammation, immunity ... Different dimer combinations act as transcriptional activators or repressors ... located in the enhancer region of genes involved in immune response and acute phase reactions
NFKB1.alt: switches genes on or off to steer immune defenses and inflammation

NFKB2.job: helps switch on genes for the body's immune defenses
NFKB2.basis: NF-kappa-B is a pleiotropic transcription factor ... The NF-kappa-B heterodimeric RelB-p52 complex is a transcriptional activator ... p52 binds to the kappa-B consensus sequence 5'-GGRNNYYCC-3', located in the enhancer region of genes involved in immune response and acute phase reactions

NFKBIA.job: keeps a key inflammation switch locked outside the cell's control center until needed
NFKBIA.basis: Inhibits the activity of dimeric NF-kappa-B/REL complexes by trapping REL (RELA/p65 and NFKB1/p50) dimers in the cytoplasm ... On cellular stimulation by immune and pro-inflammatory responses, becomes phosphorylated promoting ubiquitination and degradation, enabling the dimeric RELA to translocate to the nucleus and activate transcription

NFU1.job: builds tiny iron-sulfur parts and delivers them to other proteins
NFU1.basis: Iron-sulfur cluster scaffold protein which can assemble [4Fe-4S] clusters and deliver them to target proteins

NGF.job: helps the nerves that sense pain and touch grow and survive
NGF.basis: Nerve growth factor is important for the development and maintenance of the sympathetic and sensory nervous systems ... activates cellular signaling cascades to regulate neuronal proliferation, differentiation and survival

NGLY1.job: strips sugar tags off faulty proteins so the cell can break them down
NGLY1.basis: mediates deglycosylation of N-linked glycoproteins ... recognizes misfolded proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum that are exported to the cytosol to be destroyed and catalyzes their deglycosylation, a prerequisite for subsequent proteasome-mediated degradation

NHEJ1.job: helps hold broken DNA ends together so they can be rejoined
NHEJ1.basis: DNA repair protein involved in DNA non-homologous end joining (NHEJ); it is required for double-strand break (DSB) repair ... holding together the broken DNA until it is repaired

NHLRC1.job: helps cells clear away abnormal sugar clumps and misfolded proteins
NHLRC1.basis: involved in the clearance of toxic polyglucosan and protein aggregates via multiple pathways ... suppresses the cellular toxicity of misfolded proteins by promoting their degradation ... thus decreasing glycogen accumulation

NHS.job: helps shape the eyes, teeth, brain and face as they develop
NHS.basis: Involved in the regulation eye, tooth, brain and craniofacial development

NIPBL.job: loads a ring-shaped protein onto DNA that holds and organizes the strands
NIPBL.basis: Plays an important role in the loading of the cohesin complex on to DNA ... mediates the loading of the cohesin complex onto chromatin

NKX2-1.job: switches on the genes the thyroid needs to make its hormones
NKX2-1.basis: Transcription factor that binds and activates the promoter of thyroid specific genes such as thyroglobulin, thyroperoxidase, and thyrotropin receptor ... Crucial in the maintenance of the thyroid differentiation phenotype

NKX2-5.job: switches on genes that help the heart and spleen develop
NKX2-5.basis: Transcription factor required for the development of the heart and the spleen

NLGN4X.job: helps nerve cells stick together where they connect
