NLGN4X.basis: Cell surface protein involved in cell-cell-interactions via its interactions with neurexin family members

NNT.job: helps the cell's power plants recharge molecules that neutralize harmful byproducts
NNT.basis: The transhydrogenation between NADH and NADP is coupled to respiration ... functions as a proton pump across the membrane ... May play a role in reactive oxygen species (ROS) detoxification in the adrenal gland

NOD2.job: detects bits of bacteria and alerts the immune system, especially in the gut
NOD2.basis: Pattern recognition receptor (PRR) that detects bacterial peptidoglycan fragments and other danger signals and plays an important role in gastrointestinal immunity ... This in turn leads to the transcriptional activation of hundreds of genes involved in immune response

NODAL.job: helps an early embryo form its middle tissue layer and body layout
NODAL.basis: Essential for mesoderm formation and axial patterning during embryonic development

NOG.job: blocks bone-building signals so joints and cartilage form properly
NOG.basis: Inhibitor of bone morphogenetic proteins (BMP) signaling ... Essential for cartilage morphogenesis and joint formation

NONO.job: grabs DNA and RNA in the cell's nucleus to help edit and control genes
NONO.basis: DNA- and RNA binding protein, involved in several nuclear processes ... Involved in pre-mRNA splicing ... NONO is involved in transcriptional regulation

NOTCH1.job: picks up signals from neighboring cells that help decide what each cell becomes
NOTCH1.basis: Functions as a receptor for membrane-bound ligands Jagged-1 (JAG1), Jagged-2 (JAG2) and Delta-1 (DLL1) to regulate cell-fate determination

NOTCH2.job: picks up signals from neighboring cells that help decide what each cell becomes
NOTCH2.basis: Functions as a receptor for membrane-bound ligands Jagged-1 (JAG1), Jagged-2 (JAG2) and Delta-1 (DLL1) to regulate cell-fate determination

NOTCH3.job: picks up signals from neighboring cells that help decide what a cell becomes
NOTCH3.basis: Functions as a receptor for membrane-bound ligands Jagged1, Jagged2 and Delta1 to regulate cell-fate determination

NOVA2.job: edits gene messages in nerve cells so the brain wires up properly
NOVA2.basis: Functions to regulate alternative splicing in neurons by binding pre-mRNA ... being essential for central nervous system development by regulating neural networks wiring

NPC1.job: moves cholesterol out of the cell's recycling centers so the cell can use it
NPC1.basis: Intracellular cholesterol transporter which acts in concert with NPC2 and plays an important role in the egress of cholesterol from the endosomal/lysosomal compartment ... Mediates cholesterol transfer from lysosomes to endoplasmic reticulum

NPC2.job: helps move cholesterol out of the cell's recycling centers
NPC2.basis: Intracellular cholesterol transporter which acts in concert with NPC1 and plays an important role in the egress of cholesterol from the lysosomal compartment

NPHP1.job: helps kidney cells organize the junctions that hold them together
NPHP1.basis: Involved in the organization of apical junctions in kidney cells together with NPHP4 and RPGRIP1L/NPHP8

NPHP3.job: helps cells build and run their antenna-like sensing hairs
NPHP3.basis: Required for normal ciliary development and function

NPHS1.job: helps build the kidney's filter that keeps proteins in the blood
NPHS1.basis: Seems to play a role in the development or function of the kidney glomerular filtration barrier. Regulates glomerular vascular permeability.

NPRL2.job: tells cells to slow their growth when nutrients run low
NPRL2.basis: functions as an inhibitor of the amino acid-sensing branch of the mTORC1 pathway ... In response to amino acid depletion ... inhibiting mTORC1 signaling

NPRL3.job: helps cells slow their growth when nutrients run low
NPRL3.basis: functions as an inhibitor of the amino acid-sensing branch of the mTORC1 pathway ... In response to amino acid depletion ... inhibiting mTORC1 signaling

NR2E3.job: switches on genes that make the eye's rod cells and keeps cone genes off
NR2E3.basis: Transcriptional factor that is an activator of rod development and repressor of cone development ... Enhances rhodopsin expression. Represses M- and S-cone opsin expression

NR2F1.job: switches other genes on or off by binding to DNA
NR2F1.basis: transcription factor binds to the ovalbumin promoter and ... stimulates initiation of transcription ... Represses transcriptional activity of LHCG

NR2F2.job: switches genes on or off, including some that guide early ovary development
NR2F2.basis: Ligand-activated transcription factor ... May be required to establish ovary identity during early gonad development

NR3C2.job: responds to the hormone aldosterone to help the body hold salt and water
NR3C2.basis: Receptor for both mineralocorticoids (MC) such as aldosterone ... The effect of MC is to increase ion and water transport and thus raise extracellular fluid volume and blood pressure

NR4A2.job: switches on genes that help dopamine-making brain cells develop and survive
NR4A2.basis: Transcriptional regulator which is important for the differentiation and maintenance of meso-diencephalic dopaminergic (mdDA) neurons during development ... It is crucial for expression of a set of genes

NR5A1.job: switches on genes that form the sex organs and the glands that make steroid hormones
NR5A1.basis: Transcriptional activator. Essential for sexual differentiation and formation of the primary steroidogenic tissues

NRAS.job: passes on signals that tell cells to grow, divide and survive
NRAS.basis: Signal transducer in the Ras-MAPK signaling pathway that regulates cell proliferation and survival

NRL.job: switches on genes that rod cells in the eye need to sense light
NRL.basis: Acts as a transcriptional activator which regulates the expression of several rod-specific genes, including RHO and PDE6B

NRROS.job: switches on a key growth signal that the brain's immune cells need
NRROS.basis: Key regulator of transforming growth factor beta-1 (TGFB1) specifically required for microglia function in the nervous system ... Required for activation of latent TGF-beta-1 in macrophages and microglia

NRXN1.job: helps nerve cells link up and form connections with each other
NRXN1.basis: Neuronal cell surface protein involved in cell recognition and cell adhesion ... Plays a role in formation of synaptic junctions

NSD1.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging proteins to turn genes up or down
NSD1.basis: Histone methyltransferase that dimethylates Lys-36 of histone H3 (H3K36me2) ... capable of both negatively or positively influencing transcription

NSD2.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging proteins to help control which genes are on
NSD2.basis: Histone methyltransferase which specifically dimethylates nucleosomal histone H3 at 'Lys-36' (H3K36me2) ... By methylating histone H3 at 'Lys-36', involved in the regulation of gene transcription during various biological processes

NSUN2.job: adds chemical tags to RNA messages that keep them stable and help make proteins
NSUN2.basis: methylates cytosine to 5-methylcytosine (m5C) in various RNAs, such as tRNAs, mRNAs ... acts by increasing protein synthesis; cytosine C(5)-methylation promoting tRNA stability and preventing mRNA decay

NTHL1.job: removes chemically damaged letters from DNA so they can be repaired
NTHL1.basis: catalyzes the first step in base excision repair (BER), the primary repair pathway for the repair of oxidative DNA damage ... The DNA N-glycosylase activity releases the damaged DNA base from DNA

NTRK1.job: picks up nerve growth signals that help nerve cells develop and survive
NTRK1.basis: Receptor tyrosine kinase involved in the development and the maturation of the central and peripheral nervous systems through regulation of proliferation, differentiation and survival of sympathetic and nervous neurons. High affinity receptor for NGF which is its primary ligand

NUBPL.job: helps build the cell's main energy-making machinery in mitochondria
NUBPL.basis: involved in the assembly of the mitochondrial membrane respiratory chain NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I)

NUP188.job: is part of the gateways that let molecules in and out of the cell's nucleus
NUP188.basis: Component of the nuclear pore complex (NPC), a complex required for the trafficking across the nuclear envelope ... Required for proper protein transport into the nucleus

NUP93.job: helps build the pores that let molecules in and out of the cell's nucleus
NUP93.basis: Plays a role in the nuclear pore complex (NPC) assembly and/or maintenance

NUS1.job: helps make a fatty carrier that attaches sugars to newly made proteins
NUS1.basis: forms the dehydrodolichyl diphosphate synthase (DDS) complex, an essential component of the dolichol monophosphate (Dol-P) biosynthetic machinery ... a precursor of dolichol phosphate which is utilized as a sugar carrier in protein glycosylation

NYX.job: helps the retina pass on light signals for normal vision
NYX.basis: Required for normal vision. Is a critical factor for light-induced depolarization of retinal ON-bipolar cells

OAT.job: converts the amino acid ornithine into building blocks for other amino acids
OAT.basis: Catalyzes the reversible interconversion of L-ornithine and 2-oxoglutarate to L-glutamate semialdehyde and L-glutamate

OCA2.job: helps cells make the pigment that colors skin, hair and eyes
OCA2.basis: modulates melanosomal pH for optimal tyrosinase activity required for melanogenesis ... One of the components of the mammalian pigmentary system ... ethnic skin color variation ... Major determinant of brown and/or blue eye color

OCRL.job: trims a fatty signal tag from cell membranes to steer traffic inside cells
OCRL.basis: Catalyzes the hydrolysis of the 5-position phosphate of phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PtdIns(4,5)P2) ... Regulates traffic in the endosomal pathway by regulating the specific pool of phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate that is associated with endosomes

ODAD1.job: helps attach the motors that make the cell's tiny hairs beat
ODAD1.basis: Component of the outer dynein arm-docking complex (ODA-DC) that mediates outer dynein arms (ODA) binding onto the doublet microtubule ... onto ciliary microtubules

ODAD2.job: helps attach the motors that make the cell's tiny hairs beat
ODAD2.basis: mediates outer dynein arms (ODA) binding onto the doublet microtubule ... Involved in mediating assembly of both ODAs and their axonemal docking complex onto ciliary microtubules

ODAD3.job: helps anchor the motors that make the cell's tiny hairs beat
ODAD3.basis: Component of the outer dynein arm-docking complex (ODA-DC) that mediates outer dynein arms (ODA) binding onto the doublet microtubule ... Involved in mediating assembly of both ODAs and their axonemal docking complex onto ciliary microtubules

ODAD4.job: helps anchor the motors that make the cell's hair-like cilia beat
ODAD4.basis: Component of the outer dynein arm-docking complex (ODA-DC) that mediates outer dynein arms (ODA) binding onto the doublet microtubule ... the docking of ODA in ciliary axoneme

OFD1.job: helps cells build their antenna-like sensing hairs
OFD1.basis: Involved in the biogenesis of the cilium ... The cilium is a cell surface projection found in many vertebrate cells required to transduce signals

OGDH.job: helps cells burn sugar, fat and protein for energy
OGDH.basis: Plays a key role in the Krebs (citric acid) cycle, which is a common pathway for oxidation of fuel molecules, including carbohydrates, fatty acids, and amino acids

OPA1.job: helps fuse and shape the cell's energy-making mitochondria
OPA1.basis: essential for normal mitochondrial morphology by mediating fusion of the mitochondrial inner membranes, regulating cristae morphology and maintaining respiratory chain function

OPHN1.job: helps brain cells build and keep the connections they use to signal
OPHN1.basis: implicated in growth and stabilization of dendritic spines, and therefore in synaptic function

OPN1LW.job: senses red light in the eye's color-detecting cells
OPN1LW.basis: G protein-coupled photoreceptor that selectively activates transducin G alpha protein (G(t)) in response to long-wavelength (red) light ... Mediates visual perception of red light in cone photoreceptor cells

OPN1MW.job: senses green light in the eye, helping you see color
OPN1MW.basis: G protein-coupled photoreceptor that selectively activates transducin G alpha protein (G(t)) in response to medium-wavelength (green) light ... Mediates visual perception of green light in cone photoreceptor cells

OPTN.job: helps cells sort and ship materials and clear out invading bacteria
OPTN.basis: Plays an important role in the maintenance of the Golgi complex, in membrane trafficking ... Autophagy receptor that interacts directly with both the cargo to become degraded ... targets ubiquitin-coated bacteria (xenophagy)

ORC6.job: marks the spots where cells start copying their DNA
ORC6.basis: Component of the origin recognition complex (ORC) that binds origins of replication ... ORC is required to assemble the pre-replication complex necessary to initiate DNA replication

OSTM1.job: helps bone-clearing cells and pigment-making cells mature and work
OSTM1.basis: Required for osteoclast and melanocyte maturation and function

OTC.job: helps the liver turn toxic ammonia into urea to be flushed out
OTC.basis: Catalyzes the second step of the urea cycle ... The urea cycle ensures the detoxification of ammonia by converting it to urea for excretion

OTOA.job: helps hold parts of the inner ear in place by sticking them together
OTOA.basis: May act as an adhesion molecule
OTOA.alt: helps cells stick to each other or to their surroundings

OTOF.job: helps inner ear hair cells release chemical signals that carry sound to nerves
OTOF.basis: Key calcium ion sensor involved in the Ca(2+)-triggered synaptic vesicle-plasma membrane fusion and in the control of neurotransmitter release ... at ribbon synapses of cochlear inner hair cells (IHCs) to trigger exocytosis of neurotransmitter

OTOG.job: helps anchor the gel-like membranes that sense sound and balance in the inner ear
OTOG.basis: Glycoprotein specific to acellular membranes of the inner ear. May be required for the anchoring of the otoconial membranes and cupulae to the underlying neuroepithelia in the vestibule ... the tectorial membrane in the cochlea

OTOGL.job: links the inner ear's sound-sensing hairs to the membrane above them
OTOGL.basis: Non-collagenous component of the tectorial membrane (TM) ... forms the links connecting outer hair cell stereocilia to the tectorial membrane, thereby ensuring efficient mechanical coupling and normal cochlear amplification

OTUD6B.job: helps control how much protein the cell makes
OTUD6B.basis: Deubiquitinating enzyme that may play a role in the ubiquitin-dependent regulation of protein synthesis ... modify its ubiquitination to repress translation
OTUD6B.alt: removes small protein tags to help control how much protein the cell makes

OTULIN.job: removes chemical tags from proteins to keep inflammation in check
OTULIN.basis: Deubiquitinase that specifically removes linear ('Met-1'-linked) polyubiquitin chains ... Acts as a key negative regulator of inflammation by restricting spontaneous inflammation and maintaining immune homeostasis

OXCT1.job: helps the body burn ketones, a fuel made from fat, for energy
OXCT1.basis: Key enzyme for ketone body catabolism ... first, rate-limiting step of ketone body utilization in extrahepatic tissues ... enter the citric acid cycle for energy production

P2RY12.job: senses ADP so platelets clump together to help blood clot
P2RY12.basis: Receptor for ADP and ATP ... Required for normal platelet aggregation and blood coagulation

PACS1.job: helps sort and deliver proteins to their proper places inside the cell
PACS1.basis: Coat protein that is involved in the localization of trans-Golgi network (TGN) membrane proteins ... Controls the endosome-to-Golgi trafficking of furin and mannose-6-phosphate receptor

PACS2.job: helps keep the cell's power plants in close contact with its protein factory
PACS2.basis: Multifunctional sorting protein that controls the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-mitochondria communication, including the apposition of mitochondria with the ER

PAK3.job: helps brain cells form the connections they use to signal each other
PAK3.basis: Plays a role in dendrite spine morphogenesis as well as synapse formation and plasticity ... In hippocampal neurons, necessary for the formation of dendritic spines and excitatory synapses

PARK7.job: protects cells from damage caused by oxidative stress
PARK7.basis: plays an important role in cell protection against oxidative stress and cell death acting as oxidative stress sensor

PARN.job: trims the tails off gene message copies so the cell can break them down
PARN.basis: 3'-exoribonuclease that has a preference for poly(A) tails of mRNAs, thereby efficiently degrading poly(A) tails. Exonucleolytic degradation of the poly(A) tail is often the first step in the decay of eukaryotic mRNAs

PAX1.job: switches on genes that help shape the developing spine before birth
PAX1.basis: This protein is a transcriptional activator ... May play an important role in the normal development of the vertebral column

PAX2.job: switches on genes that help the kidneys, urinary tract, eyes and brain develop
PAX2.basis: Transcription factor that may have a role in kidney cell differentiation ... Has a critical role in the development of the urogenital tract, the eyes, and the CNS

PAX3.job: switches on genes that guide nerve and muscle development
PAX3.basis: Transcription factor ... Involved in neural development and myogenesis

PAX5.job: switches on genes that turn young immune cells into antibody-making B cells
PAX5.basis: Transcription factor that plays an essential role in commitment of lymphoid progenitors to the B-lymphocyte lineage ... activating B-lineage-specific genes ... facilitate the generation of a diverse antibody repertoire

PAX6.job: switches on genes that help the eye, nose, brain and pancreas develop
PAX6.basis: Transcription factor with important functions in the development of the eye, nose, central nervous system and pancreas

PAX9.job: helps teeth, skull bones and several glands form during development
PAX9.basis: Transcription factor required for normal development of thymus, parathyroid glands, ultimobranchial bodies, teeth, skeletal elements of skull and larynx as well as distal limbs

PBX1.job: teams up with other proteins to switch on genes that guide body development
PBX1.basis: Transcription factor which binds the DNA sequence 5'-TGATTGAT-3' as part of a heterodimer with HOX proteins ... Acts as a transcriptional activator ... required for spleen development

PC.job: helps the liver and kidneys make sugar, and other tissues make fats
PC.basis: Catalyzes in a tissue specific manner, the initial reactions of glucose (liver, kidney) and lipid (adipose tissue, liver, brain) synthesis from pyruvate

PCARE.job: helps keep the eye's light-sensing cells healthy for vision
PCARE.basis: Plays an essential role for normal photoreceptor cell maintenance and vision

PCBD1.job: helps recycle a helper molecule and helps switch on certain genes
PCBD1.basis: Involved in tetrahydrobiopterin biosynthesis ... accelerate the formation of quinonoid-BH2 ... Coactivator for HNF1A-dependent transcription

PCCA.job: is part of an enzyme that helps break down certain fats and amino acids
PCCA.basis: one of the 2 subunits of the biotin-dependent propionyl-CoA carboxylase (PCC), a mitochondrial enzyme involved in the catabolism of odd chain fatty acids, branched-chain amino acids isoleucine, threonine, methionine, and valine

PCCB.job: is part of an enzyme that helps break down certain amino acids and fats
PCCB.basis: one of the 2 subunits of the biotin-dependent propionyl-CoA carboxylase (PCC), a mitochondrial enzyme involved in the catabolism of odd chain fatty acids, branched-chain amino acids isoleucine, threonine, methionine, and valine

PCDH19.job: helps cells stick to each other, using calcium

PCGF2.job: helps keep certain genes switched off as the body develops
PCGF2.basis: Transcriptional repressor ... required to maintain the transcriptionally repressive state of many genes, including Hox genes, throughout development

PCK1.job: helps the body make its own sugar when blood sugar runs low
PCK1.basis: acts as the rate-limiting enzyme in gluconeogenesis ... At low glucose levels, it catalyzes the cataplerotic conversion of oxaloacetate to phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), the rate-limiting step in the metabolic pathway that produces glucose from lactate and other precursors

PCNT.job: helps organize the scaffolding that pulls chromosomes apart when cells divide
PCNT.basis: Integral component of the filamentous matrix of the centrosome involved in the initial establishment of organized microtubule arrays in both mitosis and meiosis

PCSK9.job: helps control cholesterol levels in the blood by removing the liver's cholesterol catchers
PCSK9.basis: Crucial player in the regulation of plasma cholesterol homeostasis ... promotes their degradation ... enhance the degradation of the hepatic LDLR

PCYT1A.job: controls the main step in making a key fat of cell membranes
PCYT1A.basis: Catalyzes the key rate-limiting step in the CDP-choline pathway for phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis

PDE6A.job: helps the eye's rod cells turn light into nerve signals
PDE6A.basis: Catalytic alpha subunit of the rod-specific cGMP phosphodiesterase (PDE6) complex, which hydrolyzes 3',5'-cyclic GMP in the phototransduction cascade ... enabling the catalytic subunits to hydrolyze cGMP and thereby mediate visual signal transduction and amplification

PDE6B.job: helps the eye's rod cells turn light into nerve signals
PDE6B.basis: Catalytic beta subunit of the rod-specific cGMP phosphodiesterase (PDE6) complex, which hydrolyzes 3',5'-cyclic GMP in the phototransduction cascade ... enabling the catalytic subunits to hydrolyze cGMP and thereby mediate visual signal transduction and amplification

PDE6C.job: helps the eye's color-sensing cone cells turn light into nerve signals
PDE6C.basis: Catalytic alpha subunit of the cone-specific cGMP phosphodiesterase (PDE6) complex, which hydrolyzes 3',5'-cyclic GMP as part of the phototransduction cascade ... mediate visual signal transduction and amplification

PDE6G.job: acts as a brake on an enzyme that helps the eye's rod cells sense light
PDE6G.basis: Inhibitory gamma subunit of the rod-specific cGMP phosphodiesterase (PDE6) complex ... in the phototransduction cascade ... Light-activated GNAT1 relieves gamma subunit-mediated inhibition

PDGFRA.job: picks up growth signals that guide how cells grow, move and develop
PDGFRA.basis: cell-surface receptor for PDGFA, PDGFB and PDGFC and plays an essential role in the regulation of embryonic development, cell proliferation, survival and chemotaxis

PDHA1.job: helps cells turn sugar into fuel their power plants can burn
PDHA1.basis: The PDH complex catalyzes the overall conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA and CO(2), and thereby links cytoplasmic glycolysis and the mitochondrial tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle

PDHX.job: holds together a cell machine that turns sugar breakdown products into fuel
PDHX.basis: Required for anchoring dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase (E3) to the dihydrolipoamide transacetylase (E2) core of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complexes ... This specific binding is essential for a functional PDH complex

PDK3.job: helps cells switch from burning sugar to burning fat, especially during fasting
PDK3.basis: Inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase activity ... and thereby regulates glucose metabolism and aerobic respiration ... Decreases glucose utilization and increases fat metabolism in response to prolonged fasting

PDX1.job: switches on the insulin gene and helps the pancreas develop
PDX1.basis: Activates insulin ... gene transcription ... During development, specifies the early pancreatic epithelium, permitting its proliferation, branching and subsequent differentiation

PDZD7.job: helps organize the links that hold the inner ear's sound-sensing hairs together
PDZD7.basis: In cochlear developing hair cells, essential in organizing the USH2 complex at stereocilia ankle links

PEPD.job: breaks down small protein pieces left over from recycling collagen
PEPD.basis: Dipeptidase that catalyzes the hydrolysis of dipeptides with a prolyl (Xaa-Pro) or hydroxyprolyl residue in the C-terminal position ... Plays an important role in collagen metabolism

PET100.job: helps build the final energy-making machine inside the cell's power plants
PET100.basis: Plays an essential role in mitochondrial complex IV maturation and assembly

PEX1.job: recycles a helper protein that brings cargo into the cell's peroxisomes
PEX1.basis: mediates the ATP-dependent extraction of the PEX5 receptor from peroxisomal membranes, an essential step for PEX5 recycling ... release of bound cargo from PEX5

PEX11B.job: helps peroxisomes, the cell's small fat-processing compartments, grow and divide
PEX11B.basis: Involved in peroxisomal proliferation ... May regulate peroxisome division ... Promotes membrane protrusion and elongation on the peroxisomal surface

PEX12.job: helps recycle the courier that brings supplies into peroxisomes, the cell's fat-processing compartments
PEX12.basis: Component of a retrotranslocation channel required for peroxisome organization by mediating export of the PEX5 receptor from peroxisomes to the cytosol, thereby promoting PEX5 recycling

PEX13.job: forms a doorway that lets proteins into the cell's fat-processing compartments
PEX13.basis: Component of the PEX13-PEX14 docking complex, a translocon channel that specifically mediates the import of peroxisomal cargo proteins ... forms a large import pore

PEX14.job: forms a doorway that lets proteins into peroxisomes, the cell's fat-processing compartments
PEX14.basis: Component of the PEX13-PEX14 docking complex, a translocon channel that specifically mediates the import of peroxisomal cargo proteins ... forms a large import pore

PEX16.job: helps build the outer wall of peroxisomes, small compartments that break down fats
PEX16.basis: Required for peroxisome membrane biogenesis. May play a role in early stages of peroxisome assembly

PEX19.job: helps build peroxisomes, the cell's fat-processing compartments, by delivering their membrane proteins
PEX19.basis: Necessary for early peroxisomal biogenesis ... targets them to the peroxisome membrane

PEX2.job: helps build peroxisomes, the cell's small compartments that break down fats
PEX2.basis: required for peroxisome organization by mediating export of the PEX5 receptor from peroxisomes to the cytosol, thereby promoting PEX5 recycling

PEX26.job: anchors helper proteins to peroxisomes, the cell's small fat-processing compartments
PEX26.basis: Peroxisomal docking factor that anchors PEX1 and PEX6 to peroxisome membranes

PEX3.job: helps build peroxisomes, the cell's small compartments that process fats
PEX3.basis: Involved in peroxisome biosynthesis and integrity ... is necessary for the import of peroxisomal membrane proteins in the peroxisomes

PEX5.job: carries other proteins into peroxisomes, small compartments that break down fats
PEX5.basis: Receptor that mediates peroxisomal import of proteins ... Binds to cargo proteins containing a PTS1 peroxisomal targeting signal in the cytosol, and translocates them into the peroxisome matrix

PEX6.job: helps recycle the shuttle that brings supplies into peroxisomes, the cell's fat-processing compartments
PEX6.basis: mediates the ATP-dependent extraction of the PEX5 receptor from peroxisomal membranes, an essential step for PEX5 recycling ... release of bound cargo from PEX5

PEX7.job: brings certain proteins into peroxisomes, the cell's fat-processing compartments
PEX7.basis: Receptor required for the peroxisomal import of proteins containing an N-terminal PTS2-type peroxisomal targeting signal ... Specifically binds to cargo proteins containing a PTS2 peroxisomal targeting signal in the cytosol

PFN1.job: helps shape the cell's internal scaffolding by controlling how actin fibers grow
PFN1.basis: Binds to actin and affects the structure of the cytoskeleton. At high concentrations, profilin prevents the polymerization of actin, whereas it enhances it at low concentrations

PGAP3.job: helps finish the fatty anchors that hold certain proteins on the cell surface
PGAP3.basis: Involved in the fatty acid remodeling steps of GPI-anchor maturation ... The fatty acid remodeling steps is critical for the integration of GPI-APs into lipid rafts

PGM1.job: helps cells both break down and build up stores of sugar
PGM1.basis: Catalyzes the reversible isomerization of alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate to alpha-D-glucose 6-phosphate ... This enzyme participates in both the breakdown and synthesis of glucose

PGM3.job: helps make a sugar building block cells use to coat their proteins
PGM3.basis: Catalyzes the conversion of GlcNAc-6-P into GlcNAc-1-P during the synthesis of uridine diphosphate/UDP-GlcNAc, a sugar nucleotide critical to multiple glycosylation pathways including protein N- and O-glycosylation

PHEX.job: helps bones and teeth harden with minerals and keeps phosphate in the body
PHEX.basis: Regulates osteogenic cell differentiation and bone mineralization ... Promotes dentin mineralization and renal phosphate reabsorption

PHF12.job: helps hold together a protein team that switches genes down
PHF12.basis: Transcriptional repressor acting as key scaffolding subunit of SIN3 complexes which contributes to complex assembly ... stabilizes the complex ... SIN3B complex represses transcription

PHF21A.job: helps keep nerve-cell genes switched off in other kinds of cells
PHF21A.basis: Component of the BHC complex, a corepressor complex that represses transcription of neuron-specific genes in non-neuronal cells

PHF6.job: helps turn down the cell's production of parts for its protein-making machines
PHF6.basis: Transcriptional regulator that associates with ribosomal RNA promoters and suppresses ribosomal RNA (rRNA) transcription

PHF8.job: removes chemical tags from DNA's packaging proteins to switch genes on
PHF8.basis: Histone lysine demethylase with selectivity for mono- and dimethylated residues ... Acts as a transcription activator as H3K9Me1, H3K9Me2, H3K27Me2 and H4K20Me1 are epigenetic repressive marks

PHGDH.job: starts the process cells use to make serine, a building block of proteins
PHGDH.basis: the first step of the phosphorylated L-serine biosynthesis pathway

PHIP.job: helps pass on insulin and growth signals that tell cells to grow
PHIP.basis: Probable regulator of the insulin and insulin-like growth factor signaling pathways. Stimulates cell proliferation

PHKA1.job: helps muscles release stored sugar for energy
PHKA1.basis: Phosphorylase b kinase catalyzes the phosphorylation of serine in certain substrates ... The alpha chain may bind calmodulin
PHKA1.alt: is part of a skeletal muscle enzyme that helps release stored sugar for energy

PHKB.job: is the control piece of an enzyme that tags other proteins with phosphate
PHKB.basis: Phosphorylase b kinase catalyzes the phosphorylation of serine in certain substrates ... The beta chain acts as a regulatory unit and modulates the activity of the holoenzyme

PHKG2.job: helps the body break down stored sugar for energy
PHKG2.basis: Catalytic subunit of the phosphorylase b kinase (PHK), which mediates the neural and hormonal regulation of glycogen breakdown (glycogenolysis)

PHOX2B.job: switches on genes that help certain nerve cells in the brain and body develop
PHOX2B.basis: Involved in the development of several major noradrenergic neuron populations, including the locus coeruleus. Transcription factor

PHYH.job: helps the body process certain branched fats
PHYH.basis: Catalyzes the 2-hydroxylation of not only racemic phytanoyl-CoA ... but also a variety of other mono-branched 3-methylacyl-CoA esters

PIDD1.job: helps decide whether a cell with damaged DNA survives or self-destructs
PIDD1.basis: Component of the DNA damage/stress response pathway that functions downstream of p53/TP53 and can either promote cell survival or apoptosis

PIEZO1.job: forms a channel that lets cells sense pressure, stretch and flowing blood
PIEZO1.basis: Pore-forming subunit of the mechanosensitive non-specific cation Piezo channel ... Acts as a shear-stress sensor that promotes endothelial cell organization and alignment in the direction of blood flow

PIGA.job: starts building the anchors that hold certain proteins to the cell surface
PIGA.basis: Catalytic subunit of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase (GPI-GnT) complex ... participates in the first step of GPI biosynthesis

PIGL.job: helps build the fatty anchors that hold certain proteins to the cell's surface
PIGL.basis: Catalyzes the second step of glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) biosynthesis

PIGN.job: helps build the anchors that hold certain proteins to the cell's surface
PIGN.basis: Ethanolamine phosphate transferase ... participates in the eighth step of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchor biosynthesis

PIGO.job: helps build the anchors that hold certain proteins to the cell's surface
PIGO.basis: Catalytic subunit of the ethanolamine phosphate transferase 3 complex ... participates in the tenth step of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchor biosynthesis

PIGQ.job: helps build the anchor that holds certain proteins to the cell's surface
PIGQ.basis: Part of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase (GPI-GnT) complex ... participates in the first step of GPI biosynthesis

PIGS.job: helps attach anchors that tether certain proteins to the cell's outer surface
PIGS.basis: Component of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchor (GPI-anchor) transamidase (GPI-T) complex that catalyzes the formation of the linkage between a proprotein and a GPI-anchor and participates in GPI anchored protein biosynthesis

PIGT.job: helps attach anchors that hold certain proteins to the cell's outer surface
PIGT.basis: Component of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchor (GPI-anchor) transamidase (GPI-T) complex that catalyzes the formation of the linkage between a proprotein and a GPI-anchor and participates in GPI anchored protein biosynthesis

PIK3CD.job: relays signals that help immune cells grow, move and respond to germs
PIK3CD.basis: activating signaling cascades involved in cell growth, survival, proliferation, motility and morphology. Mediates immune responses ... Required for B-cell receptor (BCR) signaling ... Required for T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling

PIK3R1.job: helps cells respond to insulin and growth signals by relaying them inward
PIK3R1.basis: acts as an adapter, mediating the association of the p110 catalytic unit to the plasma membrane. Necessary for the insulin-stimulated increase in glucose uptake and glycogen synthesis ... Plays an important role in signaling in response to FGFR1, FGFR2, FGFR3, FGFR4, KITLG/SCF, KIT, PDGFRA and PDGFRB

PIK3R2.job: helps control a signaling switch that tells cells to grow and survive
PIK3R2.basis: Regulatory subunit of phosphoinositide-3-kinase (PI3K) ... activating signaling cascades involved in cell growth, survival, proliferation

PINK1.job: senses damaged energy-producing parts of the cell and flags them for removal
PINK1.basis: acts as a sensor of mitochondrial damage ... coordinate mitochondrial quality control mechanisms that remove and replace dysfunctional mitochondrial components ... eliminating severely damaged mitochondria via PINK1-PRKN-dependent mitophagy

PIP5K1C.job: makes a fat-based signal that helps cells move, stick together and pass messages
PIP5K1C.basis: Catalyzes the phosphorylation of phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate ... to form phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PtdIns(4,5)P2/PIP2), a lipid second messenger that regulates several cellular processes such as signal transduction, vesicle trafficking, actin cytoskeleton dynamics, cell adhesion, and cell motility

PITX2.job: helps young muscle cells switch from multiplying to maturing
PITX2.basis: May play a role in myoblast differentiation ... ensuring cell proliferation ... progression towards differentiation
PITX2.alt: may help immature muscle cells mature

PJVK.job: protects the inner ear's sound-sensing cells from damage caused by loud noise
PJVK.basis: Peroxisome-associated protein required to protect auditory hair cells against noise-induced damage

PKD1.job: helps kidney cells sense fluid flow and form their tiny tubes
PKD1.basis: Involved in renal tubulogenesis ... Involved in fluid-flow mechanosensation by the primary cilium in renal epithelium

PKD2.job: forms a channel in cells' antenna-like hairs that senses fluid flow in the kidney
PKD2.basis: Forms a nonselective cation channel ... In primary cilium functions as a cation channel ... Involved in fluid-flow mechanosensation by the primary cilium in renal epithelium

PKHD1.job: helps shape the kidney's tiny tubes as they form
PKHD1.basis: Promotes ciliogenesis in renal epithelial cells and therefore participates in the tubules formation and/ or ensures the maintenance of the architecture of the lumen of the kidney

PKLR.job: helps cells get energy from sugar
PKLR.basis: Pyruvate kinase that catalyzes the conversion of phosphoenolpyruvate to pyruvate with the synthesis of ATP, and which plays a key role in glycolysis

PKP2.job: helps glue neighboring cells together, especially heart muscle cells
PKP2.basis: A component of desmosome cell-cell junctions which are required for positive regulation of cellular adhesion ... Required for the formation of desmosome cell junctions in cardiomyocytes

PLA2G6.job: trims and renews the fats that make up cell membranes
PLA2G6.basis: Calcium-independent phospholipase involved in phospholipid remodeling with implications in cellular membrane homeostasis, mitochondrial integrity and signal transduction ... Plays a role in regulation of membrane dynamics and homeostasis

PLCB1.job: splits a membrane fat into chemical messengers that relay signals inside cells
PLCB1.basis: Catalyzes the hydrolysis of 1-phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate into diacylglycerol (DAG) and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3) and mediates intracellular signaling downstream of G protein-coupled receptors ... into the second messengers

PLCB4.job: makes chemical messengers that relay signals inside cells, including for jaw and ear development
PLCB4.basis: catalyze the production of the second messenger molecules diacylglycerol (DAG) and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3) involved in G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathways ... plays an essential role in lower jaw and middle ear structures development

PLCE1.job: makes chemical messengers that relay signals inside cells, including kidney filter cells
PLCE1.basis: The production of the second messenger molecules diacylglycerol (DAG) and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3) is mediated by activated phosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase C enzymes ... In podocytes, is involved in the regulation of lamellipodia formation

PLD1.job: cuts a common fat in cell membranes to pass along signals and move membranes
PLD1.basis: Function as phospholipase selective for phosphatidylcholine ... Implicated as a critical step in numerous cellular pathways, including signal transduction, membrane trafficking

PLEC.job: links the cell's internal support fibers and anchors them to cell junctions
PLEC.basis: Interlinks intermediate filaments with microtubules and microfilaments and anchors intermediate filaments to desmosomes or hemidesmosomes

PLEKHG5.job: helps motor nerves keep passing signals to muscles
PLEKHG5.basis: regulates autophagy of synaptic vesicles in axon terminal of motoneurons
PLEKHG5.alt: helps motor nerve endings recycle their message-carrying bubbles

PLG.job: breaks down blood clots once they are no longer needed
PLG.basis: Protease which primary function is to degrade fibrin, the main component of blood clots

PLIN1.job: coats fat droplets in fat cells to protect stored fat from being broken down
PLIN1.basis: Modulator of adipocyte lipid metabolism. Coats lipid storage droplets to protect them from breakdown by hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL).

PLN.job: controls how fast heart muscle pulls calcium back in to relax between beats
PLN.basis: Modulates the contractility of the heart muscle in response to physiological stimuli via its effects on ATP2A2. Modulates calcium re-uptake during muscle relaxation and plays an important role in calcium homeostasis in the heart muscle

PLP1.job: helps build the fatty insulation that wraps nerve fibers in the brain and spinal cord
PLP1.basis: This is the major myelin protein from the central nervous system. It plays an important role in the formation or maintenance of the multilamellar structure of myelin

PMM2.job: helps make a sugar building block used to coat proteins with sugar chains
PMM2.basis: Involved in the synthesis of the GDP-mannose and dolichol-phosphate-mannose required for a number of critical mannosyl transfer reactions

PMP22.job: helps build the protective coating around nerves in the arms, legs and body
PMP22.basis: Might be involved in growth regulation, and in myelinization in the peripheral nervous system
PMP22.alt: helps build the protective coating around nerves in the body's limbs and organs

PMPCA.job: helps trim the address tags off proteins newly brought into mitochondria
PMPCA.basis: Substrate recognition and binding subunit of the essential mitochondrial processing protease (MPP), which cleaves the mitochondrial sequence off newly imported precursors proteins

PMS2.job: fixes spelling mistakes made when cells copy their DNA
PMS2.basis: Component of the post-replicative DNA mismatch repair system (MMR) ... It introduces single-strand breaks near the mismatch and thus generates new entry points for the exonuclease EXO1 to degrade the strand containing the mismatch

PNKP.job: tidies the broken ends of DNA so they can be rejoined
PNKP.basis: Plays a key role in the repair of DNA damage ... PNK ensures that DNA termini are compatible with extension and ligation

PNP.job: helps cells break down and recycle building blocks of DNA and RNA
PNP.basis: Catalyzes the phosphorolytic breakdown of the N-glycosidic bond in the beta-(deoxy)ribonucleoside molecules, with the formation of the corresponding free purine bases

PNPLA2.job: starts breaking down stored fat so the body can use it for energy
PNPLA2.basis: Catalyzes the initial step in triglyceride hydrolysis in adipocyte and non-adipocyte lipid droplets ... providing free fatty acids to other tissues to be oxidized in situations of energy depletion

PNPLA6.job: breaks down fats that make up cell membranes
PNPLA6.basis: Phospholipase B that deacylates intracellular phosphatidylcholine (PtdCho) ... Catalyzes the hydrolysis of several naturally occurring membrane-associated lipids

PNPLA8.job: trims fats from cell membranes to make signaling molecules and keep mitochondria working
PNPLA8.basis: catalyzes the esterolytic cleavage of fatty acids from glycerophospholipids to yield free fatty acids and lysophospholipids, hence regulating membrane physical properties and the release of lipid second messengers ... essential for maintaining efficient bioenergetic mitochondrial function through tailoring mitochondrial membrane lipid metabolism and composition

PNPO.job: turns vitamin B6 into the active form the body can use
PNPO.basis: Catalyzes the oxidation of either pyridoxine 5'-phosphate (PNP) or pyridoxamine 5'-phosphate (PMP) into pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP)

POC1B.job: helps build centrioles, the structures that anchor the cell's hair-like antennae
POC1B.basis: Plays an important role in centriole assembly and/or stability and ciliogenesis ... Required for primary cilia formation

POGLUT1.job: attaches sugars to other proteins, helping a key growth signal guide muscle development
POGLUT1.basis: catalyzes the transfer of glucose and xylose ... Acts as a positive regulator of Notch signaling by mediating O-glucosylation of Notch, leading to regulate muscle development

POGZ.job: helps dividing cells split their chromosomes evenly and repair broken DNA
POGZ.basis: Plays a role in mitotic cell cycle progression ... plays a role in mitotic chromosome segregation ... Promotes the repair of DNA double-strand breaks

POLD1.job: copies DNA accurately when cells divide, and proofreads its own work
POLD1.basis: plays a crucial role in high fidelity genome replication, including in lagging strand synthesis, and repair ... Exhibits both DNA polymerase and 3'- to 5'-exonuclease activities ... expresses higher proofreading activity

POLE.job: copies DNA when cells divide and fixes copying mistakes
POLE.basis: Participates in chromosomal DNA replication ... Has 3'-5' proofreading exonuclease activity that corrects errors arising during DNA replication

POLH.job: copies DNA past spots damaged by sunlight so cells can keep copying
POLH.basis: DNA polymerase specifically involved in the DNA repair by translesion synthesis (TLS) ... complete bypass of DNA lesions ... Particularly important for the repair of UV-induced pyrimidine dimers

POLR1C.job: is part of the machines that copy DNA into RNA for building the cell's proteins
POLR1C.basis: DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyzes the transcription of DNA into RNA ... Common component of RNA polymerases I and III which synthesize ribosomal RNA precursors and short non-coding RNAs including 5S rRNA, snRNAs, tRNAs

POLR1D.job: is part of the machinery that copies DNA into RNA for the cell's protein factories
POLR1D.basis: DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyzes the transcription of DNA into RNA ... Common component of RNA polymerases I and III which synthesize ribosomal RNA precursors and short non-coding RNAs

POLR3A.job: helps copy genes into RNA molecules the cell needs to build proteins
POLR3A.basis: Catalytic core component of RNA polymerase III (Pol III), a DNA-dependent RNA polymerase which synthesizes small non-coding RNAs ... Synthesizes 5S rRNA, snRNAs, tRNAs and miRNAs
POLR3A.alt: is the core of a machine that copies DNA into small RNAs cells need to build proteins

POLR3B.job: is part of the machine that copies DNA into small RNA molecules cells need
POLR3B.basis: Catalytic core component of RNA polymerase III (Pol III), a DNA-dependent RNA polymerase which synthesizes small non-coding RNAs ... Synthesizes 5S rRNA, snRNAs, tRNAs and miRNAs

POMGNT1.job: adds a sugar to certain proteins so more sugars can be built on top
POMGNT1.basis: catalyzing the addition of N-acetylglucosamine to O-linked mannose on glycoproteins ... providing the necessary basis for the addition of further carbohydrate moieties

POMGNT2.job: helps attach sugars to a protein that anchors muscle cells to their surroundings
POMGNT2.basis: Involved in the biosynthesis of the phosphorylated O-mannosyl trisaccharide ... a carbohydrate structure present in alpha-dystroglycan (DAG1), which is required for binding laminin G-like domain-containing extracellular proteins with high affinity

POMT1.job: attaches sugar units to other proteins, especially one that anchors muscle cells
POMT1.basis: Transfers mannosyl residues to the hydroxyl group of serine or threonine residues ... Essentially dedicated to O-mannosylation of alpha-DAG1 and few other proteins

POMT2.job: adds sugar tags to a protein that anchors muscle cells to their surroundings
POMT2.basis: Transfers mannosyl residues to the hydroxyl group of serine or threonine residues ... Essentially dedicated to O-mannosylation of alpha-DAG1 and few other proteins

POPDC3.job: is thought to help keep the heart working
POPDC3.basis: May play a role in the maintenance of heart function mediated, at least in part, through cAMP-binding
POPDC3.alt: may help keep the heart working

POR.job: passes electrons to the enzymes that process drugs, hormones and other chemicals
POR.basis: This enzyme is required for electron transfer from NADP to cytochrome P450 in microsomes. It can also provide electron transfer to heme oxygenase and cytochrome B5

PORCN.job: attaches a fatty tag to Wnt signals so they can switch on cells
PORCN.basis: acts as a key regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway by mediating the attachment of palmitoleate ... to Wnt proteins ... Serine palmitoleoylation of WNT proteins is required for efficient binding to frizzled receptors

POT1.job: protects the ends of chromosomes and helps control their length
POT1.basis: Component of the shelterin complex (telosome) that is involved in the regulation of telomere length and protection ... protects chromosome ends

POU3F3.job: switches on genes that help the brain's nerve cells develop
POU3F3.basis: Transcription factor ... Plays a role in neuronal development

POU3F4.job: switches on genes that guide the early development of the nervous system
POU3F4.basis: Probable transcription factor which exert its primary action widely during early neural development

POU4F3.job: switches on genes that help the inner ear's sound-sensing hair cells mature
POU4F3.basis: Acts as a transcriptional activator ... required for terminal differentiation of hair cells in the inner ear

PPA2.job: breaks down a phosphate waste product to keep the cell's power plants working
PPA2.basis: Hydrolyzes inorganic pyrophosphate ... This activity is essential for correct regulation of mitochondrial membrane potential, and mitochondrial organization and function

PPARG.job: switches on genes that make fat cells and control how the body handles fat and sugar
PPARG.basis: Ligand-activated transcription factor ... acts as a key regulator of biological processes, such as adipocyte differentiation, lipid metabolism, glucose homeostasis

PPM1D.job: switches off the DNA-damage alarm so cells can resume dividing
PPM1D.basis: Required for the relief of p53-dependent checkpoint mediated cell cycle arrest ... dephosphorylates 'Ser-15' of TP53 and 'Ser-345' of CHEK1 which contributes to the functional inactivation of these proteins

PPOX.job: helps make heme, the iron-holding part of blood that carries oxygen
PPOX.basis: Catalyzes the 6-electron oxidation of protoporphyrinogen-IX to form protoporphyrin-IX

PPP1CB.job: removes chemical tags from many proteins, helping control cell division and growth signals
PPP1CB.basis: Protein phosphatase that associates with over 200 regulatory proteins to form highly specific holoenzymes which dephosphorylate hundreds of biological targets. Protein phosphatase (PP1) is essential for cell division ... regulates the MAPK pathway activation

PPP1R12A.job: guides an enzyme that relaxes muscle by unlocking the muscle motor protein myosin
PPP1R12A.basis: Key regulator of protein phosphatase 1C (PPP1C). Mediates binding to myosin.

PPP1R13L.job: helps decide whether damaged cells self-destruct and keeps inflammation in check
PPP1R13L.basis: plays a central role in regulation of apoptosis and transcription via its interaction with NF-kappa-B and p53/TP53 proteins ... suppressing the subsequent activation of apoptosis ... negative regulation of inflammatory response

PPP1R21.job: helps carry gene messages to the right spots inside cells
PPP1R21.basis: functions as a RAB5A effector involved in the localization and the distribution of specific mRNAs most likely by mediating their endosomal transport ... The complex recruits mRNAs and ribosomes to early endosomes

PPP2CA.job: removes chemical tags from other proteins to switch many cell signals off
PPP2CA.basis: Catalytic subunit of protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A), a serine/threonine phosphatase involved in the regulation of a wide variety of enzymes, signal transduction pathways, and cellular events ... Can dephosphorylate various proteins

PPP2R1A.job: holds together an enzyme that removes chemical switches from other proteins
PPP2R1A.basis: The PR65 subunit of protein phosphatase 2A serves as a scaffolding molecule to coordinate the assembly of the catalytic subunit and a variable regulatory B subunit ... STRIPAK complexes have critical roles in protein (de)phosphorylation and are regulators of multiple signaling pathways

PPP2R5C.job: helps steer an enzyme that removes chemical tags from other proteins
PPP2R5C.basis: The B regulatory subunit might modulate substrate selectivity and catalytic activity, and might also direct the localization of the catalytic enzyme ... may specifically dephosphorylate and activate TP53

PPP2R5D.job: helps direct an enzyme to the proteins it acts on
PPP2R5D.basis: The B regulatory subunit might modulate substrate selectivity and catalytic activity, and might also direct the localization of the catalytic enzyme to a particular subcellular compartment
PPP2R5D.alt: guides an enzyme that removes chemical tags from proteins to its targets in the cell

PPP3CA.job: relays calcium signals inside cells by removing phosphate tags from other proteins
PPP3CA.basis: Calcium-dependent, calmodulin-stimulated protein phosphatase which plays an essential role in the transduction of intracellular Ca(2+)-mediated signals

PPT1.job: removes fatty tags from proteins so they can be broken down
PPT1.basis: Has thioesterase activity against fatty acid thioesters with 14 -18 carbons, including palmitoyl-CoA ... and palmitoylated proteins ... PPT1 can hydrolyze palmitoylated proteins and palmitoylcysteine

PQBP1.job: helps cells edit gene messages and supports brain cell development
PQBP1.basis: involved in different processes, such as pre-mRNA splicing, transcription regulation, innate immunity and neuron development ... regulates alternative splicing of target pre-mRNA species

PRDM16.job: switches on genes that turn precursor cells into heat-burning brown fat
PRDM16.basis: Transcription regulator ... acts as a key chromatin adapter that mediates differentiation of brown and beige adipocytes, which are specialized in dissipating chemical energy in the form of heat ... activating genes that are highly expressed in brown adipocytes

PRF1.job: punches holes in infected or cancerous cells so immune cells can kill them
PRF1.basis: Pore-forming protein that plays a key role in granzyme-mediated programmed cell death, and in defense against virus-infected or neoplastic cells ... Can insert into the membrane of target cells in its calcium-bound form, oligomerize and form large pores

PRKAG2.job: is part of a sensor that tells cells when they are running low on energy
PRKAG2.basis: AMP/ATP-binding subunit of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), an energy sensor protein kinase that plays a key role in regulating cellular energy metabolism ... In response to reduction of intracellular ATP levels, AMPK activates energy-producing pathways and inhibits energy-consuming processes

PRKAR1A.job: keeps a key signaling enzyme switched off until the cell gets a chemical cue
PRKAR1A.basis: Regulatory subunit of the cAMP-dependent protein kinases involved in cAMP signaling in cells

PRKCD.job: helps decide whether damaged cells live or self-destruct, and keeps immune cells in check
PRKCD.basis: plays contrasting roles in cell death and cell survival ... Negatively regulates B cell proliferation and also has an important function in self-antigen induced B cell tolerance induction

PRKCSH.job: helps trim sugar tags on newly made proteins so they mature properly
PRKCSH.basis: Regulatory subunit of glucosidase II that cleaves sequentially the 2 innermost alpha-1,3-linked glucose residues from the Glc(2)Man(9)GlcNAc(2) oligosaccharide precursor of immature glycoproteins

PRKDC.job: senses broken DNA and holds the broken ends together for repair
PRKDC.basis: acts as a molecular sensor for DNA damage ... required to (1) protect and align broken ends of DNA, thereby preventing their degradation, (2) and sequester the DSB for repair by NHEJ

PRKG1.job: relays nitric oxide signals that relax the muscles lining blood vessels
PRKG1.basis: key mediator of the nitric oxide (NO)/cGMP signaling pathway ... Smooth muscle relaxation is mediated through lowering of intracellular free calcium ... resulting in vasorelaxation

PRKN.job: tags damaged mitochondria, the cell's power plants, for removal and recycling
PRKN.basis: catalyzing the covalent attachment of ubiquitin moieties onto substrate proteins ... coordinate mitochondrial quality control mechanisms that remove and replace dysfunctional mitochondrial components ... eliminating severely damaged mitochondria via mitophagy

PROC.job: keeps blood from clotting too much by switching off clotting factors
PROC.basis: regulates blood coagulation by inactivating factors Va and VIIIa

PROK2.job: carries the brain's body-clock signal that sets daily activity rhythms
PROK2.basis: May function as an output molecule from the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) that transmits behavioral circadian rhythm

PROKR2.job: picks up a signal from outside the cell and passes it inside
PROKR2.basis: Receptor for prokineticin 2 ... Activation leads to mobilization of calcium
PROKR2.alt: picks up the signal prokineticin 2 and passes its message into the cell

PROM1.job: helps shape the stacked membrane disks in the eye's light-sensing cells
PROM1.basis: During early retinal development acts as a key regulator of disk morphogenesis

PRORP.job: trims the ends of molecules that help the cell's power plants make proteins
PRORP.basis: Catalytic ribonuclease component of mitochondrial ribonuclease P ... which cleaves tRNA molecules in their 5'-ends

PROS1.job: keeps blood from clotting too much
PROS1.basis: Anticoagulant plasma protein which directly binds coagulation factors Va (F5) and Xa (F10) and inhibits their activity

PRPF3.job: helps cut and paste genetic messages before they are used to make proteins
PRPF3.basis: Plays a role in pre-mRNA splicing as component of the U4/U6-U5 tri-snRNP complex that is involved in spliceosome assembly

PRPF31.job: helps cut and paste the gene messages that cells read to make proteins
PRPF31.basis: Involved in pre-mRNA splicing as component of the spliceosome ... Required for the assembly of the U4/U5/U6 tri-snRNP complex, one of the building blocks of the spliceosome

PRPF8.job: helps cut and paste the gene's working copy into a finished recipe for proteins
PRPF8.basis: Plays a role in pre-mRNA splicing as core component of precatalytic, catalytic and postcatalytic spliceosomal complexes ... Functions as a scaffold that positions spliceosomal U2, U5 and U6 snRNAs at splice sites on pre-mRNA substrates, so that splicing can occur

PRPH2.job: helps build the stacked disks that catch light in the eye's light-sensing cells
PRPH2.basis: Essential for retina photoreceptor outer segment disk morphogenesis ... may also play a role with ROM1 in the maintenance of outer segment disk structure

PRPS1.job: makes a key starting material the body uses to build DNA's building blocks
PRPS1.basis: Catalyzes the synthesis of phosphoribosylpyrophosphate (PRPP) that is essential for nucleotide synthesis

PRR12.job: is thought to help keep copied chromosomes together until the cell divides
PRR12.basis: May play a role in the regulation of cohesin complex loading onto chromatin
PRR12.alt: may help keep copied chromosomes held together until the cell divides

PRRT2.job: helps nerve cells release their chemical messages to each other
PRRT2.basis: may be involved in synaptic transmission in the central nervous system ... plays an important role in the final steps of neurotransmitter release

PRSS1.job: is an enzyme that cuts proteins at specific points
PRSS1.basis: Has activity against the synthetic substrates Boc-Phe-Ser-Arg-Mec, Boc-Leu-Thr-Arg-Mec, Boc-Gln-Ala-Arg-Mec and Boc-Val-Pro-Arg-Mec
PRSS1.alt: cuts small protein pieces at specific spots

PRSS56.basis: Serine protease required during eye development

PRX.job: helps maintain the insulating coat around nerves in the arms and legs
PRX.basis: Required for the maintenance of the peripheral myelin sheath that is essential for normal transmission of nerve impulses

PSAP.job: hands fatty molecules to enzymes that break them down in the cell's recycling centers
PSAP.basis: act as activator proteins for lysosomal sphingolipid-degrading enzymes, facilitating the hydrolysis of sphingolipids by extracting lipid substrates from membranes and presenting them to their respective enzymes

PSAT1.job: helps cells make serine, an amino acid, from sugar
PSAT1.basis: Involved in L-serine biosynthesis via the phosphorylated pathway, a three-step pathway converting the glycolytic intermediate 3-phospho-D-glycerate into L-serine

PSMD12.job: is part of the cell's machine that breaks down damaged or unneeded proteins
PSMD12.basis: Component of the 26S proteasome, a multiprotein complex involved in the ATP-dependent degradation of ubiquitinated proteins ... by removing misfolded or damaged proteins ... and by removing proteins whose functions are no longer required

PTCH1.job: keeps a growth signal switched off until the right cue arrives
PTCH1.basis: Negative regulator of the smoothened signaling pathway, which acts as a receptor for hedgehog (SHH, IHH and DHH) morphogens ... In absence of hedgehog, acts as an inhibitor of smoothened protein (SMO) ... Hedgehog-binding inhibits PTCH1 cholesterol transporter activity, promoting SMO activation

PTCHD1.job: helps a key relay hub deep in the brain develop and work
PTCHD1.basis: Required for the development and function of the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN), a part of the thalamus that is critical for thalamocortical transmission

PTCRA.job: helps young immune cells called T cells mature in early development
PTCRA.basis: Component of the pre-T-cell receptor complex ... that has a crucial role in early T-cell development, particularly alpha-beta T cell differentiation

PTEN.job: acts as a brake on signals that tell cells to grow and divide
PTEN.basis: Antagonizes the PI3K-AKT/PKB signaling pathway by dephosphorylating phosphoinositides and thereby modulating cell cycle progression and cell survival

PTPN11.job: helps pass signals from the cell's surface to its control center
PTPN11.basis: participate in the signal transduction from the cell surface to the nucleus

PTPRC.job: helps switch on T cells, the immune cells that fight infections
PTPRC.basis: Protein tyrosine-protein phosphatase required for T-cell activation through the antigen receptor

PTPRQ.job: helps the inner ear's sound-sensing hairs mature
PTPRQ.basis: Required for hair bundle maturation, a process that enables hair cells to detect and transmit sound and balance signals effectively

PTS.job: helps make a helper molecule the body needs to process certain amino acids
PTS.basis: Involved in the biosynthesis of tetrahydrobiopterin, an essential cofactor of aromatic amino acid hydroxylases

PUF60.job: helps cut and paste genetic messages so genes are read correctly
PUF60.basis: DNA- and RNA-binding protein, involved in several nuclear processes such as pre-mRNA splicing, apoptosis and transcription regulation ... Is also involved in pre-mRNA splicing ... Modulates alternative splicing of several mRNAs

PURA.job: binds DNA to help switch on certain genes
PURA.basis: probable transcription activator that specifically binds the purine-rich single strand of the PUR element

PUS1.job: fine-tunes the molecules cells use to build proteins
PUS1.basis: Pseudouridylate synthase that catalyzes pseudouridylation of tRNAs and mRNAs
PUS1.alt: chemically fine-tunes the RNA molecules cells use to read genes and build proteins

PXDN.job: cross-links collagen to strengthen the thin sheets that support tissues
PXDN.basis: mediates the formation of sulfilimine cross-links between methionine and hydroxylysine residues within an uncross-linked collagen IV/COL4A1 NC1 hexamer ... an event essential to basement membrane integrity

PYCR1.job: makes proline, one of the building blocks of proteins
PYCR1.basis: catalyzes the last step in proline biosynthesis, which corresponds to the reduction of pyrroline-5-carboxylate to L-proline

PYCR2.job: makes proline, one of the building blocks of proteins
PYCR2.basis: catalyzes the last step in proline biosynthesis

PYGL.job: breaks down stored sugar in the liver to keep blood sugar steady
PYGL.basis: catalyzes the rate-limiting step in glycogen catabolism, the phosphorolytic cleavage of glycogen to produce glucose-1-phosphate, and plays a central role in maintaining cellular and organismal glucose homeostasis

PYGM.job: breaks down stored sugar in muscle to fuel movement
PYGM.basis: catalyzes the rate-limiting step in glycogen catabolism, the phosphorolytic cleavage of glycogen to produce glucose-1-phosphate
PYGM.alt: breaks down stored sugar in muscles for quick energy

PYROXD1.job: protects a repair enzyme from oxygen damage
PYROXD1.basis: protect RTCB, the catalytic subunit of the tRNA ligase complex (tRNA-LC) involved in tRNA splicing ... from oxidative inactivation ... triggers the timed release of RTCB, enabling its subsequent activation
PYROXD1.alt: shields a key RNA-repair enzyme from oxygen damage until it is needed

QARS1.job: loads the amino acid glutamine onto its carrier for building proteins

QDPR.job: recycles a helper molecule so the body can use it again
QDPR.basis: Catalyzes the conversion of quinonoid dihydrobiopterin into tetrahydrobiopterin
QDPR.alt: recycles a helper molecule, tetrahydrobiopterin, so it can be used again

QRICH1.job: switches on genes that help cells cope when their protein-making goes wrong
QRICH1.basis: Transcriptional regulator that acts as a mediator of the integrated stress response (ISR) through transcriptional control of protein homeostasis under conditions of ER stress

RAB23.job: helps cells deliver materials to their antenna-like sensing hairs and tunes growth signals
RAB23.basis: key regulators of intracellular membrane trafficking ... drives the localization of specific G protein-coupled receptors ... to primary cilia ... involved in the down-regulation of Shh signaling

RAB27A.job: helps immune cells release their germ-killing packets
RAB27A.basis: Plays a role in cytotoxic granule exocytosis in lymphocytes. Required for both granule maturation and granule docking and priming at the immunologic synapse

RAB28.job: helps the eye's color-sensing cells shed and clear away worn-out parts
RAB28.basis: RAB28 is required for shedding and phagocytosis of cone cell outer segments (OS) discs in the retina

RAB39B.job: directs the tiny bubbles that ferry materials around inside brain and other cells
RAB39B.basis: The small GTPases Rab are key regulators of intracellular membrane trafficking, from the formation of transport vesicles to their fusion with membranes ... regulate AMPAR composition at the post-synapses and thus synaptic transmission

RAB3GAP1.job: switches off molecular traffic signals that direct cargo inside cells
RAB3GAP1.basis: Catalytic subunit of the Rab3 GTPase-activating (Rab3GAP) complex ... which accelerates the otherwise slow GTP hydrolysis catalyzed by Rab proteins ... involved in regulating non-synaptic vesicular release of neurotransmitters

RAB3GAP2.job: helps switch on and off the molecular switches that steer cargo inside cells
RAB3GAP2.basis: Regulatory subunit of the Rab3 GTPase-activating (Rab3GAP) complex ... which accelerates the otherwise slow GTP hydrolysis catalyzed by Rab proteins ... has guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) activity towards RAB18

RAB7A.job: directs the traffic of cargo bubbles to the cell's recycling centers
RAB7A.basis: key regulators of intracellular membrane trafficking ... playing a key role in the regulation of endo-lysosomal trafficking ... endosome-lysosome transport

RAC1.job: acts as an on-off switch that helps cells change shape and move
RAC1.basis: small GTPase which cycles between active GTP-bound and inactive GDP-bound states ... regulate cellular responses such as ... migration ... and growth-factor induced formation of membrane ruffles ... Essential for the SPATA13-mediated regulation of cell migration

RAC2.job: helps immune cells make the chemical blasts they use to kill germs
RAC2.basis: Regulatory subunit of the phagocyte NADPH oxidase complex that mediates the transfer of electrons from cytosolic NADPH to O2 to produce the superoxide anion (O2(-))

RAD21.job: holds copied chromosomes together until the cell divides
RAD21.basis: As a member of the cohesin complex, involved in sister chromatid cohesion from the time of DNA replication in S phase to their segregation in mitosis, a function that is essential for proper chromosome segregation

RAD51C.basis: Essential for the homologous recombination (HR) pathway of DNA repair ... homologous recombination repair (HRR) pathway of double-stranded DNA breaks

RAD51D.basis: Involved in the homologous recombination repair (HRR) pathway of double-stranded DNA breaks

RAF1.job: passes along signals that tell cells whether to grow, divide or mature
RAF1.basis: acts as a regulatory link between the membrane-associated Ras GTPases and the MAPK/ERK cascade, and this critical regulatory link functions as a switch determining cell fate decisions including proliferation, differentiation

RAG1.job: cuts and reshuffles DNA so immune cells can recognize many different germs
RAG1.basis: mediates the DNA cleavage phase during V(D)J recombination ... assembles a diverse repertoire of immunoglobulin and T-cell receptor genes in developing B and T-lymphocytes through rearrangement of different V (variable), in some cases D (diversity), and J (joining) gene segments

RAG2.job: helps immune cells cut and shuffle DNA to make many different germ detectors
RAG2.basis: Core component of the RAG complex, a multiprotein complex that mediates the DNA cleavage phase during V(D)J recombination. V(D)J recombination assembles a diverse repertoire of immunoglobulin and T-cell receptor genes in developing B and T-lymphocytes through rearrangement of different V (variable), in some cases D (diversity), and J (joining) gene segments

RAI1.job: helps switch on genes that run the body's daily clock
RAI1.basis: Transcriptional regulator of the circadian clock components ... Positively regulates the transcriptional activity of CLOCK a core component of the circadian clock

RALA.job: acts as a molecular switch that helps cells ship materials out, move and divide
RALA.basis: Multifunctional GTPase involved in a variety of cellular processes including gene expression, cell migration, cell proliferation, oncogenic transformation and membrane trafficking ... Acts as a GTP sensor for GTP-dependent exocytosis of dense core vesicles

RARB.job: senses a vitamin A signal and switches on genes in response
RARB.basis: Receptor for retinoic acid ... regulate gene expression in various biological processes ... acts mainly as an activator of gene expression

RARS1.job: helps load amino acids onto their carriers so cells can build proteins
RARS1.basis: Forms part of a macromolecular complex that catalyzes the attachment of specific amino acids to cognate tRNAs during protein synthesis

RARS2.job: attaches the building block arginine to its carrier molecule for making proteins
RARS2.basis: Catalyzes the attachment of arginine to tRNA(Arg)

RASGRP1.job: switches on growth signals that help immune cells develop and respond
RASGRP1.basis: specifically activating Ras through the exchange of bound GDP for GTP ... Regulates T-cell/B-cell development, homeostasis and differentiation by coupling T-lymphocyte/B-lymphocyte antigen receptors to Ras

RASGRP2.job: helps platelets clump together and immune cells stick where needed
RASGRP2.basis: Functions in aggregation of platelets and adhesion of T-lymphocytes and neutrophils

RB1.job: acts as a brake that keeps cells from dividing until the time is right
RB1.basis: key regulator of the G1/S transition of the cell cycle ... binds transcription regulators of the E2F family, preventing transcription of E2F-responsive genes ... thereby activating transcription of E2F responsive genes and triggering entry into S phase

RBCK1.job: tags proteins and stored sugar for handling, helping steer inflammation and glycogen breakdown
RBCK1.basis: Atypical E3 ubiquitin ligase that catalyzes ubiquitination of both proteins and carbohydrates, and which is involved in various processes, such as glycophagy, NF-kappa-B activation and regulation of inflammation ... promoting trafficking of ubiquitin-conjugated glycogen to lysosomes, where glycogen is degraded

RBFOX2.job: helps decide how a gene's message is cut and pieced together
RBFOX2.basis: RNA-binding protein that regulates alternative splicing events

RBM10.job: helps edit genetic messages before they are used to make proteins
RBM10.basis: Binds to ssRNA ... May be involved in post-transcriptional processing, most probably in mRNA splicing

RBM20.job: edits genetic messages to make the right versions of heart muscle proteins
RBM20.basis: RNA-binding protein that acts as a regulator of mRNA splicing of a subset of genes encoding key structural proteins involved in cardiac development, such as TTN (Titin)

RBM8A.job: marks where gene messages were spliced, guiding how they're used or discarded
RBM8A.basis: Core component of the splicing-dependent multiprotein exon junction complex (EJC) deposited at splice junctions on mRNAs ... The EJC marks the position of the exon-exon junction in the mature mRNA for the gene expression machinery ... thereby influencing downstream processes including nuclear mRNA export, subcellular mRNA localization, translation efficiency and nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD)

RBP3.job: carries vitamin A molecules between the eye's light-sensing cells and their support layer
RBP3.basis: Mediates the transport of 11-cis- and all-trans-retinoids between the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and photoreceptors, facilitating retinoid exchange required for the visual cycle

RBP4.job: carries vitamin A in the blood from the liver to the rest of the body
RBP4.basis: mediates retinol transport in blood plasma ... Delivers retinol from the liver stores to the peripheral tissues

RCBTB1.job: is thought to help control cell division
RCBTB1.basis: May be involved in cell cycle regulation by chromatin remodeling

RD3.job: escorts key light-signaling enzymes to the right spot in the eye's light-sensing cells
RD3.basis: Required for regulation and trafficking of retinal membrane guanylyl cyclases GUCY2D/RetGC1 and GUCY2F/RetGC2 in photoreceptor cells ... Mediates the export of retinal guanylyl cyclases (RetGCs) from the endoplasmic reticulum and inhibits their basal and GCAP-stimulated catalytic activity during intracellular transport to the photoreceptor outer segment

RDH12.job: converts vitamin A compounds and clears toxic byproducts in the eye's light-sensing cells
RDH12.basis: Retinoids dehydrogenase/reductase ... Displays high activity towards 9-cis, 11-cis and all-trans-retinal ... May play an important function in photoreceptor cells to detoxify 4-hydroxynonenal and potentially other toxic aldehyde products resulting from lipid peroxidation

RDH5.job: converts vitamin A into the form the eye's light sensors need
RDH5.basis: Catalyzes the oxidation of cis-isomers of retinol, including 11-cis-, 9-cis-, and 13-cis-retinol ... Plays a significant role in 11-cis retinol oxidation in the retinal pigment epithelium cells (RPE)

RDX.job: links the cell's inner support fibers to its outer membrane
RDX.basis: Probably plays a crucial role in the binding of the barbed end of actin filaments to the plasma membrane

RECQL4.job: unwinds short stretches of the DNA double strand
RECQL4.basis: An ATP-dependent DNA helicase which unwinds dsDNA with a 3'-overhang in a 3'-5' direction ... Does not unwind more than 18 bp of dsDNA

REEP6.job: helps keep the eye's light-sensing cells working and alive
REEP6.basis: Required for correct function and survival of retinal photoreceptors

RELA.job: switches on genes for inflammation and immune defense
RELA.basis: NF-kappa-B is a pleiotropic transcription factor ... initiated by a vast array of stimuli related to many biological processes such as inflammation, immunity ... The NF-kappa-B heterodimeric RELA-NFKB1 and RELA-REL complexes, for instance, function as transcriptional activators

RELB.job: switches on genes that help immune cells mature and work
RELB.basis: NF-kappa-B heterodimeric RelB-p50 and RelB-p52 complexes are transcriptional activators ... Is required for both T and B lymphocyte maturation and function

RELN.job: guides young brain cells into their proper layers as the brain develops
RELN.basis: plays a role in layering of neurons in the cerebral cortex and cerebellum by coordinating cell positioning during neurodevelopment

REN.job: starts the chain reaction that raises blood pressure
REN.basis: generate angiotensin I from angiotensinogen in the plasma, initiating a cascade of reactions that produce an elevation of blood pressure

RERE.job: helps switch off certain genes as the body develops
RERE.basis: Plays a role as a transcriptional repressor during development

RET.job: picks up growth signals that guide nerve and kidney development
RET.basis: Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase involved in numerous cellular mechanisms including cell proliferation, neuronal navigation, cell migration, and cell differentiation in response to glia cell line-derived growth family factors ... involved in the development of enteric nervous system and renal organogenesis during embryonic life

RETREG1.job: helps cells break off worn pieces of their protein-making factory for recycling
RETREG1.basis: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-anchored autophagy regulator which mediates ER delivery into lysosomes through sequestration into autophagosomes ... Promotes membrane remodeling and ER scission

RFC1.job: helps hold the DNA-copying machinery in place
RFC1.basis: Subunit of the replication factor C (RFC) complex which acts during elongation of primed DNA templates by DNA polymerases delta and epsilon, and is necessary for ATP-dependent loading of proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) onto primed DNA
RFC1.alt: helps load the clamp that holds DNA-copying machinery in place

RFX3.job: switches on genes that build the cell's hair-like antennae and hormone-making pancreas cells
RFX3.basis: Transcription factor required for ciliogenesis and islet cell differentiation during endocrine pancreas development ... Regulates the expression of genes involved in ciliary assembly

RFX5.job: switches on genes that let immune cells show germ pieces to other immune cells
RFX5.basis: Activates transcription from class II MHC promoters

RFX6.job: helps the pancreas form its hormone-making cells, including those that make insulin
RFX6.basis: Transcription factor required to direct islet cell differentiation during endocrine pancreas development ... and for the production of insulin

RFX7.job: switches on certain genes, helping keep natural killer immune cells going
RFX7.basis: Transcription factor ... Acts as a transcriptional activator by binding to promoter regions of target genes ... Plays a role in natural killer (NK) cell maintenance and immunity

RFXANK.job: switches on genes for the molecules immune cells use to show germ fragments
RFXANK.basis: Activates transcription from class II MHC promoters

RFXAP.job: helps switch on genes for the immune system's germ-display molecules
RFXAP.basis: Part of the RFX complex that binds to the X-box of MHC II promoters

RHBDF2.job: controls a cutting enzyme that releases growth and inflammation signals from cells
