RHBDF2.basis: Regulates ADAM17 protease, a sheddase of the epidermal growth factor (EGF) receptor ligands and TNF, thereby plays a role in sleep, cell survival, proliferation, migration and inflammation

RHO.job: catches light in the eye so you can see in dim light
RHO.basis: G protein-coupled photoreceptor that activates the G protein transducin (t) signaling pathway in response to light and is essential for image-forming vision under low-light conditions

RHOBTB2.job: helps control when cells grow and when they self-destruct
RHOBTB2.basis: Regulator of cell proliferation and apoptosis

RIN2.job: helps cells take in material from outside by switching on a sorting protein
RIN2.basis: May function as an upstream activator and/or downstream effector for RAB5B in endocytic pathway ... required for activating the RAB5 proteins
RIN2.alt: helps cells take in material from their surface by switching on a transport protein

RIPK1.job: decides whether a cell under inflammatory attack survives or self-destructs
RIPK1.basis: key regulator of TNF-mediated apoptosis, necroptosis and inflammatory pathways ... regulate cell death (apoptosis and necroptosis) and kinase-independent scaffold functions regulating inflammatory signaling and cell survival

RIPOR2.job: helps build and maintain the inner ear's sound-sensing hairs
RIPOR2.basis: Required for normal development of inner and outer hair cell stereocilia within the cochlea of the inner ear ... Plays a role for maintaining the structural organization of the basal domain of stereocilia

RIT1.job: passes on nerve growth signals that help nerve cells mature
RIT1.basis: Plays a crucial role in coupling nerve growth factor (NGF) stimulation to the activation of both EPHB2 and MAPK14 signaling pathways and in NGF-dependent neuronal differentiation

RLBP1.job: carries vitamin A molecules the eye recycles to keep sensing light
RLBP1.basis: Soluble retinoid carrier essential the proper function of both rod and cone photoreceptors. Participates in the regeneration of active 11-cis-retinol and 11-cis-retinaldehyde, from the inactive 11-trans products of the rhodopsin photocycle

RMND1.job: helps the cell's power plants build their own proteins
RMND1.basis: Required for mitochondrial translation, possibly by coordinating the assembly or maintenance of the mitochondrial ribosome

RNASEH2A.job: cuts stray RNA pieces out of DNA as cells copy it
RNASEH2A.basis: endonuclease that specifically degrades the RNA of RNA:DNA hybrids. Participates in DNA replication ... Mediates the excision of single ribonucleotides from DNA:RNA duplexes

RNASEH2B.job: is a supporting part of an enzyme that snips stray RNA pieces out of DNA
RNASEH2B.basis: Non catalytic subunit of RNase H2, an endonuclease that specifically degrades the RNA of RNA:DNA hybrids ... Mediates the excision of single ribonucleotides from DNA:RNA duplexes
RNASEH2B.alt: helps clear stray bits of RNA out of DNA as it is copied

RNASEH2C.job: is a supporting part of an enzyme that snips stray RNA bits out of DNA
RNASEH2C.basis: Non catalytic subunit of RNase H2, an endonuclease that specifically degrades the RNA of RNA:DNA hybrids ... Mediates the excision of single ribonucleotides from DNA:RNA duplexes
RNASEH2C.alt: is part of an enzyme that clears stray RNA pieces from DNA as it copies

RNF168.job: calls repair proteins to spots where DNA has broken
RNF168.basis: required for accumulation of repair proteins to sites of DNA damage ... Recruited to sites of DNA damage at double-strand breaks (DSBs)

RNF43.job: tags certain growth-signal receivers on cells for removal, damping those signals
RNF43.basis: acts as a negative regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway by mediating the ubiquitination, endocytosis and subsequent degradation of Wnt receptor complex components Frizzled

ROBO3.job: helps growing nerve fibers find their way across the body's midline
ROBO3.basis: Receptor involved in axon guidance during development ... In spinal cord development plays a role in guiding commissural axons

ROGDI.job: helps cells keep the right acid level inside their compartments
ROGDI.basis: Probably involved in the regulation of intracellular pH ... may control the assembly of the proton-pumping V-ATPase complex and therefore regulate organelle acidification
ROGDI.alt: helps cells control how acidic their inner compartments are

RORB.job: switches on genes that help the eye's light-sensing cells develop
RORB.basis: Nuclear receptor that binds DNA ... Considered to have intrinsic transcriptional activity ... Required for normal postnatal development of rod and cone photoreceptor cells

RP1.job: helps build the stacked light-catching disks in the eye's light-sensing cells
RP1.basis: regulating the stability and length of the microtubule-based axoneme of photoreceptors ... it plays a role in the organization of the outer segment of rod and cone photoreceptors ensuring the correct orientation and higher-order stacking of outer segment disks

RP1L1.job: helps the eye's light-sensing cells develop and organize their light-catching parts
RP1L1.basis: Required for the differentiation of photoreceptor cells. Plays a role in the organization of outer segment of rod and cone photoreceptors

RP2.job: helps deliver proteins to the cell's hair-like antennae
RP2.basis: involved in trafficking between the Golgi and the ciliary membrane. Involved in localization of proteins, such as NPHP3, to the cilium membrane

RPE65.job: recycles vitamin A so the eye's light-sensing cells can keep detecting light
RPE65.basis: Critical isomerohydrolase in the retinoid cycle involved in regeneration of 11-cis-retinal, the chromophore of rod and cone opsins ... Essential for the production of 11-cis retinal for both rod and cone photoreceptors

RPGR.job: helps move materials along the hair-like antennae of the eye's light-sensing cells
RPGR.basis: facilitate ciliary trafficking ... Involved in photoreceptor integrity

RPGRIP1.job: helps build the stacked discs that catch light in the eye's light-sensing cells
RPGRIP1.basis: Required for normal disk morphogenesis and disk organization in the outer segment of photoreceptor cells

RPGRIP1L.job: helps control protein breakdown at the base of the cell's antenna-like sensing hair
RPGRIP1L.basis: Involved in regulation of proteasomal activity at the primary cilium
RPGRIP1L.alt: helps cells in a tissue line up facing the same direction

RPL10.job: is part of the ribosome, the cell's machine for building proteins
RPL10.basis: Component of the large ribosomal subunit ... Plays a role in the formation of actively translating ribosomes

RPL5.job: is part of the ribosome, the cell's machine for building proteins
RPL5.basis: Component of the ribosome, a large ribonucleoprotein complex responsible for the synthesis of proteins in the cell ... it is an essential component of the LSU, required for its formation

RPS10.job: is part of the ribosome, the cell's machine for building proteins
RPS10.basis: Component of the 40S ribosomal subunit ... The ribosome is a large ribonucleoprotein complex responsible for the synthesis of proteins in the cell

RPS19.job: is part of the ribosome, the cell's machine for making proteins
RPS19.basis: Component of the small ribosomal subunit ... The ribosome is a large ribonucleoprotein complex responsible for the synthesis of proteins in the cell

RPS24.job: is part of the ribosome, the machine that builds proteins in every cell
RPS24.basis: Component of the small ribosomal subunit ... The ribosome is a large ribonucleoprotein complex responsible for the synthesis of proteins in the cell

RPS6KA3.job: relays growth signals that tell cells to grow, survive and specialize
RPS6KA3.basis: acts downstream of ERK (MAPK1/ERK2 and MAPK3/ERK1) signaling ... mediates cellular proliferation, survival, and differentiation

RRAS2.job: acts as a switch in signals that control how cells grow and develop
RRAS2.basis: GTP-binding protein with GTPase activity, involved in the regulation of MAPK signaling pathway and thereby controlling multiple cellular processes ... Regulates craniofacial development

RS1.job: helps hold retina cells together so the retina keeps its normal structure
RS1.basis: May play a role in cell-cell adhesion processes in the retina ... Required for normal structure and function of the retina

RSPH1.job: helps cell hairs and sperm tails beat so they can move
RSPH1.basis: Functions as part of axonemal radial spoke complexes that play an important part in the motility of sperm and cilia

RSPH3.job: is part of the spokes that help sperm tails and cell hairs beat
RSPH3.basis: Functions as part of axonemal radial spoke complexes that play an important part in the motility of sperm and cilia

RSPH4A.job: helps cells' tiny hair-like structures beat and move
RSPH4A.basis: Component of the axonemal radial spoke head which plays an important role in ciliary motility

RSPH9.job: helps cells' hair-like cilia and sperm tails beat and move
RSPH9.basis: Functions as part of axonemal radial spoke complexes that play an important part in the motility of sperm and cilia

RSRC1.job: helps cut and paste genetic messages before they are used to make proteins
RSRC1.basis: Involved in both constitutive and alternative pre-mRNA splicing

RTEL1.job: unwinds DNA to protect chromosome ends and keep DNA stable
RTEL1.basis: ATP-dependent DNA helicase implicated in telomere-length regulation, DNA repair and the maintenance of genomic stability ... ensure the dynamics and stability of the telomere

RTN4IP1.job: helps cells make coenzyme Q10, a molecule they need to produce energy
RTN4IP1.basis: NAD(P)H oxidoreductase involved in the ubiquinone biosynthetic pathway

RUNX1.job: switches on genes that guide the making of blood cells
RUNX1.basis: RUNX members modulate the transcription of their target genes ... Essential for the development of normal hematopoiesis

RXYLT1.job: helps attach a sugar chain that lets muscle cells grip their surroundings
RXYLT1.basis: catalyzes the transfer of UDP-D-xylose to ribitol 5-phosphate (Rbo5P) to form the Xylbeta1-4Rbo5P linkage on O-mannosyl glycan ... a carbohydrate structure present in alpha-dystroglycan (DAG1), which is required for binding laminin G-like domain-containing extracellular proteins with high affinity

RYR1.job: releases stored calcium inside muscle cells to make muscles contract
RYR1.basis: calcium channel that mediates the release of Ca(2+) from the sarcoplasmic reticulum into the cytosol and thereby plays a key role in triggering muscle contraction

RYR2.job: releases stored calcium inside heart muscle cells to make the heart contract
RYR2.basis: calcium channel that mediates the release of Ca(2+) from the sarcoplasmic reticulum into the cytosol and thereby plays a key role in triggering cardiac muscle contraction

S1PR2.job: picks up signals from a fat-based messenger that guide how cells grow and move
S1PR2.basis: Receptor for the lysosphingolipid sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) ... S1P is a bioactive lysophospholipid that elicits diverse physiological effects on most types of cells and tissues ... suppression of germinal center (GC) B cell growth and migration

SAG.job: switches off the light signal in the eye's rod cells after light hits them
SAG.basis: playing a key role in signal termination after rhodopsin (RHO) has been activated by light in rod photoreceptors

SALL1.job: switches off genes to help organs like the kidneys form
SALL1.basis: Transcriptional repressor involved in organogenesis. Plays an essential role in ureteric bud invasion during kidney development

SAMD9.job: helps cells defend themselves against viruses
SAMD9.basis: acts as an antiviral factor by playing an essential role in the formation of cytoplasmic antiviral granules

SAMD9L.job: helps cells pull growth signal receivers inside to tone down growth signals
SAMD9L.basis: Mediates down-regulation of growth factor signaling via internalization of growth factor receptors

SAMHD1.job: blocks viruses from copying themselves by using up the cell's DNA building blocks
SAMHD1.basis: acts both as a host restriction factor involved in defense response to virus ... dNTPase activity reduces cellular dNTP levels to levels too low for retroviral reverse transcription to occur, blocking early-stage virus replication

SASH3.job: helps pass signals along inside immune cells
SASH3.basis: May function as a signaling adapter protein in lymphocytes
SASH3.alt: helps pass signals along inside immune cells called lymphocytes

SATB1.job: folds DNA into loops to switch genes on or off, especially in immune cells
SATB1.basis: Transcriptional repressor controlling nuclear and viral gene expression ... by binding to matrix attachment regions (MARs) of DNA and inducing a local chromatin-loop remodeling ... recruiting corepressors (HDACs) or coactivators (HATs) directly to promoters and enhancers. Modulates genes that are essential in the maturation of the immune T-cell CD8SP from thymocytes

SATB2.job: loops DNA to switch genes on or off as the brain and skeleton develop
SATB2.basis: Transcription factor controlling nuclear gene expression, by binding to matrix attachment regions (MARs) of DNA and inducing a local chromatin-loop remodeling ... regulatory determinant of corticocortical connections in the developing cerebral cortex ... regulating skeletal development and osteoblast differentiation

SBDS.job: helps finish building ribosomes, the cell's protein-making machines
SBDS.basis: Required for the assembly of mature ribosomes and ribosome biogenesis ... activating ribosomes for translation competence ... Required for normal levels of protein synthesis

SBF2.job: switches on helpers that let cells deliver waste to their recycling centers
SBF2.basis: Guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) which activates RAB21 ... activates RAB21 which in turn binds to and regulates SNARE protein VAMP8 endolysosomal transport required for SNARE-mediated autophagosome-lysosome fusion

SCAF4.job: keeps gene copies from being cut off too early as they're made
SCAF4.basis: Anti-terminator protein required to prevent early mRNA termination during transcription ... thereby preventing the accumulation of non-functional truncated proteins

SCAPER.basis: CCNA2/CDK2 regulatory protein that transiently maintains CCNA2 in the cytoplasm
SCAPER.alt: helps time cell division by holding a cell-cycle protein outside the nucleus

SCARB2.job: steers a fat-digesting enzyme to the cell's recycling centers
SCARB2.basis: Acts as a lysosomal receptor for glucosylceramidase (GBA1) targeting

SCLT1.job: helps control a sodium channel in nerve cells
SCLT1.basis: Adapter protein that links SCN10A to clathrin. Regulates SCN10A channel activity, possibly by promoting channel internalization
SCLT1.alt: links a sodium channel in nerve cells to the cell's recycling machinery

SCN11A.job: lets sodium into nerve cells that carry pain signals to the brain
SCN11A.basis: Sodium channel mediating the voltage-dependent sodium ion permeability of excitable membranes ... Involved in membrane depolarization during action potential in nociceptors which function as key relay stations for the electrical transmission of pain signals from the periphery to the central nervous system

SCN1A.job: lets sodium into nerve cells so they can fire electrical signals
SCN1A.basis: Pore-forming subunit of Nav1.1, a voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channel that directly mediates the depolarizing phase of action potentials in excitable membranes ... In the open conformation they allow Na(+) ions to selectively pass through the pore ... initiating the propagation of electrical signals throughout cells and tissues ... By regulating the excitability of neurons

SCN1B.job: fine-tunes the sodium channels that let nerve and muscle cells fire electrical signals
SCN1B.basis: Regulatory subunit of multiple voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channels directly mediating the depolarization of excitable membranes ... initiating the propagation of electrical signals throughout cells and tissues ... The accessory beta subunits participate in localization and functional modulation of the Nav channels

SCN2A.job: lets sodium into nerve cells so they can fire electrical signals
SCN2A.basis: Mediates the voltage-dependent sodium ion permeability of excitable membranes ... the protein forms a sodium-selective channel through which Na(+) ions may pass

SCN3A.job: lets sodium into nerve cells to fire electrical signals
SCN3A.basis: Pore-forming subunit of Nav1.3, a voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channel that directly mediates the depolarizing phase of action potentials in excitable membranes ... they allow Na(+) ions to selectively pass through the pore ... initiating the propagation of electrical signals throughout cells and tissues

SCN4A.job: lets sodium into muscle cells to spark the electrical signals that make muscles contract
SCN4A.basis: Pore-forming subunit of Nav1.4, a voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channel ... allow Na(+) ions to selectively pass through the pore ... Highly expressed in skeletal muscles, Nav1.4 generates the action potential crucial for muscle contraction

SCN5A.job: lets sodium into heart muscle cells to start each heartbeat
SCN5A.basis: In the open conformation they allow Na(+) ions to selectively pass through the pore ... Nav1.5 is the predominant sodium channel expressed in myocardial cells and it is responsible for the initial upstroke of the action potential in cardiac myocytes, thereby initiating the heartbeat

SCN8A.job: forms a channel that lets sodium into nerve cells so they can fire signals
SCN8A.basis: Pore-forming subunit of a voltage-gated sodium channel complex ... through which sodium ions selectively pass ... Contributes to neuronal excitability by regulating action potential threshold and propagation

SCNN1A.job: forms part of a channel that lets sodium into cells, helping the body balance salt and water
SCNN1A.basis: one of the three pore-forming subunits of the heterotrimeric epithelial sodium channel (ENaC), a critical regulator of sodium balance and fluid homeostasis ... mediates the electrodiffusion of sodium ions from extracellular fluid through the apical membrane of cells, with water following osmotically

SCNN1G.job: is part of a channel that lets salt into cells to balance body fluids
SCNN1G.basis: one of the three pore-forming subunits of the heterotrimeric epithelial sodium channel (ENaC), a critical regulator of sodium balance and fluid homeostasis ... mediates the electrodiffusion of sodium ions from extracellular fluid through the apical membrane of cells

SCO1.job: delivers copper to an enzyme the cell's power plants need to make energy
SCO1.basis: Copper metallochaperone essential for the maturation of cytochrome c oxidase subunit II (MT-CO2/COX2) ... involved in delivering copper to the Cu(A) site on MT-CO2/COX2

SCO2.job: delivers copper to a key energy-making enzyme in the cell's power plants
SCO2.basis: Copper metallochaperone essential for the synthesis and maturation of cytochrome c oxidase subunit II (MT-CO2/COX2) ... facilitates the incorporation of copper into the Cu(A) site of MT-CO2/COX2

SCP2.job: helps cells break down certain fats and make bile acids
SCP2.basis: Plays a crucial role in the peroxisomal oxidation of branched-chain fatty acids ... Catalyzes the last step of the peroxisomal beta-oxidation of branched chain fatty acids and the side chain of the bile acid intermediates
SCP2.alt: helps cells break down certain branched fats and make bile acids

SDCCAG8.job: helps cells build their antenna-like sensing hairs
SDCCAG8.basis: plays an essential role in ciliogenesis ... requires the presence of intact primary cilia

SDHA.job: helps the cell's power plants turn food into energy
SDHA.basis: involved in complex II of the mitochondrial electron transport chain and is responsible for transferring electrons from succinate to ubiquinone (coenzyme Q)

SDHAF1.job: helps assemble an enzyme that cells' power plants use to make energy
SDHAF1.basis: Plays an essential role in the assembly of succinate dehydrogenase (SDH), an enzyme complex ... that is a component of both the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and the mitochondrial electron transport chain

SDHAF2.job: helps build an enzyme that cells' power plants use to make energy
SDHAF2.basis: Plays an essential role in the assembly of succinate dehydrogenase (SDH), an enzyme complex ... that is a component of both the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and the mitochondrial electron transport chain

SDHC.job: anchors a key energy-making enzyme inside the cell's power plants
SDHC.basis: Membrane-anchoring subunit of succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) that is involved in complex II of the mitochondrial electron transport chain

SDHD.job: anchors an energy-making enzyme in the cell's power plants
SDHD.basis: Membrane-anchoring subunit of succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) that is involved in complex II of the mitochondrial electron transport chain

SEC23B.job: helps package newly made proteins into bubbles for shipping inside the cell
SEC23B.basis: Component of the coat protein complex II (COPII) which promotes the formation of transport vesicles from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) ... the selection of cargo molecules for their transport to the Golgi complex

SEC63.job: helps move newly made proteins into the cell's protein-processing compartment
SEC63.basis: Mediates cotranslational and post-translational transport of certain precursor polypeptides across endoplasmic reticulum (ER)

SELENON.job: protects cells from oxidative damage and helps them manage their calcium stores
SELENON.basis: Plays an important role in cell protection against oxidative stress and in the regulation of redox-related calcium homeostasis ... Regulates the calcium level of the ER by protecting the calcium pump ATP2A2 against the oxidoreductase ERO1A-mediated oxidative damage

SEMA6B.job: steers growing nerve fibers in the brain's memory center by pushing them away
SEMA6B.basis: Functions as a cell surface repellent for mossy fibers of developing neurons in the hippocampus where it plays a role in axon guidance

SERAC1.job: helps bring serine, a building block, into mitochondria, the cell's power plants
SERAC1.basis: Facilitates the transport of serine from the cytosol to the mitochondria ... playing a fundamental role in the one-carbon cycle responsible for the synthesis of nucleotides needed for mitochondrial DNA replication

SERPINC1.job: keeps blood from clotting too much by blocking clotting proteins
SERPINC1.basis: Most important serine protease inhibitor in plasma that regulates the blood coagulation cascade ... AT-III inhibits thrombin ... as well as factors IXa, Xa and XIa

SERPIND1.job: blocks thrombin, a key clotting protein, to keep blood from clotting too much
SERPIND1.basis: Thrombin inhibitor activated by the glycosaminoglycans, heparin or dermatan sulfate

SERPINE1.job: keeps blood clots from breaking down too quickly
SERPINE1.basis: Is a primary inhibitor of tissue-type plasminogen activator (PLAT) ... it is required for fibrinolysis down-regulation and is responsible for the controlled degradation of blood clots

SERPINF2.job: switches off certain protein-cutting enzymes, mainly plasmin and trypsin
SERPINF2.basis: Serine protease inhibitor. The major targets of this inhibitor are plasmin and trypsin

SERPING1.job: keeps part of the immune system's germ-attacking defenses in check
SERPING1.basis: Serine protease inhibitor, which acrs as a regulator of the classical complement pathway

SERPINI1.job: blocks certain enzymes that cut other proteins
SERPINI1.basis: Serine protease inhibitor that inhibits plasminogen activators and plasmin ... May protect neurons from cell damage by tissue-type plasminogen activator
SERPINI1.alt: blocks certain protein-cutting enzymes, which may help protect nerve cells

SET.job: helps package DNA around its protein spools and keep certain genes quiet
SET.basis: Multitasking protein, involved in apoptosis, transcription, nucleosome assembly and histone chaperoning ... HAT inhibition leads to silencing of HAT-dependent transcription

SETD1B.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging that help switch genes on
SETD1B.basis: Histone methyltransferase that catalyzes methyl group transfer ... to ... histone H3 (H3K4) ... forms H3K4me1, H3K4me2 and H3K4me3 methylation marks at active chromatin sites where transcription and DNA repair take place

SETD2.job: adds chemical tags to DNA's packaging that mark active genes and guide DNA repair
SETD2.basis: Histone methyltransferase that specifically trimethylates 'Lys-36' of histone H3 (H3K36me3) ... a specific tag for epigenetic transcriptional activation ... Acts as a key regulator of DNA mismatch repair

SETD5.job: controls how DNA is packed to guide how genes are read during brain development
SETD5.basis: Chromatin regulator required for brain development: acts as a regulator of RNA elongation rate

SETX.job: unwinds tangles of RNA stuck to DNA so genes can finish being read
SETX.basis: ATP-dependent 5'-3' helicase that preferentially unwinds RNA:DNA substrates over DNA:DNA substrates, playing a crucial role in resolving 5'-overhang RNA:DNA hybrids (R-loops) and promoting transcription termination

SF3B4.job: is part of the machinery that cuts unneeded pieces out of a gene's message
SF3B4.basis: Component of the 17S U2 SnRNP complex of the spliceosome, a large ribonucleoprotein complex that removes introns from transcribed pre-mRNAs

SFTPA2.job: helps keep the lung's tiny air sacs from collapsing so breathing stays easy
SFTPA2.basis: binds to surfactant phospholipids and contributes to lower the surface tension at the air-liquid interface in the alveoli of the mammalian lung and is essential for normal respiration

SFTPB.job: helps keep the lungs' tiny air sacs from collapsing
SFTPB.basis: Pulmonary surfactant-associated proteins promote alveolar stability by lowering the surface tension at the air-liquid interface in the peripheral air spaces

SFTPC.job: helps keep the lungs' tiny air sacs open by lowering surface tension
SFTPC.basis: Pulmonary surfactant associated proteins promote alveolar stability by lowering the surface tension at the air-liquid interface in the peripheral air spaces

SFXN4.job: carries amino acids into the cell's power plants
SFXN4.alt: carries amino acids into the cell's energy-making compartments

SGCA.job: helps anchor muscle cells to their surroundings so they hold up as they contract
SGCA.basis: Component of the sarcoglycan complex, a subcomplex of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex which forms a link between the F-actin cytoskeleton and the extracellular matrix
SGCA.alt: is one of four parts of the muscle sarcoglycan bundle that ties each cell's inner frame to its outside support

SGCB.job: helps anchor muscle cells to their surroundings so they hold up as they contract
SGCB.basis: Component of the sarcoglycan complex, a subcomplex of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex which forms a link between the F-actin cytoskeleton and the extracellular matrix
SGCB.alt: is the beta piece of a muscle-cell anchor tying the cell's inner skeleton to its surroundings

SGCD.job: helps anchor muscle cells to their surroundings so they hold up as they contract
SGCD.basis: Component of the sarcoglycan complex ... which forms a link between the F-actin cytoskeleton and the extracellular matrix
SGCD.alt: links the inner scaffolding of skeletal, heart and smooth muscle cells to their surroundings

SGCG.job: helps anchor muscle cells to their surroundings so they hold up as they contract
SGCG.basis: Component of the sarcoglycan complex, a subcomplex of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex which forms a link between the F-actin cytoskeleton and the extracellular matrix
SGCG.alt: is the gamma part of a muscle anchor linking each fiber's inner scaffold to its surroundings

SGPL1.job: breaks down a fat-based signaling molecule so the body can clear it
SGPL1.basis: Cleaves phosphorylated sphingoid bases (PSBs), such as sphingosine-1-phosphate, into fatty aldehydes and phosphoethanolamine

SGSH.job: helps the cell's recycling centers break down a long sugar chain
SGSH.basis: Catalyzes a step in lysosomal heparan sulfate degradation

SH2B3.job: helps pass on signals inside immune cells
SH2B3.basis: Links T-cell receptor activation signal to phospholipase C-gamma-1, GRB2 and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase
SH2B3.alt: passes on activation signals inside immune T cells

SH2D1A.job: helps immune cells pass on signals that switch on their attack on infected cells
SH2D1A.basis: Cytoplasmic adapter regulating receptors of the signaling lymphocytic activation molecule (SLAM) family ... Positively regulates CD244/2B4- and CD84-mediated natural killer (NK) cell functions ... In the context of NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity enhances conjugate formation with target cells

SH3PXD2B.job: helps cells build tiny feet that break down the material around them
SH3PXD2B.basis: Adapter protein involved in invadopodia and podosome formation and extracellular matrix degradation

SH3TC2.job: helps build the insulating coat that wraps nerve fibers
SH3TC2.basis: Is involved in nerve myelination and is required for the integrity of nodes of Ranvier

SHANK1.job: helps hold together the receiving side of connections between brain cells
SHANK1.basis: adapter protein in the postsynaptic density (PSD) of excitatory synapses that interconnects receptors of the postsynaptic membrane ... Plays a role in the structural and functional organization of the dendritic spine and synaptic junction

SHANK2.job: links signal receivers to the inner scaffolding where brain cells connect
SHANK2.basis: adapter protein in the postsynaptic density (PSD) of excitatory synapses that interconnects receptors of the postsynaptic membrane ... and the actin-based cytoskeleton

SHH.job: sends signals that shape the body's layout as an embryo develops
SHH.basis: a morphogen that activates the smoothened signaling pathway, and which is essential for a variety of patterning events during development

SHOC2.job: holds together a team that switches on growth signals inside cells
SHOC2.basis: Core component of the SHOC2-MRAS-PP1c (SMP) holophosphatase complex that regulates activation of the MAPK pathway ... Acts as a scaffolding protein in the SMP complex ... stimulating their kinase activities

SIL1.job: helps newly made proteins fold into the right shape inside the cell
SIL1.basis: Required for protein translocation and folding in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) ... nucleotide exchange factor for the ER lumenal chaperone HSPA5

SIX1.job: switches on genes that help the kidneys, muscles and inner ear develop
SIX1.basis: Transcription factor that is involved in the regulation of cell proliferation, apoptosis and embryonic development ... Plays an important role in the development of several organs, including kidney, muscle and inner ear

SKI.job: turns down growth signals that shape how cells develop
SKI.basis: Functions as a repressor of TGF-beta signaling

SKIC2.job: helps the cell break down used or faulty genetic messages
SKIC2.basis: Helicase component of the SKI complex, a multiprotein complex that assists the RNA-degrading exosome during the mRNA decay and quality-control pathways ... channels mRNA to the cytosolic exosome for degradation

SKIC3.job: helps cells clear away used or faulty gene messages for disposal
SKIC3.basis: Component of the SKI complex, a multiprotein complex that assists the RNA-degrading exosome during the mRNA decay and quality-control pathways ... channels mRNA to the cytosolic exosome for degradation

SLC10A7.job: helps build the sugar-coated material that lets bones and teeth form and harden
SLC10A7.basis: Involved in teeth and skeletal development ... essential role in the biosynthesis and trafficking of glycosaminoglycans and glycoproteins, to produce a proper functioning extracellular matrix. Required for extracellular matrix mineralization

SLC11A2.job: helps absorb iron from food and carries it into cells
SLC11A2.basis: Essential for maintenance of iron homeostasis by modulating intestinal absorption of dietary Fe(2+) and TF-associated endosomal Fe(2+) transport in erythroid precursors and other cells

SLC12A1.job: helps the kidneys pull salt back from urine into the body
SLC12A1.basis: Renal sodium, potassium and chloride non-electrogenic ion symporter that mediates the transepithelial NaCl reabsorption in the thick ascending limb and plays an essential role in the urinary concentration and volume regulation

SLC16A2.job: carries thyroid hormone into and out of cells, including into the brain
SLC16A2.basis: Specific thyroid hormone transmembrane transporter, that mediates both uptake and efflux of thyroid hormones across the cell membrane ... Acts as an important mediator of thyroid hormone transport, especially T3, through the blood-brain barrier

SLC17A5.job: moves leftover sugar pieces out of the cell's recycling centers
SLC17A5.basis: Exports glucuronic acid and free sialic acid derived from sialoglycoconjugate degradation out of lysosomes

SLC17A8.job: loads the chemical messenger glutamate into packets nerve cells release to signal
SLC17A8.basis: mainly functions as an uniporter that mediates the uptake of L-glutamate into synaptic vesicles at presynaptic nerve terminals of excitatory neural cells

SLC18A2.job: packs brain chemical messengers like dopamine and serotonin into tiny sacs for release
SLC18A2.basis: accumulate high concentrations of monoamines inside the vesicles prior to their release via exocytosis ... Transports a variety of catecholamines such as dopamine, adrenaline and noradrenaline, histamine, and indolamines such as serotonin

SLC1A2.job: clears the chemical messenger glutamate from between brain cells after signaling
SLC1A2.basis: mediates the uptake of L-glutamate ... Essential for the rapid removal of released glutamate from the synaptic cleft, and for terminating the postsynaptic action of glutamate

SLC1A3.job: clears the chemical messenger glutamate from between brain cells after signals
SLC1A3.basis: mediates the uptake of L-glutamate ... rapid removal of released glutamate from the synaptic cleft, which is essential for terminating the postsynaptic action of glutamate

SLC1A4.job: swaps small amino acids like serine in and out of cells, including brain cells
SLC1A4.basis: Sodium-coupled antiporter of neutral amino acids ... exchanges neutral amino acids between the extracellular and intracellular compartments ... Exchanges neutral amino acids such as L- and D-serine, L-threonine, L-asparagine and L-alanine ... In astrocytes at excitatory synapses, mediates electrogenic D-serine influx coupled to L-serine efflux and L-serine shuttling to neurons

SLC22A5.job: brings carnitine into cells, a nutrient they need to burn fat for energy
SLC22A5.basis: high affinity carnitine transporter. Involved in the active cellular uptake of carnitine

SLC24A1.job: pumps calcium out of the eye's light-sensing cells to adjust to changing light
SLC24A1.basis: Is involved in calcium homeostasis in retinal rod photoreceptors and plays a central role in light adaptation ... it mediates calcium efflux ... enable adaptation to changing light conditions

SLC25A1.job: moves citrate out of the cell's power plants so cells can make fats
SLC25A1.basis: exports citrate from the mitochondria into the cytosol in exchange for malate ... In the cytoplasm, citrate plays important roles in fatty acid and sterol synthesis

SLC25A13.job: swaps two amino acids across the walls of the cell's energy factories
SLC25A13.basis: Mitochondrial electrogenic aspartate/glutamate antiporter that favors efflux of aspartate and entry of glutamate and proton within the mitochondria

SLC25A15.job: swaps building blocks in and out of the cell's power plants to help clear waste nitrogen
SLC25A15.basis: Mitochondrial ornithine-citrulline antiporter ... Catalyzes the exchange between cytosolic ornithine and mitochondrial citrulline ... Plays a crucial role in the urea cycle, by connecting the cytosolic and the intramitochondrial reactions of the urea cycle

SLC25A20.job: carries fats into the cell's power plants so they can be burned for energy
SLC25A20.basis: Key player in the mitochondrial oxidation pathway, it translocates the fatty acids in the form of acylcarnitines into the mitochondrial matrix ... to undergo fatty acid beta-oxidation

SLC25A22.job: carries glutamate, an amino acid, into the cell's energy factories
SLC25A22.basis: Responsible for the transport of glutamate from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix

SLC25A24.job: moves the cell's energy molecule in and out of the cell's power plants
SLC25A24.basis: Electroneutral antiporter that mediates the transport of adenyl nucleotides through the inner mitochondrial membrane. Originally identified as an ATP-magnesium/inorganic phosphate antiporter
SLC25A24.alt: moves ATP, the cell's energy molecule, in and out of mitochondria, the cell's power plants

SLC25A26.job: brings a key chemical-tagging molecule into the cell's power plants
SLC25A26.basis: Mitochondrial S-adenosyl-L-methionine/S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine antiporter ... Mediates the exchange of cytosolic S-adenosyl-L-methionine, the predominant methyl-group donor for macromolecule methylation processes, for mitochondrial S-adenosylhomocysteine(SAH), a by-product of methylation reactions

SLC25A4.job: swaps spent fuel for fresh energy across the walls of the cell's power plants
SLC25A4.basis: ADP:ATP antiporter that mediates import of ADP into the mitochondrial matrix for ATP synthesis, and export of ATP out to fuel the cell

SLC25A46.job: helps shape and organize mitochondria, the cell's power plants
SLC25A46.basis: Transmembrane protein of the mitochondrial outer membrane that controls mitochondrial organization

SLC26A2.job: brings sulfate into cartilage cells so cartilage can form properly
SLC26A2.basis: Sulfate transporter which mediates sulfate uptake into chondrocytes in order to maintain adequate sulfation of proteoglycans which is needed for cartilage development

SLC26A4.job: moves chloride and iodide in and out of cells
SLC26A4.basis: Sodium-independent transporter of chloride and iodide ... Mediates electroneutral chloride-bicarbonate, chloride-iodide and chloride-formate exchange

SLC29A3.job: moves DNA and RNA building blocks out of the cell's recycling centers
SLC29A3.basis: Uniporter that mediates the facilitative transport of nucleoside across lysosomal and mitochondrial membranes ... May direct the nucleoside transport from lysosomes to cytosol or cytosol to mitochondria to facilitate nucleic acid salvage pathways

SLC2A1.job: carries sugar into cells, including across the barrier into the brain
SLC2A1.basis: Facilitative glucose transporter, which is responsible for constitutive or basal glucose uptake ... Most important energy carrier of the brain: present at the blood-brain barrier and assures the energy-independent, facilitative transport of glucose into the brain

SLC2A10.job: moves sugar into cells and helps the heart and blood vessels develop
SLC2A10.basis: Facilitative glucose transporter required for the development of the cardiovascular system

SLC30A2.job: moves zinc into storage pockets inside cells and into breast milk
SLC30A2.basis: concentrating zinc ions into a variety of intracellular organelles ... Regulates the zinc concentration of milk, through the transport of zinc ions into secretory vesicles of mammary cells

SLC30A9.job: moves zinc out of mitochondria, the cell's power plants
SLC30A9.basis: Mitochondrial proton-coupled zinc ion antiporter mediating the export of zinc from the mitochondria

SLC34A1.job: helps the kidneys take phosphate back into the body
SLC34A1.basis: actively transporting phosphate into cells via Na(+) cotransport in the renal brush border membrane

SLC35A2.job: carries a sugar into the cell's packaging center for decorating proteins and fats
SLC35A2.basis: Transports uridine diphosphate galactose (UDP-galactose) from the cytosol into the Golgi apparatus ... As a provider of UDP-galactose to galactosyltransferases present in the Golgi apparatus

SLC35C1.job: carries the sugar fucose into the cell's packaging center so it can tag proteins
SLC35C1.basis: Antiporter specific for GDP-l-fucose ... Involved in GDP-fucose import from the cytoplasm into the Golgi lumen

SLC35D1.job: carries sugar building blocks into the cell's factory to make sugar chains
SLC35D1.basis: transports nucleotide sugars across the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane ... which are used by ER glucosyltransferases as sugar donors for the synthesis of sugar chains of glycoproteins, glycolipids and oligosaccharides

SLC38A8.job: carries amino acids like glutamine into cells, including brain cells
SLC38A8.basis: Electrogenic sodium-dependent amino acid transporter with a preference for L-glutamine ... May facilitate glutamine uptake in both excitatory and inhibitory neurons

SLC39A13.job: moves zinc out of the cell's packaging center into the rest of the cell
SLC39A13.basis: Functions as a zinc transporter transporting Zn(2+) from the Golgi apparatus to the cytosol

SLC39A4.job: helps the gut absorb zinc from food
SLC39A4.basis: Selective transporter that mediates the uptake of Zn(2+) ... Plays an essential role for dietary zinc uptake from small intestine

SLC3A1.job: helps the kidneys reclaim cystine and other amino acids from urine
SLC3A1.basis: Acts as a chaperone that facilitates biogenesis and trafficking of functional transporter heteromers to the plasma membrane ... SLC7A9-SLC3A1 acts as a major transporter for reabsorption of L-cystine and dibasic amino acids across the brush border membrane in early proximal tubules

SLC40A1.job: moves iron out of cells and into the blood
SLC40A1.basis: Transports Fe(2+) from the inside of a cell to the outside of the cell ... Transports iron from intestinal, splenic, hepatic cells, macrophages and erythrocytes into the blood to provide iron to other tissues

SLC46A1.job: absorbs folate, a B vitamin, from food in the gut and carries it into the brain
SLC46A1.basis: Proton-coupled folate symporter that mediates folate absorption ... Involved in the intestinal absorption of folates ... and the transport from blood to cerebrospinal fluid across the choroid plexus

SLC4A10.job: moves sodium and bicarbonate into cells to control acidity, especially in brain cells
SLC4A10.basis: Sodium/bicarbonate cotransporter which plays an important role in regulating intracellular pH ... Controls neuronal pH

SLC52A2.basis: Plasma membrane transporter mediating the uptake by cells of the water soluble vitamin B2/riboflavin

SLC52A3.job: brings vitamin B2 into cells, including from food in the gut
SLC52A3.basis: Plasma membrane transporter mediating the uptake by cells of the water soluble vitamin B2/riboflavin ... must obtain it via intestinal absorption

SLC6A19.job: pulls protein building blocks from food and urine back into the body
SLC6A19.basis: Transporter that mediates resorption of neutral amino acids across the apical membrane of renal and intestinal epithelial cells

SLC6A3.job: pulls the brain messenger dopamine back into nerve cells after use
SLC6A3.basis: Mediates sodium- and chloride-dependent transport of dopamine

SLC6A5.job: pulls the chemical messenger glycine back into nerve cells after signaling
SLC6A5.basis: Sodium- and chloride-dependent glycine transporter ... Terminates the action of glycine by its high affinity sodium-dependent reuptake into presynaptic terminals

SLC6A8.job: carries creatine, an energy-storing nutrient, into cells, including brain cells
SLC6A8.basis: Creatine:sodium symporter which mediates the uptake of creatine ... Plays an important role in supplying creatine to the brain via the blood-brain barrier

SLC6A9.job: clears the messenger chemical glycine from junctions between nerve cells
SLC6A9.basis: Sodium- and chloride-dependent glycine transporter ... Essential for regulating glycine concentrations at inhibitory glycinergic synapses

SLC7A7.job: moves certain amino acids, like arginine, out of cells
SLC7A7.basis: functions as an antiporter which operates as an efflux route by exporting cationic amino acids from inside the cells ... via the transport of L-arginine

SLC7A9.job: helps the kidneys reclaim cystine and other amino acids from urine
SLC7A9.basis: Required for reabsorption of L-cystine and dibasic amino acids across the brush border membrane in renal proximal tubules

SLC9A6.job: keeps the cell's internal delivery bubbles from getting too acidic
SLC9A6.basis: Endosomal Na(+), K(+)/H(+) antiporter ... counteracts the acidity generated by vacuolar (V)-ATPase, thereby limiting luminal acidification. Responsible for alkalizing and maintaining the endosomal pH

SLITRK6.job: helps nerve fibers grow so hearing and vision develop normally
SLITRK6.basis: Regulator of neurite outgrowth required for normal hearing and vision

SMAD2.job: carries growth-factor signals from the cell surface to switch on genes
SMAD2.basis: intracellular signal transducer and transcriptional modulator activated by TGF-beta (transforming growth factor) ... Binds the TRE element in the promoter region of many genes that are regulated by TGF-beta and, on formation of the SMAD2/SMAD4 complex, activates transcription

SMAD3.job: carries growth-factor signals from the cell surface to switch genes on
SMAD3.basis: intracellular signal transducer and transcriptional modulator activated by TGF-beta (transforming growth factor) ... Binds the TRE element in the promoter region of many genes that are regulated by TGF-beta and, on formation of the SMAD3/SMAD4 complex, activates transcription

SMAD4.job: carries growth-control signals from the cell's surface to its genes
SMAD4.basis: Common SMAD (co-SMAD) is the coactivator and mediator of signal transduction by TGF-beta (transforming growth factor) ... Promotes binding of the SMAD2/SMAD4/FAST-1 complex to DNA and provides an activation function required for SMAD1 or SMAD2 to stimulate transcription

SMAD6.job: dampens growth signals that guide how bones and other tissues form
SMAD6.basis: Acts as an inhibitory regulator of signaling mediated by the TGF-beta superfamily, with strong selectivity toward BMP-dependent pathways ... Blocks the BMP-SMAD1 signaling pathway

SMAD9.job: carries bone-growth signals from the cell surface to switch genes on or off
SMAD9.basis: Transcriptional modulator activated by BMP (bone morphogenetic proteins) type 1 receptor kinase

SMARCA4.job: uses energy to unpack DNA so certain genes can switch on or off
SMARCA4.basis: ATPase involved in transcriptional activation and repression of select genes by chromatin remodeling ... changing chromatin structure by altering DNA-histone contacts within a nucleosome in an ATP-dependent manner

SMARCAL1.job: rewinds stretches of unwound DNA, helping when DNA copying stalls
SMARCAL1.basis: catalyzes the rewinding of the stably unwound DNA ... May play an important role in DNA damage response by acting at stalled replication forks

SMARCB1.job: is part of a team that unpacks DNA to control which genes are used
SMARCB1.basis: Core component of the BAF (hSWI/SNF) complex. This ATP-dependent chromatin-remodeling complex plays important roles in cell proliferation and differentiation ... The nBAF complex along with CREST plays a role regulating the activity of genes

SMARCC1.job: is part of a machine that unpacks DNA to switch certain genes on or off
SMARCC1.basis: Involved in transcriptional activation and repression of select genes by chromatin remodeling ... Component of SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes

SMARCC2.job: is part of a machine that unpacks DNA to switch certain genes on or off
SMARCC2.basis: Involved in transcriptional activation and repression of select genes by chromatin remodeling ... Component of SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes

SMARCE1.job: is part of a team that unpacks DNA to switch certain genes on or off
SMARCE1.basis: Involved in transcriptional activation and repression of select genes by chromatin remodeling (alteration of DNA-nucleosome topology). Component of SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes

SMC1A.job: holds copied chromosomes together until the cell divides
SMC1A.basis: Involved in chromosome cohesion during cell cycle and in DNA repair. Central component of cohesin complex. The cohesin complex is required for the cohesion of sister chromatids after DNA replication ... At anaphase, the complex is cleaved and dissociates from chromatin, allowing sister chromatids to segregate

SMC3.job: holds copied chromosomes together until the cell is ready to divide
SMC3.basis: Central component of cohesin, a complex required for chromosome cohesion during the cell cycle ... At anaphase, the complex is cleaved and dissociates from chromatin, allowing sister chromatids to segregate

SMCHD1.job: packs DNA tightly to keep certain genes switched off
SMCHD1.basis: plays a key role in epigenetic silencing by regulating chromatin architecture ... Promotes heterochromatin formation in both autosomes and chromosome X

SMG8.job: helps cells destroy faulty genetic messages that would make broken proteins
SMG8.basis: Involved in nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) of mRNAs containing premature stop codons

SMO.job: passes on hedgehog signals that switch on genes guiding how the body develops
SMO.basis: G protein-coupled receptor, which transduces the smoothened signaling pathway ... Activated by cholesterol in response to hedgehog (DHH, IHH or SHH) morphogens ... promote release of GLI (GLI1, GLI2 and GLI3) transcription factors, which activate expression of target genes

SMPD1.job: breaks down a fatty substance called sphingomyelin in the cell's recycling centers
SMPD1.basis: Converts sphingomyelin to ceramide ... one that is targeted to the endolysosomal compartment

SMPX.job: helps muscle cells keep their structure as they grow and repair
SMPX.basis: Plays a role in the regulatory network through which muscle cells coordinate their structural and functional states during growth, adaptation, and repair
SMPX.alt: helps muscle cells keep their structure and work in step as they grow and repair

SMS.job: makes spermine, a small molecule cells need to grow and work properly
SMS.basis: Catalyzes the production of spermine from spermidine and decarboxylated S-adenosylmethionine (dcSAM)

SNAP25.job: helps nerve cells release chemical messages to their neighbors
SNAP25.basis: t-SNARE involved in the molecular regulation of neurotransmitter release ... Associates with proteins involved in vesicle docking and membrane fusion

SNCA.job: helps nerve cells release chemical messages to each other
SNCA.basis: Neuronal protein that plays several roles in synaptic activity such as regulation of synaptic vesicle trafficking and subsequent neurotransmitter release

SNRNP200.job: helps cut and paste gene messages into their final form
SNRNP200.basis: Catalyzes the ATP-dependent unwinding of U4/U6 RNA duplices, an essential step in the assembly of a catalytically active spliceosome ... Plays a role in pre-mRNA splicing as a core component of precatalytic, catalytic and postcatalytic spliceosomal complexes

SNUPN.job: carries gene-editing helper molecules into the cell's control center
SNUPN.basis: Functions as an U snRNP-specific nuclear import adapter. ... Involved in the trimethylguanosine (m3G)-cap-dependent nuclear import of U snRNPs

SNX10.job: helps sort and deliver proteins inside cells, including to bone-clearing cells
SNX10.basis: involved in protein sorting and membrane trafficking in endosomes ... Involved in osteoclast differentiation and therefore bone resorption

SNX14.job: helps cells clear out worn-out parts by delivering them to recycling centers
SNX14.basis: Required for autophagosome clearance, possibly by mediating the fusion of lysosomes with autophagosomes

SOCS1.job: turns down immune alarm signals so the body's defenses don't overreact
SOCS1.basis: Essential negative regulator of type I and type II interferon (IFN) signaling, as well as that of other cytokines ... Down-regulates cytokine signaling by inhibiting the JAK/STAT signaling pathway

SOD1.job: destroys harmful molecules that cells make as a natural byproduct
SOD1.basis: Destroys radicals which are normally produced within the cells and which are toxic to biological systems

SON.job: helps cells edit gene messages correctly, including ones needed for brain development
SON.basis: RNA-binding protein that acts as a mRNA splicing cofactor by promoting efficient splicing of transcripts that possess weak splice sites ... Essential for correct RNA splicing of multiple genes critical for brain development

SORD.job: turns sorbitol, a sugar alcohol, into fructose as the body processes sugar
SORD.basis: Is mostly active with D-sorbitol (D-glucitol) ... leading to the C2-oxidized products D-fructose ... Is a key enzyme in the polyol pathway that interconverts glucose and fructose via sorbitol, which constitutes an important alternate route for glucose metabolism

SOS1.job: switches on a growth-signal relay inside cells, passing messages along
SOS1.basis: Promotes the exchange of Ras-bound GDP by GTP ... Probably by promoting Ras activation, regulates phosphorylation of MAP kinase MAPK3/ERK1 in response to EGF ... participates in transduction of signals from Ras to Rac

SOS2.job: switches on a protein that passes growth signals inside cells
SOS2.basis: Acts as guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) for RAS proteins ... resulting in an increase of the active GTP-bound form of HRAS
SOS2.alt: switches on RAS, a protein that passes growth signals inside cells

SOX10.job: switches on genes that build the protective coating around nerve fibers
SOX10.basis: Transcription factor that plays a central role in developing and mature glia ... Specifically activates expression of myelin genes ... thereby playing a central role in oligodendrocyte maturation and CNS myelination

SOX11.job: switches on genes that help developing tissues survive and form organs
SOX11.basis: Transcription factor that acts as a transcriptional activator ... cell survival of developing tissues such as the neural tube, branchial arches and somites, thereby contributing to organogenesis

SOX17.job: switches on genes that help the embryo's gut, heart and blood vessels form
SOX17.basis: Acts as a transcription regulator that binds target promoter DNA ... Plays a key role in the regulation of embryonic development. Required for normal development of the definitive gut endoderm. Required for normal looping of the embryonic heart tube. Plays an important role in embryonic and postnatal vascular development

SOX5.job: switches on genes that help the body build cartilage
SOX5.basis: Transcription factor involved in chondrocytes differentiation and cartilage formation ... promotes expression of genes important for chondrogenesis

SOX6.job: switches on genes that help build cartilage as the skeleton develops
SOX6.basis: Transcription factor that plays a key role in several developmental processes, including neurogenesis, chondrocytes differentiation and cartilage formation ... promotes expression of genes important for chondrogenesis

SOX9.job: switches on genes that turn early skeleton cells into cartilage
SOX9.basis: Transcription factor that plays a key role in chondrocytes differentiation and skeletal development ... promotes expression of genes important for chondrogenesis

SP110.job: helps switch on genes that respond to vitamin A signals
SP110.basis: Transcription factor ... Enhances transcription of genes with retinoic acid response elements (RARE)

SPAG1.job: helps assemble the motors that make the cell's tiny hairs beat
SPAG1.basis: May play a role in the cytoplasmic assembly of the ciliary dynein arms

SPART.job: helps nerve cells break down and recycle their stored fat droplets
SPART.basis: Lipophagy receptor that plays an important role in lipid droplet (LD) turnover in motor neurons ... to deliver LDs to autophagosomes for degradation via lipophagy

SPEF2.job: helps build the sperm's swimming tail and shape the sperm head
SPEF2.basis: Required for correct axoneme development in spermatozoa. Important for normal development of the manchette and sperm head morphology

SPEG.job: helps muscle cells in artery walls grow and mature
SPEG.basis: Isoform 3 may have a role in regulating the growth and differentiation of arterial smooth muscle cells
SPEG.alt: may help control how artery muscle cells grow and mature

SPEN.job: helps switch genes on or off
SPEN.basis: May serve as a nuclear matrix platform that organizes and integrates transcriptional responses ... supports transcription activation ... essential corepressor protein, which probably regulates different key pathways such as the Notch pathway ... suppresses the transactivation activity of Notch signaling
SPEN.alt: helps switch genes on or off, including turning down a key growth-signaling pathway

SPG11.job: helps nerve cells keep their inner scaffolding stable
SPG11.basis: May play a role in neurite plasticity by maintaining cytoskeleton stability and regulating synaptic vesicle transport
SPG11.alt: helps nerve cells keep their inner scaffolding stable and move signal-carrying packets

SPG7.job: breaks down worn-out or misfolded proteins inside the cell's power plants
SPG7.basis: Catalytic component of the m-AAA protease, a protease that plays a key role in proteostasis of inner mitochondrial membrane proteins ... ensures protein quality control by degrading misfolded polypeptides

SPI1.job: switches on genes that steer blood stem cells into becoming immune cells
SPI1.basis: Pioneer transcription factor, which controls hematopoietic cell fate by decompacting stem cell heterochromatin ... Transcriptionally activates genes important for myeloid and lymphoid lineages

SPINK5.job: keeps the skin's protective barrier intact by reining in skin-shedding enzymes
SPINK5.basis: Contribute to the integrity and protective barrier function of the skin by regulating the activity of defense-activating and desquamation-involved proteases

SPOP.job: tags certain other proteins so the cell knows to break them down
SPOP.basis: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex that mediates the ubiquitination of target proteins, leading most often to their proteasomal degradation

SPR.job: carries out the final steps in making tetrahydrobiopterin, a small helper molecule
SPR.basis: Catalyzes the final one or two reductions in tetra-hydrobiopterin biosynthesis to form 5,6,7,8-tetrahydrobiopterin

SPRED1.job: puts the brakes on growth signals that tell cells to multiply
SPRED1.basis: inhibits growth-factor-mediated activation of MAP kinase

SPTAN1.job: helps shape the scaffolding just under the cell's outer surface
SPTAN1.basis: Fodrin, which seems to be involved in secretion ... candidate for the calcium-dependent movement of the cytoskeleton at the membrane
SPTAN1.alt: helps shape the scaffolding under the cell's outer membrane in non-blood cells

SPTBN1.job: helps shape the support scaffolding under cell membranes, especially in the developing brain
SPTBN1.basis: candidate for the calcium-dependent movement of the cytoskeleton at the membrane ... Plays a critical role in central nervous system development and function

SPTBN2.job: helps form the inner scaffolding that shapes and supports nerve cell membranes
SPTBN2.basis: Probably plays an important role in neuronal membrane skeleton
SPTBN2.alt: helps form the inner scaffolding that supports nerve cell membranes

SPTBN4.job: holds electrical channels in place along nerve fibers and in heart muscle
SPTBN4.basis: Cytoskeletal adapter/scaffold involved in the organization of select excitable membrane microdomains (nodes of Ranvier, axon initial segment, cardiomyocyte intercalated disk) ... supports ion-channel clustering ... Plays a role in the clustering of voltage-gated sodium channel SCN8A at axon initial segments and nodes of Ranvier

SPTLC1.job: starts the first step in making sphingolipids, special fats that build cell membranes
SPTLC1.basis: Component of the serine palmitoyltransferase multisubunit enzyme (SPT) that catalyzes the initial and rate-limiting step in sphingolipid biosynthesis

SPTLC2.job: starts the first step in making sphingolipids, special fats found in cell membranes
SPTLC2.basis: Component of the serine palmitoyltransferase multisubunit enzyme (SPT) that catalyzes the initial and rate-limiting step in sphingolipid biosynthesis

SRCAP.job: swaps parts of DNA's packaging to help switch certain genes on
SRCAP.basis: Acts both as a chromatin remodeler and transcription coregulator ... mediates the ATP-dependent exchange of histone H2AZ/H2B dimers for nucleosomal H2A/H2B, leading to transcriptional regulation of selected genes expression through chromatin remodeling ... Acts as a coactivator

SRD5A3.job: helps make a fatty carrier the cell needs to attach sugars to proteins
SRD5A3.basis: Plays a key role in early steps of protein N-linked glycosylation by being involved in the conversion of polyprenol into dolichol ... Dolichols are required for the synthesis of dolichol-linked monosaccharides and the oligosaccharide precursor used for N-glycosylation

SSBP1.job: helps copy the DNA inside the cell's energy-making mitochondria
SSBP1.basis: required to maintain the copy number of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and plays a crucial role during mtDNA replication

ST3GAL5.job: adds a sugar tag to fats on cell surfaces, making molecules that guide cell growth
ST3GAL5.basis: Transfers the sialyl group ... to the non-reducing terminal galactose (Gal) of glycosphingolipids forming gangliosides (important molecules involved in the regulation of multiple cellular processes, including cell proliferation and differentiation

STAC3.job: helps skeletal muscles contract when nerves signal them
STAC3.basis: Required for normal excitation-contraction coupling in skeletal muscle and for normal muscle contraction in response to membrane depolarization

STAG1.job: helps hold copied chromosomes together until the cell divides
STAG1.basis: Component of cohesin complex, a complex required for the cohesion of sister chromatids after DNA replication ... At anaphase, the complex is cleaved and dissociates from chromatin, allowing sister chromatids to segregate

STAT1.job: carries interferon alarm signals into the cell to switch on virus-fighting genes
STAT1.basis: mediates cellular responses to interferons (IFNs) ... enters the nucleus ... to activate the transcription of IFN-stimulated genes (ISG), which drive the cell in an antiviral state

STAT3.job: carries signals from immune and growth messengers to switch on genes
STAT3.basis: Signal transducer and transcription activator that mediates cellular responses to interleukins, KITLG/SCF, LEP and other growth factors ... recruits coactivators, such as NCOA1 or MED1, to the promoter region of the target gene

STAT5B.job: carries hormone and growth signals into the cell to switch genes on
STAT5B.basis: Signal transducer and transcription activator that mediates cellular responses to cytokines, hormones and growth factors

STAT6.job: carries signals from immune messengers to switch on genes
STAT6.basis: Carries out a dual function: signal transduction and activation of transcription. Involved in IL4/interleukin-4- and IL3/interleukin-3-mediated signaling

STIL.job: helps cells copy the structures that organize cell division
STIL.basis: Plays an important role in the regulation of centriole duplication. Required for the onset of procentriole formation and proper mitotic progression

STIM1.job: senses when the cell's calcium stores run low and opens channels to refill them
STIM1.basis: Acts as a Ca(2+) sensor that gates two major inward rectifying Ca(2+) channels at the plasma membrane ... Plays a role in mediating store-operated Ca(2+) entry (SOCE), a Ca(2+) influx following depletion of intracellular Ca(2+) stores

STK11.job: puts the brakes on cell growth when the cell is low on energy
STK11.basis: Acts as a key upstream regulator of AMPK ... inhibition of signaling pathways that promote cell growth and proliferation when energy levels are low

STK4.job: helps control organ size by slowing cell growth and triggering cell death
STK4.basis: Key component of the Hippo signaling pathway which plays a pivotal role in organ size control ... by restricting proliferation and promoting apoptosis

STRC.job: links the tops of the inner ear's sound-sensing hairs together
STRC.basis: Essential to the formation of horizontal top connectors between outer hair cell stereocilia

STT3A.job: attaches sugar chains to new proteins as they are being made
STT3A.basis: Catalytic subunit of the oligosaccharyl transferase (OST) complex that catalyzes the initial transfer of a defined glycan ... to an asparagine residue ... in nascent polypeptide chains, the first step in protein N-glycosylation ... STT3A ... mediates cotranslational N-glycosylation of most sites on target proteins

STX11.job: helps immune killer cells release their toxic packets to destroy infected cells
STX11.basis: essential proteins for intracellular membrane fusion ... plays a critical role in the regulated exocytosis of cytotoxic granules by natural killer (NK) cells and cytotoxic T-lymphocytes

STX1B.job: helps nerve endings get ready to release chemical messages
STX1B.basis: Potentially involved in docking of synaptic vesicles at presynaptic active zones

STXBP1.job: helps nerve cells release chemical messengers to signal each other
STXBP1.basis: Essential for neurotransmission ... Involved in the release of neurotransmitters from neurons

STXBP2.job: helps immune killer cells release their toxic granules to destroy targets
STXBP2.basis: Functions in intracellular vesicle trafficking ... regulates cytotoxic granule exocytosis in natural killer (NK) cells

SUCLA2.job: helps cells make energy from food inside their power plants
SUCLA2.basis: ATP-specific succinyl-CoA synthetase functions in the citric acid cycle (TCA), coupling the hydrolysis of succinyl-CoA to the synthesis of ATP

SUFU.job: keeps a growth-and-development signal switched off until it's needed
SUFU.basis: Negative regulator in the hedgehog/smoothened signaling pathway that acts by sequestering the GLI (GI1, GLI2 and GLI3) transcription factors in the cytoplasm ... When smoothened signaling is initiated, GLI transcription factors dissociate from SUFU, translocate to the nucleus and activate expression of target genes ... Required for normal embryonic development

SUMF1.job: switches on a family of enzymes that break down sulfur-tagged molecules
SUMF1.basis: catalyzes the conversion of cysteine to 3-oxoalanine on target proteins ... occurs in the maturation of arylsulfatases

SUOX.job: turns sulfite into harmless sulfate as the body breaks down certain amino acids
SUOX.basis: Catalyzes the oxidation of sulfite to sulfate, the terminal reaction in the oxidative degradation of sulfur-containing amino acids

SURF1.job: helps assemble a key energy-making machine in the cell's power plants
SURF1.basis: Component of the MITRAC (mitochondrial translation regulation assembly intermediate of cytochrome c oxidase complex) complex, that regulates cytochrome c oxidase assembly

SYCE1.job: helps hold paired chromosomes together while egg and sperm cells form
SYCE1.basis: Major component of the transverse central element of synaptonemal complexes (SCS), formed between homologous chromosomes during meiotic prophase

SYN1.job: helps nerve cells control the release of their chemical messages
SYN1.basis: Neuronal phosphoprotein that coats synaptic vesicles ... Acts as a regulator of synaptic vesicles trafficking, involved in the control of neurotransmitter release at the pre-synaptic terminal

SYNCRIP.job: binds the cell's gene-message copies and helps process, edit and break them down
SYNCRIP.basis: Heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein (hnRNP) implicated in mRNA processing mechanisms ... may modulate the postranscriptional C to U RNA-editing of the APOB mRNA ... May be involved in translationally coupled mRNA turnover

SYNE1.job: anchors the cell's nucleus to its internal scaffolding and helps position it
SYNE1.basis: forms a linking network between organelles and the actin cytoskeleton ... involved in the connection between the nuclear lamina and the cytoskeleton ... play an important role in the transmission of mechanical forces across the nuclear envelope and in nuclear movement and positioning

SYNGAP1.job: helps brain cells fine-tune their connections for learning
SYNGAP1.basis: Major constituent of the PSD essential for postsynaptic signaling ... it may play a role in NMDAR-dependent control of AMPAR potentiation, AMPAR membrane trafficking and synaptic plasticity

SYNJ1.job: helps nerve endings recycle the tiny bubbles that carry chemical messages
SYNJ1.basis: Phosphatase that hydrolyzes phosphate groups from the inositol ring of phosphoinositides ... participates in the rapide neck formation of the newly generated synaptic vesicle ... participates in the clathrin uncoating of synaptc vesicle formed via budding from synaptic endosomes after ultrafast endocytosis

SZT2.job: helps cells sense when nutrients run low and slow their growth
SZT2.basis: functions in the amino acid-sensing branch of the TORC1 signaling pathway ... required to negatively regulate mTORC1 signaling in absence of amino acids

TAB2.job: helps switch on signals inside cells that trigger inflammation and immune responses
TAB2.basis: Adapter required to activate the JNK and NF-kappa-B signaling pathways ... this acts as a scaffold to organize a large signaling complex ... Regulates the IL1-mediated translocation of NCOR1 out of the nucleus

TACO1.job: helps the cell's power plants build part of their energy-making machinery
TACO1.basis: Acts as a translational activator of mitochondrially-encoded cytochrome c oxidase 1
TACO1.alt: helps mitochondria make a key part of their energy-producing machinery

TAFAZZIN.job: reshapes a key fat in the membranes of the cell's power plants
TAFAZZIN.basis: Acyltransferase required to remodel newly synthesized phospholipid cardiolipin ... a key component of the mitochondrial inner membrane ... necessary for adequate mitochondrial function

TANC2.job: holds traveling message packets in place at the receiving ends of nerve cells
TANC2.basis: Scaffolding protein in the dendritic spines which acts as immobile postsynaptic posts able to recruit KIF1A-driven dense core vesicles to dendritic spines

TAOK1.job: helps cells respond to stress and helps the brain's nerve cells develop
TAOK1.basis: Acts as an activator of the p38/MAPK14 stress-activated MAPK cascade ... Plays an essential role in the regulation of neuronal development in the central nervous system

TAP1.job: carries protein fragments inside cells so they can be shown to the immune system
TAP1.basis: In complex with TAP2 mediates unidirectional translocation of peptide antigens from cytosol to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) for loading onto MHC class I (MHCI) molecules ... essential for peptide-MHCI assembly and antigen presentation

TAP2.job: moves protein fragments inside cells so they can be shown to the immune system
TAP2.basis: In complex with TAP1 mediates unidirectional translocation of peptide antigens from cytosol to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) for loading onto MHC class I (MHCI) molecules ... essential for peptide-MHCI assembly and antigen presentation

TARDBP.job: helps cells edit and manage RNA, the working copies of genes
TARDBP.basis: RNA-binding protein that is involved in various steps of RNA biogenesis and processing ... regulates the splicing of many non-coding and protein-coding RNAs

TARS2.job: loads the amino acid threonine onto its carrier for building proteins
TARS2.basis: Catalyzes the attachment of threonine to tRNA(Thr)

TAT.job: helps the body break down tyrosine, an amino acid from food
TAT.basis: Transaminase involved in tyrosine breakdown. Converts tyrosine to p-hydroxyphenylpyruvate.

TBC1D24.job: helps nerve cells grow their branches and keep their connections working
TBC1D24.basis: Involved in neuronal projection development ... Required for the maintenance of postsynaptic neuron dendritic spines in the adult ... Involved in the regulation of synaptic vesicle trafficking

TBC1D32.job: helps shape the cell's antenna-like sensing hair so cells read growth signals
TBC1D32.basis: controls the structure of the primary cilium by coordinating assembly of the ciliary membrane and axoneme, allowing GLI2 to be properly activated in response to Shh signaling

TBCD.job: helps fold the building blocks of the cell's internal scaffolding
TBCD.basis: Tubulin-folding protein implicated in the first step of the tubulin folding pathway and required for tubulin complex assembly

TBCK.job: helps carry genetic messages to the right places inside cells
TBCK.basis: Component of the FERRY complex ... involved in the localization and the distribution of specific mRNAs most likely by mediating their endosomal transport

TBK1.job: helps cells sound the alarm and fight off viruses and bacteria
TBK1.basis: plays an essential role in regulating inflammatory responses to foreign agents ... Following activation of toll-like receptors by viral or bacterial components ... leading to transcriptional activation of pro-inflammatory and antiviral genes ... Restricts bacterial proliferation

TBL1XR1.job: helps hormone-sensing proteins in the nucleus switch genes on
TBL1XR1.basis: Plays an essential role in transcription activation mediated by nuclear receptors ... leading to the subsequent proteasomal degradation of N-Cor complex, thereby allowing cofactor exchange, and transcription activation

TBX20.job: switches genes on and off to help the heart form and stay healthy
TBX20.basis: Acts as a transcriptional activator and repressor required for cardiac development and may have key roles in the maintenance of functional and structural phenotypes in adult heart

TBX22.job: helps shape the roof of the mouth as a baby develops
TBX22.basis: Probable transcriptional regulator involved in developmental processes. This is major determinant crucial to palatogenesis

TBX3.job: switches off certain genes to shape the developing limbs and breasts
TBX3.basis: Transcriptional repressor involved in developmental processes ... Probably plays a role in limb pattern formation ... Required for mammary placode induction, and maintenance of the mammary buds during development

TBX4.job: switches on genes that help the lungs, hips and legs form
TBX4.basis: Transcriptional regulator that has an essential role in the organogenesis of lungs, pelvis, and hindlimbs

TBX5.job: switches on genes that shape the heart and arms as they develop
TBX5.basis: DNA-binding protein that regulates the transcription of several genes and is involved in heart development and limb pattern formation

TBXAS1.job: makes thromboxane, a signal that tightens blood vessels and helps platelets clump
TBXAS1.basis: Catalyzes the conversion of prostaglandin H2 (PGH2) to thromboxane A2 (TXA2), a potent inducer of blood vessel constriction and platelet aggregation

TCAP.job: helps hold together the giant spring-like protein inside muscle fibers
TCAP.basis: Muscle assembly regulating factor. Mediates the antiparallel assembly of titin (TTN) molecules at the sarcomeric Z-disk

TCF12.job: switches on genes that help nerve cells form
TCF12.basis: Transcriptional regulator. Involved in the initiation of neuronal differentiation. Activates transcription by binding to the E box

TCF20.job: helps switch on other genes by boosting the proteins that control them
TCF20.basis: Transcriptional activator ... It stimulates the activity of various transcriptional activators such as JUN, SP1, PAX6 and ETS1, suggesting a function as a coactivator

TCF3.job: switches on genes that decide what young cells become, such as immune cells
TCF3.basis: Transcriptional regulator ... play major roles in determining tissue-specific cell fate during embryogenesis, like muscle or early B-cell differentiation

TCF4.job: switches on genes that help young nerve cells mature
TCF4.basis: Transcription factor that binds to the immunoglobulin enhancer Mu-E5/KE5-motif. Involved in the initiation of neuronal differentiation. Activates transcription by binding to the E box

TCF7L2.job: switches genes on or off in response to growth signals from outside the cell
TCF7L2.basis: Participates in the Wnt signaling pathway ... Acts as a repressor in the absence of CTNNB1, and as activator in its presence

TCIRG1.job: is part of a pump that makes spaces inside and around cells acidic
TCIRG1.basis: Subunit of the V0 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase) ... V-ATPase is responsible for acidifying and maintaining the pH of intracellular compartments and in some cell types, is targeted to the plasma membrane, where it is responsible for acidifying the extracellular environment

TCN2.job: carries vitamin B12 through the blood and delivers it to cells
TCN2.basis: Primary vitamin B12-binding and transport protein. Delivers cobalamin to cells

TCOF1.job: helps cells build ribosomes, the machines that make proteins
TCOF1.basis: acts as a regulator of RNA polymerase I by connecting RNA polymerase I with enzymes responsible for ribosomal processing and modification

TCTN1.job: guards the base of the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs, controlling what enters
TCTN1.basis: Component of the tectonic-like complex, a complex localized at the transition zone of primary cilia and acting as a barrier that prevents diffusion of transmembrane proteins between the cilia and plasma membranes

TCTN2.job: helps form a gate at the base of the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
TCTN2.basis: Component of the tectonic-like complex, a complex localized at the transition zone of primary cilia and acting as a barrier that prevents diffusion of transmembrane proteins between the cilia and plasma membranes

TCTN3.job: helps build the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs and pass on growth signals
TCTN3.basis: required for tissue-specific ciliogenesis ... Necessary for signal transduction through the sonic hedgehog (Shh) signaling pathway

TDP2.job: repairs DNA by removing proteins stuck to broken DNA strands
TDP2.basis: DNA repair enzyme that can remove a variety of covalent adducts from DNA ... Catalyzes the hydrolysis of dead-end complexes between DNA and the topoisomerase 2 (TOP2) active site tyrosine residue ... enable the repair of TOP2-induced DNA double-strand breaks/DSBs

TEK.job: picks up signals that help blood vessels grow and stay stable
TEK.basis: acts as a cell-surface receptor for ANGPT1, ANGPT2 and ANGPT4 and regulates angiogenesis ... but also maintenance of vascular quiescence ... Inhibits angiogenesis and promotes vascular stability in quiescent vessels

TELO2.job: helps cells respond to DNA damage by keeping key signaling proteins stable
TELO2.basis: Regulator of the DNA damage response (DDR). Part of the TTT complex that is required to stabilize protein levels of the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-related protein kinase (PIKK) family proteins

TERT.job: rebuilds the protective caps on the ends of chromosomes
TERT.basis: main activity is the elongation of telomeres by acting as a reverse transcriptase that adds simple sequence repeats to chromosome ends

TET3.job: removes chemical tags from DNA, helping reset genes after fertilization
TET3.basis: catalyzes the conversion of the modified genomic base 5-methylcytosine (5mC) into 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) and plays a key role in epigenetic chromatin reprogramming in the zygote following fertilization ... probably constitutes the first step in cytosine demethylation
