TFAP2B.job: switches on genes that shape the face and limbs as a baby develops
TFAP2B.basis: Sequence-specific DNA-binding protein that ... regulate transcription of selected genes ... AP-2-beta appears to be required for normal face and limb development

TFE3.job: switches on genes that build the cell's recycling centers when nutrients run low
TFE3.basis: Transcription factor that acts as a master regulator of lysosomal biogenesis ... Upon starvation or lysosomal stress, inhibition of MTOR induces TFE3 dephosphorylation, resulting in transcription factor activity ... binds the CLEAR-box sequence ... present in the regulatory region of many lysosomal genes, leading to activate their expression

TFR2.job: helps cells take in iron carried in the blood
TFR2.basis: Mediates cellular uptake of transferrin-bound iron

TFRC.job: brings iron into cells by grabbing iron-carrying proteins from the blood
TFRC.basis: Cellular uptake of iron occurs via receptor-mediated endocytosis of ligand-occupied transferrin receptor into specialized endosomes ... Endosomal acidification leads to iron release

TGDS.job: helps make long sugar chains needed for building the skeleton
TGDS.basis: UDP-glucose 4,6-dehydratase that converts UDP-glucose into UDP-4-keto-6-deoxyglucose, and which is required for glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis and skeletal development

TGFB2.job: makes a growth signal, plus a piece that keeps it switched off until needed
TGFB2.basis: Precursor of the Latency-associated peptide (LAP) and Transforming growth factor beta-2 (TGF-beta-2) chains, which constitute the regulatory and active subunit of TGF-beta-2
TGFB2.alt: is cut into a growth signal plus a partner piece that keeps it in check

TGFBR1.job: picks up growth-control signals at the cell surface and passes them inside
TGFBR1.basis: the non-promiscuous receptor for the TGF-beta cytokines ... Transduces the TGFB1, TGFB2 and TGFB3 signal from the cell surface to the cytoplasm and is thus regulating ... cell cycle arrest ... control of mesenchymal cell proliferation and differentiation, wound healing, extracellular matrix production

TGFBR2.job: picks up signals that control cell growth and healing
TGFBR2.basis: the receptor for the TGF-beta cytokines TGFB1, TGFB2 and TGFB3 ... Transduces the TGFB1, TGFB2 and TGFB3 signal from the cell surface to the cytoplasm and thus regulates ... control of mesenchymal cell proliferation and differentiation, wound healing, extracellular matrix production
TGFBR2.alt: picks up TGF-beta signals that control cell growth, healing and tissue building

TH.job: starts the body's production of dopamine and adrenaline
TH.basis: Catalyzes the conversion of L-tyrosine to L-dihydroxyphenylalanine (L-Dopa), the rate-limiting step in the biosynthesis of catecholamines, dopamine, noradrenaline, and adrenaline

THOC2.job: helps ship finished gene messages out of the cell's nucleus
THOC2.basis: Component of the THO subcomplex of the TREX complex which is thought to couple mRNA transcription, processing and nuclear export ... Required for efficient export of polyadenylated RNA and spliced mRNA

THOC6.job: helps carry gene messages out of the cell's control center
THOC6.basis: Component of the THO subcomplex of the TREX complex which is thought to couple mRNA transcription, processing and nuclear export ... where it functions in mRNA export to the cytoplasm

THPO.job: signals the bone marrow to make platelets, the cells that help blood clot
THPO.basis: cytokine affecting the proliferation and maturation of megakaryocytes ... It may be the major physiological regulator of circulating platelets

TIMM50.job: helps bring proteins into mitochondria, the cell's power plants
TIMM50.basis: Essential component of the TIM23 complex, a complex that mediates the translocation of transit peptide-containing proteins across the mitochondrial inner membrane

TIMM8A.job: helps carry new proteins into the cell's power plants, the mitochondria
TIMM8A.basis: Mitochondrial intermembrane chaperone that participates in the import and insertion of some multi-pass transmembrane proteins into the mitochondrial inner membrane ... guide them through the mitochondrial intermembrane space

TIMMDC1.job: helps build the first machine in the cell's energy-making chain
TIMMDC1.basis: Chaperone protein involved in the assembly of the mitochondrial NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase complex (complex I). Participates in constructing the membrane arm of complex I

TIMP3.job: blocks enzymes that break down the scaffolding between cells
TIMP3.basis: Regulates extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling through inhibition of matrix metalloproteinases (MMP)

TINF2.job: helps protect the protective caps on the ends of chromosomes
TINF2.basis: Component of the shelterin complex (telosome) that is involved in the regulation of telomere length and protection ... protects chromosome ends

TK2.job: makes building blocks for copying the DNA inside the cell's power plants
TK2.basis: Phosphorylates thymidine, deoxycytidine, and deoxyuridine in the mitochondrial matrix ... mtDNA synthesis depends solely on TK2 and DGUOK

TMC1.job: forms the channel in inner ear hair cells that turns sound into nerve signals
TMC1.basis: Pore-forming subunit of the mechanotransducer (MET) non-selective cation channel complex located at the tips of stereocilia of cochlear hair cells, where it mediates mechanoelectrical transduction required for hearing

TMEM106B.job: helps move the cell's recycling centers along nerve cells
TMEM106B.basis: In neurons, involved in the transport of late endosomes/lysosomes

TMEM126A.job: helps place new proteins into the inner walls of the cell's power plants
TMEM126A.basis: cooperates with OXA1L for the insertion of newly synthesized mitochondrial proteins into the inner membrane ... Required for the assembly of the ND4 module of mitochondrial complex I

TMEM126B.job: helps build the first machine in the cell's power plants that makes energy
TMEM126B.basis: involved in the assembly of the mitochondrial complex I ... Participates in constructing the membrane arm of complex I

TMEM127.job: helps keep cell growth in check by damping the mTOR growth signal
TMEM127.basis: Controls cell proliferation acting as a negative regulator of TOR signaling pathway mediated by mTORC1

TMEM216.job: helps cells build their antenna-like sensing hairs
TMEM216.basis: Essential for primary ciliogenesis and embryonic development, facilitating the activation of Hedgehog (Hh) signaling pathway

TMEM231.job: helps form a gate at the base of the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
TMEM231.basis: component of the tectonic-like complex, a complex localized at the transition zone of primary cilia and acting as a barrier that prevents diffusion of transmembrane proteins between the cilia and plasma membranes

TMEM237.job: helps build the base of the cell's hair-like antennae
TMEM237.basis: Component of the transition zone in primary cilia. Required for ciliogenesis

TMEM43.job: helps hold together the envelope that wraps the cell's nucleus
TMEM43.basis: May have an important role in maintaining nuclear envelope structure by organizing protein complexes at the inner nuclear membrane

TMEM67.job: helps cells build and shape their antenna-like sensing hairs
TMEM67.basis: Required for ciliary structure and function ... Involved in the regulation of cilia length and appropriate number

TMEM70.job: helps assemble the machine that makes energy inside the cell's power plants
TMEM70.basis: Scaffold protein that participates in the c-ring assembly of mitochondrial ATP synthase ... participates in the early stage of mitochondrial ATP synthase biogenesis

TMEM94.job: is thought to help store magnesium inside the cell
TMEM94.basis: Could function in the uptake of Mg(2+) from the cytosol into the endoplasmic reticulum and regulate intracellular Mg(2+) homeostasis
TMEM94.alt: may help store magnesium inside the cell

TMIE.job: helps the inner ear's sensing hairs turn sound into nerve signals
TMIE.basis: Auxiliary subunit of the mechanotransducer (MET) non-specific cation channel complex located at the tips of stereocilia of cochlear hair cells and that mediates sensory transduction in the auditory system

TMPRSS3.job: helps keep the inner ear's sound-sensing hair cells alive and working
TMPRSS3.basis: plays a role in hearing ... permissive factor for cochlear hair cell survival and activation at the onset of hearing

TMPRSS6.job: helps control how much iron the body absorbs from food
TMPRSS6.basis: Through the cleavage of cell surface hemojuvelin (HJV), a regulator of the expression of the iron absorption-regulating hormone hepicidin/HAMP, plays a role in iron homeostasis

TNFRSF13B.job: picks up signals that help immune cells make antibodies
TNFRSF13B.basis: Receptor for TNFSF13/APRIL and TNFSF13B/TALL1/BAFF/BLYS ... Involved in the stimulation of B- and T-cell function and the regulation of humoral immunity

TNFRSF1A.job: picks up an immune alarm signal that triggers inflammation or cell death
TNFRSF1A.basis: Receptor for TNF/TNFSF2 and LTA/TNFSF1, which activates the tumor necrosis factor-mediated (TNF) signaling pathway upon ligand-binding ... acts as a master regulator of the immune system, which either (1) promotes cell survival and inflammation by activating the canonical NF-kappa-B pathway or (2) trigger programmed cell death

TNFRSF9.job: helps killer immune cells survive and attack infected or abnormal cells
TNFRSF9.basis: Conveys a signal that enhances CD8(+) T-cell survival, cytotoxicity ... thereby promoting immunity against viruses and tumors

TNFSF11.job: signals cells to become bone-dissolving cells that reshape and renew bone
TNFSF11.basis: Osteoclast differentiation and activation factor ... Induces osteoclastogenesis ... to allow differentiation of osteoclasts

TNNC1.job: senses calcium to switch on heart and muscle contraction
TNNC1.basis: Troponin is the central regulatory protein of striated muscle contraction ... The binding of calcium to Tn-C abolishes the inhibitory action of Tn on actin filaments

TNNI3.job: lets heart muscle relax between beats by acting as a brake on contraction
TNNI3.basis: Troponin I is the inhibitory subunit of troponin, the thin filament regulatory complex which confers calcium-sensitivity to striated muscle actomyosin ATPase activity

TNNT1.job: helps slow-twitch skeletal muscle fibers contract when calcium signals them
TNNT1.basis: Troponin T is the tropomyosin-binding subunit of troponin, the thin filament regulatory complex which confers calcium-sensitivity to striated muscle actomyosin ATPase activity
TNNT1.alt: helps muscles contract in response to calcium

TNPO3.job: carries gene-editing helper proteins into the cell's control center, the nucleus
TNPO3.basis: Importin, which transports target proteins into the nucleus ... Specifically mediates the nuclear import of splicing factor serine/arginine (SR) proteins

TNR.job: helps form the brain's supporting scaffold that guides how nerve cells stick and grow
TNR.basis: Neural extracellular matrix (ECM) protein involved in interactions with different cells and matrix components ... evoking a stable adhesion and differentiation, or repulsion and inhibition of neurite growth

TNRC6B.job: helps tiny RNA molecules switch off genes by silencing their messages
TNRC6B.basis: Plays a role in RNA-mediated gene silencing by both micro-RNAs (miRNAs) and short interfering RNAs (siRNAs) ... Required for miRNA-dependent translational repression

TOPORS.job: attaches small tags to other proteins, marking some for breakdown and controlling cell growth
TOPORS.basis: Functions as an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase and as an E3 SUMO1-protein ligase ... involved in cell growth, cell proliferation and apoptosis that regulates p53/TP53 stability through ubiquitin-dependent degradation

TOR1AIP1.job: helps keep the membrane around the cell's nucleus intact

TP63.job: switches genes on and off to help build skin layers and limbs
TP63.basis: Acts as a sequence specific DNA binding transcriptional activator or repressor ... Plays a role in the regulation of epithelial morphogenesis ... regulate the initiation of epithelial stratification ... Required for limb formation from the apical ectodermal ridge

TP73.job: helps decide whether cells with damaged DNA should self-destruct
TP73.basis: Participates in the apoptotic response to DNA damage. Isoforms containing the transactivation domain are pro-apoptotic, isoforms lacking the domain are anti-apoptotic

TPM1.job: helps control muscle contraction, including in the heart
TPM1.basis: Plays a central role, in association with the troponin complex, in the calcium dependent regulation of vertebrate striated muscle contraction

TPM2.basis: Binds to actin filaments in muscle and non-muscle cells. Plays a central role, in association with the troponin complex, in the calcium dependent regulation of vertebrate striated muscle contraction

TPM3.job: helps control when muscles contract and keeps cell scaffolding stable
TPM3.basis: Binds to actin filaments in muscle and non-muscle cells ... Plays a central role, in association with the troponin complex, in the calcium dependent regulation of vertebrate striated muscle contraction ... In non-muscle cells is implicated in stabilizing cytoskeleton actin filaments

TPP2.job: trims leftover protein pieces into small bits so cells can reuse their building blocks
TPP2.basis: releases N-terminal tripeptides from polypeptides and is a component of the proteolytic cascade acting downstream of the 26S proteasome ... It plays an important role in intracellular amino acid homeostasis

TPRN.job: keeps the inner ear's sound-sensing hairs firmly anchored
TPRN.basis: Essential for hearing ... Required for maintenance of stereocilia on both inner and outer hair cells ... Necessary for the integrity of the stereociliary rootlet

TRA2B.job: helps decide which pieces of a gene's message are kept when it's edited
TRA2B.basis: Sequence-specific RNA-binding protein which participates in the control of pre-mRNA splicing. Can either activate or suppress exon inclusion.

TRAF3IP1.job: helps cells organize their inner scaffolding and build hair-like antennae
TRAF3IP1.basis: Involved in the regulation of microtubule cytoskeleton organization ... Involved in ciliogenesis

TRAF7.job: tags other proteins to help control immune and inflammation signals
TRAF7.basis: E3 ubiquitin and SUMO-protein ligase that plays a role in different biological processes such as innate immunity, inflammation or apoptosis

TRAPPC11.job: helps move newly made proteins from one part of the cell to the next
TRAPPC11.basis: Involved in endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi apparatus trafficking at a very early stage

TRAPPC4.job: helps move packages of cargo between the cell's internal compartments
TRAPPC4.basis: Plays a role in vesicular transport from endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi

TRAPPC6B.job: helps move materials between compartments inside cells, especially developing nerve cells
TRAPPC6B.basis: Component of a transport protein particle (TRAPP) complex that may function in specific stages of inter-organelle traffic ... Specifically involved in the early development of neural circuitry

TRAPPC9.job: is thought to help nerve cells mature
TRAPPC9.basis: Functions as an activator of NF-kappa-B through increased phosphorylation of the IKK complex. May function in neuronal cells differentiation.

TRDN.job: helps muscles release stored calcium to trigger each contraction, including heartbeats
TRDN.basis: Contributes to the regulation of lumenal Ca2+ release via the sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release channels RYR1 and RYR2, a key step in triggering skeletal and heart muscle contraction

TREX1.job: clears stray bits of DNA from inside cells so the immune system stays calm
TREX1.basis: Major cellular 3'-to-5' DNA exonuclease which digests single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) and double-stranded DNA ... Prevents cell-intrinsic initiation of autoimmunity ... Unless degraded, these DNA fragments accumulate in the cytosol and activate the cGAS-STING innate immune signaling

TRIM32.job: tags other proteins for disposal and helps cells recycle their own worn-out parts
TRIM32.basis: E3 ubiquitin ligase that plays a role in various biological processes including neural stem cell differentiation, innate immunity, inflammatory resonse and autophagy ... Ubiquitinates XIAP and targets it for proteasomal degradation

TRIM37.job: stops cells from copying their centrioles, the structures that organize cell division, too often
TRIM37.basis: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase required to prevent centriole reduplication

TRIM8.job: helps tune the body's first-line immune defenses against germs
TRIM8.basis: participates in multiple biological processes including cell survival, differentiation, apoptosis, and in particular, the innate immune response

TRIO.job: helps cells reshape their inner scaffolding to move and grow, including nerve cells
TRIO.basis: Involved in coordinating actin remodeling, which is necessary for cell migration and growth ... Plays a key role in the regulation of neurite outgrowth

TRIOBP.job: steadies the protein strands that shape cells and help them contract
TRIOBP.basis: Regulates actin cytoskeletal organization, cell spreading and cell contraction by directly binding and stabilizing filamentous F-actin and prevents its depolymerization

TRIP11.job: keeps the cell's packaging and shipping center in shape and working
TRIP11.basis: Is a membrane tether required for vesicle tethering to Golgi. Has an essential role in the maintenance of Golgi structure and function

TRIP12.job: tags certain proteins for disposal, helping control DNA repair
TRIP12.basis: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase involved in ubiquitin fusion degradation (UFD) pathway and regulation of DNA repair ... thereby forming 'Lys-29/Lys-48'-branched ubiquitin chains that accelerate proteasomal degradation of target proteins

TRIT1.job: adds a chemical tag to molecules cells use to build proteins
TRIT1.basis: Catalyzes the transfer of a dimethylallyl group onto the adenine at position 37 of both cytosolic and mitochondrial tRNAs
TRIT1.alt: adds a chemical tag to the cell's protein-building helpers, including in mitochondria

TRMT1.job: adds chemical tags to the molecules that help cells build proteins
TRMT1.basis: Dimethylates a single guanine residue at position 26 of most nuclear- and mitochondrial-encoded tRNAs

TRMT5.job: helps the cell's power plants read genetic code correctly when building proteins
TRMT5.basis: Involved in mitochondrial tRNA methylation ... a modified base adjacent to the anticodon of tRNAs and required for accurate decoding
TRMT5.alt: adds chemical tags to the mitochondria's protein-building helpers so they read genes accurately

TRMU.job: helps the cell's power plants read genetic code correctly when building proteins
TRMU.basis: Catalyzes the 2-thiolation of uridine at the wobble position (U34) of mitochondrial tRNA(Lys), tRNA(Glu) and tRNA(Gln)
TRMU.alt: tweaks the mitochondria's protein-building helpers so they read genetic code correctly

TRNT1.job: adds the finishing tail that lets tRNA molecules carry amino acids to build proteins
TRNT1.basis: catalyzes the addition and repair of the essential 3'-terminal CCA sequence in tRNAs, which is necessary for the attachment of amino acids to the 3' terminus of tRNA molecules

TRPM1.job: lets calcium into retina cells to pass on light signals
TRPM1.basis: mediate the influx of Ca(2+) ... Plays an essential role for the depolarizing photoresponse of retinal ON bipolar cells

TRPM3.job: lets calcium into cells, helping nerves sense painful heat
TRPM3.basis: non-selective divalent cation-conducting channel that is permeable to Ca(2+) ... with a high permeability for Ca(2+) ... In neurons of the dorsal root ganglia, functions as thermosensitive channel for the detection of noxious heat

TRPV4.job: lets calcium into cells when they sense swelling, pressure or heat
TRPV4.basis: Non-selective calcium permeant cation channel involved in osmotic sensitivity and mechanosensitivity ... Also activated by heat

TRRAP.job: helps add chemical tags to DNA's packaging that switch genes on
TRRAP.basis: Adapter protein, which is found in various multiprotein chromatin complexes with histone acetyltransferase activity (HAT), which gives a specific tag for epigenetic transcription activation ... Probably acts by linking transcription factors such as E1A, MYC or E2F1 to HAT complexes such as STAGA thereby allowing transcription activation

TSC1.job: helps put the brakes on cell growth when nutrients are scarce
TSC1.basis: a multiprotein complex that acts as a negative regulator of the canonical mTORC1 complex ... to promote cellular biomass generation and growth ... In absence of nutrients, the TSC-TBC complex inhibits mTORC1

TSFM.job: helps the cell's power plants build their own proteins

TSPAN12.job: helps blood vessels grow in the back of the eye
TSPAN12.basis: Plays a central role in retinal vascularization by regulating norrin (NDP) signal transduction

TTC12.job: helps build the motors that make airway hairs and sperm tails beat
TTC12.basis: plays a role in the proper assembly of dynein arm complexes in motile cilia in both respiratory cells and sperm flagella

TTC19.job: keeps part of the cell's energy-making machinery working by clearing worn-out pieces
TTC19.basis: Required for the preservation of the structural and functional integrity of mitochondrial respiratory complex III ... Involved in the clearance of UQCRFS1 N-terminal fragments

TTC21B.job: carries cargo back down the cell's hair-like antennae
TTC21B.basis: Component of the IFT complex A (IFT-A), a complex required for retrograde ciliary transport ... Essential for retrograde trafficking of IFT-1, IFT-B and GPCRs

TTC7A.job: helps place an enzyme at the cell's outer edge to make a signaling fat
TTC7A.basis: Component of a complex required to localize phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase (PI4K) to the plasma membrane ... The complex acts as a regulator of phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PtdIns(4)P) synthesis

TTC8.job: is part of a protein coat that sorts cargo into the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
TTC8.basis: The BBSome complex is thought to function as a coat complex required for sorting of specific membrane proteins to the primary cilia ... Required for proper BBSome complex assembly and its ciliary localization
TTC8.alt: helps deliver proteins into the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs

TTLL5.job: adds small chemical tags to the tiny scaffolding tubes inside cells
TTLL5.basis: Polyglutamylase which modifies tubulin, generating polyglutamate side chains on the gamma-carboxyl group of specific glutamate residues within the C-terminal tail of tubulin

TTR.job: carries thyroid hormone in the blood
TTR.basis: Thyroid hormone-binding protein. Probably transports thyroxine from the bloodstream to the brain
TTR.alt: carries thyroid hormone in the blood, likely ferrying it to the brain

TUBA1A.job: builds the tiny tubes that give cells their shape and internal tracks
TUBA1A.basis: Tubulin is the major constituent of microtubules, protein filaments consisting of alpha- and beta-tubulin heterodimers

TUBB1.job: builds the tiny tubes that give cells their shape and move things around inside them
TUBB1.basis: Tubulin is the major constituent of microtubules, a cylinder consisting of laterally associated linear protofilaments composed of alpha- and beta-tubulin heterodimers
TUBB1.alt: forms one half of the paired building blocks of the hollow tubes that shape cells

TUBB2A.job: builds the tiny tubes that give cells their shape and move things around inside them
TUBB2A.basis: Tubulin is the major constituent of microtubules ... composed of alpha- and beta-tubulin heterodimers
TUBB2A.alt: is one half of the paired building blocks that form tiny supporting tubes inside cells

TUBB2B.job: builds the cell's internal scaffolding and helps nerve cells find their place
TUBB2B.basis: Tubulin is the major constituent of microtubules ... Plays a critical role in proper axon guidance ... Implicated in neuronal migration

TUBB3.job: builds the inner scaffolding of nerve fibers and helps them find their way
TUBB3.basis: Tubulin is the major constituent of microtubules ... TUBB3 plays a critical role in proper axon guidance and maintenance

TUBB4A.job: builds the tiny tubes that give cells their shape and move things around inside them
TUBB4A.basis: Tubulin is the major constituent of microtubules, a cylinder consisting of laterally associated linear protofilaments composed of alpha- and beta-tubulin heterodimers
TUBB4A.alt: is one form of beta-tubulin, a building block of the cell's tube-shaped internal scaffolding

TUBB4B.job: builds the tiny tubes that give cells their shape and move things around inside them
TUBB4B.basis: Tubulin is the major constituent of microtubules, a cylinder consisting of laterally associated linear protofilaments composed of alpha- and beta-tubulin heterodimers
TUBB4B.alt: pairs with a partner protein to build microtubules, the tiny tubes inside cells

TUBG1.job: starts the growth of the tiny tubes that shape cells and pull chromosomes apart
TUBG1.basis: Gamma-tubulin is a key component of the gamma-tubulin ring complex (gTuRC) which mediates microtubule nucleation ... a critical step in centrosome duplication and spindle formation

TULP1.job: helps the eye's light-sensing cells work, connect and survive
TULP1.basis: Required for normal development of photoreceptor synapses. Required for normal photoreceptor function and for long-term survival of photoreceptor cells.

TULP3.job: carries signal-receiving proteins into the cell's antenna-like sensing hairs
TULP3.basis: Protein-protein adapter that drives transport of G protein-coupled receptors into primary cilia

TUSC3.job: helps attach sugar chains to newly made proteins
TUSC3.basis: Acts as accessory component of the N-oligosaccharyl transferase (OST) complex which catalyzes the transfer of a high mannose oligosaccharide ... to an asparagine residue ... in nascent polypeptide chains

TWIST1.job: switches genes on or off to guide how the skull's bones form and join
TWIST1.basis: Acts as a transcriptional regulator ... Regulates cranial suture patterning and fusion ... Heterodimerization is also required for osteoblast differentiation

TWNK.job: unzips the DNA inside mitochondria, the cell's power plants, so it can be copied
TWNK.basis: Mitochondrial helicase involved in mtDNA replication and repair ... Has DNA strand separation activity needed to form a processive replication fork

TXNDC15.job: helps cells build their hair-like antennae and pass on signals through them
TXNDC15.basis: Acts as a positive regulator of ciliary hedgehog signaling ... Involved in ciliogenesis

TXNL4A.job: helps cut and paste genetic messages into their final working form
TXNL4A.basis: Plays a role in pre-mRNA splicing as component of the U5 snRNP and U4/U6-U5 tri-snRNP complexes that are involved in spliceosome assembly

TYMP.job: helps grow and maintain blood vessels
TYMP.basis: May have a role in maintaining the integrity of the blood vessels. Has growth promoting activity on endothelial cells, angiogenic activity in vivo

TYR.job: starts making melanin, the pigment that colors skin, hair and eyes
TYR.basis: functions in the formation of pigments such as melanins ... Catalyzes the initial and rate limiting step in the cascade of reactions leading to melanin production from tyrosine

UBA2.job: helps attach small tags that change how other proteins work
UBA2.basis: acts as an E1 ligase for SUMO1, SUMO2, SUMO3 ... mediates ATP-dependent activation of SUMO proteins
UBA2.alt: helps attach small protein tags called SUMO that change how other proteins work

UBA5.job: starts attaching a small tag protein to other proteins
UBA5.basis: E1-like enzyme which specifically catalyzes the first step in ufmylation ... Activates UFM1
UBA5.alt: starts the process of attaching a small tag protein, UFM1, to other proteins

UBE2A.job: attaches small tags to other proteins, marking some for disposal or changing what they do
UBE2A.basis: E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme that accepts ubiquitin from the ubiquitin-activating enzyme E1 and transfers it to a E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase ... plays a role in transcription regulation by catalyzing the monoubiquitination of histone H2B ... is involved in N-end rule-dependent protein degradation

UBE3A.job: tags other proteins for disposal, helping shape connections between brain cells
UBE3A.basis: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase which accepts ubiquitin from an E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme in the form of a thioester and transfers it to its substrates ... Acts as a regulator of synaptic development by mediating ubiquitination and degradation of ARC

UBE3B.job: tags other proteins for disposal, helping control metabolism and nerve cell branching
UBE3B.basis: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase which ... directly transfers the ubiquitin to targeted substrates. Ubiquitinates BCKDK and targets it for degradation, thereby regulating various metabolic processes ... Involved in the positive regulation of neurite branching in hippocampal neurons

UBQLN2.job: delivers worn-out or misfolded proteins to the cell's disposal machinery
UBQLN2.basis: Mediates the proteasomal targeting of misfolded or accumulated proteins for degradation by binding (via UBA domain) to their polyubiquitin chains and by interacting (via ubiquitin-like domain) with the subunits of the proteasome

UBR1.job: tags certain proteins by their starting end so the cell breaks them down
UBR1.basis: Recognizes and binds proteins bearing specific N-terminal residues that are destabilizing according to the N-end rule, leading to their ubiquitination and subsequent degradation

UBTF.job: switches on the genes that make the cell's protein-building machinery
UBTF.basis: Recognizes the ribosomal RNA gene promoter and activates transcription mediated by RNA polymerase I (Pol I)

UCHL1.job: recycles the cell's disposal tags so worn-out proteins can be cleared
UCHL1.basis: Deubiquitinase ... recognizes and hydrolyzes a peptide bond at the C-terminal glycine of ubiquitin to maintain a stable pool of monoubiquitin that is a key requirement for the ubiquitin-proteasome and the autophagy-lysosome pathways

UFM1.job: acts as a small tag that attaches to other proteins to change what they do
UFM1.basis: Ubiquitin-like modifier which can be covalently attached via an isopeptide bond to lysine residues of substrate proteins ... Ufmylation is involved in various processes, such as ribosome recycling, response to DNA damage, transcription or reticulophagy

UMOD.job: forms a gel-like layer lining kidney tubes that helps keep water in
UMOD.basis: Functions in biogenesis and organization of the apical membrane of epithelial cells of the thick ascending limb of Henle's loop (TALH), where it promotes formation of complex filamentous gel-like structure that may play a role in the water barrier permeability

UNC13A.job: helps nerve cells get chemical messages ready for release
UNC13A.basis: Involved in neurotransmitter release by acting in synaptic vesicle priming prior to vesicle fusion

UNC13D.job: helps immune cells release the toxic packets they use to kill infected cells
UNC13D.basis: Plays a role in cytotoxic granule exocytosis in lymphocytes ... fuses with perforin-containing granules at the immunologic synapse and licences them for exocytosis

UPF3B.job: helps cells find and destroy faulty gene messages before they make bad proteins
UPF3B.basis: Involved in nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) of mRNAs containing premature stop codons ... serving as link between the EJC core and NMD machinery

UROD.job: helps make heme, the iron-holding part of blood that carries oxygen
UROD.basis: participates in the fifth step in the heme biosynthetic pathway

UROS.job: helps build heme, the part of blood that carries oxygen
UROS.basis: Catalyzes cyclization of the linear tetrapyrrole, hydroxymethylbilane, to the macrocyclic uroporphyrinogen III ... the various sub-pathways leading to the wide diversity of porphyrins ... oxygen transport (heme)

USH1C.job: holds together the inner ear's sound-sensing hairs so they can detect sound
USH1C.basis: Anchoring/scaffolding protein ... that mediates mechanotransduction in cochlear hair cells. Required for normal development and maintenance of cochlear hair cell bundles

USP7.job: removes disposal tags from other proteins so they aren't broken down
USP7.basis: Hydrolase that deubiquitinates target proteins ... preventing their degradation

USP9X.job: removes disposal tags from other proteins, saving them from being broken down
USP9X.basis: Deubiquitinase involved both in the processing of ubiquitin precursors and of ubiquitinated proteins ... preventing degradation of proteins through the removal of conjugated ubiquitin

VAPB.job: links the cell's protein-making network to other compartments it trades materials with
VAPB.basis: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-anchored protein that mediates the formation of contact sites between the ER and endosomes

VARS1.job: loads the amino acid valine onto its carrier so cells can build proteins
VARS1.basis: Catalyzes the attachment of valine to tRNA(Val)

VARS2.job: attaches the protein building block valine to its carrier molecule, ready for protein-making
VARS2.basis: Catalyzes the attachment of valine to tRNA(Val)

VCAN.job: helps connect cells to the supportive material that surrounds them
VCAN.basis: May play a role in intercellular signaling and in connecting cells with the extracellular matrix ... Binds hyaluronic acid

VCL.job: links the cell's inner skeleton to the spots where cells anchor and attach
VCL.basis: Actin filament (F-actin)-binding protein involved in cell-matrix adhesion and cell-cell adhesion

VCP.job: pulls damaged or misfolded proteins out so the cell can break them down
VCP.basis: binds ubiquitinated proteins and is necessary for the export of misfolded proteins from the ER to the cytoplasm, where they are degraded by the proteasome ... Required for cytoplasmic retrotranslocation of stressed/damaged mitochondrial outer-membrane proteins and their subsequent proteasomal degradation ... the clearance of ubiquitinated protein by autophagy

VHL.job: tags low-oxygen alarm proteins for disposal when oxygen levels are normal
VHL.basis: Involved in the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation ... recruits hydroxylated hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) under normoxic conditions

VIPAS39.job: helps cells sort and deliver materials to the right side of the cell
VIPAS39.basis: Proposed to be involved in endosomal maturation ... may play a role in the apical RAB11A-dependent recycling pathway and in the maintenance of the apical-basolateral polarity

VLDLR.job: pulls fat-carrying particles from the blood into cells and helps guide young brain cells
VLDLR.basis: cell surface receptor that binds VLDL and transports it into cells by endocytosis ... transmit the extracellular RELN signal ... required for the correct positioning of newly generated neurons

VPS11.job: helps deliver cell materials to the cell's recycling centers for breakdown
VPS11.basis: Plays a role in vesicle-mediated protein trafficking to lysosomal compartments ... Required for fusion of endosomes and autophagosomes with lysosomes

VPS13B.job: moves fats between compartments inside cells and helps keep cell traffic flowing
VPS13B.basis: Mediates the transfer of lipids between membranes at organelle contact sites ... to assist traffic between early and recycling endosomes

VPS33B.job: helps deliver cargo bubbles to the cell's recycling centers
VPS33B.basis: May play a role in vesicle-mediated protein trafficking to lysosomal compartments and in membrane docking/fusion reactions of late endosomes/lysosomes

VPS35.job: helps cells rescue useful proteins from the trash and send them back for reuse
VPS35.basis: component of the retromer cargo-selective complex (CSC) ... acting to prevent missorting of selected transmembrane cargo proteins into the lysosomal degradation pathway ... endosome-to-plasma membrane transport for cargo protein recycling

VWF.job: helps platelets stick to injured blood vessels so blood can clot
VWF.basis: Important in the maintenance of hemostasis, it promotes adhesion of platelets to the sites of vascular injury

WAC.job: links gene reading to chemical tags on DNA's packaging proteins
WAC.basis: Acts as a linker between gene transcription and histone H2B monoubiquitination ... thereby linking and regulating H2BK120ub1 and gene transcription

WARS2.job: helps the cell's power plants build their own proteins
WARS2.basis: Catalyzes the attachment of tryptophan to tRNA(Trp)

WAS.job: helps cells reshape their inner scaffolding
WAS.basis: Regulates insulin sensitivity and metabolic homeostasis ... Protects against age-dependent and diet-induced insulin resistance. Note: this text describes MOTS-c, a small peptide normally assigned to the mitochondrial MT-RNR1 gene. The WAS gene usually makes a different protein, WASP, so the gene-to-text pairing should be checked before publishing.
WAS.alt: helps cells reshape their inner scaffolding, and may help immune cells and platelets work

WDFY3.job: helps cells gather clumped proteins and send them for disposal
WDFY3.basis: Required for selective macroautophagy (aggrephagy). Acts as an adapter protein by linking specific proteins destined for degradation to the core autophagic machinery

WDPCP.job: helps cells build their hair-like antennae and line up in tissues
WDPCP.basis: Probable effector of the planar cell polarity signaling pathway which regulates the septin cytoskeleton in both ciliogenesis and collective cell movements ... CPLANE (ciliogenesis and planar polarity effectors) complex

WDR19.job: helps carry cargo inside the cell's hair-like antennae
WDR19.basis: component of the IFT complex A (IFT-A), a complex required for retrograde ciliary transport and entry into cilia of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), it is involved in cilia function and/or assembly

WDR26.job: helps relay signals inside cells and tag certain proteins for disposal
WDR26.basis: G-beta-like protein involved in cell signal transduction ... Core component of the CTLH E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex that selectively accepts ubiquitin from UBE2H and mediates ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation

WDR35.job: helps carry cargo along the cell's hair-like antennae and build them
WDR35.basis: As a component of the IFT complex A (IFT-A), a complex required for retrograde ciliary transport ... it is involved in ciliogenesis and ciliary protein trafficking

WDR37.job: helps immune cells store calcium and keeps their numbers steady
WDR37.basis: Required for normal ER Ca2+ handling in lymphocytes ... it plays an essential role in stabilizing peripheral lymphocyte populations

WDR45.job: helps cells package their own waste and worn-out parts for recycling
WDR45.basis: Component of the autophagy machinery that controls the major intracellular degradation process by which cytoplasmic materials are packaged into autophagosomes and delivered to lysosomes for degradation

WDR62.job: helps the brain's outer layer grow by guiding nerve cell growth and movement
WDR62.basis: Required for cerebral cortical development. Plays a role in neuronal proliferation and migration

WDR72.job: helps form hard, mature tooth enamel
WDR72.basis: Plays a major role in formation of tooth enamel ... Specifically required during the maturation phase of amelogenesis for normal formation of the enamel matrix

WFS1.job: helps cells manage their internal calcium stores and handle stress
WFS1.basis: Participates in the regulation of cellular Ca(2+) homeostasis, at least partly, by modulating the filling state of the endoplasmic reticulum Ca(2+) store ... Negatively regulates the ER stress response

WHRN.job: helps build and maintain the inner ear's sound-sensing hairs and supports vision
WHRN.basis: Involved in hearing and vision as member of the USH2 complex. Necessary for elongation and maintenance of inner and outer hair cell stereocilia in the organ of Corti in the inner ear

WIPF1.job: helps reshape the cell's inner scaffolding so cells can change shape
WIPF1.basis: Plays a role in the reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton ... resulting in the disassembly of stress fibers in favor of filopodia formation. Plays a role in the formation of cell ruffles

WNK1.job: helps control blood pressure by managing how salts move into cells
WNK1.basis: acts as a key regulator of blood pressure and regulatory volume increase by promoting ion influx

WNK4.job: helps the kidneys balance salt and potassium, which helps control blood pressure
WNK4.basis: key regulator of ion transport in the distal nephron and blood pressure ... regulates the balance between renal salt reabsorption and K(+) secretion

WNT10A.job: sends signals that help teeth, skin, hair and sweat glands develop
WNT10A.basis: Ligand for members of the frizzled family ... Plays a role in normal ectoderm development ... Required for normal tooth development ... Required for normal postnatal development and maintenance of tongue papillae and sweat ducts ... Required for normal hair follicle function

WRN.job: unwinds tangled DNA to help copy and repair it
WRN.basis: DNA-helicase activity ... May play an important role in the dissociation of joint DNA molecules that can arise as products of homologous recombination, at stalled replication forks or during DNA repair. Alleviates stalling of DNA polymerases at the site of DNA lesions ... Plays a role in double-strand break repair

WWOX.job: helps damaged cells self-destruct and helps bones develop normally
WWOX.basis: plays a role in apoptosis. Required for normal bone development ... May function synergistically with p53/TP53 to control genotoxic stress-induced cell death

XIAP.basis: regulates not only caspases and apoptosis, but also modulates inflammatory signaling and immunity ... Acts as a direct caspase inhibitor ... Acts as an important regulator of innate immunity
XIAP.alt: stops cells from self-destructing and helps the immune system respond to germs

XPA.job: finds DNA damaged by sunlight and starts its repair
XPA.basis: Involved in DNA nucleotide excision repair (NER). Initiates repair by binding to damaged sites ... sites of DNA damage after UV irradiation

XPC.job: spots damaged spots in DNA so repair crews can fix them
XPC.basis: Involved in global genome nucleotide excision repair (GG-NER) by acting as damage sensing and DNA-binding factor ... The XPC complex is proposed to represent the first factor bound at the sites of DNA damage

XPNPEP3.job: trims the first building blocks off certain small protein pieces
XPNPEP3.basis: Catalyzes the removal of a penultimate prolyl residue from the N-termini of peptides

YARS1.job: loads the amino acid tyrosine onto its carrier so cells can build proteins
YARS1.basis: Tyrosine--tRNA ligase that catalyzes the attachment of tyrosine to tRNA(Tyr)

YARS2.job: attaches the building block tyrosine to its carrier molecule for making proteins
YARS2.basis: Catalyzes the attachment of tyrosine to tRNA(Tyr)

YIF1B.job: helps ship newly made proteins to the right places inside cells
YIF1B.basis: Functions in endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi vesicle-mediated transport ... Plays a key role in targeting to neuronal dendrites receptors such as HTR1A ... probably through protein transport to these compartments

YY1.job: switches many genes on or off by binding where they start
YY1.basis: Multifunctional transcription factor that exhibits positive and negative control on a large number of cellular and viral genes by binding to sites overlapping the transcription start site

ZAP70.job: relays the alarm that switches on T cells, a key type of immune cell
ZAP70.basis: plays an essential role in regulation of the adaptive immune response ... When antigen presenting cells (APC) activate T-cell receptor (TCR), a serie of phosphorylations lead to the recruitment of ZAP70 ... ultimately lead to lymphokine production, T-cell proliferation and differentiation

ZBTB11.basis: May be involved in transcriptional regulation
ZBTB11.alt: may help control which genes are switched on or off

ZBTB18.job: switches off certain genes to guide brain and muscle development
ZBTB18.basis: Transcriptional repressor that plays a role in various developmental processes such as myogenesis and brain development

ZBTB20.basis: May be a transcription factor ... Plays a role in postnatal myogenesis
ZBTB20.alt: may help switch genes on or off

ZBTB24.job: is thought to help switch on genes in response to a growth signal
ZBTB24.basis: May be involved in BMP2-induced transcription
ZBTB24.alt: may help switch on genes in response to a growth signal

ZC4H2.job: helps nerve cells develop and connect to muscles
ZC4H2.basis: Involved in neuronal development and in neuromuscular junction formation

ZDHHC9.job: attaches fatty tags to other proteins, helping them work at cell membranes
ZDHHC9.basis: Palmitoyltransferase that catalyzes the addition of palmitate onto various protein substrates ... thereby promoting membrane translocation

ZEB2.job: binds DNA to switch certain genes off
ZEB2.basis: Transcriptional inhibitor that binds to DNA sequence 5'-CACCT-3' in different promoters ... Represses transcription of E-cadherin

ZFHX4.job: is thought to help nerve and muscle cells mature
ZFHX4.basis: May play a role in neural and muscle differentiation (By similarity). May be involved in transcriptional regulation
ZFHX4.alt: may help nerve and muscle cells mature by switching genes on or off

ZFPM2.job: helps switch on genes that shape the developing heart and its blood vessels
ZFPM2.basis: Transcription regulator that plays a central role in heart morphogenesis and development of coronary vessels from epicardium, by regulating genes that are essential during cardiogenesis

ZIC1.job: switches on genes that help the brain and spinal cord develop
ZIC1.basis: Acts as a transcriptional activator. Involved in neurogenesis. Plays important roles in the early stage of organogenesis of the CNS, as well as during dorsal spinal cord development and maturation of the cerebellum

ZIC3.job: switches on genes that help the embryo set up its left and right sides
ZIC3.basis: Acts as a transcriptional activator. Required in the earliest stages in both axial midline development and left-right (LR) asymmetry specification

ZMIZ1.job: helps switch on certain genes, including ones that respond to male hormones
ZMIZ1.basis: Acts as a transcriptional coactivator. Increases ligand-dependent transcriptional activity of AR

ZMPSTE24.job: trims lamin A, a protein that gives the cell's control center its shape
ZMPSTE24.basis: Transmembrane metalloprotease whose catalytic activity is critical for processing lamin A/LMNA on the inner nuclear membrane

ZMYM2.basis: Involved in the negative regulation of transcription

ZMYND10.job: helps assemble the motors that make the cell's tiny hairs beat
ZMYND10.basis: Involved in axonemal pre-assembly of inner and outer dynein arms (IDA and ODA, respectively) for proper axoneme building for cilia motility

ZMYND11.job: reads chemical tags on DNA's packaging to slow down busy genes
ZMYND11.basis: Chromatin reader that specifically recognizes and binds histone H3.3 trimethylated at 'Lys-36' (H3.3K36me3) and regulates RNA polymerase II elongation ... Colocalizes with highly expressed genes and functions as a transcription corepressor

ZMYND8.job: reads chemical tags on DNA's packaging to help switch genes on or off
ZMYND8.basis: Chromatin reader that recognizes dual histone modifications ... May act as a transcriptional corepressor ... Also activates transcription elongation by RNA polymerase II

ZNF292.basis: May be involved in transcriptional regulation
ZNF292.alt: may help control which genes are switched on

ZNF341.job: switches on genes that keep the immune system in balance
ZNF341.basis: Transcriptional activator of STAT3 involved in the regulation of immune homeostasis ... Also able to activate STAT1 transcription

ZNF462.job: controls how DNA is packed to guide which genes switch on as nerve cells develop
ZNF462.basis: involved in transcription by regulating chromatin structure and organization ... Regulates neuronal development and neural cell differentiation

ZNF711.job: switches on genes that help the brain and its nerve cells develop
ZNF711.basis: Transcription regulator required for brain development ... leading to activated expression of genes involved in neuron development

ZSWIM6.job: helps the brain and nerves develop, including areas that control movement
ZSWIM6.basis: involved in nervous system development, important for striatal morphology and motor regulation
